title_en: Langfang Telecom escorts the silver-haired digital life.
body_en:
Recently, Hebei Langfang Telecom went to the local elderly care center to carry out activities to assist and respect the elderly, bringing thoughtful services and heartfelt care to the elderly. 
At the event, the staff of the Langfang Telecom Love Wing Station quickly got involved in the service work. They provided free mobile phone screen protectors and cleaning services for the elderly, with every action being meticulous in order to provide the best user experience for the elderly. Faced with various problems encountered by the elderly in using their phones, the staff remained patient, answering and solving each one. 
Considering that the elderly generally have difficulty operating smartphones, the staff adopted a one-on-one software guidance approach, teaching the elderly how to use apps step by step. From WeChat video calls, sharing moments, to Alipay online payments, and utility bill payments, the staff provided detailed explanations and demonstrations, allowing the elderly to better enjoy the convenience brought by the smart era and bridge the "digital divide." 
While providing practical mobile phone services, anti-fraud education was also a key focus of this activity. The staff carefully selected classic anti-fraud videos, combined with real and common fraud cases in life, and used easy-to-understand language to explain common fraud methods and prevention techniques to the elderly. In order to deepen the understanding of anti-fraud knowledge, the love ambassadors also innovated in their approach, using scenario simulations and interactive quizzes to encourage active participation and discussion among the elderly. 
The successful organization of this event not only effectively improved the digital life skills of the elderly, enabling them to use smartphones more freely and enjoy the convenience of smart living, but also built a solid anti-fraud "firewall" within the elderly community, enhancing their awareness and self-protection abilities. Langfang Telecom will continue to deepen its services for the elderly, closely focusing on the actual needs of the elderly to carry out more diverse and content-rich activities, allowing the convenience of smart living to benefit more elderly people, and ensuring that the traditional virtues of respecting and caring for the elderly are passed down and promoted throughout society.
sentiment_reason: Not related to Alibaba's physical entities

title_en: The world's attention/Hong Kong IPO gathers 5 trillion, ranking among the top in the world for 28 years.
body_en:
In the past 28 years since Hong Kong's return to the motherland, the IPO market has also experienced 28 years of vigorous development. Data shows that in the past 28 years, the cumulative fundraising amount in the Hong Kong new stock market is about 5 trillion yuan, and the fundraising scale has long been among the top in the world, injecting strong vitality into the financial market. Chen Liang, Chairman of CICC, told Ta Kung Pao reporters that Hong Kong's significant achievements are not only due to the rapid rise of the mainland economy, but also to Hong Kong's active integration into the overall development of the country. He emphasized that in the long run, Hong Kong will still be the preferred platform for mainland companies to list overseas, and will continue to play an important role as a link between international capital and mainland assets. Ta Kung Pao reporter Jiang Quqiao

"In the past 28 years, the fundraising scale of Hong Kong IPOs has always maintained a leading position in the global market, which is a remarkable achievement." Chen Liang evaluated the progress made by the Hong Kong IPO market. CICC has been deeply cultivating the Hong Kong market for many years and found that the hot development trend of the new stock market is inseparable from the combined effects of "institutional innovation," "international positioning," and "mainland economic dividends."

In recent years, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange has successively introduced a number of reforms favorable to the IPO market, including allowing companies with a dual-class share structure to list in 2018. After the implementation of the reform, well-known companies such as Alibaba (09988), JD.com (09618), and Meituan (03690) have come to Hong Kong. In addition, the introduction of the Chapter 18A system allows biotechnology companies without profits to list, and the new Chapter 18C system targeting special technology companies in 2023. At the same time, the launch of the mutual market access mechanism has broken down barriers to the flow of funds between the mainland and Hong Kong, significantly improving market liquidity.

Listing reforms facilitate innovative corporate financing
Chen Liang concluded that the Hong Kong capital market, through continuous institutional innovation, has continuously expanded the inclusiveness of listings, becoming the preferred listing place for Chinese innovative companies. He pointed out that with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange continuously launching mechanisms such as Chapter 18C and "Science and Technology Enterprise Line" from 2023, the new stock market has entered a new development period, with not only a significant increase in the number of listed companies, but also continuous optimization of the structure.

In addition to institutional reforms, Chen Liang believes that Hong Kong's deep international background has successfully attracted mainland companies and global capital to converge, which is also an important driving force for the development of the IPO market. He continued to say that Hong Kong's legal system is based on common law, and the regulatory rules of regulatory agencies follow international standards, highly aligning with global financial markets, making the Hong Kong market the preferred platform for mainland companies to go international and for global capital to invest in China.

This year's fundraising data is 200 billion, returning to the top of the world
"Among the approximately 2,600 listed companies in Hong Kong, 57% are mainland companies, and their total market value accounts for over 90%." Chen Liang frankly stated that the rapid growth of the mainland economy has nurtured a large number of strong and rapidly developing excellent companies, which are the important pillars of the Hong Kong capital market. He also mentioned that the listing of leading mainland companies in Hong Kong has attracted the attention of global investors, significantly enhancing the influence of the Hong Kong stock market.

Looking back on the 28 years of development, the Hong Kong new stock market has experienced wind and rain, but has become more resilient. After experiencing the impact of the epidemic, the market has shown strong recovery momentum, and the fundraising scale has continued to improve since 2023. This year, the fundraising amount is expected to reach 200 billion yuan, returning to the top of the global fundraising rankings. Chen Liang believes that Hong Kong should fully leverage its own advantages in the future, continuously optimize the listing system, attract more high-quality companies from the mainland and overseas to list, and quickly fill in the current gaps to further enhance competitiveness.
sentiment_reason: Hong Kong's IPO policy reform helps Alibaba go public

title_en: Zhao Baofeng lets the old taste stay on more people's taste buds (picture)
body_en:
"Red Soil Braised Pork" is a long-standing Tianjin delicacy that takes 24 hours to prepare. It is described as "rich in sauce, fatty but not greasy, melts in the mouth, and leaves a lasting aftertaste." Zhao Baofeng, the fourth-generation inheritor of this dish who has dedicated 13 years to perfecting the craft, had his own dreams and profession before focusing on "Red Soil Braised Pork." He was not only a hot air balloon pilot in China but also a sailor. In 2012, he officially joined the production of "Red Soil Braised Pork," assisting his father Zhao Chenglin in expanding the production from a workshop to a factory, allowing this delicious Tianjin dish to reach beyond Tianjin.

Behind the traditional flavor
are the cultural memories of generations
Reporter: Please introduce the historical origin of "Red Soil Braised Pork."
Zhao Baofeng: My father, Zhao Chenglin, learned the craft from the second-generation inheritor Wei Shaoqi. According to Wei Shaoqi, "Red Soil Braised Pork" originated from a grand dish served at the 60th birthday banquet of Empress Dowager Cixi in the late Qing Dynasty. A chef in the imperial kitchen created this dish by meticulously cutting a piece of pork belly into the shape of the Chinese character "万" (meaning longevity) and steaming it until tender. The dish was then served with the skin side down and flipped onto a plate, presenting a vibrant color and a clear "万" character. Empress Dowager Cixi was delighted by the dish, praising its taste. After the fall of the Qing Dynasty, the chefs from the imperial kitchen scattered, and Wei Shaoqi's master, Zhang Youlin, learned the art of braised pork from a former imperial chef who had fled.

Reporter: How did "Red Soil Braised Pork" develop?
Zhao Baofeng: My father, Zhao Chenglin, started learning to make "Red Soil Braised Pork" at the age of 13 and has been in this profession for 60 years. In the 1990s, as society progressed and living standards improved, my father gained recognition for his skill in making "Red Soil Braised Pork." He boldly transformed and updated the traditional techniques, creating a unique flavor profile to cater to modern tastes, especially those of Tianjin locals. He developed a 18-step production process and insisted on using traditional methods like steaming with wood fire. Making a bowl of "Red Soil Braised Pork" takes 24 hours. The perfect dish should have a bright red color and a pure meaty aroma.

My father adhered to the concept of green food production, packaging the product in vacuum-sealed frozen form to meet the demand for traditional flavors. The stylish gift box of "Red Soil Braised Pork" is convenient, affordable, and symbolizes auspiciousness, attracting a constant stream of buyers during traditional festivals.

Reporter: How did "Red Soil Braised Pork" transition from a manual workshop to a modern factory?
Zhao Baofeng: With the continuous development of the economy, my father's workshop "Zhaoji Braised Pork" could no longer meet the growing market demand, often facing shortages, especially during the Chinese New Year. Additionally, there was a need to improve food safety and hygiene standards. Therefore, my father and I established the "Zhao Chenglin (Tianjin) Food Co., Ltd." to produce "Red Soil Braised Pork" in a factory that meets national standards. We also registered the trademark "Zhao Chenglin Red Soil Braised Pork." It was during this time that I was officially recognized as the fourth-generation inheritor of "Red Soil Braised Pork."

To upgrade the production of "Red Soil Braised Pork" from a workshop to a modern factory, my father and I went through hardships. The traditional techniques of making "Red Soil Braised Pork" and the technical standards of modern food production enterprises are quite different, sometimes conflicting. For example, the traditional method requires steaming with wood fire, but for environmental reasons, modern production processes cannot use wood fire. This difference in production methods affects the taste of the final product.

This dilemma troubled my father, but with his years of experience and expertise, he devised a set of production equipment that met the requirements. We then collaborated with renowned food machinery manufacturers in Tianjin and Beijing to develop custom equipment. Using this equipment and new processes, we were able to produce a product that met modern food safety standards while preserving the original flavor.

Staying true to the original intention
Craftsmen should focus on their craft
Reporter: After more than a decade of practice and exploration, what are your thoughts on the development of this intangible cultural heritage?
Zhao Baofeng: Whether it tastes good and retains the traditional flavor, customers can tell with just one bite. We cannot be careless in production, ensuring that the ingredients are clean and using the best quality materials to interpret the traditional craftsmanship with ingenuity. While preserving traditional techniques, we must also keep up with the times in terms of promotion, market structure, and sales. In my opinion, the key is to focus on the product itself. Regardless of changing circumstances, we have certain rules, and the quality of the product speaks for itself. Ultimately, the core of braised pork lies in its fragrance. In our inheritance, we adhere to a return to nature and staying true to our original intentions, emphasizing that craftsmen should focus on their craft.

Reporter: What are the biggest challenges encountered in the inheritance and development of this intangible cultural heritage?
Zhao Baofeng: The most challenging part is preserving the original taste of the intangible cultural heritage. As times change and technology innovates, productivity and cultural ideas differ from tradition. Being conservative will lead to being replaced by innovation, which is inevitable. Inheriting intangible cultural heritage requires balancing tradition and innovation, finding a middle ground between the two seemingly contradictory aspects.

Reporter: With the development of the times, what efforts have you made to better inherit this intangible cultural heritage?
Zhao Baofeng: In order to preserve traditional craftsmanship while meeting the needs of modern production, we designed and invented steaming and stirring equipment that simulates the manual state and complies with food safety regulations. For example, our developed steamer can accurately simulate the heat of a wood fire, allowing the braised pork to retain its original flavor to the maximum during the steaming process, making it popular among Tianjin residents. In the past, our braised pork packaging was relatively simple. With changing market demands, we realized that packaging is not only for product protection but also a cultural display. Therefore, we began to focus on packaging design, incorporating elements of Chinese culture, using red and yellow as the main color scheme, and featuring my father Zhao Chenglin's image as the main logo, preserving traditional charm while adding a sense of fashion. Although we have new packaging, we also retained some traditional packaging to continue our brand culture. Initially, our products were mainly sold locally in Tianjin. Now, we actively expand the market, establishing direct stores in various districts of Tianjin, including unmanned stores for 24-hour customer convenience. Additionally, we utilize e-commerce platforms to promote "Red Soil Braised Pork" nationwide. In terms of sales strategy, in addition to retail, we have also engaged in group purchases, especially during festivals like the Chinese New Year, to meet the gifting needs of people visiting friends and relatives.

Reporter: What is your view on the role of online communication in the inheritance of intangible cultural heritage?
Zhao Baofeng: The internet provides us with a broad sales channel and promotional platform. We conduct online sales through platforms like Douyin and Taobao, allowing more people to learn about and purchase "Zhao Chenglin Red Soil Braised Pork." In terms of promotion, we create exquisite videos and images showcasing the production process and finished products, attracting consumers. For example, the braised pork production videos we posted on Douyin received a lot of likes and attention, with many out-of-town customers being drawn in by these videos and placing orders.

We also actively engage in Douyin live streaming. For example, on March 31, 2023, the "Qingyun China · Spring Hope" Dongli District live broadcast assistance activity was conducted on the "Dongli Zhi Jia" Douyin account, where the sales of "Red Soil Braised Pork" reached 6,000 yuan during the live broadcast. In addition, we invited students from the Civil Aviation University of China to act as small anchors, entering the "Zhao Chenglin Red Soil Braised Pork" live broadcast room to introduce the brand's heritage story and production techniques, garnering 11,000 likes during the live stream. Through Douyin live streaming, "Red Soil Braised Pork" has reached a broader market, allowing more people to learn about this traditional Tianjin delicacy.

title_en: E-commerce giants are stepping up their efforts in instant retail, leading to explosive growth.
body_en:
Currently, with the increased investment from internet giants such as JD.com, Taobao, and Meituan, instant retail is experiencing explosive growth. The continuous efforts of internet platforms have also driven the rapid development of the third-party instant delivery industry. Industry insiders believe that the current "takeout war" is in the first half of the competition stage in the catering industry, and the second half will expand to department stores, groceries, supermarkets, pharmacies, and other fields, ushering in an industry tipping point. With the investment from various platforms to collectively increase industry penetration, it is expected that in 3 years, the daily volume of takeout plus instant retail will exceed that of e-commerce.
By Jiang Yongxia, a reporter from this newspaper
This year, instant retail has undoubtedly become the focus within the retail industry. With JD.com, Taobao, and other e-commerce giants intensifying their efforts in instant retail business, market competition is becoming increasingly fierce. In this instant retail market battle, whether third-party instant delivery platforms such as SF Express and Shansong can get a piece of the pie remains to be seen and will require time to test.
Intense competition in instant retail
Currently, with the increased investment from internet giants such as JD.com, Taobao, and Meituan, instant retail is experiencing explosive growth.
It is understood that JD.com's takeout business has been online for only 4 months, with a daily order volume exceeding 25 million, over 1.5 million high-quality dining establishments have joined, and the number of full-time delivery riders has exceeded 120,000.
Currently, the daily order volume of Taobao Flash Sale has exceeded 60 million. Furthermore, not long ago, Alibaba announced the merger of Ele.me into Alibaba's China e-commerce business group, focusing on unified goals and operations to promote the rapid development of instant retail.
Recently, Meituan announced that it will comprehensively expand instant retail. For example, Xiaoxiang Supermarket will gradually expand to all first and second-tier cities and gradually cover 200 high-quality county-level agricultural areas nationwide in the supply chain. Meituan Flash Sale will continue to expand its categories, such as 3C electronics, fresh food, alcoholic beverages, fast-moving daily necessities, etc., to optimize the consumer shopping experience.
The strategic adjustments made by e-commerce giants around instant retail business all reveal their emphasis on instant retail.
Shortly after the launch of JD.com's takeout service, Liu Qiangdong, the founder and chairman of JD.com, not only personally experienced delivering takeout but also invited delivery riders to dine together to promote JD.com's takeout service. On June 24th, there were reports that Alibaba's founder Jack Ma and Alibaba Group CEO Daniel Zhang appeared at the Ele.me office to participate in Taobao Flash Sale's weekly meeting.
The high level of attention and direct participation from giants have further accelerated the intense competition in the instant retail market.
JD Logistics enters the battlefield
The instant retail competition sparked by the takeout war is further evolving.
Recently, JD Logistics announced in a statement on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange that with the rapid development of JD.com's takeout business, JD Logistics has started recruiting full-time delivery riders to participate in JD.com's delivery service.
In addition to recruiting full-time delivery riders, JD Logistics has also established the position of deputy station manager in its branches to manage full-time delivery riders on a daily basis, but there will be no changes in the order and dispatch logic for full-time delivery riders.
It is understood that JD Logistics, as a mature logistics brand, has the most abundant courier management experience in the industry, and its logistics advantages, which Liu Qiangdong considers as JD's "moat," are something to be proud of. Now, JD Logistics has announced the recruitment of full-time delivery riders and the establishment of the position of deputy station manager for professional management, which will undoubtedly help further professionalize full-time delivery riders, improve their service levels, and optimize consumers' experience of using JD.com's takeout service.
Moreover, recently, JD Logistics launched the industry's first "Instant Delivery Warehouse" integrated service. As the first nationwide open instant retail warehouse and distribution integrated solution provider, JD Logistics uses a "shared front warehouse + self-operated delivery" model to lower the entry barriers for merchants in the instant retail sector.
Specifically, the "Instant Delivery Warehouse" can pre-position goods to the "nearest location to consumers," relying on JD Logistics' service level and self-operated delivery capabilities to achieve an average delivery time of 30 minutes in core areas. More importantly, through the shared warehouse model, it helps merchants break free from the constraints of high investment and high operating costs of self-built warehouses.
With the efforts of JD Logistics, a new round of "timeliness war" in instant delivery may be staged.
Third-party companies actively layout
With e-commerce giants entering the instant retail and instant delivery sectors, their order volumes are soaring, and the number of full-time delivery riders is increasing. So, do third-party instant delivery companies still have a chance?
At the beginning of the development of instant retail, in the delivery process, platforms and merchants mainly relied on social transportation resources, which also drove the rapid development of the third-party instant delivery industry. Companies such as Dada, Shansong, and SF Express have grown rapidly in this wave of dividends, and while expanding in scale, they have also successively entered the capital market. These third-party instant delivery companies not only promote industry development but also witness the industry evolution under market changes.
Recently, a person in charge of SF Express mentioned the current competitive landscape and the future development space of their own company at a shareholder meeting. The person in charge believes that the "takeout war" has driven the development of instant retail and instant delivery, leading the industry to a major outbreak. The person in charge further stated that the current "takeout war" is in the first half of the competition stage in the catering industry, and the second half will expand to department stores, groceries, supermarkets, pharmacies, and other fields, ushering in an industry tipping point. The current takeout industry is at a high point, with various platforms investing funds to collectively increase industry penetration. It is expected that in 3 years, the daily volume of takeout plus instant retail will exceed that of e-commerce.
This trend is also evident in the data from Taobao Flash Sale. According to information released by Taobao Flash Sale, the number of non-catering orders has increased by as much as 179% year-on-year. Consumer purchasing habits have shown a significant shift under the influence of "6.18," no longer limited to catering but starting to use instant delivery for various items.
With the continuous expansion of non-catering scenes in instant retail, SF Express will also have more opportunities to shine. It is reported that SF Express focuses on customized capacity for all scenarios, covering various long-distance, heavy-weight non-standard deliveries, and providing differentiated solutions for vertical categories such as supermarkets, pharmacies, and digital products. At the same time, through synergy with the SF Express ecosystem, they are creating an integrated supply chain of "warehousing + transfer + same-city instant delivery," providing one-stop fulfillment services from warehouse to warehouse, warehouse/store to consumer, to help more e-commerce brands transform and improve efficiency.
In addition, with the continued efforts of e-commerce giants, SF Express believes that they have unique advantages. "Large customers are concerned about the sustainability of dividends, unwilling to be strongly tied to platforms, and more willing to use third-party cooperation to build product brands and develop private domains. We can solve the problem of service integrity in multi-platform operations. Middle-tier merchants can leverage platform traffic to increase exposure. The company will continue to accept orders from small and medium-sized merchants, forming a diverse order ecosystem, which is beneficial for the stability and activity of delivery riders." The person in charge mentioned, "The backend also provides delivery riders with a better running environment and choices. Through technological scheduling combined with human management, dispersed delivery riders can become an efficient system, and this 'knight culture' system is solidly implemented."
sentiment_reason: Taobao is increasing investment in instant retail, and developing instant retail business can be seen as a growth point.

title_en: Express public opinion
body_en:
"The lychee season is the third peak period of the year for branches, in addition to Double 11 and 618," said a branch manager in Maoming, Guangdong, describing the busy state of the lychee season.
Similar to the above branch, as the fruit season arrives after June, many express delivery branches are putting extra effort into handling fruit parcels, even using automatic equipment to improve efficiency.
Some branches set new records for lychee delivery
Maoming, Guangdong, is known as the hometown of fruits, not only ranking among the top in the country for longan and bananas production, but also being the largest lychee producing area in the world.
Meng Lingbo, the general manager of the Jiutu Maoming branch, has been in the express delivery industry for 6 years. Every March, he estimates the lychee production in advance to prepare for the lychee season in May.
He told Yicai that this year is a bumper lychee year, "Lychee production is generally 'big' one year and 'small' the next. Last year was a small year, and the amount of lychee parcels delivered by our branch was around 200 tons." This year's delivery volume needs to be compared with the previous bumper year, with Meng Lingbo's branch reaching 600 tons in 2023, setting a new record this year at 900 tons, the largest amount of lychee parcels in his 6 years in the express delivery industry. During the lychee peak season starting at the end of May, fruit parcels accounted for nearly 30% of the daily volume at the Jiutu Maoming branch.
Handling large-scale lychee deliveries is not easy for branches. From a transportation perspective, lychee is similar to cherries, requiring high timeliness. Meng Lingbo said, "Lychee delivery is relatively difficult, as it requires high timeliness. Usually, next-day delivery is needed to ensure freshness. In the packaging process, we need to use ice packs, aluminum foil, and foam cotton, then add foam boxes on the outside to preserve freshness as much as possible. During transportation, we need to plan the optimal schedule in advance. For the final delivery, lychee parcels need to be prioritized once they arrive at the terminal branch. The taste of the same box of lychee received in the morning and in the afternoon is different."
After estimating the lychee production, branches begin preparations: communicating with transfer centers to prepare for priority transfers, reserving unloading docks, preparing direct delivery vehicles in advance, and hiring temporary receiving staff. This year, Meng Lingbo recruited a total of 60 receiving staff.
From an e-commerce perspective, Meng Lingbo said that orders come from various sources, including Pinduoduo, Taobao, Douyin, Xiaohongshu, Weishi, and other platforms, with a higher number of orders from Pinduoduo and Douyin.
In terms of improving efficiency, technology is mainly used for route planning and backend monitoring. "The lychee delivery process is interconnected. During transportation, smart scheduling algorithms provide drivers with the optimal transportation route. In case of delays, we can monitor the vehicles through the backend to ensure that each vehicle arrives at the transfer center on time," Meng Lingbo explained.

title_en: The automotive industry is exploring new models for going global.
body_en:
At the LanTu Automobile Digital Assembly Workshop in the Wuhan Economic Development Zone in Hubei Province, the 200,000th complete vehicle of LanTu Automobile rolled off the production line. Xinhua News Agency reporter Wu Zhizun
The picture shows the new energy vehicle production line of NIO's second factory in the Anhui Hefei Xinqiao Intelligent Electric Vehicle Industrial Park. Xinhua News Agency reporter Zhang Duan
Currently, the global automotive industry is undergoing accelerated transformation, and international trade relations are becoming increasingly complex, bringing many uncertainties to the supply chain structure of the automotive industry. China's new energy vehicle industry is actively participating in global cooperation with an open and innovative attitude. Strengthening the connection between China's automotive industry and the world, promoting supply chain collaboration, is crucial for the green transformation and innovative development of the global automotive industry.
Strengthening localization operations
Under the drive of electrification and intelligence, the regional pattern of the global automotive industry is undergoing profound changes. China's new energy vehicle industry is rising and has established a relatively complete industrial chain system. The latest data shows that from January to May this year, China exported 2.49 million complete vehicles, a year-on-year increase of 7.9%; and exported 855,000 new energy vehicles, a year-on-year increase of 64.6%.
At the 2025 Global New Energy Vehicle Cooperation Development (Shanghai) Forum held recently, Zhang Yongwei, Vice Chairman and Secretary-General of the China Electric Vehicle Hundred People's Association, stated that China's automotive industry needs to explore new development paths based on the new global automotive situation.
The traditional globalization cooperation model is facing bottlenecks. On the one hand, barriers to complete vehicle sales are increasing and extending to the supply chain; on the other hand, the supply chain of new energy vehicles is highly complex and may be affected by geopolitical, technological barriers, and cross-industry integration, facing potential risks.
"In this context, the previous 'brand going global + complete vehicle investment' model is difficult to work, and it is necessary to restructure the cooperation logic and path." Zhang Yongwei suggested promoting deep links between Chinese complete vehicle enterprises and supply chains with the world automotive market. Relying on China's rich variety of models and a relatively complete incremental supply chain mainly based on new energy and intelligence, empower the global automotive industry development, help other countries develop local automotive industries, and even create local brands, achieve industrial complementarity, resource sharing. At the same time, export digital, intelligent, standardized service systems, and accelerate integration into the global market.
Globalization of brands and localization of operations are gradually becoming a new model for Chinese automotive companies to expand cooperation globally.
Tang Zhikun, General Manager of the International Business Center of Guangdong Xiaopeng Automobile Technology Group Co., Ltd., introduced that Xiaopeng has explored four market models in Europe, including direct sales agents, agency system, "subsidiary + dealers," and general agents, basically achieving full coverage of the European market. In terms of brand building, they have tried cross-border marketing to help the brand penetrate local communities and cultures. For example, Norwegian consumers prefer outdoor sports, Xiaopeng Automobile has sponsored local cycling events for three consecutive years, deepening consumer recognition of the brand.
According to the latest plan of LanTu Automobile, by 2026, LanTu Automobile will cover the mainstream new energy vehicle market, enter 60 countries' markets by 2030, and establish more than 500 stores. Gao Yuan, Senior Director of Overseas Business of LanTu Automobile Technology Co., Ltd., said: "LanTu Zhiyin Global Edition is developed adaptively for overseas markets, integrating local service resources and financial supply chains to achieve win-win results by serving local users with local resources."
Collaborative layout of the entire chain ecosystem
As Chinese new energy vehicle companies go international, battery export has become an important part of the coordinated development of the industry chain.
"Global development must adhere to long-termism and drive industrial development with technology." Xiong Yonghua, Vice President of Strategy and Operations of Guoxuan High-tech, said that the company's passenger car product line has developed to the fourth generation of battery cells, establishing 8 research and development centers and 20 production bases globally, with more than 10,000 global patent technologies applied.
Many countries in Europe, America, and Southeast Asia have introduced policies related to battery localization production, carbon footprint, etc., imposing higher requirements on enterprises. For example, the EU's "New Battery Act" requires battery producers to take extended responsibility, including collection, processing, recycling, and disposal of batteries. "We plan to build 99 recycling points this year through two modes: self-built recycling supply chain and co-construction of recycling system with overseas strategic partners." Xiong Yonghua said the company has built a vertically integrated industrial chain from mineral extraction of battery raw materials, material production, battery manufacturing, product application to battery recycling and utilization.
The supply chain of traditional automotive industry includes car companies, parts suppliers, and service providers, while the new energy vehicle industry requires hardware manufacturers, energy service providers, and data service providers to build the entire value network together. Cheng Dandan, Deputy General Manager of the European subsidiary of Ruipulan Jun Energy Co., Ltd., believes that China is breaking technological monopolies through innovation in core new energy technologies such as batteries, intelligent driving, and electronic control, achieving a strategic shift from "OEM manufacturing" to "rule-making."
For new energy vehicles to truly go green overseas, it is essential to have a complete charging and swapping infrastructure, as well as a coordinated layout of vehicles, piles, networks, and storage throughout the entire chain. Sun Maojian, Vice Chairman of Hunan Jingneng New Energy Technology Co., Ltd., believes that with the current penetration rate of electrification exceeding 40%, the supply chain is shifting from cost-driven to ecology-driven. New global collaborative demands are driving the entire supply chain to break boundaries and reconstruct.
Sun Maojian stated that during the company's overseas practice, they found that the global supercharging standards are fragmented, and the rate of repeated testing for supercharging certification is high. He called for the establishment of a global high-quality intelligent supercharging network, promoting mutual recognition of testing results between China, Europe, and ASEAN, eliminating digital barriers to repeated certification, and creating a technology-sharing platform.
"For Chinese companies to successfully enter markets such as Europe, they need to pay attention not only to product competitiveness but also to a deep understanding and adaptation to local markets, regulations, culture, and user habits." Luca Ford, Director and Executive Vice President of Eldo Group, stated that establishing charging infrastructure in Europe faces multiple obstacles such as urban land constraints and complex policies, requiring Chinese supply chain companies to strengthen cooperation with local governments and enterprises to create infrastructure solutions suitable for local conditions.
Building an overseas service system
China has become the world's largest exporter of automobiles, undergoing a transformation from selling products to providing services, and then to deepening cultivation of the local market. From "going out" to "integrating in," this poses higher requirements for local operations and innovation capabilities, requiring multiple parties to work together to build a comprehensive service system for the automotive industry to go global.
In the era of digital transformation and going global, automotive companies are facing new challenges. "Safety and compliance are the first steps in the overseas plan. We cannot rush out, sell products, fail, and then retreat." Shen Tao, General Manager of the Industry Cluster of Amazon Web Services (China), analyzed that the automotive industry not only has regional compliance requirements but also needs to meet new requirements including generative AI applications, data privacy protection, etc.
Bai Hua, General Manager of the Solution and Delivery Department of China Unicom Smart Internet Technology, suggested that referring to the internationalization experience of German and Japanese car companies, Chinese car companies should design a global compliance management platform that is risk-identifiable, process-controllable, and responsibility-traceable when establishing overseas subsidiaries, to ensure alignment with local companies and laws and regulations.
"Chinese automotive going global is not just about exporting products but also about the overall breakthrough of the global layout of the industrial chain." Bai Hua believes that this requires integration with local culture, market, and industrial chain, achieving a "one country, one strategy" approach. Relying on the support of the full industry chain digital base, China Unicom Smart Internet has rooted in local operations, deploying local vehicle networking service platforms and service teams in Frankfurt, Riyadh, Singapore, and Mexico City. Next, the company will expand its digital services from vehicle networking to industry digitalization, integrating compliance solutions, overseas smart computing center solutions, digital manufacturing systems, and marketing systems.
Driven by intelligence and globalization, the automotive industry is transitioning from "electrification going global" to "intelligence going global," promoting the continuous improvement of China's international competitiveness in the automotive industry. Xing Di, Deputy General Manager of the AI Automotive Industry of Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group, introduced that Alibaba Cloud Tongyi Large Model has full-size, full-modal, and wide-open-source capabilities. The application of large models on vehicles will further improve the experience of intelligent assisted driving and intelligent cabins. Alibaba Cloud will continue to invest, accelerate the construction of a global cloud computing network, deploy full-stack AI capabilities at every node globally, and serve enterprises going global.
The automotive industry chain is long, with a long usage cycle. As the global stock of new energy vehicles increases, related companies' value overseas needs to extend from research, development, production, and sales to usage and service. Jiang Yongxing, Founder and CEO of Open Thinking Era Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., pointed out that new energy vehicle models iterate quickly, have many components, and require complex technical support. Overseas car owners may face problems such as a lack of authorized repair shops nearby and different operating system ecosystems.
Jiang Yongxing suggested that in the aftermarket of new energy vehicles going global, suppliers should jointly build a digital network, connect information such as mainframe authorization, parts maintenance, and warranty traceability, to provide better services to car owners of global car manufacturers. (Reporter Jia Jiao)

title_en: Old German companies talk about "Investing in China" Drum Tower篇
body_en:
□ Reporter Dong Xiang Correspondent Gu Xuan
"In the first five months of this year, the continuous implementation of the old-for-new policy has significantly boosted our retail sales." On June 20th, at the Gu Lou Innovation Square in Nanjing, Song Linbing, the President of Bosch Home Appliances Group in Greater China, revealed the company's latest performance. This foreign-funded enterprise, rooted in China for over 30 years, remains optimistic about the Chinese market and is committed to developing in the Chinese market.
Looking back to 1994, when China's market economy had just opened its doors, Bosch Home Appliances from Germany crossed the oceans and entered the Chinese market. Three years later, the company established Bosch China Sales Company in the Zhongnan International Building in the Gulou District of Nanjing, building a sales and service network in China.
Based in Nanjing and radiating across the country, over the past nearly 30 years, Bosch Home Appliances' industrial layout has accelerated continuously - in 2004, a home appliance park was established in Nanjing, with three factories for washing machines, kitchen appliances, and motors; in 2011, a research and development center was established in Nanjing; in 2021, the new headquarters building in China was put into use at the Gu Lou Innovation Square; last year, the China Research and Development Center was upgraded to a global research and development center, and the Home Appliance Talent Center was simultaneously unveiled.
Today, among the 7 companies Bosch Home Appliances has invested in in China, 4 are located in Nanjing, including investment companies, sales, customer service companies, and the full value chain of the home appliance park and research and development center, which have successively been recognized as the first regional headquarters of multinational companies in Nanjing and the first batch in our province. It has become the largest foreign-funded home appliance manufacturer in the Chinese market.
The advantage of talent from China has provided the company with a continuous source of innovation. The global research and development center, built with an investment of 400 million yuan, has a team of 700 engineers. Washing and drying sets complete clothing wrinkle removal in 19 minutes, refrigerators thaw deep-frozen meat in 10 minutes, embedded drinking machines achieve direct drinking and separate routes for living water, dishwashers combine sterilization and energy saving... In China for 30 years, closely following the Chinese market, carrying out localized innovation, a series of innovative products tailored to Chinese consumers have become Bosch Home Appliances' winning strategy in China.
"We are particularly grateful for the series of stable foreign investment policies continuously introduced by the Chinese government in recent years, which have strengthened our confidence and determination in investment and development in China." Song Linbing said. In August last year, the Ministry of Commerce and four other departments launched the "old-for-new" policy for home appliances. Upon hearing the news, Bosch Home Appliances immediately formed a team, participated in the enterprise selection conducted by the provincial Department of Commerce, and successfully boarded the first train at the end of September.
"Thanks to the incentive of the old-for-new policy, our retail sales achieved double-digit growth from September to December last year, especially with a significant increase in the sales proportion of emerging categories and high-efficiency products." Song Linbing introduced that the company seized the opportunity to showcase its "self-selected actions", cooperated with Suning to create a brand festival, and upgraded online stores in cooperation with Tmall and JD. A new high-performance range hood product launched for the Chinese market this year made it to the best-selling list on a certain e-commerce platform during the "6.18" period.
New market opportunities have arrived. Currently, China's demand for home appliances is shifting from new house matching to old house renovation and transformation. Residences delivered 10-15 years ago have entered a period of renovation for their kitchens and home appliances. Bosch Home Appliances, which has long been familiar with China, deeply understands this trend and actively connects with local retailers to provide a one-stop solution covering decoration design, home appliance selection, and installation services as a breakthrough in opening up new markets.
"China is one of the world's largest and most dynamic home appliance markets, and also one of Bosch Home Appliances' most important markets." Song Linbing stated that they will firmly uphold the development concept of "in China, for China, and also for the world", and tell the story of "investing in China" with practical actions.

title_en: Promote food culture and open up the value chain.
body_en:
Traditional advantageous food production areas and local specialty food industries are important development carriers and key growth engines of China's food industry. In recent years, under a series of policy guidance, various regions have been cultivating characteristic advantageous food production areas and industries according to local conditions, turning small specialties into large industries, effectively driving farmers' income growth and the high-quality development of the food industry.

A Variety of Specialty Foods Blossoming

In recent years, various regions have fully considered the development foundation and growth potential of the local food industry, taking into account factors such as local customs, dietary habits, and cultural heritage, to determine key industries for cultivation and priority development of characteristic food industries, promoting the gradual formation of a pattern of diversified development.

In Liuzhou City, Guangxi, the history of "suo" snails dates back 20,000 years, while the consumption of rice noodles can be traced back to the Qin Dynasty. In the late 1970s, in the bustling streets of Liuzhou, the clever combination of the two gave birth to the specialty snack known as snail rice noodles.

Through industrial concepts, industry chain thinking, and internet marketing, Liuzhou City has transformed snail rice noodles from a street-side "small rice noodle" into a large industry with global reach. By the end of 2020, the snail rice noodle industry in Liuzhou had surpassed three hundred million yuan. By 2024, the total sales revenue of the snail rice noodle industry chain in Liuzhou reached 75.964 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 13.4%.

Also growing into a billion-yuan industry is the Chinese prickly ash in Guizhou. Originally a "wild fruit" mainly found in Guizhou, Chinese prickly ash has been valued for its high vitamin C content compared to most fruits. Since the beginning of this century, it has been gradually developed into one of the key agricultural specialty industries in Guizhou Province. The former Chief Engineer of the State Forestry Administration, Feng Jiaping, believes that Chinese prickly ash is an industry unique to Guizhou, which can avoid industrial homogenization and is conducive to continuously expanding the market.

In recent years, Guizhou Province has strongly supported the Chinese prickly ash industry in creating high-quality products, nurturing leading enterprises, and expanding the scale of the industry. Currently, the planting area of Chinese prickly ash in Guizhou has exceeded 2 million mu, with an annual comprehensive output value exceeding one hundred billion yuan.

In Qinxian County, Changzhi City, Shanxi Province, the golden-colored and pearl-shaped Qinzhou yellow millet, as a key cultivation target of Shanxi's traditional advantageous food production areas and local specialty food industries, is becoming the "golden engine" driving local economic development and farmers' income growth.

Qinxian's yellow millet has a long history of cultivation, and the local area has now formed a pattern of large-scale, standardized, and industrialized development. There are more than 30 professional cooperatives engaged in the cultivation of "Qinzhou yellow" in Qinxian, with over 30,000 households involved. The planting area has reached 100,000 mu, with an annual millet production in Qinxian exceeding 30,000 tons.

Traditional Industries Moving towards Modern Cluster Development

The growth of small specialties into large industries relies on regions breaking away from traditional development thinking, continuously extending the industrial chain, and nurturing and expanding modern industrial clusters.

"Liuzhou City adheres to the concept of the entire industry chain, promotes the aggregation of elements in various links of the industrial chain and supply chain, and has created a modern industrial cluster centered around Liuzhou snail rice noodles, integrating 'production + processing + technology + cultural tourism,'" said Yang Zhigang, Director of the Liuzhou Municipal Bureau of Commerce.

Liuzhou City has vigorously developed customized agriculture, fully implemented standardized production, identified 20 demonstration bases for the production of raw materials for snail rice noodles, and the scale of core raw material planting and breeding has exceeded 200,000 mu; it has established the Liuzhou snail rice noodle industrial park, Liuzhou snail rice noodle production aggregation area, and Liuzhou snail rice noodle e-commerce industrial park, attracting more than 100 upstream and downstream enterprises such as raw material supply, product processing, e-commerce, and logistics distribution to settle in the park; deepened technical cooperation with more than 10 scientific research institutions, established the country's first "Snail Rice Noodle Industry College," created a number of research and development platforms, and carried out key research on the core common technologies of the snail rice noodle industry.

Guizhou Province is focusing on enhancing the influence and visibility of the "Guizhou Chinese prickly ash" public brand, promoting the modernization of the industrial cluster by leveraging the core advantages of the Chinese prickly ash production area.

Currently, various regions in Guizhou are exploring models such as "planting enterprises + cooperatives + farmers" and "processing enterprises + integrated industries + farmers" to promote large-scale planting of Chinese prickly ash. At the same time, they are strengthening the integration of production and research, creating an integrated platform covering the entire industry chain of "management, learning, research, production, processing, and sales."

Guizhou Province has collaborated with research institutions such as Sun Yat-sen University, Beijing Technology and Business University, and Guizhou University to complete 44 research projects. The Guizhou Provincial Department of Science and Technology has implemented 15 Chinese prickly ash research projects, achieving certain results in the utilization of Chinese prickly ash functional components, optimization of deep processing, and quality control improvement.

From the field to the table, Shanxi's Qinzhou yellow millet has established a green development system covering the entire industry chain of planting, processing, warehousing, logistics, sales, and services. Qinxian has introduced special support policies, investing a total of 67.31 million yuan in the past three years to support key agricultural enterprises. At the same time, it is vigorously promoting the "winter sowing millet" technology, implementing "organic dry farming," and encouraging farmers to adopt new technologies and models through policy subsidies.

Qinxian has cooperated with the national millet and sorghum industry technology system to establish a system of "technology system + leading enterprises + breeding base," creating 19 standardized green and organic breeding bases covering 3,205 mu, and cultivating excellent varieties such as "Qinhuang No. 2."

Brand Leading the Exploration of Domestic and International Markets

In the process of cultivating industrial clusters, regions focus on brand leadership to accelerate the entry of local famous products into domestic and international markets.

Leveraging the influence of the snail rice noodle brand, Liuzhou City is vigorously promoting the integration of culture and tourism. Liuzhou has created a boutique cultural experience route for snail rice noodles, launching special routes for "snail rice noodle tours" and "snail rice noodle study tours"; it has deeply explored the unique street culture of snail rice noodles nationwide, creating snail rice noodle experiential destinations for intangible cultural heritage. "Next, Liuzhou will continue to promote the internationalization and high-quality development of the snail rice noodle industry, transforming Liuzhou snail rice noodles from a local traditional specialty product into a global 'internet-famous food,'" said Yang Zhigang.

Guizhou is relying on the core advantages of the Chinese prickly ash production area to continuously enhance the influence and visibility of the "Guizhou Chinese prickly ash" public brand, creating flagship brands such as "Cinengji," empowering Chinese prickly ash to expand into the national market.

At the same time, Guizhou is advancing the sales and brand promotion of Chinese prickly ash in accordance with the strategy of coordinated online and offline development, implementing the "three-step advancement" strategy of sales and brand promotion for Chinese prickly ash in the province, the country, and globally. It is cooperating with e-commerce platforms such as JD.com and Taobao, and actively participating in offline exhibition and promotion activities to help Chinese prickly ash products "set sail overseas." The relevant person in charge of the Guizhou Industry and Information Technology Department stated that Guizhou will take the "Guizhou Chinese prickly ash" public brand as a guide, fully implement the brand strengthening enterprise strategy, and create well-known Chinese prickly ash enterprise brands and product brands.

Qinxian County, Shanxi Province, also focuses on the brand building and market expansion of Qinzhou yellow millet. On the one hand, it enhances brand visibility through geographical indication protection, organic certification, etc., and "Qinzhou yellow" has successively obtained national green and organic food certifications; on the other hand, it actively builds sales platforms, with online sales accounting for 30% of total sales. In the future, Qinxian will strengthen brand protection, publicity, and promotion, enhance brand reputation, and make Qinzhou yellow millet, the "golden pearl of the Taihang Mountains," more popular among consumers.

title_en: 【Stable Employment Enterprises in Action】Alibaba increases efforts to introduce and cultivate AI talents.
body_en:

Luo, a student from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, said that he has been paying attention to the internship recruitment dynamics since the beginning of this year. On the second day of the Alibaba Group's 2026 Spring Internship Recruitment in February, he applied for a position at Alibaba Cloud. Fortunately, he quickly received the first offer letter from the group.
Currently, many companies are actively taking measures to create more diversified job opportunities by increasing research and development investment, innovating business models, and other means. As one of the leading companies in the Internet industry, Alibaba Group is relying on its own technological advantages and platform resources to continue to focus on the AI field, continuously strengthening the recruitment and training of talents in the field of artificial intelligence.
As of now, the Alibaba Group's 2026 Spring Internship Recruitment has been completed. This recruitment activity is different from the past, as in addition to continuing to focus on positions in the technical field, there has been a significant increase in the emphasis on the field of artificial intelligence. It is reported that this internship recruitment provided more than 3,000 positions, with AI-related positions accounting for nearly half, and some AI business departments having even higher proportions, with around 65% for Alibaba Cloud's AI positions and over 80% for some AI positions.
Taotian Group under Alibaba issued over 1,000 offers for this internship recruitment, adding a large number of AI positions covering various fields such as AI algorithms, AI engineering, AI products, AI operations, and AI design.
At the same time, the "Top Talent T-Star Program" has launched a special internship recruitment, marking the first time the T-Star Program has recruited interns. Previously, this talent program mainly targeted top talents in global cutting-edge technology competitions, academia, and practical experience. It is reported that students who participate in the internship and perform well will be provided with a full-time offer under the T-Star Program by Taotian.
Wen Dao, a doctoral graduate from the Computer Department of Beihang University, joined Taotian through the T-Star project in 2024. He is currently working on training a large model for video generation at Taotian, responsible for the "Taobao Xingchen - Image Video Model."
"When I was looking for a job, I mainly applied to the talent programs of major companies. T-Star has a lot of value in terms of interview difficulty and salary level. Taotian has stable business and cash flow, which can guarantee the application of the business, as well as a lot of computing resources. For me, I can focus on long-term research and development in a certain direction, working on influential projects in the industry," Wen Dao said.
The recruitment official website shows that the positions open at Taotian are closely related to the research of new technologies in the AI field, covering algorithm engineers (large model training direction), multimodal, 3D reconstruction and generation, AIGC direction, digital human image generation and driving, natural language processing, machine learning, video coding and decoding, computer vision, basic platform development, etc.
"As a technology company that has always been committed to exploration and innovation, Alibaba is increasing its efforts to recruit and train talents in the AI field. We hope to provide a broad development space for more outstanding young talents and jointly embrace the huge development opportunities of the AI era," said Jiang Fang, Chief Talent Officer of Alibaba Group.

Gravity Media Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "the Company" or "Gravity Media") recently received the "Information Disclosure Regulatory Inquiry Letter Regarding Gravity Media Co., Ltd.'s 2024 Annual Report" (Shangzheng Gonghan [2025] No. 0648) (hereinafter referred to as the "Inquiry Letter") issued by the Shanghai Stock Exchange. In accordance with the requirements of the "Inquiry Letter," the Company, together with Yongzhonghe Certified Public Accountants (Special General Partnership), has diligently reviewed and implemented each question raised in the "Inquiry Letter." The relevant questions and their responses are as follows:

1. Regarding Business Model and Revenue Recognition. The annual report shows that the company's main business is brand marketing, social marketing, e-commerce marketing and operation services, etc., and its profit comes mainly from customer service fees and media platform channel incentives. In 2024, the company achieved a total operating income of 6.29 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 32.7%; the net profit attributable to the parent company before and after deducting non-recurring items was -18.105 million yuan and -17.281 million yuan respectively, turning from profit to loss; among which, the operating income in the fourth quarter was significantly higher than in other quarters, but the net profit declined sharply and incurred losses. The company failed to disclose its 2024 performance by the end of January 2025 as required, which the company stated was due to significant changes in domestic media platform channel policies in 2024, leading to a large deviation in the company's forecast for its 2024 performance.

Please supplement and disclose:
(1) Detailed breakdown of the main business models, including the company's service content and processes, key performance indicators, pricing methods, major customers, suppliers, and settlement policies, etc.;

[Company Reply]
Gravity Media's main business is mainly composed of three different business models: brand marketing, e-commerce marketing and operation services, and social marketing.

1. Brand Marketing
Service Content: The company provides clients with brand strategy and creative design, integrated communication, market research, and data services. Among these, brand strategy and creative design services mainly provide clients with brand positioning, content creative design, content marketing, IP customization, and other services; integrated communication services mainly provide clients with media resource purchasing plans and services for online video media, social marketing media, television media, offline advertising, and other media resources; market research and data services rely on the company's data research and application capabilities to provide consulting services such as market analysis and consumer insights for clients.
Service Process: The company participates in the client's bidding process, wins bids after rounds of comparison, and then signs an annual framework service contract or a single project service contract with the client. In the annual framework service contract model, the company recommends media advertising resources to the client and agrees on the prices of different advertising resources for various media with the client. Within the time limit specified in the annual framework service contract, the company designs a media placement plan with the client based on marketing goals, and then produces advertising materials (e.g., creative copy, image materials, video materials, etc.) according to the client's needs and places them on the media. In the single project service contract model, the company recommends media advertising resources to the client and provides services for single advertising material production and media placement.
Performance Indicators: Performance indicators for brand services and content creative services include brand awareness index, content engagement rate, etc.; integrated communication services are measured by metrics such as CPM (Cost Per Mille) and ROI (Return on Investment).
Major Customers: The company's major customers include Yili, etc.
Customer Pricing Method: The company charges fees based on the actual advertising placement after the advertisement is placed on the media. The price charged by the company to the client = Media advertising resource list price * Media discount * Agency discount rate. The company calculates the agency discount rate offered to clients based on the rebate rate of different media, taking into account the company's operating costs.
Customer Settlement Method: The company settles with clients and issues invoices after the advertisement is placed on the media. Generally, clients pay within 45 days after the company issues the invoice.
Major Suppliers: The company's major suppliers include media such as Tencent.
Supplier Settlement Method: After the advertisement is placed on the media, the company settles with the media based on the media advertising resource list price * media discount as the price benchmark, and pays the supplier after a certain settlement period.
