title_en: 8 Chinese companies listed in "Time" magazine's top 100, the rise of innovative forces in cultural and technological creativity.
body_en:
Bubble Mart, DeepSeek, and Meixue Group from mainland China have been listed on the 2025 TIME100 Most Influential Companies list, showcasing the economic strength of the mainland. The list includes disruptors like Bubble Mart, DeepSeek, and Yushu Technology; innovators like Alibaba and BYD; and titans like Meixue Group, ByteDance, and Huawei. This recognition of multiple mainland companies in TIME magazine is seen as a significant symbol, indicating that these companies have significant influence in their respective fields and are globally recognized, reflecting the increasing economic strength of the mainland.

Bubble Mart has gained global popularity due to its exclusive licensing of the popular toy Labubu. By selling various Labubu plush toy products in blind boxes and featuring Labubu in numerous TikTok unboxing videos, Bubble Mart has experienced rapid business growth. In 2024, Bubble Mart's revenue and profits more than doubled compared to 2023. Additionally, Bubble Mart is known not only for selling toys but also for creating immersive in-store experiences, such as a store in Vietnam designed like a medieval castle accessible by cable car, attracting global attention.

DeepSeek, on the other hand, gained international attention with its R1 reasoning model released in January, which was claimed to be on par with OpenAI's latest model but at a lower training cost. This led to DeepSeek's free chatbot application briefly surpassing OpenAI's ChatGPT and topping the Apple App Store rankings, shaking investors' confidence in other leading global artificial intelligence companies and causing a $1 trillion market cap loss in the US stock market. DeepSeek's rise has become a significant "wake-up call" for the US, making it one of the tech companies globally watched by the public.

BYD, which continued to be listed in 2025, has become the undisputed leader in electric vehicles, surpassing Tesla in global sales for the second consecutive quarter. BYD's focus on developing new technologies has allowed it to occupy the market-leading position, with innovations like the "God's Eye" advanced driver assistance system and a battery that can be fully charged in just 5 minutes, capable of driving 249 miles.

Market opinions suggest that the recognition of multiple mainland companies in TIME magazine holds significant symbolic meaning, indicating that these companies have significant influence in their respective fields and are globally recognized, reflecting the strong economic power of the mainland. In fact, the stock performance of these listed mainland companies that are already publicly traded has been quite impressive this year, with Bubble Mart rising 188%, Meixue Group rising over 150%, Alibaba rising 37%, and BYD rising 40% since the beginning of the year.

title_en: When the Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail meets Jiangxi
body_en:
Open the map of China's high-speed rail lines, the dense high-speed rail lines in the central region indicate the vitality and potential of this area's development. On June 28, 2015, the opening and operation of the Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail line, one of the main channels of the "Eight Vertical and Eight Horizontal" high-speed rail network in China, broke through the long-standing geographical barriers and temporal barriers in areas such as southern Anhui, northeastern Jiangxi, and northern Fujian. It also outlined the "cross skeleton" of Jiangxi's high-speed rail in northeastern Jiangxi, highlighting Jiangxi's locational advantages. In the past ten years, the Fuzhou-Ganzhou section of the Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail has accumulated 140 million passenger trips. Recently, reporters visited areas along the Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail line to experience the vitality and pulsation that high-speed rail has brought to Jiangxi's economic and social development.

"The activation of 'cool resources' leads to 'hot industries'"
At noon on June 18, Li Dongqin, a villager from Beishan Village in Sishiba Town, Guangxin District, Shangrao City, was hosting her sister who had come back from Zhejiang to visit. "In the past, when they came from Hangzhou to Shangrao, they still had to take a bus to the village after arriving in Shangrao, which took one to two hours on the road. After the Wufu Mountain Station opened, it only takes a little over ten minutes to come from Shangrao by high-speed rail, and you arrive at the doorstep when you get off the train," Li Dongqin said.

The Wufu Mountain Station mentioned by Li Dongqin is located in Sishiba Town. This small station, covering an area of over 2000 square meters, can only accommodate up to 400 people, making it one of the smallest high-speed rail stations in the country.

The opening of the Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail has shortened the distance between the small town and the outside world, bringing more and more tourists.

Wufu Mountain Town in Guangxin District, Shangrao City is located in the northern part of the Wuyi Mountains. In recent years, relying on the unique "cool resources" such as the "National Forest Park," the local area has vigorously developed summer tourism, with nearly a hundred homestays emerging, opening up a new path for rural tourism industrialization and helping villagers increase their income and become prosperous.

"The temperature here is 3 to 4 degrees Celsius lower than in the urban area all year round. You don't need to turn on the air conditioning when you sleep at night. In the summer, a large number of tourists come here to play in the water and relax and cool off," Zhong Fusheng, a villager from Chuankeng She Village in Wufu Mountain Town, is renovating his She-style courtyard to welcome this year's summer tourists. In 2021, he invested 260,000 yuan to transform his self-occupied house into a homestay. "During the peak summer season, you have to book more than 20 days in advance to get a room," Zhong Fusheng said. In the year the homestay opened, he increased his income by more than 100,000 yuan.

Wufu Mountain Town has turned "cool resources" into "hot industries," relying on local resources to make full use of the "four sales" - selling water, selling air, selling mountain products, and selling lifestyle, to drive the cluster development of homestays. "The homestays in the village started in 2020. Everyone can make money, and the enthusiasm is very high. In just four or five years, the number has increased to 95, with over 1,000 beds, driving employment for over 900 people," said Hong Xiaohua, secretary of the Chuankeng She Village Party Branch. In 2024, Wufu Mountain Town received a total of 200,000 visitors.

The once small mountain village is now full of vitality.

"Connecting good scenery to form a chain"
Before 2015, Wuyuan, known as the "most beautiful village in China," was hindered by inconvenient transportation, and the tourism market was limited to nearby short-distance tourists, with a narrow customer base and limited development. At that time, it took 4 hours to drive from Wuyuan to Nanchang and 18 hours to Beijing.

With the opening and operation of the Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail, Wuyuan Station was put into use. "I was so excited the first time I took the high-speed rail back to Wuyuan," recalled Yu Qinying, a villager from Shangmeizhou Village in Rancun Street, Wuyuan County. "Before the opening of the Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail, most of the tourists who came to Wuyuan were self-driving, with the majority being locals from Jiangxi. Now, over 80% of the guests arrive by high-speed rail." Liu Fang, the owner of Houtang Manor in Wuyuan, said.

Convenient transportation has transformed Wuyuan from an ecologically hidden small city to a popular national tourist destination. Today, more than 60 high-speed trains stop at Wuyuan every day, connecting Wuyuan closely with the Yangtze River Delta, the Pearl River Delta, the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, and other areas, significantly increasing the proportion of long-distance tourists and causing a significant change in the tourism customer structure. In 2024, Wuyuan County received 28.037 million visitors and achieved a comprehensive tourism income of 27.62 billion yuan.

With the high-speed rail in operation, life has become more prosperous.

Zhang Ming is a tour guide at the Gexian Village Resort in Gexian Village, Wuyuan County. He told reporters that there are now many tourists from Shanghai, Hangzhou, Fuzhou, and Xiamen, and the annual number of visitors to the scenic area has increased from 150,000 in 2015 to 1.8 million in 2024, with the average length of stay increasing from 1.2 days to 2.8 days. "My monthly income has increased from over 2,000 yuan to over 5,000 yuan, and people in the village have renovated their houses to open homestays and restaurants, making life more prosperous," Zhang Ming said.

The high-speed rail has expanded the radius of tourism and promoted cooperation between cities along the line. In January 2021, the four cities of Quzhou in Zhejiang Province, Huangshan in Anhui Province, Nanping in Fujian Province, and Shangrao in Jiangxi Province jointly established the cross-provincial tourism cooperation organization - the Zhejiang-Anhui-Fujian-Jiangxi "Alliance Garden," forming a cross-regional tourism model of "one trip, multiple cities." Today, the "Alliance Garden" one-code travel platform has attracted 99 scenic spots from the four cities, more than 2,300 merchants, launched 155 self-driving routes, and over 1,000 tourism products.

The high-speed rail has brought new economic vitality
One city, two high-speed rail lines, pressing the "fast forward button" for the economic development of Shangrao.

On June 19, reporters visited the Shangrao High-speed Rail Economic Pilot Zone and saw tall buildings everywhere, showing a modern atmosphere. Lian Gang, deputy director of the Shangrao High-speed Rail Economic Pilot Zone Management Committee, sighed, "When the pilot zone was established in 2016, it was still barren hills and wild ridges. Now the physical space that the pilot zone can accommodate is close to 1 million square meters, with an enterprise occupancy rate of nearly 70%, and the development speed is very fast."

Since its establishment, the pilot zone has always adhered to the development orientation of modern service industries led by the digital economy, continuously laying out in the four major areas of digital cultural creativity, information security, software and information technology services, and digital medical care, attracting more than 1,300 digital economy companies such as JD.com, Alibaba, and Netease to settle in. Last year, the pilot zone's digital economy companies achieved operating income of 101 billion yuan.

"Thanks to the convenient travel conditions, Shangrao has become the favorite city for investment by Zhejiang businessmen," Lian Gang told reporters. Currently, 70% of the merchants in the pilot zone come from the Yangtze River Delta region. Last year, three leading companies in the Internet field, Tencent Esports, Ximalaya, and Xiaohongshu, "joined hands" with Shangrao, further enriching the digital industrial ecological chain of Shangrao.

The digital industry is the leading industry in the pilot zone. In response to the call of "Shangrao Merchants Return," Wu Xubo, the founder of Tanwan Games, led his team back to Shangrao in 2015 and changed the company's main body to Jiangxi Tanwan Information Technology Co., Ltd. (referred to as Tanwan Company).

As one of the first companies to settle in the Shangrao High-speed Rail Economic Pilot Zone, Tanwan Company has evolved from a simple game operation company to a comprehensive internet game company integrating research and development, distribution, and operation, with a cumulative registered user base of over 600 million. In 2024, the company achieved operating income of 4.8 billion yuan.

"The Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail has opened an important channel for Jiangxi to the north, allowing us to reach the vast user base in Fujian and coastal areas more conveniently, and penetrate the vast market hinterland of the Yangtze River Delta," said Li Huijun, vice president of Tanwan Company. In recent years, with the help of the high-speed rail, the company has introduced a large number of technical talents from cities such as Shanghai and Hangzhou, held dozens of product launch events in Hefei, Fuzhou, and other places, attracted over 200,000 new users, and reached cooperation projects with 12 companies along the line.

The high-speed rail is not just a simple railway line but also a "Ganxin Line" that connects to national strategies and promotes economic development. This "golden link" traversing three provinces is now accelerating the efficient circulation of resources such as information, technology, and talent with a daily operation density of over 70 pairs of trains.

title_en: Involved in 126 million yuan case, hundreds of people were deceived: Victims tell the story of the scam of "proxy for affordable housing" in Haikou.
body_en: With both hands leaning on a shiny cane, Wu Xiaofen, who has physical disabilities, appeared trembling in front of the reporter. It was a normal morning in late June, with the sunlight shining on the glass of a tea restaurant on Jinpan Road in Haikou. Wu Xiaofen struggled to climb a step and sat down, placing the cane in the corner to the left of her seat. The backpack she carried was filled with a thick stack of materials, the most prominent of which was a criminal ruling made by the Higher People's Court of Hainan Province, as well as a long list of victims. Wu Xiaofen was one of the victims in this criminal ruling. Three years ago, she entrusted someone to help her purchase affordable housing in Haikou, only to be cheated out of 300,000 yuan. For an ordinary worker, this 300,000 yuan was almost all of Wu Xiaofen's savings. According to the criminal ruling in Wu Xiaofen's hands, 291 victims (as of February 29, 2024) were cheated through various channels to purchase policy-based housing in Haikou (mainly affordable housing), involving a total amount of up to 126 million yuan. This housing fraud case, directed and orchestrated by three people and involving numerous "extras" driven by interests, lasted for a staggering six years in Haikou, leaving people bewildered. On February 5 of this year, the mastermind of the case - Gan Xiaoyan, an unemployed person in Haikou, the legal representative of a real estate agency Li Yechun, and the former traffic assistant police officer in Haikou, Qiu Wenqin, were sentenced to life imprisonment, 13 years, and 10 years respectively for fraud, and their personal property was confiscated or fined. On April 17, the Higher People's Court of Hainan Province made a final ruling on the case, upholding the original verdict. How were the 291 victims deceived, how did the total amount of 126 million yuan become the basis of this fraud case, and what thoughts did this case leave people with? By opening the relevant criminal rulings and judgments, perhaps the answers can be found. "Hooked" by real estate short videos "Although the three scammers have been sentenced, our money, the victims, has not been recovered." On the morning of June 24, Chen Shiyong, a victim of the "Haikou 1.26 billion yuan real estate fraud case," told China Real Estate News that he was cheated out of 400,000 yuan when buying a house. Since being cheated out of buying affordable housing in 2022, Chen Shiyong has become particularly vigilant. When communicating with reporters via WeChat or being interviewed face-to-face, he always looked suspicious at first, spoke very little, and appeared extremely cautious. In Chen Shiyong's intermittent narration, the reporter learned that his purchase of the house was purely accidental. Chen Shiyong, who does renovations in Haikou, likes to watch short videos in his spare time. "I was watching videos and came across a real estate agent selling affordable housing, saying 'interested, private chat'." Chen Shiyong told the reporter that he and his family were crowded in a small rental house, "thinking of buying an affordable house in Haikou to settle down." Following the "interested, private chat," Chen Shiyong contacted the real estate agent through a video account, who then introduced him to a person named "Li Yechun." According to the relevant criminal judgment, Li Yechun, born in 1991, was one of the main criminals in the "Haikou 1.26 billion yuan real estate fraud case." At the time of the crime, Li Yechun's identity was the legal representative of a real estate agency in Haikou and the actual controller of a real estate agency office in Haikou for a company in Sanya. The relevant information provided by Chen Shiyong shows that on February 16, 2022, he signed a "House Purchase Agency Agreement" with Li Yechun's company, intending to purchase a 110-square-meter house in the Meishe Shijia community in Haikou. Li Yechun was responsible for helping Chen Shiyong obtain the qualifications to purchase the house, with a unit price not exceeding 9,000 yuan per square meter. The Meishe Shijia project in Haikou was one of the first affordable housing projects in Haikou to be piloted. Although the project had a small land area and only two high-rise buildings with a total of over 200 units, its location on the "golden" section of Guoxing Avenue and Wazao Road in Haikou naturally attracted the attention of homebuyers. According to the housing policy at the time, the affordable housing in Haikou was sold through a lottery system, and the Meishe Shijia project had only 217 units available for sale, attracting over 2,000 applicants. Additionally, the affordable housing project implemented a government-mandated sales price, with a unit price of 15,000 yuan per square meter. Chen Shiyong also did some calculations and realized that if he could get a house for less than 9,000 yuan per square meter, it would be a good deal. After signing the agreement, Chen Shiyong paid Li Yechun a total of 400,000 yuan for "agency service fees" and "down payment" in multiple installments. Behind the house purchase is the word "fraud" Wu Xiaofen, who was interviewed with a cane, had a different experience in purchasing a house compared to Chen Shiyong and other victims. Wu Xiaofen told the reporter that she was introduced by a classmate's classmate to purchase affordable housing from one of the main criminals in the case, Gan Xiaoyan. Who is Gan Xiaoyan? According to the aforementioned criminal judgment, Gan Xiaoyan, born in 1982, is a Haikou native with a junior high school education and unemployed. "The classmate's classmate said that Gan Xiaoyan had connections and could help with the purchase of affordable housing qualifications; the other party also said 'don't ask too many questions,' which seemed very mysterious." Wu Xiaofen told the reporter that based on her trust in her classmate, she did not inquire too much and paid Gan Xiaoyan 300,000 yuan for "housing quota fees" and other expenses. In the aforementioned judgment, a witness with the surname Wang stated that Gan Xiaoyan had indeed helped someone apply for public rental housing before and succeeded in less than two months. After that, Gan Xiaoyan's claim of having connections spread within a certain range, becoming the most powerful "trust tool" for her later fraud. "At that time, everyone around believed in her 'supernatural powers,' and few people doubted her at first." Wu Xiaofen said that whether it was Li Yechun, Gan Xiaoyan, or Qiu Wenqin, they not only played the role of "accomplice" to each other but also deceived each other. The judgment recorded that Gan Xiaoyan once had someone photoshop the official announcement information from the housing department's website and send it to Li Yechun's side, claiming that Li's client had obtained the affordable housing lottery qualification, but the traces of the photoshop were too obvious and were discovered. Driven by interests, an invisible and vast "network of interests" was formed, including various personnel such as real estate agents, social individuals, etc. Friends introduced friends, relatives introduced relatives, classmates introduced classmates, and successfully introducing clients could earn a "tea fee" of 20,000 to 50,000 yuan per unit. In addition, Gan Xiaoyan and others provided a "base price," allowing intermediaries to arbitrarily increase the price above this "base price," for example, a "base price" of 350,000 yuan per unit, with some people raising it to 600,000 yuan per unit. The reporter learned that to gain the trust of homebuyers, the fraudsters arranged for personnel to play different roles as "accomplices," taking buyers to the sales center of the affordable housing project in batches to sign contracts on-site. "The sales center staff warmly served us tea, and the purchase agreement was signed at the project site. You had no reason not to believe it." Wu Xiaofen said. Finding ways to delay time is a common trick used by Gan Xiaoyan and others to stabilize homebuyers. The judgment stated that if the victims did not receive the house as requested and asked for a refund, Gan Xiaoyan would delay by changing the community, paying a small amount of liquidated damages, making fake "pre-purchase notification letters," and fake screenshots of official website information, then continue to deceive the victims by gradually asking for money under the guise of paying for parking spaces, verification fees, etc. Another important "role" in this case, Qiu Wenqin, used his position as a traffic assistant police officer (resigned around August 2021) from January 2020 to fabricate his acquaintance with relevant department leaders, falsely claiming that he could help victims obtain qualifications to purchase affordable housing through internal connections. During this time, Qiu Wenqin used private seals and forged materials such as a fake "Haikou Affordable Housing Subscription Letter" to delay the handover time agreed upon with the victims, continuing to deceive them by asking for money under the pretext of paying the down payment, locking the house, etc. The judgment stated that by the time of the crime, Gan Xiaoyan had collected a total of 71,117,873.11 yuan from the victims, refunded 7,522,278 yuan before the crime. Except for a small portion used to repay previous debts, she spent the rest on buying private lotteries, cross-border gambling, and personal extravagance. Li Yechun collected 37,825,830 yuan from the victims, refunded 1,510,000 yuan before the crime. Except for a small portion used to repay previous debts, he spent the rest on gambling, repaying personal debts, paying intermediary fees, etc. Qiu Wenqin collected 5,791,566 yuan from the victims, refunded 90,000 yuan before the crime. Except for a small portion used to repay previous debts, he spent the rest on gambling, daily expenses, and personal extravagance. According to audits by relevant agencies, a total of 291 victims paid a total of 126,345,670.68 yuan to Gan Xiaoyan, Li Yechun, Qiu Wenqin, and other intermediaries through bank transfers, WeChat, Alipay, cash, etc. The amount involved in the case has not been refunded to the victims, with 109,624,658.68 yuan still outstanding. Reflections on the real estate fraud case The truth will eventually come to light. This real estate scam in Haikou lasted for six years, growing more and more inflated. On February 22, 2023, the Haikou police arrested Gan Xiaoyan at the Qunshang Square in Meilan District; on February 27, Li Yechun had a dispute with homebuyers at his residence and reported it to the police, leading to the discovery of his involvement with Gan Xiaoyan and others in the fraud case; on March 13, Qiu Wenqin voluntarily surrendered to the police. Qiu Wenqin's statement to the police after surrendering is quite meaningful: from early 2020 to around May 2021, when Haikou officially introduced the policy for applying to purchase affordable housing, he, relying on his position as a traffic assistant police officer, falsely claimed to have the ability to purchase affordable housing in Haikou's Daok He and Yuefang and Meishe Jiayuan Phase II projects, collecting 80,000 to 150,000 yuan from multiple clients. He later tried to seek help from relevant leaders, but the response was "not possible." It is understood that local policy-based housing includes low-rent housing, public rental housing, economically affordable housing, limited-price commercial housing, and affordable commercial housing. These types of housing have specific conditions and restrictions for application and purchase. In fact, after checking the identities of the 270 victims in this case, it was found that 106 individuals had obtained pre-purchase qualifications, but there was no evidence to show that these victims' housing qualifications were related to Gan Xiaoyan and others. It is understood that in Hainan, such real estate fraud cases are not isolated incidents. Through each case, we are forced to reflect on whether these incidents have occurred too frequently: why do such things happen repeatedly? Around 2021, the heads of two real estate agencies in Sanya City used the pretext of selling internal resettlement housing at low prices to defraud 165 homebuyers of a total of 140 million yuan, creating a major fraud case that shocked the entire country. In 2023, Zhao Mouwen, a labor dispatch worker at the Haikou Xiuying District Housing Acquisition Service Center, helped others purchase houses in the Rongjin Huayuan community, resulting in dozens of homebuyers being defrauded of up to 10 million yuan... Many homebuyers initially chose to trust Gan Xiaoyan and others for several reasons: First, information asymmetry. The victims were not very familiar with the policies and measures regarding affordable housing and other security housing. Although they were eligible to apply, they chose to use the services of scammers for convenience; it was difficult for them to distinguish between truth and falsehood regarding the scammers' carefully crafted lies and staged signing scenes. Second, greed. The government's set price for affordable housing was 15,000 yuan per square meter, but the scammers claimed that they could get a house for 6,000 to 7,000 yuan per square meter. The victims did some calculations and thought that even if they paid tens of thousands of yuan, it would still be a good deal. Third, a sense of luck. Government-subsidized housing is mainly aimed at urban low-income groups, teachers, doctors, and other special groups, and their applications require certain qualifications. Some people who did not meet the conditions held a "pick up" mentality. Fourth, driven by interests. In this case, if it were just Gan Xiaoyan and a few others "running the business," they would not have been able to create such a fraud case. Under the direction and temptation of Gan Xiaoyan and others, a carefully woven "network of interests" spread to innocent homebuyers. This network included real estate agents, social individuals, etc., who could freely increase the price above the "base price" and charge 20,000 to 50,000 yuan per unit as a "tea fee," leading some people to take risks. Gan Xiaoyan and others have paid the price for their illegal activities, but for the 291 victims, recovering their losses and healing their emotional wounds may be difficult in the short term. After Chen Shiyong and other victims finished telling their stories to the reporter, it was close to noon, and the bright sunlight was scorching the city's streets and buildings. Chen Shiyong rolled up his materials into a tube-shaped bundle and told the reporter that although he later obtained the qualifications to purchase affordable housing, he "no longer has the money to buy a house." Wu Xiaofen put the materials back in her backpack, picked up the shiny wooden cane from the corner to the left of the seat, struggled to stand up, then walked down the steps and towards the door. She skillfully started the light three-wheeled electric vehicle parked on the side of the road, passing through the dappled sunlight on the street, disappearing into the bustling crowd... (The victims in this article are all pseudonyms)

title_en: The consumer appeal behind "valley rice"
body_en:
During the Dragon Boat Festival holiday, a "Gu Zi" flash mob event in Wangfujing, Beijing attracted a large number of young people to queue up for check-ins, and limited edition badges and action figures were sold out within hours. Anime IPs have already jumped out of the screen, transforming into "Gu Zi" merchandise, social content, and offline traffic entrances, attracting young consumer groups in the commercial district.

In today's constantly evolving urban commercial landscape, "second dimension" culture is reshaping the offline consumption ecology with astonishing mobilization power. A flash mob of anime IPs, a distinctive "Gu Zi store," a set of limited edition trading cards or action figures can often trigger a queue frenzy, injecting vitality into deserted shopping malls. Transitioning from "self-cultivation" to "affecting regional foot traffic," "second dimension" is no longer a niche label, but an important commercial variable that integrates content, social interaction, and experiential scenes. The term "Gu Zi" comes from the English word "Goods," referring to peripheral products derived from IPs. According to iMedia Research, by 2029, the market size of China's "Gu Zi economy" will exceed 300 billion yuan, becoming a new driving force for regional consumption, cultural tourism integration, and urban renewal.

The related trends have become increasingly prominent in recent consumer trends. For example, after the release of the animated film "Ne Zha 2" during the Spring Festival, its peripheral products sold over 300 million yuan on Taobao platforms in less than a month, driving sales in multiple stores to the tens of millions level; during holidays such as May Day and the Dragon Boat Festival, anime flash mobs and "Gu Zi" sales events frequently took place in major cities across the country. In places like Wangfujing in Beijing, Nanjing East Road in Shanghai, Beijing Road in Guangzhou, and Jianghan Road in Wuhan, many "Gu Zi stores" and IP flash mob events have seen long queues, with products selling out in seconds and resale at a premium becoming the norm.

The appeal of "Gu Zi" lies not in its functional attributes, but as an emotional medium and cultural label. For the "Z generation," queuing for hours for a limited edition badge or a co-branded drink is a spirit of "expressing love through possession." IPs are no longer just visual content but have become a medium for identity, community belonging, and social interaction. The peripherals stuffed in "pain bags" have also become new "traffic nodes" in urban consumption scenes.

This high stickiness of cultural consumption is reshaping the operational logic of offline commercial districts. The Joy City in Wangfujing, Beijing, uses popular IP combinations to guide the gathering of foot traffic; Hangzhou Hubin Intime introduces "dimensional" stores and flash installations, driving an increase in foot traffic on the entire floor; Chengdu Taikoo Li creates a "Gu Zi block," where anime peripheral sales also drive growth in dining, beverages, and accommodation. According to some property management companies, after the introduction of "Gu Zi stores," overall foot traffic on weekends increased by nearly 20%, and holidays are showing a "full house" trend.

The downward trend of the "Gu Zi economy" is also evident. In many university areas and subway commercial districts, collective "Gu Zi" stores have quickly become gathering places for trendsetters. Third and fourth-tier cities activate local consumption through anime exhibitions, Cosplay festivals, and other activities. For example, in Zhejiang Jiande, the anime carnival revitalized the old street night market economy, while in Wuhan, the combination of "cherry blossoms + second dimension" created a popular scene in the university area, indicating a quiet transformation in cultural tourism consumption structure.

More importantly, the "Gu Zi economy" has significant repurchase capability and scene extensibility. Brands continuously create "freshness" through limited releases, selection mechanisms, cross-border collaborations, etc., extending consumers' paths to stores and their stay time. Deep integration with online communities blurs the boundaries between "shopping" and "participation," and from murder mystery games, themed cafes to immersive exhibitions, the experiential formats derived from "Gu Zi" are constructing a set of three-dimensional consumption scenes.

Behind "Gu Zi" is also a reflection of urban cultural vitality. In recent years, many local governments have attempted to link local cultural and tourism resources with IPs to achieve a win-win situation of cultural revitalization and consumption transformation. For example, the Henan Museum developed action figures based on traditional jade pendants and linked them to exhibitions and sales, while Guangxi collaborated with the game "Light and Night Love" to promote district renewal. By aggregating the interests of the "Z generation" through the "Gu Zi economy," the expression of urban youthfulness is gradually emerging.

Of course, the "Gu Zi craze" is not without worries. Currently, some "Gu Zi stores" rely heavily on a single IP, lack content updates, and experience a sharp decline in foot traffic once the hype fades; flash projects struggle to retain regular customers, quickly losing momentum after holidays; scalping, false blind boxes, and other irregularities also damage consumer trust. Moving from a traffic economy to sustainable development, the "Gu Zi economy" still needs to overcome many obstacles.

In the future, to truly unleash the long-term value of the "Gu Zi economy," cities and enterprises need to shift from "grabbing hotspots" to "building platforms." This includes promoting local IP originality, creating youth brands with greater local cultural recognition, and deep operational management of offline commercial space content, transitioning from "selling goods" to "selling experiences," "selling emotions," and "selling communities," constructing reusable and immersive consumer experiences.

(Wang Qichen)

title_en:
Alibaba Cloud globally deploys full-stack AI capabilities
Empowering Chinese enterprises to go global
body_en:
This report is from reporter Song Jing: On June 24th, at the 2025 Alibaba Cloud International Summit in Shenzhen, Liu Weiguang, Senior Vice President of Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group and President of the Public Cloud Business Unit, stated that Alibaba Cloud will accelerate the creation of a global cloud computing network, deploying full-stack AI capabilities at every node worldwide, enhancing compliance, service, and ecosystem team building for international expansion, and fully serving global enterprises.
After more than 20 years of development, Chinese companies going global have shown new characteristics. Liu Weiguang pointed out that firstly, the industries going global are becoming more high-end, shifting from manufacturing to intelligent manufacturing; secondly, the regions going global are becoming more diverse, expanding from Europe and America to the entire world; and finally, the operations going global are becoming more localized and networked. From the early stages of going out, it has evolved into global operations, meaning that research and development, production, supply chain, and sales services are all part of a global network collaboration.
Currently, South China is one of the most dynamic regions in the Chinese economy and a frontier for Chinese companies going global. It is reported that Alibaba Cloud has been deeply cultivating this region for many years, supporting large customers in fields such as the internet, AI hardware, mobile phones, automobiles, home appliances, robots, etc., to go global, such as Meitu, 37 Interactive Entertainment, Huiliang Technology, Transsion, Xiaopeng Motors, GAC, Midea, TCL, Cloud Whale, and others. Overall, AI capabilities have become a significant "label" for these companies going global, allowing Alibaba Cloud's full-stack AI capabilities to find a "place to shine."
Taking Raybird as an example, Raybird's innovative AI glasses have covered over 25 countries and regions globally, with a market share of over 40% in North America, Japan, and South Korea. Based on the scenarios and hardware features of Raybird AI glasses, Alibaba Cloud has designed an overall multimodal interaction architecture based on the Tongyi series large model base, customized the development of "cloud + end" models to help products achieve high response, low latency, and high-quality multimodal AI interaction experience. At the same time, the two parties have carried out functional customization and development around the actual usage scenarios of the glasses, and continue to iterate and update on the Raybird AI glasses product. In terms of Agents, Raybird has built an Agent ecological development platform based on the Alibaba Cloud Bailian platform to support developers in quickly building their own Agents and releasing them. Currently, the first AI glasses Raybird V3 equipped with the Tongyi VL series models have been launched.
Another example is Xiaopeng Motors, which has deeply cultivated the European market and simultaneously promoted localization research and development and layout in Southeast Asia. In the first quarter of this year, Xiaopeng Motors' overseas sales ranked first among new energy vehicle exports, with overseas sales increasing by 370% year-on-year. To support the rapid expansion of overseas markets, Xiaopeng Motors relies on Alibaba Cloud's global infrastructure to achieve the global rapid deployment of key business systems. At the same time, Alibaba Cloud's full-stack AI advantage is helping Xiaopeng Motors accelerate the construction of an overseas technical system. Based on Alibaba Cloud's Lingjun Zhi Suan, Xiaopeng Motors has built the first large-scale intelligent computing cluster in the domestic automotive industry, with a computing power reserve of up to 10 EFLOPS, a peak cluster utilization rate of 98%, and established a high-availability disaster recovery system for second-level fault detection and disposal. This cluster has shortened the average iteration cycle of Xiaopeng Motors' "cloud model factory" to 5 days, supporting rapid iteration of large models. Currently, Xiaopeng Motors is advancing the training and optimization of a 720 billion parameter model, building a full-process closed loop to support pre-training, post-training, model distillation, and on-vehicle training. The 720 billion parameter world base model has stronger long-chain reasoning (CoT) capabilities, and the latest generation of large model achievements has been loaded onto the Xiaopeng G7.
"AI Cloud has become the core competitiveness of Alibaba Cloud, and AI Cloud will also shape the core competitiveness of Chinese companies going global." Liu Weiguang stated, "Alibaba Cloud will make strategic investments to enhance its own international capabilities, accompany more Chinese companies in going global, and jointly explore the global market."
sentiment_reason: Alibaba's Alibaba Cloud supports numerous enterprises, with global deployment, demonstrating strong competitiveness and business growth points.

title_en: Deep enterprise enters the global unicorn list.
body_en:
Shenzhen Special Zone News (Reporter Zhang Cheng) On June 26, the Hurun Research Institute released the "2025 Global Unicorn List", listing non-listed companies worldwide founded after 2000 with a value of over 1 billion US dollars, with SpaceX, OpenAI, ByteDance, xAI, and Ant Group ranking in the top five. Shenzhen has a total of 37 unicorn companies on the list, ranking sixth among global cities, and is one of the fastest-growing cities for unicorn companies in China.

The list shows that there are 1523 unicorn companies worldwide, an increase of 70 from last year, distributed in 307 cities in 52 countries. Among them, the United States leads with 758 unicorn companies, an increase of 55; China ranks second with 343 unicorn companies, an increase of 3. Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Guangzhou, and Hangzhou are the top five cities in terms of the number of unicorn companies in China, with Shenzhen, Hefei, and Chongqing being the fastest-growing cities for unicorn companies in China.

WeBank, Honor, Horizon Robotics, DJI, and Huolala, five Shenzhen unicorn companies, entered the top 100 on the list. Horizon Robotics, which entered the list this time, is an intelligent car manufacturing platform spun off from Huawei. In less than a year, its value has exceeded 1 billion US dollars, reaching 115 billion yuan. In addition, companies like Jialichuang and Tracekey also made it onto the list, showcasing the excellent industry ecology of Shenzhen's unicorn companies.

A review by reporters found that in China's top ten unicorn companies, half are from the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Apart from WeBank (4) and Honor (8) from Shenzhen, Shein from Guangzhou and Oppo and Vivo from Dongguan rank 3rd, 6th, and 9th domestically, demonstrating the active innovation momentum in the Greater Bay Area.

The list points out that the total value of the top ten companies on this year's list accounts for 26% of the total value of global unicorn companies, increasing by 4 trillion yuan, almost 80% of this year's total new value. The total value has risen to 10.6 trillion yuan. Currently, 77% of unicorn companies sell software and services, mainly in the fields of financial technology, software services, and AI, while 23% of unicorn companies sell physical products, mainly focusing on semiconductors, new energy, biotechnology, and health technology.
sentiment_reason: Ant Group, under Alibaba, ranks in the top 5 on the Hurun Global Unicorn List, its massive market value demonstrating its influence.

title_en: Foreigners in Weihai are enthusiastic about "sweeping goods"
body_en:
Li Xiaoqian

In June, Weihai, Shandong, was full of international style on the streets and alleys. In the century-old street of Qixia Street in the Wei Cheng area, groups of foreign tourists leisurely enjoyed coffee in the street cafes. At the intangible cultural heritage art market, foreign tourists stopped from time to time, taking photos, making purchases, and enthusiastically interacting with craftsmen.

Walking along Qixia Street, retro cultural and creative shops, specialty stores, and hot spring resorts lined the street. Korean and Japanese restaurants and imported supermarkets were interspersed among them, allowing foreign tourists to encounter diverse cultures at every corner. They could also choose unique items carrying memories of Weihai, exploring the internationalized life map of the old street.

Korean tourist Kim Mi-hyang couldn't get enough of Weihai's tin inlay craftsmanship: "The patterns on this tea set are very beautiful, with elements of Weihai's history, culture, and scenery. I bought two sets to bring to my family and friends." On-site, the craftsmen skillfully punched holes in porcelain, repaired cracks with tin nails, and the carving craftsmen meticulously carved mythical stories, flowers, birds, fish, and insects on small fruit pits, bringing them to life. At the booth of intangible cultural heritage silk products, Ms. Park, a friend of Kim Mi-hyang, kept trying on silk scarves and ended up buying several cultural and creative scarves. She said, "This scarf has a very traditional Chinese style, and the design is very fashionable."

"We hold events such as retro national tide festivals, intangible heritage markets, intangible heritage flash mobs, and literary symphony garden parties to create a more exquisite and distinctive historical and cultural block in Weihai. This allows foreign tourists to deeply feel the fashionable charm of the collision between traditional culture and modern trends, creating a 'one-stop' tourism consumption scene that integrates cultural experiences, specialty shopping, and international cuisine." Xu Xiaohui, the project manager of Qixia Street, introduced. After the transformation and upgrade, Qixia Street, which has been in operation since July last year, has successively been awarded titles such as "Shandong Province's Characteristic Commercial Street" and "Qilu Internet Celebrity Food Street."

At the Jiulong City Shopping Plaza in the Jiulong Bay Cultural and Leisure District in Weihai, the "smooth" payment method amazed Russian tourist Nikolai, "Alipay is linked to our bank card, just a touch and payment is made, it's so convenient."

Korean internet celebrity blogger An Zhihui values the selection of products more, "These cosmetics, clothing, and electronic product stores are very distinctive, with many styles that Korea does not have, the consumer experience is very good." She also shares her consumer experience with tens of thousands of "fans" worldwide through social platforms.

Since last year, various shops in Jiulong City have optimized foreign card binding payment services, opened the function of binding cards for payment through WeChat, Alipay, and UnionPay Cloud Flash Payment, and guided foreign consumers to smoothly bind cards through multilingual promotional materials, achieving "no difference" in payment between overseas and domestic cards. "As payment methods continue to upgrade, consumption becomes more convenient, and the number of foreign card transactions is also on the rise," said Ms. Xu, a staff member at the "HI Find Goods" store.

The person in charge of the Weihai Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism introduced that since last year, Weihai has promoted barrier-free payment services in 6 commercial districts such as Jiulong City and Hanlefang, upgraded and renovated POS machines for 557 key merchants, and implemented hardware and software upgrades for foreign card acceptance devices in 32 hotels above three stars and 19 key tourist attractions. Next, Weihai will continue to enhance the international level of tourism consumption services, allowing foreign tourists to shop with peace of mind and comfort.

title_en: Taobao sellers will "move the universe"
body_en:
When shopping on Taobao, the seller's location was shown as Jiangsu Province, but the package was sent from Shandong Province. Mr. Wang, a citizen, reported to our hotline 23602777 about the suspicious incident he encountered while shopping on the Taobao platform. What made him even more dissatisfied was that, without his consent, the platform directly "helped" him with compensation, closing complaints, and other operations.

On June 8th, Mr. Wang purchased a car air freshener from the Boge Boutique store on the Taobao platform. Upon receiving the package, he found that the brand and packaging of the product were different from what he had purchased. "The product page showed that it was shipped from Wuxi, Jiangsu, but my package was sent from Shandong." On June 11th, Mr. Wang filed a complaint with the Taobao platform. A day later, Mr. Wang received a call from a manufacturer in Shandong claiming that the Taobao seller had provided Mr. Wang's address to them and requested them to ship the product.

Investigation by reporters revealed that the car air freshener Mr. Wang purchased from Xiang Bai Nian was a well-known brand. However, the product he received had simple packaging with only a string of English letters on the cover, and the manufacturer was Xiang Geer (Shandong) Home Technology Co., Ltd. Searching on various online shopping platforms including Taobao did not yield any information about this product. When reporters opened the Taobao store link provided by Mr. Wang, they found that the product had been taken down, and multiple attempts to contact the seller went unanswered. During the investigation, Mr. Wang received another call from Taobao customer service, stating that the seller was engaged in "counterfeit branding" behavior, and advised Mr. Wang to apply for a refund, offering him a cash red envelope worth 30 yuan. Mr. Wang refused. However, when he checked the order complaint page again, he found that the complaint had been closed without his consent, and he was compensated with a 20 yuan coupon. Helpless, Mr. Wang had no choice but to return the product.

Subsequently, reporters contacted Taobao customer service, who stated that the complaint had been resolved, but did not mention anything about supervision or punishment. The customer service representative said, "We will report this to the higher-ups." As of the deadline, reporters had not received an explanation from the Taobao platform regarding this issue.
sentiment_reason: The Taobao platform has failed to address the issue of users encountering counterfeit branded goods, and its attitude and resolution have been unsatisfactory.

title_en: Carta de nuestro Presidente y nuestro CEO
body_en: Fiscal year 2025 marked a year of solid progress as Alibaba Group advanced our “user first, AI-driven” strategy. This year, we focused on our two core businesses — e-commerce and “AI + Cloud” — which are the twin engines powering our long-term growth. With AI at the heart of our future, we significantly increased investments in cloud computing and AI infrastructure to accelerate innovation and drive the industrial adoption of AI technologies. We also made disciplined moves to streamline our portfolio, including the divestiture of non-core assets such as Sun Art and Intime. Meanwhile, we steadily improved operating efficiency across our Internet platform businesses. Hujing Digital Media and Entertainment Group and Amap, for instance, each achieved a profitable quarter in fiscal year 2025. As AI unlocks new synergies across our diverse ecosystem, we are adopting a group-wide strategy that optimizes holistic value creation. In the face of historic opportunities brought by AI, we want to share our forward-looking perspective – our strategic positioning, competitive strengths, and how we intend to capture the next wave of growth. Our first strategic focus, “user first,” continues to guide our Internet platform businesses. With over 1.1 billion Internet users, China is the world’s largest online retail market, where e-commerce accounts for nearly 27% of total retail consumption. In China commerce, our Taobao and Tmall Group remained focused on user growth and improving user experience. As China’s leading e-commerce platform, we also strengthened the operating environment for merchants, supporting those who offer high-quality products and services. Our efforts to build a sustainable ecosystem that benefits consumers, merchants, and the platform have gained momentum. In fiscal year 2025, we saw a rise in consumer and merchant trust, which in turn fueled business acceleration. In international commerce, Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group (AIDC) delivered robust revenue growth, driven by the cross-border e-commerce businesses. We enhanced local supply in key markets and diversified our offerings to meet consumer needs across regions worldwide. Operating efficiency continued to improve, and we remain confident in achieving a profitable quarter for our international commerce business in the coming fiscal year. Our second strategic focus, “AI-driven,” reflects our view of AI as both a core driver of business growth and a transformative force for the future. Over the next decade, AI is expected to reshape every industry. At Alibaba, we are investing aggressively in AI infrastructure and frontier innovation to enhance global competitiveness and generate long-term business momentum. Alibaba Cloud, our core business that is driven by AI, benefited from surging AI demand. Public cloud revenue accelerated, and revenue from AI-related products posted triple-digit growth for seven straight quarters, pushing overall revenue to double-digit growth for the fiscal year. In foundation models, we are expanding the frontier of model capabilities while remaining committed to open-source development. In April 2025, we released our next-generation Qwen3 model, which ranked among the top models globally on multiple authoritative benchmarks. As of the end of April 2025, over 200 models in the Qwen family series had been open-sourced, generating more than 300 million global downloads and over 100,000 derivative models, making Qwen the world’s largest open-source model family. These achievements reflect our deep expertise in AI research and will help accelerate the adoption of AI across various industries. We believe our open-source strategy will empower global developers to co-create progress in human intelligence and contribute to the long-term goal of artificial general intelligence (AGI). Across our broader Internet platform ecosystem, we are expanding the application of AI with an open and forward-looking mindset. We believe AI is not only a catalyst for upgrading existing services but also a key to unlocking entirely new user experiences and value. In fiscal year 2025, Alibaba generated strong cash flow from our core businesses. We improved operating efficiency across multiple platform businesses, strengthening the foundations of previously loss-making businesses, a number of which are now on track to profitability. Our disciplined capital allocation efforts helped unlock shareholder value, including significant capital recovery from the divestment of non-core assets such as Sun Art and Intime. This enables us to double down on our core businesses and invest strategically in AI. To return value to shareholders, we distributed US$4 billion in annual and special dividends for fiscal year 2024 and have announced a total of US$4.6 billion in dividends for fiscal year 2025. In addition, we repurchased US$11.9 billion of our shares, which resulted in 5.1% net reduction in total outstanding shares, driving accretion in earnings per share. Looking ahead, we remain committed to enhancing shareholder value through multiple avenues. The rapid evolution of AI is ushering in sweeping changes across industries and, with it, unprecedented growth opportunities for Alibaba. Over the next decade, AI will be the primary driver of incremental value and transformation. For Alibaba, this means developing world-class AI models, pushing the limits of model capabilities, and building a globally competitive AI-enabled cloud infrastructure. Together, these capabilities will position “AI + Cloud” as our key growth engine for the future. To realize this vision, we are ramping up investments in three key areas: AI and cloud infrastructure, AI foundation models and native applications, and the AI-driven transformation of our existing businesses. In fiscal year 2025, we announced that our planned investment in cloud and AI infrastructure over the next three years will exceed the total investment made in the past decade. In this new era, Alibaba is strategically well-positioned. We are a key player in the China cloud computing market and the top cloud services provider in Asia Pacific. Alibaba Cloud is expanding its global cloud computing infrastructure and scaling international deployment of AI-related products to support the globalization of Chinese enterprises.
