title_en: The US stock market fluctuated, with the Dow Jones falling more than 100 points, and Nvidia hitting a new high.
body_en:
* Technology stocks surged, with the Nasdaq rising 0.3%;
* US new home sales in May fell by 13.7%, hitting a near three-year high;
* Federal Reserve Chairman Powell: Expect tariffs to bring inflation.
The US stock market fluctuated, with the market focusing on the situation in the Middle East and weighing Federal Reserve Chairman Powell's second day of congressional testimony. The Dow fell 106.59 points, or 0.25%, to 42,982.43 points, the Nasdaq rose 0.31%, with a three-day streak, to 19,973.55 points, and the S&P 500 index fell by less than 0.01%, to 6,092.16 points.
Market Overview
Powell attended a Senate hearing on Wednesday, stating that tariffs in the coming months will bring some inflation. Powell said that these taxes are expected to cost billions of dollars annually, "some of which will fall on consumers, we are just waiting for more data."
On Tuesday, Powell said in his speech to the House Financial Services Committee that the Fed can continue to wait and assess how the US economy responds to policy changes before adjusting monetary policy.
Boston Fed President Collins said on Wednesday that she believes the current monetary policy stance is "moderately restrictive," although she is inclined to cut rates later in 2025. "This largely depends on whether the 'price shocks' caused by tariffs will quickly dissipate without undermining inflation expectations, and whether the associated slowdown in actual economic activity is limited."
According to Xinhua News Agency, US President Trump posted on social media on the 24th that the ceasefire agreement between Israel and Iran has taken effect, warning all parties not to violate the agreement. Israel later accused Iran of violating the ceasefire agreement, while Iran denied launching missiles at Israel after the ceasefire took effect.
According to CCTV News, on the 25th local time, Trump said at the NATO summit in The Hague, "Iran's nuclear program has regressed by decades." Trump said, "Iran wants to restore relations with the United States," and "I think we will eventually establish relations with Iran."
Ryan Detrick, Chief Market Strategist at Carson Group, said, "It almost feels like we're back in a bull market, we're dealing with tariff issues, dramatic events in the Middle East are expected to be resolved, as people realize that the US economy still has considerable resilience, the stock market continues to rise."
Long-term US bond yields remained stable, with the 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields holding steady at 3.78% and 4.29%, respectively.
In terms of economic data, US new home sales in May saw the largest decline in nearly three years. According to government data released on Wednesday, sales of new single-family homes fell by 13.7% to an annualized rate of 623,000 units, the lowest level in seven months.
The Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) in the US stated that despite a slight increase in interest rates, mortgage applications in the US rebounded slightly last week, rising by 1.1%, due to an increase in refinancing of loans by the Federal Housing Administration.
The final value of US GDP for the first quarter will be released on Thursday, and the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) report on Friday will help investors determine the economic impact of Trump's tariffs, which have kept global markets on edge since the beginning of the year. According to the FedWatch tool from the Chicago Mercantile Exchange Group, the likelihood of a 25 basis point rate cut in September this year is close to 70%.
In terms of individual stocks,
Nvidia rose 4.3%, hitting a record high, with a market value of $3.75 trillion.
Loop Capital raised the target price of this tech giant from $175 to $250, while maintaining a buy rating. The institution stated that the artificial intelligence trend that has boosted Nvidia's stock price in recent years shows no signs of weakening and may propel the chipmaker's market value beyond other companies, eventually reaching $6 trillion.
Tesla fell by 3.8%. Data from the European Automobile Manufacturers Association showed that the electric car maker's new car sales in Europe in May fell by nearly 28% year-on-year, marking the fifth consecutive month of decline.
FedEx fell by 3.3% as the company forecasted quarterly profits below expectations due to tariffs putting pressure on global demand.
General Mills fell by 5.1% as the food giant issued disappointing profit guidance.
The Nasdaq Golden Dragon Index fell by 0.6%. Alibaba fell by 2.1%, NetEase fell by 0.6%, Baidu remained flat, and JD.com rose by 1.1%.
International oil prices rebounded slightly, benefiting from signs of strong US demand and continued easing of geopolitical tensions. WTI crude oil for near-month delivery rose by 0.85% to $64.92 per barrel, while Brent crude oil for near-month delivery rose by 0.80% to $67.68 per barrel.
International gold prices stabilized, with COMEX gold futures for June delivery on the New York Mercantile Exchange rising by 0.29% to $1,327.10 per ounce.

title_en: Wu's credit card fraud case
body_en:
Storage number 2024-04-1-139-001
Keywords
Criminal credit card fraud Credit card cash out Self money laundering
Basic case
In March 2021, the defendant Wu Mou was employed at a hotel in Jiexiu City, Shanxi Province. The hotel owner, Yue Mou, provided Wu Mou with a mobile phone for Douyin live streaming. The phone was registered with a WeChat account and linked to a credit card under Yue Mou's name. Yue Mou informed Wu Mou of the WeChat payment password to use for tipping on the Douyin platform. On July 19, 2021, without Yue Mou's permission, Wu Mou used the mobile phone linked to the credit card to recharge his own phone number with RMB 200. From July 21 to 26, 2021, Wu Mou contacted credit card cash out personnel via WeChat on the mobile phone during Douyin live streaming. He clicked on the link sent by the credit card cash out personnel and made seven payments totaling RMB 31,996 using the WeChat linked credit card. After deducting the handling fee, the other party transferred a total of RMB 31,329 to Wu Mou via WeChat and Alipay, resulting in a total of RMB 32,196 being fraudulently charged on Yue Mou's credit card. After the incident, Wu Mou voluntarily surrendered to the public security organs on December 17, 2021, constituting voluntary surrender; his family returned all the stolen money.
The People's Procuratorate of Yingze District, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province, filed a public prosecution against the defendant Wu Mou for credit card fraud and money laundering with the People's Court of Yingze District, Taiyuan City. The People's Court of Yingze District, Taiyuan City, issued Criminal Judgment No. (2022) Jin 0106 Xing Chu 227 on December 7, 2022: the defendant Wu Mou was convicted of credit card fraud and sentenced to one year in prison and fined RMB 20,000. After the verdict, the prosecution appealed against the first instance's failure to convict Wu Mou of money laundering. The Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court issued Criminal Ruling No. (2023) Jin 01 Xing Zhong 142 on June 29, 2023: the appeal was rejected, and the original judgment was upheld.
Judgment reasons
The focus of the dispute in this case is whether the defendant Wu Mou should be punished for both credit card fraud and money laundering for using someone else's credit card for cash out through the internet and having the cash out personnel transfer the cash out funds to Wu Mou's account via WeChat and Alipay after deducting the handling fee.
Firstly, the defendant Wu Mou's actions constitute credit card fraud. Article 196 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates that using someone else's credit card for credit card fraud activities, with a significant amount involved, constitutes credit card fraud. Article 5, paragraph 1 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Obstructing Credit Card Management" (Judicial Interpretation [2009] No. 19, revised in 2018) clearly states that amounts between 5,000 yuan and less than 50,000 yuan should be considered "significant" as per Article 196 of the Criminal Law. In this case, Wu Mou used the mobile phone belonging to the victim Yue Mou for Douyin live streaming and obtained the WeChat payment password linked to the phone for tipping on the Douyin platform. However, without Yue Mou's permission, Wu Mou illegally appropriated the money in Yue Mou's credit card by using it for cash out through the internet and having the cash out personnel transfer over 30,000 yuan to Wu Mou's account via WeChat and Alipay. Clearly, the above actions meet the requirements of Article 196 of the Criminal Law and constitute credit card fraud.
Secondly, the defendant Wu Mou's actions do not constitute money laundering. The "Amendment XI to the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China," which came into effect on March 1, 2021, amended Article 191 of the Criminal Law to criminalize the act of "self money laundering." According to Article 191 of the Criminal Law, transferring funds through transfers or other payment settlement methods to conceal or disguise the proceeds of financial fraud crimes and their sources and nature constitutes money laundering. Therefore, for the act of "self money laundering" involving the transfer of funds obtained from financial fraud crimes through transfers or other payment settlement methods, it should be punished as money laundering. In judicial practice, the criminalization of "self money laundering" should adhere to the principle of unity of subjective and objective aspects and the prohibition of double jeopardy, and make accurate judgments. In this case, from a subjective perspective, Wu Mou committed the crime with the aim of illegally appropriating the funds in Yue Mou's credit card, without knowing the cash out merchants, the process of fund circulation, or having any relevant communication with the cash out personnel, and without any intention to conceal or disguise. From an objective perspective, the cash out personnel transferred the funds after deducting the handling fee to Wu Mou's WeChat and Alipay accounts, which was a necessary means for Wu Mou to obtain the proceeds of his credit card fraud crime. Therefore, Wu Mou directly obtained the cash out payment link from the cash out personnel and directly received the cash out funds from them, which constitutes directly obtaining the proceeds of the crime of credit card fraud and is the completion of the crime, and should not be considered as "self money laundering." Therefore, Wu Mou should not be punished for money laundering.
In conclusion, the defendant Wu Mou's use of someone else's credit card, involving a significant amount, constitutes credit card fraud but not money laundering. Considering Wu Mou's voluntary surrender after the crime, his family returning all the stolen money, and other circumstances of the case, the court sentenced him to one year in prison for credit card fraud and fined him RMB 20,000.
Judgment summary
When the perpetrator uses someone else's credit card for fraudulent activities and requests cash out personnel to transfer the fraudulently obtained funds through fictitious transactions to their own account, it is the completion of the upstream crime, which does not change or exceed the scope of evaluation of the upstream crime and should not be considered as "self money laundering." Such actions do not constitute money laundering and should be punished for credit card fraud according to law.
Related indexes
Article 191, Article 196 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China
Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Obstructing Credit Card Management (Judicial Interpretation [2009] No. 19, revised in 2018), Article 5
First instance:
People's Court of Yingze District, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province (2022) Jin 0106 Xing Chu 227 Criminal Judgment (December 7, 2022)
Second instance:
Shanxi Provincial Higher People's Court, Taiyuan City (2023) Jin 01 Xing Zhong 142 Criminal Ruling (June 29, 2023)

title_en: Sensitive skin care, anti-aging, men's skin care and other segmented tracks continue to expand - the skin care product market is expected to become the core growth engine of the beauty industry.
body_en:
A comprehensive analysis of data from institutions such as the Head Leopard Research Institute and Frost Sullivan reveals that although the total transaction volume (GMV) of skincare products in China in 2024 has decreased compared to 2023, with the outbreak of demand for sensitive skin care and anti-aging, as well as the rise of the male skincare market, the skincare product market in China is expected to rebound and further expand. It is estimated that the GMV will exceed 530 billion yuan by 2029, with a compound annual growth rate of 4.8% from 2024 to 2029. The skincare industry in China has entered a stage of high-quality development, and with the right positioning and continuous innovation, enterprises are sure to have great potential in the skincare product race.

Domestic brands are gradually rising
According to Qingyan Intelligence data, the GMV of skincare products in China exceeded 420 billion yuan in 2024, a year-on-year decrease of 12.5% (see Figure 1). However, the GMV of the top 20 skincare brands on the four major online platforms (Taobao and Tmall, JD.com, Douyin, Pinduoduo) increased by 22.8% year-on-year; among them, 8 domestic brands all achieved varying degrees of growth, with a GMV increase of 28.0%, higher than the overall growth rate. It can be seen that the concentration of the skincare product market in China has significantly increased.
Looking back at the development of the skincare product market in China, it can be divided into three periods.
From 2012 to 2018, domestic brands took advantage of their leading position in offline channel layout and seized the opportunity of the online market boom, ushering in a golden age of development. Domestic brands such as Pechoin, Herborist, and One Leaf quickly rose through precise marketing; at the same time, American brands saw a significant decline in market share due to difficulties in channel transformation and brand aging.
From 2018 to 2021, international brands began to counterattack. European and American brands such as Lancome, La Mer, and Guerlain significantly increased their market share; Japanese brands like SK-II and Shiseido also significantly improved their competitiveness; while domestic traditional brands like One Leaf and Bai Cao Ji saw a decline in market share due to lack of innovation.
From 2021 to 2024, domestic brands rose again. Domestic skincare brands emerged one after another like bamboo shoots after a spring rain, surpassing international brands in sales once again; at the same time, the concentration of the skincare product market continued to increase, with top domestic brands leveraging online channels to achieve top sales. Based on online sales in 2024, Pechoin's GMV exceeded 10 billion yuan, surpassing L'Oreal's 9.8 billion yuan, ranking first. The trend towards high-end product development is also becoming increasingly evident, with domestic brands increasing research investment to compete in the high-end market with international brands such as La Mer and Helena.
In 2024, against the backdrop of an overall decline in the skincare product market in China, top and mid-tier domestic brands achieved counter-trend growth, with online channel growth particularly significant.
In terms of sales data, among many domestic brands, top brands such as Pechoin, Hanshu, and Weleda occupy important positions. From 2022 to 2024, the online sales of the top ten domestic skincare brands in China increased from 24.4 billion yuan to 43.55 billion yuan, with an average growth rate of 33.6%; among them, the total sales of the top three brands Pechoin, Hanshu, and Weleda increased from 13.38 billion yuan to 22.93 billion yuan, accounting for over 50%. For example, Pechoin occupies about 25% of the market share, with sales increasing from 5.91 billion yuan to 10.76 billion yuan, a growth of over 80%; as the second largest brand, Hanshu has seen a surge in online sales in recent years through deep integration with the Douyin ecosystem and the creation of explosive series, with online sales increasing from 1.37 billion yuan in 2022 to 8.05 billion yuan in 2024, with an average growth rate of 142.8%.
In addition, the brands Gu Yu and Kefumei have seen their competitiveness rise continuously through differentiated ingredients and precise marketing. They have established a competitive advantage through patented ingredients; at the same time, they have made online channels their core sales and promotion platform, collaborating with influencers and placing short dramas to achieve efficient product exposure, thereby securing a place in the fiercely competitive market.
Navigating the demand in segmented fields
By dividing skincare products into facial care and body care products based on the application area, it is evident that consumers' demand and attention for facial care far exceed that of body care.
In 2024, the transaction volume of skincare products on the four major online platforms exceeded 390 billion yuan, with facial care products accounting for over 80% of the transaction volume.
Facial care sets with a transaction volume of over 70 billion yuan firmly hold the top spot in the facial care subcategory, accounting for 24% of the market share of facial skincare products (see Figure 2), with brands such as Hanshu, L'Oreal, and Pechoin leading the way. Looking at the competitive situation in the facial care set market, domestic brands are accelerating their rise. On one hand, Pechoin is leading growth on the Taobao and Tmall platforms; on the other hand, brands like Hanshu and Gu Yu are using Douyin traffic to boost sales on Taobao and Tmall platforms, creating cross-platform synergy.
Facial essence, as the second largest subcategory of facial care products, saw a transaction volume of over 60 billion yuan on the four major platforms in 2024, a year-on-year increase of 13.2%, becoming the main category driving market expansion. In terms of concepts/efficacy claims, consumers have a strong demand for acne treatment and sensitive skin care, making the facial essence market show strong consumer vitality. For example, in the first quarter of 2025, sales of facial essence on the Taobao and Tmall platforms exceeded 3 billion yuan, with sales of over 11 million units; among them, sales of soothing, acne-fighting, and oil-controlling products achieved year-on-year growth rates of 5.3%, 13.4%, and 6.3% respectively. In addition, secondary facial essence products are favored by consumers for their long-lasting moisturizing, sterile design, and precise dosage.
In 2024, the transaction volume of lotions/creams on the four major online platforms was nearly 56 billion yuan, accounting for 18% of the market share of facial skincare products. From the perspective of social media volume, topics related to lotions/creams such as "staying up late," "anti-aging," and "sensitive skin" have seen a significant increase in popularity. International high-end brands like Helena Rubinstein, Shu Uemura, and Estee Lauder are targeting "staying up late" and "anti-aging" as their main selling points, while also increasing their efforts in the "sensitive skin" category; domestic brand Weleda has adopted a "big single product" strategy targeting the sensitive skin group.
Body care products mainly consist of individual items such as body lotion, cream, and essential oils. In 2024, the transaction volume of body care products on the four major online platforms was approximately 36 billion yuan, with the transaction volume of body lotion, cream, and essential oils accounting for over 75% of the category.
Under the trend of precise skincare, localized specialized care such as neck, chest, and hand care has become a new growth point. In 2024, the transaction volume of neck, chest, and hand care products on the four major online platforms increased by 33%, 18%, and 3% respectively.
In terms of brand layout, international brands such as L'Occitane, Vaseline, and Olay dominate the body lotion/cream market; neck care, as the fastest-growing category in body care, is led by domestic brands such as SDX, KAZOO, and Longliqi due to their cost-effectiveness, occupying the top three positions on Taobao, Tmall, and Douyin platforms. In addition, international brands like Fontiv and Yves Rocher are exploring the neck essence subcategory, driving the market into a new stage of functional care.
In terms of ingredients and efficacy, new body care products are becoming more specialized and diversified, with innovative products focusing on niche functions such as fragrance, whitening, repair, and anti-aging becoming key to competition. At the same time, as body care consumption scenarios continue to expand, the demand for products for occasions such as holiday gifting and sports fitness is growing, with multifunctional products being highly favored.
Skincare track full of potential
Although the GMV of skincare products in China in 2024 has decreased compared to 2023, the market is never short of new opportunities. Currently, the population of sensitive skin is increasing, leading to a surge in demand for sensitive skin care; consumers are paying more attention to anti-aging, resulting in a sharp increase in demand for related products; at the same time, awareness of male skincare is awakening, leading to a strong rise in the male skincare market. With these positive factors working together, the skincare product market is expected to quickly rebound and further expand in scale. It is estimated that by 2029, the transaction volume of skincare products in China will exceed 530 billion yuan, with a compound annual growth rate of 4.8% from 2024 to 2029, making the future market development promising.
Surveys show that the incidence of sensitive skin in China exceeds 36%, with nearly 80% of sensitive skin issues caused by environmental factors, lifestyle, and skincare habits. Effective products and care methods can help consumers with sensitive skin conditions improve their skin. Over 70% of consumers with sensitive skin use methods such as cleansing, moisturizing, hydration, and sun protection for skincare, which effectively drives rapid growth in the skincare product market, especially for plant-based high-efficiency skincare products.
With the continuous penetration of anti-aging concepts and the rise of the silver economy, the presence of anti-aging effects has become an important consideration for consumers when choosing skincare products. Efficacy claims directly related to anti-aging mainly focus on wrinkle reduction, firming, spot lightening, and sun protection. From 2022 to 2024, the number of registered products with related efficacy claims grew rapidly at a rate of 70%; by 2024, the total number of registered products exceeded 100,000, with over 95% of them having wrinkle reduction and firming effects. In addition, as eye care is a key part of anti-aging skincare, eye care products are expected to grow at a faster rate, with their share in the anti-aging skincare product market expected to further increase.
In recent years, male consumers' emphasis on personal image management has been increasing, and the "he economy" is becoming a dark horse in the skincare product consumer market, unleashing strong purchasing power and showing rapid growth in related skincare product demand. From January to October 2024, the sales of men's body care, hair care, makeup, perfume, and skincare products on the Douyin platform exceeded 1.8 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 65%. Male consumers' demand for skincare product efficacy is becoming more refined, with brands and product categories continuously expanding from basic skincare to high-end skincare. It is worth noting that against the backdrop of the rise of the "he economy," the male skincare market is showing a pattern of dual-drive consumption levels and growth momentum. Among them, the group with a monthly income of 5,000 to 20,000 yuan has a stable consumption capacity, with skincare expenses accounting for 3.8% to 4.2% of disposable income, forming the backbone of the consumption pyramid. Currently, the men's skincare product market in China maintains a strong growth momentum, with a market size of 15.6 billion yuan in 2024, expected to exceed 20 billion yuan by 2026 (see Figure 3).
Overall, driven by consumer upgrades and the explosion of segmented demands, the skincare product industry will usher in new opportunities. The sensitive skin care, anti-aging for the silver generation, and male skincare tracks will continue to expand, combined with ingredient innovation and the rise of domestic brands, making the skincare product market a core growth engine in the beauty industry.
(This article is provided by the Head Leopard Research Institute and Frost Sullivan)

title_en: Commercialization Process of Self-Driving Taxis Accelerates
body_en:
By Our Reporter Zhang Wenxiang

The concept of autonomous driving has been continuously popular recently. Data from East Money Choice shows that as of the closing on June 25th, the autonomous driving sector saw a gain of 1.55%, while the sector's closing gains for the previous two trading days were 3.55% and 1.70% respectively.

Concurrently, autonomous driving companies have also been very active recently. Tesla has launched pilot Robotaxi (autonomous driving taxi) operational services in the United States, and domestic Robotaxi companies are also accelerating their overseas expansion. Many industry insiders believe that the commercialization process of Robotaxi is further accelerating, and large-scale implementation is expected in 2026.

Companies Accelerate Layout

On June 22nd, U.S. time, Tesla launched its Robotaxi pilot operational service in the United States. The initial service deployment includes ten Tesla Model Y vehicles, and the first batch of passengers using the service will pay a fixed fee of $4.2.

At the same time, domestic companies are also accelerating their Robotaxi business layout. On June 23rd, Shanghai Hello Mobility Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Hello") posted on its official WeChat account that the company, in cooperation with Ant Group and CATL, has registered Shanghai Zaofu Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. in Shanghai through its investment entity. The registered company will focus on L4-level autonomous driving technology research and development, safety applications, and commercial implementation.

A relevant person from Hello told "Securities Daily" reporters: "With continuous breakthroughs in core technologies and engineering implementation, the intelligent driving industry is entering a phase of large-scale commercial implementation. In recent years, the company has continuously deepened its mobility business and promoted the deep application of artificial intelligence in the field of mobility, accumulating rich experience for entering the Robotaxi field."

In the market competition of the Robotaxi industry, overseas markets have become the focus of attention. On June 13th of this year, Wanma Technology Co., Ltd. stated in its investor relations activity record that "the company has actively laid out overseas markets in recent years, establishing entities in countries with regulatory requirements for communication and data compliance. The company maintains close communication and business cooperation with major global operators, actively promoting the implementation of scenarios including passenger cars and Robotaxis in key regions worldwide."

According to data, Wanma Technology's main business covers the basic industry communication sector and the emerging industry intelligent connected vehicle sector. The company's cooperation with autonomous driving companies is mainly focused on the connected field. The Robotaxi connectivity solutions provided by the company can offer high-quality network services required for domestic and global operations.

On June 15th of this year, Guangzhou WeRide Co., Ltd. signed a cooperation agreement with the Dubai Road and Transport Authority (RTA) and Uber to jointly deploy commercial Robotaxi mobility services in Dubai. On May 27th of this year, Pony.ai announced that it will deploy a Robotaxi fleet in Dubai.

"The cost of hiring foreign drivers is higher, making Robotaxi easier to implement, and overseas markets are a good choice for Chinese companies. However, the domestic market is larger, and more Robotaxi companies will likely focus on both markets," said Ji Xuehong, director of the Automotive Industry Innovation Research Center at North China University of Technology, to "Securities Daily" reporters.

Expected to Usher in Rapid Growth

Industry insiders believe that with the gradual maturity of technology and increased policy support, the Robotaxi industry is expected to usher in rapid growth.

In overseas markets, Tesla is expected to become the "pioneer" in the promotion of Robotaxi business. According to research reports from Zheshang Securities Co., Ltd., the operation of Tesla Robotaxis is a strong validation of the effectiveness of Tesla's "pure vision + end-to-end" solution, proving the feasibility of the route of "large-scale computing power + data-driven" to enhance the intelligence of autonomous driving. Combined with Elon Musk's plans, Tesla's Robotaxi fleet will rapidly expand to 1,000 vehicles in the coming months, and by the end of 2026, over 1 million autonomous driving Teslas will be in operation in the United States.

In the domestic market, China is actively working on policy levels to help the Robotaxi industry commercialize and scale up rapidly. Currently, cities such as Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin, and Wuhan are continuously promoting the implementation of the autonomous driving industry. On April 28, 2025, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology released the "Key Points for Automotive Standardization Work in 2025," proposing to accelerate the research and development of mandatory national standards for autonomous driving system safety requirements.

According to research reports from Jianghai Securities Co., Ltd., it is expected that Robotaxi will achieve large-scale commercialization around 2026. Initially, Robotaxi will enter the intelligent mobility market, targeting individuals currently using private cars or public transportation. In 2026, the domestic market size will be close to 500 billion yuan. It is estimated that by 2030, Robotaxis will be widely used globally, with a penetration rate of 31.8% in China's intelligent mobility.

"For Robotaxi to achieve large-scale implementation, policy support is needed, and related insurance and compensation mechanisms must also keep pace," said Zhang Xiang, Secretary-General of the International Society of Intelligent Transportation Systems. Based on an analysis of current factors, the large-scale implementation of Robotaxi business in 2026 has a high probability.

title_en: From "Traveling in China" and "Shopping in China" to see the heat of the Chinese economy.
body_en:
Xinhua News Agency reporter Fan Yu
Recently, on social media, the practical tips of "bringing an empty suitcase to China" have sparked heated discussions. From "touring China" to "shopping in China," the experience of "traveling + shopping" has made foreign tourists exclaim "so good."
With high-quality and cost-effective products, convenient and fast payment methods, and "buy now, refund upon departure" tax refund policies, the convenience and attractiveness of "touring China" continue to rise. Traveling in China and shopping in China have become a new choice for more and more international tourists, making China a hot spot for global tourism shopping. From policy dividends, industrial strength to cultural charm, the "China craze" shows the world a modern China that is open, inclusive, and full of vitality.
The appeal of the "China craze" comes from policy promotion. From continuously expanding the visa-free "circle of friends," optimizing the payment environment for overseas tourists, to improving the convenience of tax refunds upon departure, China is using concrete policies to extend a warm invitation to global tourists. Recently, China decided to implement a visa-free entry policy for five South American countries, including Brazil, increasing the number of countries with unilateral visa-free policies to 43. The coverage of foreign card POS machines has increased, and the capabilities of mobile payment methods such as Alipay and WeChat for "foreign cards inside and outside" and "foreign cards inside and outside" have been continuously upgraded, allowing many regions to achieve "one-touch" payment. China is also continuing to make efforts in tax refund policies, expanding the "buy now, refund upon departure" tax refund service measures from pilot projects to nationwide implementation, lowering the starting point for tax refunds upon departure, optimizing the layout of tax refund shops upon departure, and improving the supply level of tax refund goods. A series of convenient measures convey China's clear attitude of continuously expanding its openness to the outside world, driving the "China craze" to continue heating up. During the May Day holiday, the number of foreign nationals entering and exiting China increased by 43.1% compared to the same period last year, and the number and amount of transactions processed by UnionPay and NetsUnion for payments by overseas visitors to China increased by 244.86% and 128.04% respectively compared to the same period last year. The UAE's WAM news agency reported that China has become a more attractive tourist consumption destination, not only promoting economic and trade exchanges between China and foreign countries but also achieving a deep integration of domestic and international markets.
The "China craze" reflects the quality core of "Made in China." In recent years, the shopping lists of foreign tourists coming to China have continued to expand, from clothing, food to mobile phones, translators, from small household appliances to smart homes. The high-tech content of "Made in China" has significantly increased, making it more competitive in the global market and attracting foreign tourists to continue to come to China to "hunt for good products." Smartphones, computers, smart wearable devices, drones, and other products have become popular items for "reverse purchasing," reflecting not only the innovative capabilities and technological strength of China's manufacturing industry but also China's rising position in the global value chain. From clothing and shoes to electronic products, from affordable daily necessities to high-end luxury goods, the richness of product categories and the diversity of choices in the Chinese consumer goods market attract foreign consumers in droves. Foreign tourists load their suitcases with goods, casting a "vote of confidence" for "Made in China" and acknowledging China's development. Malaysia's Sin Chew Daily said that foreign tourists not only experience the high quality and cost-effectiveness of "Made in China" but also touch the pulse of China's development.
The "China craze" also benefits from the deep integration of China's cultural and tourism development. In addition to traditional goods such as silk, tea, and porcelain, modern national trends, cultural and creative products, and technological goods are becoming new favorites of foreign tourists. The upgrading of China's cultural and tourism formats promotes the integration of tourism with culture, technology, and other fields, not only pushing "Made in China" onto the international stage but also allowing foreigners to immerse themselves in the charm of Chinese culture and gain a deeper understanding of China's modern development. They may stroll along Beijing's central axis, experience Hanfu makeup in Xi'an, enjoy ethnic customs in Yunnan, or experience a sense of the future in Shenzhen's technology parks. Many foreign tourists choose to travel to China because of their love for Chinese culture, and through tourism, they can further experience the unique charm of Chinese culture and the pulse of China's development. The U.S. magazine "Around the World" said that with its profound cultural heritage and modern urban charm, China is gradually becoming the ideal destination for tourists from all over the world. With better product supply, more diverse consumption scenarios, and more convenient services, the appeal of "touring China" is still on the rise.
Industrial upgrading, the increasingly diverse consumer ecology, and the continuous expansion of opening up to the outside world are all factors that, when combined, become the key to China capturing the world's "flow" and injecting new vitality into the high-quality development of the Chinese economy. Today, when globalization is encountering headwinds and protectionism is on the rise, China insists on expanding opportunities through greater openness and deeper cooperation, proving to the world that true economic security comes from deep interconnection rather than isolation. It can be said that the significance of "touring China" and "shopping in China" goes beyond the economic level, adding new footnotes to international exchanges and connectivity.

title_en: 【Red Chip State-owned Enterprise Warrants】Funds change horses to chase after the lagging, Yuexiu Real Estate can roar
body_en:
Zhang Yi
The tension in the Middle East continues to cool down, with the Hang Seng Index reaching as high as 24,533 points yesterday and closing at 24,475 points, up 297 points or 1.23%. Both the intraday and closing indices broke through the high resistance level of June 11th. With the market successfully breaking through, it is beneficial for funds to flow into relatively lagging sectors or individual stocks. Among them, the strength of Chinese real estate stocks, such as Yuexiu Property (0123), is worth paying attention to.
Yuexiu Property had dropped to 4.13 yuan on Monday this week, the lowest level since late September last year. However, after hitting bottom that day, it turned around and rose for three consecutive trading days. The stock closed at 4.36 yuan yesterday, up 8 cents or 1.87%, also regaining the 10-day and 20-day moving averages. With signs of funds flowing back into strong Chinese lagging stocks, there may be room for further rebound in the future.
In terms of performance, as of the end of last year, Yuexiu Property recorded a profit of 1.04 billion yuan, a 67.3% year-on-year decrease. The group's operating income increased by 7.7% to 86.4 billion yuan last year. Gross profit margin decreased by 4.8 percentage points to 10.5%. The cumulative contract sales amount for the year was 114.54 billion yuan, a 19.4% year-on-year decrease. As of the end of last year, the group maintained a "green file" for the "three red lines," with asset-liability ratio excluding advance receipts, net debt ratio, and cash short-term debt ratio at 68.1%, 51.7%, and 2.1 times, respectively.
The latest operational data shows that the group achieved a contract sales amount of approximately 9.581 billion yuan in May, a year-on-year decrease of about 4.9%, with a contract sales area of approximately 244,600 square meters, a year-on-year decrease of about 33.9%. In the first five months of this year, the company's cumulative contract sales amount was approximately 50.7 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of about 26.5%, with a cumulative contract sales area of approximately 1.1691 million square meters, a year-on-year decrease of about 16.1%. The cumulative contract sales amount accounted for 42.1% of the 2025 contract sales target of 120.5 billion yuan.
The group's performance last year was not ideal, and sales have yet to improve this year, which are believed to be the reasons for the recent pressure on the stock price. In terms of valuation, Yuexiu Property has a historical price-earnings ratio of 15.87 times, although higher than many first and second-tier peers, its price-to-book ratio is only 0.3 times, indicating significant undervaluation. title_en: The college entrance examination products are rich in meaning, don't let blessings become a burden.
body_en:
As the 2025 college entrance examination approaches, the consumption season for the college entrance examination is also rapidly heating up: cheongsams symbolizing "opening the way to victory," stationery gift boxes symbolizing "making the list of successful candidates" ... Beijing Youth Daily reporters investigated multiple e-commerce platforms and found that many goods with blessings and meanings for examinees are being sought after by many parents. Purchasing clothing, food, and accessories with symbolic meaning in the name of blessings is a significant feature of the college entrance examination season consumption market, carrying the earnest hopes and good wishes of parents for their children. However, psychologists believe that overly extravagant expressions of affection may bring pressure to examinees. They suggest that parents should "quietly support the exam," help examinees maintain a good mindset, and treat the college entrance examination with a calm attitude.
"Opening the way to victory" "Green lights all the way"
Symbolic goods favored during the college entrance examination season
From the "making the list of successful candidates" gift box to the college entrance examination stationery set, from ceremonial gifts to various prayer items, behind the diverse goods on various e-commerce platforms is a mature consumption ecosystem tailored for the college entrance examination season.
Among the many goods for sending examinees, the sending of cheongsams symbolizing "opening the way to victory" is undoubtedly the most eye-catching. A search for sending cheongsam goods on Taobao by a reporter from the Beijing Youth Daily revealed that the price range for basic cotton cheongsams is mostly between 100 and 300 yuan; while cheongsams made of mulberry silk fabric, although priced around 500 yuan, still sold over 600 pieces in a single store. In terms of color selection, the bright red cheongsam is leading in sales due to its symbolism of "opening the way to victory," while the dark green style is also popular because of the homophonic meaning of "green lights all the way."
In addition to cheongsams, cultural shirts printed with slogans like "good luck bursting" and "performing exceptionally well" are also very popular. Cotton T-shirts priced between 20 and 80 yuan, which both showcase individuality and carry symbolic meanings. In a store on Taobao, a short-sleeved T-shirt with the slogan "making the list of successful candidates" topped the sales list, with over 4000 pieces sold as of yesterday. In addition, some merchants have also introduced parent-child outfits for sending examinees, extending the sense of ceremony of the college entrance examination from individuals to families. Similarly, on the Taobao platform, a short-sleeved T-shirt with the words "wishing my daughter/brother/sister to make the list of successful candidates" priced at 29.9 yuan has sold over ten thousand pieces.
Among food items, Ding Sheng cakes are undoubtedly one of the most popular "auspicious foods" during the college entrance examination season. The Beijing Youth Daily reporter found that the prices of most chain brand Ding Sheng cakes on various e-commerce platforms range from 20 to 50 yuan. Among them, a hot-selling gift box in a store on Taobao has accumulated over 9000 additional purchases, with a single-day order volume exceeding 200 units. Another gift box called "Zhuangyuan cake and zongzi making the list of successful candidates" on Taobao, containing 10 zongzi, 4 pieces of Ding Sheng cake, and 4 pieces of mung bean cake, is priced at 187 yuan, far exceeding the price of ordinary Ding Sheng cakes, with sales also exceeding one hundred units.
In addition, various types of "lucky charms" for the college entrance examination are also welcomed by examinees and parents. In a store on Taobao, a colorful bracelet named "Putuo Mountain Changshu Seven Wisdom" is priced at 302 yuan, with sales exceeding 100 units. In another store, a product named "Hangzhou Lingyin Temple Wenchang knot bracelet" attracted over a hundred buyers in just one week, with weekly sales tripling compared to usual.
The stationery market has also seen a burst of creativity during the college entrance examination season. The Beijing Youth Daily reporter found that a certain brand has launched a "luxury stationery suitcase" printed with the words "a promising future" and "hitting the jackpot three times" (including three sets of answer cards, bookmarks, scrolls, erasers, etc.) priced at 119 yuan, with over 600 units sold as of the time of writing. In addition, customized college entrance examination stationery gift boxes are also popular. On e-commerce platforms, a college entrance examination stationery gift box priced at 153 yuan, containing a thermos cup, notebook, metal bookmark, fountain pen, etc., with each item free to engrave the examinee's name or a blessing message, has sold over 30,000 units so far.
Crocheted bouquets, zongzi, and red envelopes
"Handmade" becomes a new carrier for expressing feelings
In addition to purchasing finished products, homemade handmade gifts are becoming another choice for the college entrance examination season due to their unique emotional value. Recently, Xiao Wu hand-crocheted a bouquet of symbolic knitted flowers for her niece Xiao Cheng (pseudonym) who is about to take the college entrance examination. The bouquet includes sunflowers symbolizing "winning in one fell swoop," orange petals symbolizing "specified success (orange)," pink palms representing "as easy as turning over one's hand," embroidered balls symbolizing "a bright future," horse chestnuts symbolizing "success at hand," and osmanthus flowers symbolizing "achieving success."
Even for a skilled crafter like Xiao Wu, making these flowers took quite a bit of effort. She explained that after crocheting the first sunflower, the petals curled together and could not be opened because she did not include shaping wire. She had to redo the work and simultaneously embed shaping wire during the production process. In addition, the osmanthus flowers and embroidered balls are made up of a large number of tiny stamens, each of which needs to be embedded with wire, wrapped with cotton thread for fixation, and finally assembled. Xiao Wu spent two weeks completing this bouquet of flowers. When she took a photo of the finished crocheted bouquet and sent it to Xiao Cheng, the young girl expressed great delight, "She replied to me on WeChat with a long string of excited and cute emojis." To avoid disturbing Xiao Cheng as the exam approached, Xiao Wu had already sent the gift during the May Day holiday.
"In addition to the bouquet, we also prepared a large gift box for the child." It turns out that in Xiao Wu's hometown, it is a traditional custom for uncles to prepare gift boxes for their nephews taking exams, with the homophonic meaning of "success." As an aunt, Xiao Wu also carefully prepared a gift box for Xiao Cheng, including zongzi, grapes, oranges, pistachios, rice cakes, cola, etc., jokingly calling it a "collection of homophonic puns." In addition, Xiao Wu and her husband also prepared two red envelopes, with amounts of 211 yuan and 985 yuan respectively, expressing their earnest hopes for Xiao Cheng to enter her ideal university.
Xiao Wu told the Beijing Youth Daily reporter that Xiao Cheng's mother put more effort into sending her off than she did: "She bought a red cheongsam, symbolizing opening the way to victory; she also picked out clothes with the Nike logo for Xiao Cheng, hoping the child 'gets all the answers right.'" In addition, Xiao Cheng's mother also asked Xiao Wu to make several different colored headbands, which Xiao Cheng will wear to the exam on the day of the college entrance examination: green symbolizes "green lights all the way," red represents "good luck," and gray-yellow color symbolizes the hope of "moving towards brilliance."
In Xiao Wu's view, these gifts carry the importance and love of family and friends for Xiao Cheng. "Every family has different ways of expressing themselves, and it's up to each individual. But I think handmade gifts can more concretely convey these expectations and love, and they will be cherished for a long time."
Expert Opinion
Parents should express themselves moderately to avoid invisible pressure
However, the societal evaluation of the ceremonial college entrance examination economy is not consistent. The Beijing Youth Daily reporter found on social media that many netizens believe that frequent blessings from relatives and friends can sometimes bring invisible pressure to examinees, as if conveying a signal of "the pressure is on your side." In response, national second-level psychological counselor Yan Yifei believes that if expressions of affection are too extravagant, they may indeed become a source of pressure for examinees, "for example, some exaggerated sending-off ceremonies may easily reinforce subconscious suggestions such as 'this exam determines fate' or 'must succeed.'"
She said that if a family is usually creative and ceremonial, a series of special arrangements before and during the college entrance examination may be a natural extension; on the other hand, if the family is usually simple and plain, suddenly planning and exaggerating before the exam may make it difficult for the examinee to cope, exacerbating their nervousness. "Therefore, when parents make any plans for sending off the examinee, they should prioritize the examinee's feelings, keep it light rather than heavy, and make reasonable arrangements based on the child's personality and family habits." Yan Yifei said.
Yan Yifei pointed out that currently, examinees face multiple psychological challenges, including exam-related tension, lack of confidence, high parental expectations, and uncertainty about the future. Among them, "fear of disappointing parents" is the main source of pressure for most examinees. "Teenagers both crave attention and reject excessive care. Parents' anxiety often unconsciously transmits to examinees through expressions, actions, or words, increasing their psychological burden."
"Any deliberate special behavior can become a source of pressure for examinees. In fact, what children really need is not heavy rituals before the exam and anxious waiting outside the exam room, but the same smiles and acceptance from family members when they return home after the exam." Yan Yifei suggested that parents should adjust their mindset, try to treat the college entrance examination as "normal," such as dressing casually, speaking calmly, which is more effective than repeatedly emphasizing "don't be nervous"; at the same time, parents should convey the concept that "nervousness is normal" to their children and turn verbal reassurances of "it's okay if you don't do well" into concrete actions of support."
By/Reporter Wang Jingyi
