title_en: Chinese Translation Association 2022 Work Summary
body_en:
Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the Party Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping as the core has attached great importance to the development of the translation cause, making a series of important instructions and directives. Superior departments, including the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, have made a series of important deployments to implement the requirements of the Party Central Committee. The Translators Association of China (TAC) has always taken the spirit of General Secretary Xi Jinping's important instructions and the deployments and requirements of the Party Central Committee as its fundamental follow-up and action guide. Guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, TAC has comprehensively implemented the Party Central Committee's series of major deployments on building international communication capabilities and constructing a discourse system. With the aim of serving the country, society, the industry, and its members, and with the mission of connecting China and foreign countries and communicating with the world, TAC adheres to the development concepts of demand-driven, talent-based, technology-empowered, and serving the overall situation. It fully leverages the organizational advantages and industry-leading role of a national social organization, emancipates the mind, seeks truth from facts, forges ahead with determination, and pioneers innovation. New breakthroughs, progress, and achievements have been made in serving the overall situation of the Party and the country, strengthening the construction of the discourse system, promoting the development of the language service industry, expanding international exchange and cooperation, and strengthening its own organizational and institutional development.

I. Deeply Studying and Implementing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, Promoting New Progress in Building International Communication Capabilities

In accordance with the spirit of central documents and implementing the general requirement to "innovate foreign propaganda methods, strengthen the construction of the discourse system, and strive to create new concepts, new categories, and new expressions that integrate China and foreign countries," TAC has integrated industry resources and established work mechanisms, actively participating in the construction of national projects such as "China Keywords" and the "International Communication Translation Talent Pool." It has actively engaged in the fight against the COVID-19 pandemic, timely launching standardized achievements in foreign translation, and making pioneering explorations from the professional perspective of a national translation organization to strengthen international communication capabilities and the construction of the discourse system, playing a demonstrative role in improving national translation capabilities and the quality and level of foreign translation work.

(I) Undertaking Major National Projects and Important Translation Tasks, Assisting in the Construction of the Discourse System for Foreign Communication in the New Era

Since 2015, the Association has participated in the implementation of the national key project "China Keywords Multilingual Foreign Communication Platform" for many consecutive years, innovatively carrying out multilingual, multimedia, multi-channel, and multi-format foreign discourse translation and communication work. Keywords have been released to the outside world in 19 languages including Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, German, Portuguese, Italian, Turkish, Thai, Vietnamese, Indonesian, Lao, Kazakh, Brazilian Portuguese, and Cyrillic Mongolian, totaling over 10,000. Among them, English expressions of keywords such as "community with a shared future for mankind" and "Belt and Road Initiative" have been adopted as authoritative expressions by official institutions such as the United Nations Translation Service and the Directorate-General for Translation of the European Commission. A series of 12 thematic books and over 160 types of foreign translation and dissemination products, including books, e-books, and short videos, have been compiled and released. These have been featured multiple times at important domestic and international conferences and events such as the Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation, the Conference on Dialogue of Asian Civilizations, and the BRICS Meeting on Governance. They have also been promoted and showcased at large international exhibitions and events such as the China International Import Expo, the China International Fair for Trade in Services, and the China-ASEAN Expo. By organizing and implementing major national translation tasks, the Association has maintained alignment with strategic needs, synchronized with superior organ deployments, coordinated with industry peers, and advanced with talent team development, contributing to the creation of brand projects and public products for foreign discourse innovation.

Relying on its branches such as the Committee for Foreign Discourse System Research, the Committee for Foreign Communication Translation, and the Committee for Foreign Affairs Translation, the Association has conducted joint research on the standardization of foreign translation. It has continued to improve the consultation mechanism involving multiple parties, such as seminars on Chinese-English, Chinese-French, and Chinese-Japanese translation, and has timely released reference translations for important terminology and coordinated their use within the industry, providing important references and work insights for China's foreign affairs and propaganda departments and other international communication agencies. Based on the consultation mechanism, a committee of experts for reviewing major translation work has been established to provide professional mechanism guarantees for organizing and implementing major translation tasks, researching and formulating translation work plans, analyzing and approving the latest important terminology translations, and building a high-end translation talent team. In 2021, on the occasion of celebrating the 100th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China, under the unified command of the China Foreign Languages Publishing Administration, the review expert committee, in collaboration with the China Translation Academy and the Translation Academy of the China Foreign Languages Publishing Administration, organized expert teams to successfully complete the high-quality English translation and publication of important documents such as "The Historical Mission and Action Value of the Communist Party of China" and government white papers such as "China's Moderately Prosperous Society in All Respects," "China's Democracy," and "Democratic Development in Hong Kong under 'One Country, Two Systems'." They also completed major national translation tasks such as the multilingual translation of the explanatory texts for the Museum of the Communist Party of China in English, French, Russian, Spanish, and Arabic, contributing to a better portrayal of the image of a major party and a major country.

Branches such as the Committee for Social Science Translation and the Committee for Foreign Communication Translation, as well as member units, have also leveraged their advantages to excel in major translation tasks such as the multilingual and ethnic minority language translation for Party congresses, plenary sessions of the CPC Central Committee, and the "Two Sessions."

(II) Telling China's Story of Fighting the Epidemic, Uniting and Leading the Domestic and International Translation Community to Contribute to Epidemic Prevention and Control

Following the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, TAC immediately issued "Working Together in Unity to Overcome Difficulties, TAC is with You – A Letter to All Members and National Translation Professionals," to strengthen the confidence and motivation of the translation community to stick to their posts and shoulder social responsibilities. The Association, together with the China Translation Academy, successfully organized the major translation and publication tasks of the English, French, Russian, Spanish, Arabic, German, and Japanese versions of the government white paper "China's Actions to Combat COVID-19." Multilingual series products such as "China Keywords: Fighting COVID-19" and "Chinese-Foreign Bilingual Vocabulary for Fighting COVID-19" have told the story of the Chinese people's fight against the epidemic, effectively serving foreign work during this extraordinary period.

Branches such as the Committee for Ethnic Minority Language Translation, the Committee for Translation Services, the Committee for Localization, and the Committee for Legal Translation, as well as TACs in various regions nationwide including Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin, Hubei, Henan, Shandong, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Jiangsu, Sichuan, Chengdu, Guangdong, and Shenzhen, and numerous member units such as universities and enterprises, have actively responded to TAC's call. They have fully committed to epidemic prevention and control work, bravely taking responsibility, proactively acting, fighting closely, and turning crises into opportunities, contributing to epidemic prevention and control and international cooperation, achieving good social benefits. The International Federation of Translators' "ATA Chronicle" published a special article introducing the anti-epidemic experiences of the Chinese translation and language service sectors.

Against the backdrop of the global fight against the epidemic, TAC has united and led the Chinese translation community to exert energy and contribute wisdom in international anti-epidemic cooperation. It took the lead in organizing the "Asia-Pacific Translation Cloud Forum on Combating the Epidemic," calling for translation professionals in the Asia-Pacific region to unite and cooperate to aid epidemic control. This initiative has generated strong reactions and resonance within the international translation community, further demonstrating TAC's important role on the international stage and expanding the international discourse power and influence of the Chinese translation community.

(III) Language Services Empowered to Tell the Story of the Winter Olympics

In 2022, the Beijing Winter Olympics were held. Language services played a crucial role in communication and exchange among athletes and event organizers from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds. Member units of TAC, prioritizing service to the overall national situation and practical needs, provided professional language services to ensure the successful hosting of the Winter Olympics and Paralympics.

The China Foreign Languages Publishing Administration, as TAC's supervisory authority, organized its affiliated units to plan and publish 24 key thematic books in Chinese and English. These include the English version of "Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics and Paralympic Games Public Reader: Charm of Winter Olympics," compiled by the Beijing Winter Olympics Organizing Committee and translated and published by units affiliated with the China Foreign Languages Publishing Administration. They also compiled the "Olympic Knowledge Popularization for Youth" series and the "Beijing Winter Olympics in Progress" series, and undertook the translation of important documents such as the English and French programs for the opening and closing ceremonies of the Winter Olympics and Paralympics.

Among TAC's member units, Pactera Translation Co., Ltd. successfully completed the language service assurance tasks for the Winter Olympics and Paralympics with high standards, quality, and professionalism. iFlytek provided automatic translation and related multilingual speech conversion, speech recognition, and speech synthesis technologies for the Winter Olympics, facilitating seamless communication within and outside the venues. Teacher teams from universities such as Beijing Foreign Studies University and Beijing International Studies University provided professional language services for the Winter Olympics, while also dispatching numerous volunteer teachers and students to assist and support various aspects of the Winter Olympics. Numerous similar cases exist and cannot be listed one by one.

II. Innovating and Enhancing Organizational Service Capabilities, Achieving New Breakthroughs in Industry Development

TAC attaches great importance to the standardization of the industry, promoting the formulation of the first industry plan for translation and social group standards and norms for the translation industry. It facilitates the organic integration of government, industry, academia, and research, building platforms for industry-academia-research cooperation and exchange, contributing to strengthening the construction of the translation talent team, actively fostering the maturity of the translation and language service industry, and laying a solid foundation and creating a favorable environment for the innovative, efficient, and sustainable development of the industry.

(I) Implementing Standardized Management, Reaching New Levels in Industry Planning and Standardization System Construction

As the only industry organization for language services in China, TAC has played an irreplaceable and important role in promoting the rapid development of standardization in China's language service industry. The Association has continuously conducted industry surveys and research, formulating the first "China Language Service Industry Plan (2017-2021)." It has compiled and released four annual "China Language Service Industry Development Reports," providing authoritative references for domestic and international stakeholders to understand industry trends and development momentum, and taking innovative steps in top-level industry design. The "China Language Service Industry Development Report" has become the most comprehensive and widely surveyed industry report recognized by the industry.

Since the birth of the first social group standard for the translation industry in 2016, the Association has developed and released 11 national and social group industry standards and norms, expanding the scope and scale of standardization work and achieving important breakthroughs in standardization construction.

On the basis of continuously improving the industry standard system, the Association launched a certification program for interpreting and translation services in 2018, filling a gap in the industry certification field, promoting the standardization of the language service market and the improvement of the national service certification system, and driving the further maturity and progress of China's translation and language service industry.

The influence of the Association's standardization work has been continuously expanding and has been fully recognized by the Standardization Administration of China. In 2019, TAC established cooperation with the Standardization Administration of China, participating in the management of the National Technical Committee for Language and Terminology Standardization (SAC/TC62) and jointly establishing the Working Committee for Language Service Standardization, providing organizational and institutional guarantees for industry standardization construction. TAC's participation at the national level in organizing and formulating industry standards has led language service standardization into a new, higher level of development.

(II) Strengthening Talent Team Construction, Achieving New Results in the Integration of Government, Industry, Academia, and Research

Translation discipline construction and translation talent training have always been one of the focal points of the Association's work. TAC has actively played a leading and driving role in the construction of translation disciplines and talent teams, participating in promoting the formulation of plans for the development of translation talent teams and assisting relevant ministries and commissions in strengthening top-level design for the development of translation talent teams. It continues to promote the brand building of faculty training for translation programs in higher education institutions nationwide, innovatively carrying out advanced training activities for high-end applied translation talents in multilingual current affairs and culture, and innovatively organizing international award and recognition events, further promoting the integrated development of government, industry, academia, and research.

With the unremitting efforts of TAC's broad membership, especially universities and faculty nationwide, translation professional education has achieved leapfrog development, and the construction of translation master's programs and graduate training has steadily expanded. Statistics show that from 2015 to 2021, the number of universities offering translation master's programs nationwide increased from 206 to 316, the number of languages offered increased from 6 to 11, and the annual enrollment increased from over 8,000 to over 10,000. The cumulative number of graduates over the past seven years has reached 50,000.

In terms of innovation in talent training and business integration, the Association, in conjunction with the National Steering Committee for Translation Professional Degree Graduate Education, has organized 8 sessions of faculty training. This has formed a complete training system combining online and offline learning, covering 4 modules and 10 courses in translation teaching, skills, theory, and technology. Training effectiveness has significantly improved, with increasing participation numbers, broader regional origins, and expanding brand effects, effectively meeting the urgent demand for faculty and talent in the booming translation professional education. According to incomplete statistics, from 2015 to 2021, over 3,500 foreign language and translation faculty members from higher education institutions in 29 provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the central government, as well as Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan, and countries such as the United States, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, Egypt, and Vietnam, participated in the training, accounting for 37% of the total number of participants since the inception of faculty training in 1997. Faculty training for translation programs in higher education institutions nationwide has become the largest and most comprehensive translation faculty training event in terms of scale and content system organized domestically and internationally, receiving high praise and attention from international organizations such as the International Federation of Translation and Interpreting Schools and the translation community at home and abroad.

Building upon faculty training for translation programs, the Association, in response to national practical needs, has expanded training groups and established mechanisms for advanced translation talent training. It has organized several advanced training courses on multilingual translation of Chinese current affairs discourse and Chinese culture for foreign audiences, and planned and launched a series of training and exchange activities, bringing together over 800 translation professionals from foreign affairs, propaganda, cultural exhibition, art troupes, universities, and research institutions, as well as over 200 experts and scholars from more than 10 countries and regions for dialogue, exchange, and mutual learning. Advanced training activities have gradually formed a brand, exploring new models for cultivating high-quality translation talents for foreign communication, and have been warmly welcomed and positively received by the industry.

The Association has actively promoted regional collaboration, university-enterprise cooperation, and industry cooperation, expanding the fields and methods of talent training. TAC has participated in promoting the establishment of postdoctoral research workstations at the China Foreign Languages Publishing Administration and cooperative mechanisms for training high-level practical applied translation doctoral students with university member units. Currently, 12 jointly trained doctoral students are enrolled, and postdoctoral workstation recruitment began in 2021, making positive efforts to cultivate more high-quality, high-level applied international communication talents. The Association has launched special talent development programs such as the "Fu Lei Young Translation Talent Development Plan Project" in cooperation with the Pudong New Area of Shanghai, carrying out customized talent training programs for enterprises, institutions, and universities, and making beneficial explorations for cultivating cross-cultural, professional, and practical translation talents.

Member unit China Foreign Languages Publishing Administration Translation Academy (formerly Translation Professional Qualification Examination Center of China Foreign Languages Publishing Administration) has actively promoted the evaluation and certification of translation talent capabilities, making important contributions to strengthening the translation talent team and standardizing the translation job market. From 2016 to 2021, the number of applicants for the National Translation Professional Qualification Examination surged from 110,000 to a peak of 350,000, with a total of over 1.68 million applicants, and the examination scale continued to expand. The Translation Professional Qualification Examination is the only language examination included in the State Council's occupational qualification catalog and the first Chinese occupational qualification examination with overseas testing centers. Four overseas testing centers have been established in Minsk, Belarus, and St. Petersburg and Moscow, Russia, and mutual recognition with the Korean translation qualification certificate has been achieved. In 2020, the CATTI International Edition was launched for the first time, with a total of over 2,300 candidates, covering 55 countries including the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia. By the end of 2021, the translation qualification examination for overseas professionals, the CATTI International Edition for general translation enthusiasts, and the China International Language Proficiency Test for young people formed an internationalized CATTI examination system, covering 72 countries, with a total of 19,000 participants. The translation qualification examination has now formed a scale of 9 languages, 3 levels, and 55 types of examinations, and a new socialized, scientific, and standardized national translation talent evaluation system has been initially established.

Organizing translation competitions is a powerful measure for the Association to promote the development of the translation talent team. Over the past seven years, the "Han Suyin Young Translators Award" has been expanded to the "Han Suyin International Translation Competition." The competition items have expanded from English to bidirectional translation in 8 languages, covering a total of 16 categories. It has attracted participants from over 10 countries and regions, with a substantial year-on-year increase in registrations, reaching over 40,000 person-times in 2021, achieving a historic breakthrough in scale. The National Interpreting Competition has flourished, attracting nearly 40,000 participants from home and abroad. In 2021, the number of participants exceeded 10,000 for the first time, becoming the largest and most influential interpreting competition in China.

(III) Developing Language Service Technology, Achieving New Progress in Applied Practice

The innovative development of information technology has brought new opportunities to the translation cause, and new technological means are increasingly widely applied in translation practice, providing strong impetus for the development of the translation industry. With the organization and support of the Association, member units such as Pactera Translation, Translingua, iFlytek, China Electronics Financial Technology, Sidi Software, Shanghai Chuangling, Shanghai Yizhe, Xinyi Technology, Alibaba, and Tencent are committed to language technology innovation and localization services. They have developed a large number of language service technology invention patents and language technology solutions, built a series of machine translation engines, computer-aided translation software, and cross-lingual big data analysis technology platforms with independent intellectual property rights, and fostered multiple national high-tech enterprises. This has promoted the widespread application and deep integration of new technologies in the field of translation, significantly improving the efficiency of translation work. University member units such as Beijing Foreign Studies University, Shanghai International Studies University, Beijing Language and Culture University, Beijing International Studies University, Guangdong University of Foreign Studies, and Xi'an International Studies University have collaborated with language service enterprises to continuously carry out training for translation technology talents, supplying a large number of urgently needed language service talents to the translation and localization industry and the internet industry.

(IV) Pioneering Annual Meeting Exchange Mechanism, Taking New Steps in Industry Services

The Annual Conference of the Translators Association of China is an important platform for exchange and cooperation in China's translation and language service industry. Since establishing the annual meeting exchange mechanism in 2016, the Association has held four consecutive annual meetings and several supporting forums. This has built a broad platform for promoting industry exchange and uniting the translation community, playing a significant role in defining the new orientation, new tasks, and new goals of translation work in the new era, promoting exchange and cooperation in Chinese and foreign language services, and fostering the prosperous development of China's translation cause in the new era.

The Association also organized the Language Service Promotion and Negotiation Conference at the 4th China International Fair for Trade in Services, and initiated the "Yi Jiang Tang" national public lecture series, enhancing industry service levels through more professional, market-oriented, and information-driven measures. The Association's branches and local TACs have leveraged their strengths and strengthened cooperation, organizing a variety of activities such as the National Symposium on Ethnic Minority Language Translation, the National Symposium on Scientific and Technical Translation, the National Conference on Interpreting and International Symposium, the National Symposium on Social Science Translation, the National Symposium on Applied Translation, the High-Level Forum on National Translation Practice and the Construction of Foreign Discourse System, the Annual Conference of Graduate Education for Translation Professionals, the Doctoral Forum on Translation Studies, the China Public Policy Translation Forum, the National Symposium on Public Sign Translation, the Academic Symposium on the Foreign Translation of the Chinese Minority Literature Series, the Forum on the Development of China's Translation Services Industry, the Annual Conference of the Chinese Society of Intercultural Communication, the "Huazheng Cup" Legal Translation Competition, the "Shangyi Cup" Translation Competition, the "Helen Snow" Cup Translation Competition, and the Central and Western China Foreign Language Translation Competition. These activities have built a multilingual, multi-field, and multi-format service platform for academic and industry exchange.

III. Expanding International Exchange and Cooperation Platforms, Making New Contributions to Showcasing China's Image

TAC maintains close ties with international peers, actively participates in international affairs, and showcases a true, multifaceted, open, confident, humble, amiable, trustworthy, and respectable image of China on the international translation stage. It voices China's perspectives in international affairs, cooperating with foreign publicity and diplomatic fronts to create a favorable external environment for national development and rejuvenation, and practicing the concept of a community with a shared future for mankind through practical actions.

(I) Deepening Regional Exchange and Cooperation with the Asia-Pacific Translation Forum as a Platform

In 2016, TAC, in conjunction with the International Federation of Translators and its member unit Xi'an International Studies University, promoted the expansion of the Asia Translation Forum, a regional exchange platform initiated by TAC, into the Asia-Pacific Translation Forum. They jointly organized the 8th Asia-Pacific Translation Forum and established the Joint Committee of the Asia-Pacific Translation Forum. Wang Gangyi, Executive Vice President of TAC, was elected as the first chairman, providing institutional guarantees for the sustainable development of the forum and organizational exchange and cooperation within the Asia-Pacific translation community.

In 2019, TAC organized a delegation to participate in the 9th Asia-Pacific Translation Forum held in South Korea. Gao Anming, Vice Director and Editor-in-Chief of the China Foreign Languages Publishing Administration, was unanimously elected as the new chairman of the Joint Committee. Beijing Foreign Studies University, a member unit of TAC, obtained the hosting rights for the 10th Asia-Pacific Translation Forum. The scope of work of the Asia-Pacific Translation Forum has continued to expand, and its cooperative content has been continuously enriched, becoming an important platform for exchange and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region and even the international translation community.

(II) Actively Participating in International Affairs, Promoting Exchange and Mutual Learning Between China and Foreign Countries

TAC is one of the most influential member organizations of the International Federation of Translators. In recent years, the Association has fully utilized its non-governmental organization status to conduct public diplomacy, expand opening up and cooperation, and contribute to people-to-people exchanges and mutual understanding. China's translation community has made new strides in integrating into the international arena. Leaders and experts from the Association have served as council members of the International Federation of Translators, members of various committees and working groups, and editorial board members of the journal Babel, among other roles. They have represented TAC in international Federation of Translators' special projects, telling the stories of China's translation community, showcasing its demeanor, and conveying its voice, making positive efforts to promote cultural exchange and mutual learning between China and foreign countries.

"Belt and Road Initiative," language first. TAC and its branches, member units, and local TACs have utilized industry event platforms such as the TAC Annual Conference to conduct extensive exchanges with representatives from various countries. Consensus has been reached and practical cooperation has been promoted on issues of common concern, such as the training of high-end translation talents for the "Belt and Road Initiative," translation academic seminars, translation cultural exchanges, and language service technology cooperation, increasingly becoming a strategic and fundamental supporting force in the international cooperation of the "Belt and Road Initiative." At the invitation and organization of TAC, the President of the International Federation of Translators has attended the TAC Annual Conference for three consecutive years, highly praising the development and progress of China's translation cause and TAC's important contributions. Representatives of translation organizations and translators from different countries and regions have actively registered for TAC's activities such as annual conferences, training sessions, and competitions, reflecting the broad recognition of China's translation cause by the International Federation of Translators and the international translation community.

With the support of the Association, member units have actively applied to establish national language service export bases, such as the International Communication Technology and Culture Park and China (Hefei) Voice Valley. Two parks, two universities including Beijing Language and Culture University and Huaqiao University, and 10 enterprises including Pactera Translation, Jiagu Yi, Shenyang Chuangsijia Ye, Shanghai Wence, Jiangsu Shunyu, MCC Oriental, Translingua, Xinyi Technology, Language Bridge, and Wisdom Palace have been selected as the first batch of language service export bases, aiming to provide efficient and professional support for steadily improving the standardization, professionalism, and internationalization of the language service industry and promoting the "going global" of Chinese culture, products, services, technologies, and standards.

Branches such as the Committee for Legal Translation, the Committee for Localization Services, and the Committee for Interpreting, along with their member units, have leveraged their strengths in their respective fields to conduct extensive exchanges and cooperation with relevant international organizations, universities, and enterprises through academic seminars, talent training, industry-academia-research cooperation, and foreign-related language services, promoting common development.

IV. Strengthening the Association's Political Organizational Construction, Opening Up New Prospects for Association Work

(I) Promoting the Integrated Development and Mutual Improvement of Party Building and Business

The leadership of the Party is the prerequisite and fundamental guarantee for the prosperity and development of the Association. Since the establishment of the Party Branch of the Association Secretariat in March 2017, the Association has adhered to Party building leadership, enhanced its sense of mission, and made great efforts to integrate Party building with business, exploring a path of integrated development of "promoting enterprise development through Party building and guiding association development through Party building."

The Association has conducted surveys on Party building work in non-public translation enterprise member units, systematically summarizing the achievements and experiences in Party building work in non-public enterprises. It has established a coordination mechanism for Party building work in non-public enterprises of TAC, regularly visiting the Party organizations of member units, and continuously holding forums on Party building for non-public translation enterprises. This guides and encourages translation enterprises to strengthen ideological and organizational construction, and better serve the country and society. The Association has actively responded to the requirements of educational poverty alleviation, having sponsored 8 teachers from Zuoquan to participate in faculty training for translation programs in higher education institutions nationwide, and organized Zuoquan university students to participate in internships, taking practical actions to support aspirations and intelligence, and improving the sense of gain and happiness of those being assisted.

(II) Strengthening Association Organizational Construction, Expanding Membership

The Association has further expanded its business scope and areas of work, establishing 5 new branches, including the Committee for Legal Translation, the Committee for Interpreting, the Committee for Foreign Discourse System Research, the Committee for Intercultural Communication Research, and the Committee for Translation Talent Evaluation. This has increased the number of branches from 10 to 15. It has jointly established a specialized working body, the Expert Committee for Reviewing Major Translation Work, with the China Foreign Languages Publishing Administration, and the Language Service Standardization Working Committee with the National Standardization Administration. It has improved the communication mechanism between the Association Secretariat, branches, member units, and local TACs, utilizing various activities to exchange information, share experiences, and discuss cooperation. The Association's branches have adapted to the situation, pioneered, and strengthened organizational construction, institutional construction, and talent construction, widely carrying out business exchanges and cooperation, promoting industry standards and certification, and collectively promoting new developments in the Association's services to members and the industry.

The Association's members are the most active forces in the translation and language service industry. Preliminary statistics show that from 2015 to 2021, the Association added 2,902 individual members, an increase of 121%; and 856 institutional members, an increase of 136%. As of December 2021, TAC had a total of 5,302 individual members, including 1,069 expert members (approximately 20%), 3,629 members (approximately 68%), and 599 student members (approximately 11%). The Association has 1,485 institutional members, including 1,406 enterprises and institutions (approximately 95%) and 79 social organizations (approximately 5%). The substantial expansion of membership reflects the improvement of the Association's influence and cohesion, and indicates the industry's full recognition of the Association's organizational and service work.

Local TACs have worked hard to play a bridging and connecting role, uniting members across the country to carry out a series of work and activities in academic exchange, talent training, international exchange, and self-improvement through organizing competitions, forums, training sessions, and salons. For example, the translation consulting and education training services of the Shanghai Society of Translators of Science and Technology, the Zhejiang Provincial Translators Association's support for the "Belt and Road Initiative," the "Yangtze River Economic Belt," and the "Chinese Culture Going Global" strategies, the foreign translation of Shaanxi literature by the Shaanxi Provincial Translators Association, and the institutional construction by the Shanghai Foreign Affairs Translators Association are excellent cases that demonstrate the positive role of local TACs in effectively serving local government foreign exchanges and promoting local economic development.

(III) Improving Member Service Levels, Achieving Technology Empowerment

The Association responds to member demands by conducting surveys and compiling language service industry development reports to provide members with industry policy consultations. By compiling standards and norms, it improves industry self-regulation and protects members' rights and interests. By organizing training sessions and competitions, it provides platforms for high-quality talents to emerge. By organizing industry academic activities such as annual conferences, it provides members with platforms for exchange, cooperation, and market expansion. By establishing communication mechanisms between the Secretariat, local TACs, and member units, it showcases members' achievements and information, playing the Association's hub role.

The Association Secretariat has innovated technological means, successively developing and establishing multi-lingual, multi-field high-end translation talent pools, online registration and application systems, and journal online editing and management systems. This has formed a multi-media, comprehensive online exchange service and business management platform, with the Association's official website as the main body and social media such as Weibo and WeChat as auxiliary channels. This has promoted the fundamental transformation of the Association's business management and organizational services from traditional manual methods to full-process informatization and digitalization, greatly improving service quality and levels.

(IV) Innovating and Successfully Organizing Academic Platforms, Promoting Academic Debate

The Association's journal, "Chinese Translators," keeps pace with the times, strengthens the planning of major topics around national practical needs, creates an information-based editing and management platform, standardizes and improves the review process, and has significantly expanded its scope and capacity. The overall quality of the journal has been further enhanced. It was selected for the "Exhibition of Excellent Journals Celebrating the 70th Anniversary of the Founding of New China." For five consecutive years, it has been selected as one of the "Most Internationally Influential Academic Journals in China" or "Excellent Academic Journals with International Influence in China," and has been included in the "Top 100 Journals by Digital Influence." It has been rated as a core foreign language journal for many consecutive years and has been included in the "Directory of Source Journals for the Chinese Social Science Citation Index," "Chinese Core Journals of Excellence," "Chinese Humanities and Social Sciences Core Journals," and "RCCSE Chinese Core Academic Journals," demonstrating the leading role of the Association's journal in promoting translation academic research.

Journals such as "Ethnic Translation" edited and published by the Committee for Ethnic Minority Language Translation, "Chinese Scientific Translation" edited and published by the Committee for Scientific and Technical Translation, and "Cross-Cultural Research Series" founded by the Committee for Intercultural Communication Research, as well as "Shanghai Translation" edited and published by the Shanghai Society of Translators of Science and Technology, a member unit, and "Yi Yuan Xin Tan" edited and published by the Sichuan Provincial Translators Association, have opened up spaces and windows for academic exchange within the industry, played an important role in enriching translation research, and achieved good social influence.

title_en: Borrowing the "expanding domestic demand" momentum, food and beverage companies in the Shanghai market are steadily advancing and seeking development.
body_en: In 2025, under the policy of "expanding domestic demand", food and beverage companies represented by companies listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange have consolidated their foundation and achieved breakthroughs through innovation. The Economic Reference News reporter noticed that 31 companies that have disclosed their 2024 financial reports have cumulatively distributed dividends exceeding 80 billion yuan, with 18 companies having a cash dividend ratio of over 50%. Companies such as Kuaijishan, Babifood, and Youyou Food have seen their dividend amounts nearly double. Stability: Driven by domestic demand, demonstrating the resilience of basic needs. From the perspective of "stability", the essential attributes and high-frequency consumption characteristics of the food and beverage industry will continue to provide companies with stable cash flow and risk resistance. Shanghai-listed food and beverage companies that have disclosed their 2024 financial reports have a total net operating cash flow of 124.5 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 32%. In terms of performance, industry leader Maotai is as stable as a rock. Under the promotion of the policy of "expanding domestic demand and promoting consumption", measures such as the distribution of consumer vouchers directly stimulate domestic demand growth. Maotai's revenue reached 174.1 billion yuan, with a net profit attributable to the parent company of 86.2 billion yuan, and both revenue and net profit growth rates exceeding 15% year-on-year. Leading sports beverage company Dongpeng Beverage achieved a total operating income of 15.8 billion yuan in 2024, a year-on-year increase of 41%, and achieved a net profit attributable to the parent company of 3.3 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 63%. The performance of its core products was outstanding, with Dongpeng Special Drink's market share in the national energy drink market increasing from 43% in 2023 to 48%, making it the best-selling energy drink in the country for four consecutive years. Faced with uncertainties such as the United States imposing tariffs, food and beverage companies quickly adjusted their strategies and accelerated their layout in the domestic market. E-commerce platforms such as Hema and JD.com have helped food and beverage companies shift to domestic sales through traffic support, further expanding their sales channels. Wufangzhai's online sales network covers major e-commerce platforms such as Tmall, JD.com, Douyin, and Pinduoduo, with 37 self-operated stores and more than 300 cooperative stores. During the reporting period, the company continued to adapt and optimize its operational strategies, solidifying the operating benefits of each platform, and achieving a year-on-year increase in gross profit margin of 8.05%. Babifood Chairman Liu Huiping said, "Our retail business is also growing rapidly, and cooperation with some core customers is deepening, with sales continuously increasing. For example, cooperation with Hema, a representative customer, is deepening, with monthly sales increasing by more than three times, and sales through Meituan channels have also achieved good results, exceeding tens of millions of yuan for the whole year." Progress: Innovation leads, opening up multiple growth paths. From the perspective of "progress", innovation-driven will become the core driving force for enterprise development. Whether it is the rise of emerging categories or the dividend of emerging channels, they will provide new growth points for companies. At the same time, trends such as the "rise of Chinese brands" and the "silver economy" will also bring more market opportunities to companies. Shanghai-listed food and beverage companies continue to deepen their multi-category strategic layout, achieve scene breakthroughs through differentiated product innovation, and seize the opportunity of consumption upgrade. For example, sugar-free tea and functional beverages are in the stage of increasing penetration. Dongpeng Beverage's electrolyte drink "Dongpeng Rehydration" exploded in the market since its launch last year, with a year-on-year increase in sales of 280.37% in 2024, successfully extending the consumption scene from the traditional "tired" scene to the "sweat point" scene of sports rehydration with its precise positioning of "rapid electrolyte replenishment". The organic integration of bulk snacks and channel innovation helps companies break through. Many Shanghai-listed companies have seized the growth dividend of emerging high-potential channels. Youyou Food, which mainly sells pickled chicken feet, stated in its 2024 annual report that in the industry's changing landscape of continuous shrinkage of traditional retail channels, the company achieved structural breakthroughs, pioneered the establishment of a membership-based retail system, and established cooperation with top channels. In 2024, the company cooperated with Sam's Club, Costco, and other companies to enter the membership-based hypermarket channel, and the new product, deboned duck feet, launched for Sam's Club became a hit. The company made a profit of 157 million yuan for the whole year, a year-on-year increase of 35.44%. Looking ahead to 2025, Youyou Food stated that after a careful evaluation by the company, it is expected that revenue growth will not be less than 20%. According to industry professionals, emerging channels such as bulk snack channels, content e-commerce channels, and membership-based hypermarket channels are growing significantly faster than traditional channels (distribution/comprehensive e-commerce, etc.), and companies embracing omni-channel are expected to achieve product volume. The "rise of Chinese brands" and the "silver economy" have also become highlights of the industry. Time-honored brands such as Yuengzufeng have launched low-sugar pastries to cater to the health trend. The company stated that low-sugar, low-fat, high-fiber, additive-free, and other healthy baked products have become market hotspots, and functional baked goods (such as those with added probiotics and dietary fiber) are also favored by consumers. The growth of these demands has driven innovation in product research and development and raw material selection for companies. The company continues to optimize its product process technology, use healthy cooking methods, streamline ingredients, select high-quality raw materials, and ensure that products meet modern consumers' demand for healthy eating. "Chinese time-honored brand" Guangzhou Restaurant closely follows hot topics such as the silver economy and the concept of food and medicine sharing the same origin, opening up new tracks such as "Cantonese-style light nourishment" and "Cantonese-style leisure sugar water", and launching products such as ginseng intelligence chicken soup and tangerine peel lotus seed red bean paste. The company continues to delve into research and development to cultivate product items, launching a series of meat products such as squab and chicken cutlets, further enriching the product matrix. This combination of tradition and innovation not only meets the diverse needs of consumers but also injects new vitality into the brand. (Reporter Zhang Wen, Shanghai) (This article is reprinted from Economic Reference News)

title_en: Neue Klasse aims to be game-changer for BMW
body_en:
BMW is pinning high hopes on its forthcoming Neue Klasse models, especially in China, where the German carmaker hopes they refresh its brand image and revive its fortunes in the world's largest and most competitive auto market.
The first China-made Neue Klasse model, the iX3, is scheduled to hit the Chinese market in 2026. But Jochen Goller, BMW's board member responsible for customer, brand, and sales, insists that the Neue Klasse is "much more than just new cars".
Unlike the incremental updates BMW has traditionally favored, the Neue Klasse represents a comprehensive reset, involving synchronized innovation across multiple core dimensions.
Among other things, it combines a new design philosophy, cutting-edge human-machine interfaces, sixth-generation electric drive technology, and the "superbrains" that act as central control units.
More importantly, it represents a complete decoupling of vehicle architecture and core innovations. This modular approach allows for greater flexibility in development and application.
For the Chinese market, BMW is integrating features co-developed with tech giants including Alibaba, Huawei, and ByteDance in an effort to tailor the Neue Klasse to the preferences of Chinese consumers.
"We believe the Neue Klasse should redefine BMW's brand image in China," Goller said. "Many people see BMW as delivering an exceptional driving experience, but slightly trailing in smart technology. We want to change that."
Goller said he has personally test-driven two Neue Klasse models and is confident they will impress. "With the launch of these models, we hope people will say: 'It drives beautifully and leads in intelligence.'"
Like other global premium brands, BMW is seeing sales shrink in China, its largest market around the world. Tech-savvy and open-to-innovation car buyers are being wooed away by Chinese NEV startups.
Statistics show that its first-quarter sales fell 17.2 percent year-on-year in the country, although it saw decent growth in all other major markets. "But China is growing as a market, and that is good news for us," said Goller.
China's automobile market, with annual sales surpassing 24 million vehicles, presents a complex landscape of consumer preferences and fierce competition between domestic and foreign automakers.
Goller has highlighted a focused strategy targeting 3-4 percent of the market — buyers who seek a blend of driving enjoyment and advanced technology, rather than competing head-on for mass volume.
"If consumers are simply looking for a 'smartphone on wheels', there are other brands they can choose. But for those who seek pure driving passion, a spirit of exploration, and the solid engineering that underpins it all, BMW is the ideal choice.
"BMW must be sharply focused on what it stands for — pure driving pleasure and a spirit of adventure — and avoid diluting its identity," said Goller.
The German carmaker also stresses the importance of localization as a pillar of its China strategy.
Its production base in Shenyang, Liaoning province, is one of the most advanced of its global manufacturing network. Its R&D network in China is second only to the one in Germany.
Sean Green, president and CEO of BMW Group Region China, highlights the company's significant software engineering operations in Nanjing, Jiangsu province, employing more than 600 engineers dedicated to rapid innovation cycles.
This local talent pool enables BMW to tailor its offerings to Chinese consumers by integrating partnerships with tech giants such as Alibaba, Huawei, and ByteDance.
These collaborations have brought advanced AI driver assistance, entertainment features, and digital services into the Neue Klasse lineup, allowing BMW to compete with emerging Chinese EV startups on their own turf.
One example is the new operating system, of which more than 70 percent of the features were developed in China.
Despite these technical advances, BMW remains committed to preserving its traditional strengths: combining superior driving dynamics with leading-edge digital capabilities, rather than chasing every technological fad, said Goller.
While BMW continues to refine its technical offerings, it is also rethinking how it communicates with the new generation of Chinese consumers.
Goller pointed to the IMAX-style panoramic iDrive showcased at the Shanghai auto show as an example of "bold, disruptive" marketing that resonated with local audiences. He said that more of such engagement is required.
"We know what pieces are needed for success in China (in the new era)," said Goller, "And now we are putting them together."

title_en: The large-scale financial application has entered a new stage, and the 16th session of the Lujiazui Financial Salon has successfully concluded.
body_en: On June 19th, the 16th session of the "Lujiazui Financial Salon" was successfully held in Pudong, Shanghai, with the theme "Large-scale Financial Applications and Innovation - Smart Finance, Large-scale Model Driving New Quality Productivity Leap". Many guests from the financial and technology sectors shared insightful views. Currently, the application of large-scale models in the financial industry has moved from simple applications to a new stage of value creation, facing various bottlenecks in the practical process, all parties are working together to promote the deep integration of large-scale models with the financial industry. Challenges such as illusions still exist in the core scenes of AI and large-scale models in the financial industry. Pan Runhong, Vice President of China Financial Electronic Technology Group, stated in his speech that the application of large-scale model technology in financial scenarios has achieved phased results. Currently, the financial industry is at a key point in the transformation to intelligence, and applications have moved from initial scenario exploration to a new stage of value excavation. "This is not only an important opportunity for the reconstruction of financial service processes and the transformation and upgrading of the financial industry, but also poses higher requirements for the mastery of new technologies," Pan Runhong said. Xu Tong, Chief Information Officer of Hengfeng Bank, shared his experience in exploring AI+ financial applications in his speech. He stated that the application of AI in financial institutions can be divided into three stages: the first stage solves the problem from 0 to 1 in the scenario, forming a systematic scenario from a local scenario, with the core being the construction of an intelligent body of prompt word knowledge base. The second stage focuses on fine-tuning the scenario model, forming basic application capabilities and general capabilities through the intelligent body platform. The third stage, in the case of limited resources, transforms the consensus formed by business value creation within the bank into comprehensive applications. According to Xu Tong's experience, the construction of AI can be broken down into five parts: application engineering, model engineering, knowledge engineering, computing power engineering, and organizational engineering. By building a knowledge middle platform under the background of AI, banks can form differentiated points of effort and main attack points. As AI applications mature, the overall work organization structure and workflow of financial institutions will undergo progressive changes. "Financial institutions should always adhere to the value orientation of 'application as the core, scenario as the king', create an intelligent engine that empowers business, and the core is still value creation," said Cheng Long, Chief Information Officer of CICC. It is possible to quickly integrate intelligent technology into existing scenarios around three types of scenarios: user experience product innovation and competitiveness enhancement, key risk prevention and control, and operational efficiency improvement and cost reduction, in order to achieve good application effects. Cheng Long pointed out that the key to competition in the AI era lies in innovation, not just efficiency improvement. With the widespread application of large-scale model technology, in addition to using new technologies to empower auxiliary scenarios such as knowledge Q&A, intelligent customers, and virtual assistants, the real value lies in applying them to scenarios that traditional technologies find difficult or impossible to solve, enabling deep integration of AI capabilities with core business scenarios and professional processes. By using AI to strengthen risk control, develop new products, create new models and new revenue, and then enhance the company's innovation capabilities and market competitiveness. From the perspective of foreign banks, Zhang Fangchang, General Manager of the Information Technology Architecture Platform Department of Bank of East Asia, introduced that foreign banks have more cross-border businesses, and when facing multiple regulations, AI can greatly improve efficiency in areas such as data acquisition for cross-border lending, document review, and ledger organization. With limited human and computing resources, maximizing scenarios is the core theory of large-scale model applications, with customer growth, risk control, and cost efficiency as the primary goals. Wei Jiaohua, General Manager of Taibao Technology, believes that in the process of focusing on core financial business scenarios, large-scale models and AI still face some challenges. For example, the illusion problem, that is, large-scale models cannot guarantee accuracy, lack of data foundation and unstructured knowledge. If the issue of personal private domain is not resolved well, no one will be willing to contribute their own experience. In addition, in the popularization of large-scale models, the relevant technological literacy of business personnel also needs to be improved. In Wei Jiaohua's view, large-scale models are "students" and should learn from people. When large-scale models assist in decision-making, they can provide an answer, but people are responsible for making decisions. When using large-scale models, they can also be seen as a member of the team, and people can solve problems that have been replaced by AI by working harder and being better than the large-scale model. From the perspective of small and medium-sized banks, Zhao Weixing, President of Chongqing Fumin Bank, pointed out that the application of financial large-scale models needs to reconstruct cognitive logic from a strategic level. He emphasized that the synergy between general large-scale models and vertical domain expertise is far superior to the isolated development of professional models. Small and medium-sized banks should focus on "real value scenarios" that reduce costs and increase efficiency, be wary of technical application misconceptions, and build a new paradigm of an "algorithmic bank". Zhao Weixing proposed that in the future, banks need to shift from being "product-driven" to "customer demand-driven intelligent body ecology", using a combination of general large-scale model base + industry knowledge base + dynamic data flow to truly adapt financial products to enterprise operational needs, rather than being constrained by traditional risk preferences. The financial industry should avoid getting caught up in a "technological arms race" and should seek breakthroughs in the balance between computing power economy and green development. "Financial large-scale models are crucial, but financial large-scale models alone are not enough" In the process of deep integration of AI large-scale models with the financial industry, the assistance of technology companies also plays an important role. Several guests from technology companies shared insights on overcoming application bottlenecks with new technology breakthroughs based on their practical experience. Li Chao, General Manager and Chief Scientist of Tencent Cloud Tianyu, believes that the digital development of the financial industry has three main lines: transformation of data elements circulation, deepening of intelligent applications, and upgrading of inclusive finance, with financial risk control being the intersection of the three main lines. Data elements have non-competitive and high-speed cross-temporal and spatial flow characteristics, and financial institutions need to reconstruct their risk management systems to activate the potential of data elements. Intelligent technology has also brought about new types of attacks, requiring traditional risk control systems to upgrade to a more refined model confrontation mode. At the level of inclusive finance, financial risk control can reduce marginal costs and obtain better business flow by restructuring the underlying logic of business. Wang Wei, Chief Technology Officer of Ant Financial Services Group, believes that the development of financial business and AI technology go hand in hand. The financial industry has the characteristics of large business scale, high data quality, and rich scenarios, and the continuous development of AI technology brings continuous mode changes and reshaping to the financial business. Today, AI has been widely used in hot areas of finance such as services, risk control, marketing, investment research, and investment advisory, and financial institutions are the industry that has embraced the AI technology revolution most thoroughly. Wang Wei pointed out that the challenges of applying AI in financial business can be summarized into three main aspects: computing power input, data trustworthiness, and vertical pressure. In order to solidly implement the capabilities of AI and intelligent bodies in the financial industry, there are still many technological dividends to be explored in vertical domain fine-tuning, knowledge injection, model lightweighting, and algorithm architecture optimization. Large-scale models are crucial in the financial industry, but they are not enough on their own, so the landing of intelligent bodies in the financial industry is more like a jigsaw puzzle, requiring a combination of a series of capabilities to complement each other. Through sharing practical experience in the implementation of generative AI applications, Kuang Wenchuan, Chief Scientist of China Electronics and Director of the China Electronics Golden Information Research Institute, pointed out that although large-scale models and intelligent bodies demonstrate powerful capabilities, they are not universal solutions and require evaluation of their applicability in different scenarios. The deep integration of data, models, and computing power is crucial, and it is necessary to continuously explore the potential of large-scale models through scenario-oriented engineering paths, using enterprise-level knowledge engineering and other means. Faced with challenges such as industrialization in the process of building a digital intelligence infrastructure, highly customized requirements from various enterprises, and long-term stable operation, Kuang Wenchuan called for increased collaboration between the industry and the industrial side, opening up scenarios, and exploring ways to share industry datasets through a hierarchical classification approach, sharing the practical results of "from 0 to 1", and jointly promoting the scale and modernization of the application of digital intelligence infrastructure. Zhang Yande, General Manager of the Industry Project Group of Huawei's Computing Power Platform Vanguard Team, explained the importance of a solid computing power base for AI financial applications. The application of industry + AI is a systematic engineering process, and Zhang Yande summarized the engineering as "architecture first, easy first, difficult later, holistic decomposition, gradual advancement, and urgent battle" in 16 words. The engineering architecture starts from the computing power base, and customers need not only chips and servers, but also upper-level operator libraries and AI toolchains, requiring service providers to establish unified service capabilities with partners to promote the overall value of AI in the financial industry. Zheng Miao, Deputy General Manager of the New Financial Industry of Alibaba Cloud's Public Cloud Business Unit, believes that the financial industry is not lacking in scenarios, but in blockbuster scenarios. All traditional application scenarios are worth reconstructing with AI, leading to a paradigm shift in application scenarios. The construction of AI scenarios can be divided into five major projects: application engineering, model engineering, knowledge engineering, computing power engineering, and security engineering. Wu Yijun, General Manager of the Product Overall Department of Qi Anxin, focused on the security of large-scale model applications. Currently, large-scale model technology is accelerating the empowerment of thousands of industries, but its complex application architecture and development process have brought new security challenges, such as jailbreak attacks, prompt word injections, denial of service attacks, component vulnerabilities, and data leaks. Wu Yijun suggested that in the deployment and use of open-source large-scale models, a four-tier security barrier should be established in network security, permission control, content compliance, and data security, managing external access, internal services, and operations and maintenance management through three data channels. Sun Hongjun, CTO of SoftBank Financial Business Group, introduced the experience of DeepSeek driving the transformation of old and new architectures in bank systems. The system architecture of financial institutions is very complex, and updates and replacements are common requirements. Past technology stack transitions were carried out through interactions between people from requirements to design to development. AI tools replace human-to-human interactions at each node, allowing outdated systems to quickly transition to new systems, with cost, time, and quality all guaranteed. Jing Shaofei, Director of the Product Department of Boland, pointed out that financial institutions frequently encounter difficulties in obtaining computing power, managing models, developing agents, and controlling security in AI landing practices. A one-stop model construction, training, and deployment platform should emphasize security, controllability, and flexible scalability, support rapid integration with various business scenarios, and provide enterprises with full-process AI empowerment capabilities from data governance, model development to the landing of intelligent applications, helping financial customers efficiently build an autonomous and controllable intelligent business system. "AI Agent is the 'last mile' of large-scale model landing" In the roundtable discussion session on the theme of "The Landing Practice of AI Agents in the Financial Industry", representatives from several financial institutions further introduced their insights on the application of AI intelligent bodies in financial industry scenarios. Li Jiabin, Director of the Software Development Center of China Postal Savings Bank, believes that there is still a lot of work to be done in the evaluation of AI tools. AI landing scenarios are easy, but how to implement them well requires a lot of evaluation. Doing a good job of evaluation can improve the efficiency of AI Agents' landing and reduce development costs. He Peng, Director of the Data Management Department of China Minsheng Bank, pointed out that the core of AI Agents is to solve the "last mile" problem. Most of the work of a large institution revolves around the mainstream processes that have been designed, but there are many details that may not be effectively expressed and implemented in terms of technological needs. However, these parts can greatly improve the work efficiency of a large number of employees, which is why institutions pay close attention to relevant technology layouts. At the same time, the construction of the AI Agent system also requires follow-up changes in organizational systems. Chen Longqiang, Chief Digital Officer of Zhongxin Baixin Bank, suggested that the layout of AI Agents should "get on the bus quickly". Developing intelligent bodies based on MCP will bring out true intelligence, but attention should be paid to issues such as data security, model security, and ethics, "it may be very enjoyable to run after getting on the bus, but safety must be taken into account". Jia Jianguo, Executive Director and Director of the Information Technology Department of China-Europe Fund, believes that the era of multiple intelligent bodies will come quickly, and the collaborative governance of multiple intelligent bodies will become the primary task. The collaboration of multiple intelligent bodies needs to solve the problem of division of rights and responsibilities, and clarify who bears the consequences of business decisions. If there are illusions, multiple checks of multiple intelligent bodies can be attempted. Li Shuanghong, Head of the Artificial Intelligence Laboratory at Guojin Securities, believes that large-scale models are still far from using a universal interface, but now that the flow has developed, it is difficult to completely disappear like a bubble. The specific development of large-scale models in the future cannot be predicted, and it depends on the joint efforts of the industrial, technological, and AI sectors to see what results will be produced. Tan Ke, Head of the New Technology Application Product Team at China Life Research Center, stated that as the coverage of intelligent bodies becomes wider, with the continuous improvement of various capabilities, the gradual clarification of various industry standards, and the joint efforts of the entire ecosystem of vendors, the industry is confident in the future of intelligent bodies. This event was guided by the Shanghai Municipal Committee Financial Office and the Pudong New Area People's Government, co-organized by the Lujiazui Financial Salon Secretariat and China Financial Electronic Technology Group Co., Ltd., with media support from First Financial and Cailian Society. This series of events will build a regular exchange platform in response to the "Lujiazui Forum", and through mechanized, scenarized, and internationalized operations, continue to output the "Pudong Wisdom" of financial reform to empower the high-quality development of Pudong's economy, and fully promote the construction of the core area of Shanghai International Financial Center to new heights.

title_en: Chain Talk / Hong Kong digital asset market steadily advancing \ Fu Rao, Shi Jianzheng
body_en:
In terms of the current situation, the dual drive of stabilizing the currency system and digitizing real-world assets (RWA) is pushing the Hong Kong digital asset market into a new stage. Among them, green bonds, as a representative asset type, have taken the lead in tokenization trials, becoming an effective lever to promote the integration of sustainable finance and digital finance. It not only provides a concrete scenario for asset digitization but also offers technical tools for green transformation, serving as an institutional intersection to achieve the dual goals of "fintech + green development."

As an international financial and innovation center, Hong Kong is actively promoting a series of measures including stablecoin regulatory frameworks, RWA standard formulation, and trial platform construction. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's draft Stablecoin Regulations clearly stipulate that stablecoins must be 100% backed by physical assets and be regulated under a licensing system, providing an institutional foundation for asset clearing and value anchoring. At the same time, Hong Kong Cyberport and Science Park have launched RWA technology sandbox construction, encouraging institutions to design on-chain assets for green scenarios such as energy, construction, and transportation. With the joint efforts of the SAR government and various market forces, Hong Kong is expected to build a digital asset institutional foundation centered on "stable value intermediaries" and "on-chain asset representation," providing a compliant, secure, and efficient reference template for digital assetization in the Greater Bay Area, Asia, and global markets.

Moving towards "real scenario applications"
Among many trial scenarios, green bond tokenization has shown the strongest potential for implementation. Green bonds, due to their clear asset structure and specific use, have demonstrated high feasibility in tokenization practices. Recently, Fosun Wealth and Ant Group have collaborated to layout green energy RWA tokenization, in conjunction with the HKMA-supported "Green FinTech Pilot Program," focusing on on-chain confirmation, standard splitting, and intelligent management of carbon assets, renewable energy rights, marking a shift where RWA is no longer just a financial innovation concept but a practical exploration closely integrated with physical industries and sustainable development. This trend also provides insights to the market: RWA should move from "on-chain value representation" towards "real scenario applications," relying on stablecoins as a clearing medium to address past issues of asset illiquidity and lack of transparent evaluation mechanisms. In the future, green electricity, carbon emission quotas, agricultural revenue rights, marine resource usage rights, etc., are also expected to be included in the on-chain asset system, further enriching asset structures and expanding investment targets.

Although trial projects are gradually being implemented, to achieve scalable development, RWA still faces multiple challenges such as compliance verification, cross-chain settlement, information disclosure, valuation standards, etc. The global market still lacks a unified language and standard system for "on-chain finance." Currently, licensed platforms in Hong Kong such as OSL are actively building infrastructure covering KYC, data custody, AML anti-money laundering, smart contract auditing, etc., to provide underlying trust guarantees for RWA circulation.

On the other hand, stablecoins themselves as a new payment tool also need to form institutional consensus in terms of legal status, clearing risks, and value stability. Jurisdictions such as Singapore and New Zealand have classified stablecoins under the "Payment Services Act," requiring issuing institutions to undergo reserve asset audits and have mandatory redemption mechanisms. In comparison, Hong Kong's legislative process and institutional sophistication are gradually benchmarking international standards, paving the way for market development.

Furthermore, at the technical level, to achieve sustainable development of RWA, a series of underlying protocol and cross-chain interface compatibility issues still need to be addressed. Currently, most RWA trials are built on Ethereum or EVM-compatible chains, lacking modular deployment capabilities tailored for financial institutions. In the future, there should be accelerated construction of dedicated chain systems supporting multiple asset classes, privacy protection, and high-frequency clearing, interfacing with existing financial core systems (such as SWIFT, CHATS) to form a complete closed-loop system of "off-chain confirmation - on-chain trading - on-chain clearing." Only with the triple drive of institutions, industry, and technology can RWA truly move out of the trial phase and towards the mainstream capital market.

It is worth emphasizing that the true value of RWA tokenization lies not only in improving asset efficiency but also in endowing traditional assets with new combinability, traceability, and social responsibility attributes. In the context of green finance, through on-chain technology, the use of funds can be visualized, project effects quantitatively evaluated, forming a "data foundation" for sustainable finance. This "visible, calculable, traceable" financial trust mechanism not only helps improve fund allocation efficiency but also assists companies in fulfilling environmental, social, and governance (ESG) responsibilities, achieving policy transformation supporting sustainable development goals (SDGs) with digital tools. From a broader perspective, this is also the important mission of Hong Kong as an Asian financial technology hub: not only promoting asset digitization but also supporting industry decarbonization, greening, and responsibility, driving "trusted assets" to become the institutional unit of a "trusted society."

Building a "institutional pivot"
When stablecoins serve as the institutional anchor for payment clearing and RWA as the product carrier for asset mapping, the coupling of "anchoring + circulation" will increasingly highlight Hong Kong's position in the global financial restructuring. In the future, stablecoins and RWA tokenization will undoubtedly establish the institutional foundation of Hong Kong's future digital asset market. With the three-way promotion of SAR government regulation guidance, technological innovation, and industry demand, Hong Kong is expected to become the "institutional pivot" for regional asset tokenization and green financial innovation.
