title_en: Enter "a door", allowing "little brother" to have higher efficiency in safeguarding rights and lower costs.
body_en:
What do new forms of employment such as couriers and delivery drivers care most about when running orders? The answer is efficiency, speed, and time. When disputes arise, such as in the settlement of compensation, can there be a mediation model that matches the efficiency of these "delivery guys"?
It is reported that in June 2024, the Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Human Resources and Social Security, together with multiple departments, jointly issued the implementation opinions on the one-stop mediation of labor disputes in new forms of employment. One year later, the city completed the construction layout of the first batch of one-stop mediation centers for labor disputes in new forms of employment, achieving full coverage at the district level. More than 40 different levels of one-stop mediation organizations were established in districts, streets, and towns across the city, handling over 1,100 labor disputes by the end of 2024.
Multi-departmental coordination plays a role in dispute prevention, resolution, and source governance. From the perspective of the "delivery guys," all they need to do is enter "one door," or apply online and mediate online to efficiently protect their rights and reduce running around.
Aggregated linkage speeds up conflict resolution
In half a day, Xiao He and Xiao Zhang, who came to Shanghai to work and decided to return to their hometown after delivering food for a week on a certain platform, finally received their hard-earned money. They walked into the Hongkou District one-stop mediation center for labor disputes in new forms of employment.
Based on the preliminary investigation of new business formats in the district, the mediator quickly found the company involved from the list of companies and contacted the company's responsible person, Ms. Ji. Ms. Ji stated that due to the consolidation and settlement of order information, the relevant compensation would be paid on the 25th of the following month.
Learning that they had to wait for more than a month, Xiao He and Xiao Zhang became emotional. Through the mediator's coordination from multiple dimensions of emotions, reason, and law, the company paid 1,400 yuan in compensation that same afternoon.
Behind the speed-up of conflict resolution is aggregated linkage, creating a new model of one-stop mediation. The Shanghai Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Department, courts, judicial authorities, and trade unions strengthen cooperation to explore a working pattern of "human resources leading, departmental coordination, and industry participation."
Each district actively explores increasing joint mediation functions in labor dispute arbitration institutions or related mediation organizations, establishing one-stop mediation centers for labor disputes in new forms of employment based on existing human resources, judicial, and trade union mediation organizations.
It is reported that when handling a collective dispute involving a domestic service platform in Jiangpu Road Street, Yangpu District, the street judicial office, police station, law firm, and mediation center worked together. The mediation center was responsible for overall coordination and data verification, the judicial office provided legal support and participated in mediation, and the police station was responsible for maintaining order and risk prevention. Through efforts in "enterprise negotiation - data verification - employee communication," they successfully resolved a collective dispute involving more than 100 workers from 12 districts in the city, with a total amount of over 900,000 yuan.
Integrated mediation reduces the cost of safeguarding rights
During an online mediation session, the mediator, "delivery guy" Yang, the site involved, and the staff of the food delivery platform all logged on promptly and entered the mediation process.
Yang admitted that he had worked for several platforms before, earning 6 to 7 yuan per order. When he joined, the site's management informed him of the payment standards, but Yang did not pay attention to the specific pricing range, so he hoped to increase the amount appropriately.
The site manager and related personnel stated that the site where Yang worked implemented a refined calculation system for order volume, with different settlement standards for different order volume ranges. Upon review, it was found that there were indeed flaws in the notification of the settlement policy, leading to Yang misunderstanding the unit price standard. They agreed to partially reduce the accommodation and equipment costs that Yang should have borne.
Real-time communication and repeated discussions greatly reduced the cost. The two sides quickly reached an agreement, with Yang agreeing to be paid at a standard rate of 5 yuan per order by the platform and site, while the platform and site agreed to waive a total of 1,030 yuan in related expenses for Yang.
Multi-party coordination is one of the most time-consuming and labor-intensive aspects of mediating disputes. One-stop mediation conducts full-process online mediation activities for labor disputes that meet the conditions for online mediation; for cases where online mediation applications are submitted but offline mediation is required, or where mediation applications have been submitted on-site but meet the conditions for online mediation, one-stop mediation organizations strive to integrate online and offline services to provide high-quality, low-cost, and diverse dispute resolution services for new forms of employment.
Promoting substantive resolution and ensuring follow-up connections
It is understood that the platform company "Ele.me" in Putuo District has undergone two "upgrades" in its dispute mediation mechanism.
In October 2021, the Putuo District Bureau of Human Resources and Social Security guided "Ele.me" to establish the "Blue Knights" dispute mediation committee pilot work and set up an online mediation platform. In October 2024, in collaboration with the Municipal Labor Dispute Arbitration Institute, the district people's court, judicial bureau, and general trade union, they jointly established a one-stop city-district joint mediation center for labor disputes in new forms of employment with "Ele.me."
It is reported that Shanghai is focusing on areas or industries with active platform economies and more labor disputes, strengthening labor dispute negotiation and mediation work to promote the substantive resolution of conflicts.
While vigorously promoting mediation, efforts are made to ensure compliance and connect mediation with arbitration and litigation. On the one hand, the results of mediation are confirmed. If a mediation agreement is reached, the parties must promptly and fully implement the agreement. On the other hand, legal guidance is provided for arbitration and adjudication. For new forms of employment disputes where the parties do not agree to mediation or mediation is unsuccessful, if it falls within the scope of labor dispute acceptance, the parties can apply for arbitration, and the mediation organization can accept the arbitration application.
Next, the Shanghai Human Resources and Social Security Department will actively cooperate with relevant departments to continue promoting the establishment of one-stop mediation organizations for labor disputes in new forms of employment as needed, continuously improving the capacity of mediation organizations. Strengthening organizational support and personnel deployment to ensure more efficient and convenient resolution of labor disputes in new forms of employment.

title_en: Discharged from the hospital and immediately receiving compensation, "Hui Min Bao" truly benefits the people.
body_en:
[Shenzhen Commercial Daily] (Reporter Qiu Qingyue) 57-year-old Wang Cuicui (pseudonym) sat in front of the hospital bed, tightly holding the examination report, with a furrowed brow. When she was diagnosed with ovarian malignant tumor, the high cost of surgery, chemotherapy, and targeted therapy once almost made her collapse. But now, she has a sense of relief: "The doctor told me that the hospitalization expenses this time can be directly deducted from the reimbursement of 'Shenzhen Huimin Bao', so I don't have to scramble to raise money anymore."

Wang Cuicui's experience is one of the epitomes of many insured patients under "Shenzhen Huimin Bao". In 2023, the first release of "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" introduced a one-stop settlement service, breaking through the data barriers between Shenzhen medical insurance, hospitals, and commercial insurance systems, achieving "reimbursement upon discharge". This not only reduces the pressure on the masses to advance funds but also transforms the reimbursement process from "running around" to "no running at all".

Wang Cuicui's medical bills record the bitterness and hope of an ordinary family in Shenzhen. In 2024, her total treatment cost exceeded 1.21 million yuan. To raise money, she planned to mortgage her house and borrow money from relatives and friends. The turning point came in 2023. Under the joint guidance of the Shenzhen Medical Security Bureau, the Shenzhen Local Financial Management Bureau, and the Shenzhen Regulatory Bureau of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission, "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" was first introduced. The conditions for participating in "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" are lenient, not limited by age, occupation, or health condition, as long as one is covered by Shenzhen medical insurance.

In addition, as long as the insured person seeks treatment at a total of more than 9,600 designated medical institutions in Shenzhen and hospitals connected to the Guangdong provincial network settlement platform, when discharged, the system automatically deducts the reimbursement portion of Shenzhen medical insurance and "Shenzhen Huimin Bao", and the patient only needs to pay the amount they are responsible for, effectively reducing the problems of insured persons needing to advance funds, taking a long time, and requiring a lot of documentation.

As of June 6, 2025, "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" has provided one-stop settlement services for 320,000 person-times, accounting for 99%, truly achieving "more data running, less legwork for the masses".

"In the past, reimbursement required submitting identification, medical records, invoices, and other materials, now all of these are automatically captured by the system." The person in charge of the underwriting institution of "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" introduced that through data processing technology, hospitals, medical insurance, and commercial insurance parties achieve real-time data verification, eliminating false claims; AI algorithms automatically match reimbursement rules, compressing the lengthy traditional commercial insurance claims process to "instant settlement".

Feng Yonghua (pseudonym), a medical assistance recipient being treated for liver cell carcinoma at a tertiary hospital in Shenzhen, calculated a bill: the total medical expenses during the last hospitalization amounted to 213,500.95 yuan, after reimbursement by Shenzhen medical insurance, "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" compensated 62,640.92 yuan. "I used to think that commercial insurance was a luxury, but now with the 88 yuan 'Shenzhen Huimin Bao', I can be insured for up to 4 million yuan, and the government fully subsidizes our participation."

This "universal" aspect is the core of the design of "Shenzhen Huimin Bao". For special difficult groups such as medical assistance recipients in this city, registered disabled residents, difficult workers, and preferential treatment objects, relevant government functional departments also provide unified assistance for participation.

It is worth noting that the 2025 annual "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" is currently in the centralized enrollment period, with enrollment ending at the end of the month. Normal participants who pay Shenzhen medical insurance and Shenzhen residents covered by non-local medical insurance can all participate. Participants can conveniently enroll and pay through various channels, such as following the official designated participation platform "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" WeChat public account, or through "Shenzhen Medical Insurance" "Micro Insurance" WeChat public account, "Alipay" "UnionPay QuickPass" "i Shenzhen" "Bank of Communications" "Yue Sheng Shi" APP and "Yue Sheng Shi" mini-program, or visit offline service windows for consultation and processing. Please handle it in a timely manner, as missing the deadline will not allow for retroactive payment.

title_en: After Qianling Mountain Park waived the entrance fee, the number of visitors increased by 30%, and revenue exceeded ten million - with no tickets, business is booming.
body_en:
Guizhou Daily Tianyan News reporter Gao Wei
At 10 a.m. on June 14th, the non-legacy snack "Wangji Crispy Duck" in the Qianyun Hui non-legacy market in Guizhou Qianlingshan Park wafted with a tempting oil fragrance. This small shop, which is only 16 square meters, sells over 100 ducks on average per day on weekends, becoming one of the most popular consumption points in Qianlingshan Park after the admission fee was waived.
In January 2024, Qianlingshan Park announced the complete cancellation of admission fees. This decision, which seemed to be "cutting off a source of income," unexpectedly opened up new profit space. After the admission fee was waived, the park's visitor flow increased by 30% year-on-year, and the operating income from commercial assets and project operations that have been contracted exceeded 13 million yuan, creating a new development path in the cultural tourism industry of "waiving admission fees without reducing revenue."
"After the admission fee was waived, visitors are more willing to pay for unique experiences, and the per capita consumption has increased instead of decreased," said a person in charge of Qianlingshan Park management.
In the market, the owner of "Qian Tea Official," Jiang Zhijie, enthusiastically recommends the original drink "Wood Ginger Lemon Tea" to visitors: "The main ingredient of this drink, wood ginger, is a specialty ingredient in Guizhou." The store incorporates local ingredients such as prickly pear and hairy fruit into new tea drinks, selling 200 cups in a single day on weekends, and with the addition of independently designed "Qianling Monkey" cultural and creative products, the daily revenue reaches 14,000 yuan. "In August, we will launch online stores on platforms such as Xiaohongshu, Pinduoduo, Taobao, etc., so that more out-of-town customers can buy Guizhou cultural and creative products," Jiang Zhijie revealed.
Not far away, "Shrub Coffee" was filled with tourists taking photos in front of the floor-to-ceiling windows, and the "window with Qianlingshan water" as a check-in wall made the store's weekend daily turnover easily exceed ten thousand yuan, with 70% of repeat customers being female. "For the summer season, the store plans to launch a 'Afternoon Tea + Lake Tour' package in collaboration with the cruise ship, expecting to extend the visitor's stay by more than 4 hours," said Yao Suzhi, the person in charge of Shrub Coffee (Qianlingshan Park store).
In the "Qianlai Culture" cultural and creative store, the "Hip-hop Monkey" doll wearing a Miao silver collar was eagerly sought after by tourists. The host Zhang Feie introduced, "Inspired by the 'Qianling Monkey' IP and Guizhou ethnic culture, the store currently has more than 30 products in ethnic and animal series, with 90% of purchases made by out-of-town tourists." The popularity of the internet-famous golden snub-nosed monkey "Xiaolaofei" has further boosted cultural and creative sales, and "Qianlai Culture" has taken advantage of this trend to launch related derivative products, which are expected to be sold by the end of July.
These lively consumption scenes are all concentrated in the Qianyun Hui non-legacy market, which was transformed from a disused warehouse. In March of this year, the market completed its transformation with significant results. It revitalized 4,100 square meters of inefficient space, built a 1-kilometer lakeside promenade, and added public activity spaces and a music dock. Since its operation, 15 non-legacy shops have settled in, with a 40% increase in visitor flow compared to before the transformation.
Last year, the operating rights of Qianlingshan Park were transferred to a district-owned cultural tourism company, following the logic of asset marketization, re-inviting investment from outside, and introducing high-quality operating companies for market-oriented operations. Currently, the commercial area within the park has expanded to 10,200 square meters, the number of merchants has increased to 35, and the number of formats has increased to 62, with traditional projects such as cable cars and cruise ships also undergoing upgrades.
From "relying on admission tickets" to "scene revolution," Qianlingshan Park has achieved a breakthrough reconstruction of consumption formats; from "single sightseeing" to "immersive experience," it has deeply satisfied the needs of visitors. "Waiving admission fees is not the end, but a new starting point for development," said a person in charge of the park management, stating that the park will deepen the integration of "culture + tourism + commerce" development, create a more attractive urban leisure space, and provide a replicable "Guiyang solution" for the transformation of national scenic spots.

title_en: The "Clear and Rectify the Abuse of AI Technology" special action has disposed of more than 3,500 illegal AI products.
body_en:
Beijing, June 20th (China Youth Daily, China Youth Online reporter He Chunchung) The data released by the Cyberspace Administration of China today shows that since the launch of the "Clear Sky and Crackdown on the Abuse of AI Technology" special action in April 2025, more than 3,500 illegal AI products such as mini-programs, applications, and intelligent entities have been disposed of in the first phase, clearing more than 960,000 pieces of illegal information, and handling more than 3,700 accounts.

During the special action, local cyberspace authorities have taken multiple measures to fulfill their territorial management responsibilities. The Beijing Cyberspace Administration has set up a reporting channel for the governance of AI technology abuse, handling 26 related reports. The Shanghai Cyberspace Administration has promoted the implementation of identification requirements, organized 4 sessions of legal publicity and special exchanges, and key enterprises in the region have basically completed the explicit identification norms online. The Zhejiang Cyberspace Administration has increased supervision over local AI applications and website platforms, with various platforms intercepting and clearing more than 25.5 million pieces of illegal information and questions.

Key website platforms have strengthened the governance of the abuse of AI technology at the source. Tencent has raised the admission threshold, optimized inspection mechanisms, rejected and disposed of a total of more than 570 illegal mini-programs, applications, and so on. Weibo has reviewed and disposed of more than 4,800 pieces of illegal content through strategic identification, user reports, and other channels, and published typical cases. Tongyi Platform has established a secure management system around the data lifecycle, strengthening training corpus management in data collection, training, and use stages. Key platforms such as Alibaba and Kuaishou are actively promoting the implementation of implicit identification of metadata.

title_en: Strong responsibility promotes compliance and stable development.
body_en:
This newspaper (Tan Xing reporter Zhang Xiaohang)
The Market Supervision Administration of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region recently held a video conference on administrative guidance for platform enterprises in the entire region, further strengthening the main responsibility of platform enterprises, improving the compliance level of platform enterprises, and promoting the high-quality development of the platform economy in Guangxi.
The meeting pointed out that platform enterprises should strictly implement their main responsibilities, actively cooperate with market supervision departments, and jointly create an orderly and competitive online market development environment; focus on prominent issues in the platform economy such as "no refunds" and "automatic price adjustment" to carry out self-inspection and rectification, establish, modify, improve, and publicize platform agreement rules, and strictly fulfill obligations such as verification registration, product information inspection, and monitoring.
The meeting emphasized that platform enterprises should fulfill their obligations to review merchants, ensure food safety and service quality; optimize algorithm rules to protect the labor rights and interests of delivery riders; eliminate unfair competition such as "big data discrimination" and practices such as "substituting fines for management"; continuously strengthen guidance and promotion for merchants and consumers to form a good social trend of preventing food waste.
The meeting required market supervision departments at all levels in Guangxi to carry out administrative guidance and publicity and education to various platform enterprises in their jurisdiction in a targeted manner according to their territorial and business functions, effectively strengthen work responsibilities, improve regulatory effectiveness, achieve "finding people, clarifying matters, and assigning responsibilities", ensure that relevant opinions are conveyed and implemented. Focus on prominent issues that consumers strongly reflect and public opinion concentrates on in areas such as current platform rules, platform fees, and live e-commerce, comprehensively investigate the current situation of platform rules, vigorously rectify phenomena that use rules to disrupt fair competition and infringe on the legitimate rights and interests of platform merchants and consumers.
At the meeting, the heads of relevant departments of the Market Supervision Administration of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region respectively provided administrative guidance on the implementation of compliance management responsibilities by platform enterprises, investigation and rectification of prominent issues in the platform economy, urging food delivery platforms to prevent food waste, lawfully safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of instant delivery riders, and key areas of network market supervision such as prices, unfair competition, advertising, product quality, and food safety.
National platform enterprise leaders in Guangxi, such as JD.com, Taotian, Douyin, Pinduoduo, Meituan, Ele.me, Shansong, SF Express, Dada Express, and UU Run Errands, attended the meeting at the main venue. About 550 people, including relevant officials from market supervision bureaus in various cities (prefectures) of Guangxi, platform enterprise leaders in various cities, national platform enterprise local agents, and distribution partners, attended the meeting at the sub-venue.

title_en: Resolutely crack down on counterfeiting and inferior products, safeguard quality sleep | Mousse successfully cooperates with the police to crack down on multiple cases of counterfeit mattresses.
body_en:
Crackdown on Counterfeiting and Safeguarding Rights
Mousse Group has always regarded brand protection and combating counterfeit products as important tasks. Recently, we have cooperated with police forces in multiple provinces, taking strong measures to successfully crack down on a series of cases involving counterfeit "Mousse" trademarks. Recently, the court sentenced six suspects in one of the cases: all individuals involved were sentenced to imprisonment and fines; the main culprit was sentenced to five years and six months in prison, fined over 1.4 million yuan, and ordered to forfeit illegal gains. In addition, the counterfeit goods and production tools involved were confiscated, and the counterfeit production sites were completely destroyed. This series of crackdown and rights protection actions have achieved significant results!

[Case 1] Lin and others Counterfeiting Registered Trademarks
In January 2024, based on the information we provided, the Changyuan Public Security Bureau in Henan quickly conducted investigations and filed cases, and after investigations in Guangdong, Zhejiang, Hunan, Shandong, Guangxi, and other provinces and cities, a unified crackdown was carried out to comprehensively strike the criminal chain. Through these actions, the production and sales criminal dens were successfully destroyed, and the six suspects involved were arrested and brought to justice.

Recently, the court conducted the first trial and verdict on the case. The individuals involved were sentenced to imprisonment and fines, with two main suspects each sentenced to five years and six months in prison, and fined over 1.4 million and 900,000 yuan respectively. In addition, the court also required them to forfeit illegal gains, and the counterfeit goods and production equipment involved were confiscated. This judgment once again highlights the determination of judicial authorities to combat intellectual property crimes and sets an important example for enterprise rights protection.

[Case 2] Liu and others Counterfeiting Registered Trademarks
During the process of safeguarding and cracking down on counterfeiting on online platforms, the legal department of Mousse Group discovered that multiple Taobao stores were suspected of selling counterfeit products and were related. The legal department immediately reported the case to the Zhongshan Public Security Bureau. The police responded promptly, filed a case, and launched an investigation. Through in-depth data analysis, the police successfully identified the identities of the members of the criminal gang. In November 2024, the police conducted simultaneous operations in Dongguan, Foshan, Yibin, Huanggang, and other places, successfully arresting Liu, Li, Xu, and 6 other suspects, and seized 78 counterfeit mattresses and a large number of counterfeit Mousse Group registered trademarks' packaging, labels, and semi-finished products in warehouses and factories in Foshan and Huanggang. In addition, one fugitive suspect was successfully captured in February 2025. Currently, this case is still in the trial process.

Despite these counterfeit products bearing the same logo as "Mousse," their manufacturing costs, craftsmanship, and product quality are vastly different from the genuine products. Some unscrupulous merchants even deceive consumers with low prices and false advertising, not only seriously harming the legitimate rights and interests of consumers but also seriously disrupting market order and undermining the fair competition environment.

Determination to Safeguard Rights and Cooperation Mechanism
As the "gatekeeper" of Mousse's intellectual property protection, we always emphasize:
✓ Determination to Safeguard Rights: We adopt a "zero tolerance" attitude towards infringement! In 2024 alone, Mousse successfully removed over 50,000 infringing links from online platforms, with compensation for infringement by individual e-commerce stores reaching up to 1.5 million yuan;
✓ Cooperation Mechanism: Establish long-term cooperation with law enforcement departments in multiple provinces and cities nationwide; join Alibaba's Anti-Counterfeiting Alliance (AACA) and JD.com's Rights Protection Alliance to provide rights protection solutions from the platform side.

Consumer Tips
1. Choose legitimate channels: Tmall/JD flagship stores, authorized offline stores (can be checked on the official website and official WeChat account).
2. Beware of low-price traps: Genuine mattresses have transparent pricing, prices far below market prices = counterfeit goods!
3. Build a fake-free ecosystem together: If you find suspected counterfeit products, you can contact us immediately. Every report you make helps protect your family's sleep safety!

Protecting intellectual property is protecting innovative vitality. The legal department of Mousse Group will continue to cooperate with regulatory authorities to crack down severely on infringement and also call on consumers to jointly strengthen brand protection defenses.

1. E-commerce platform handling: In the first quarter of 2025, over 26,000 infringing product links have been successfully removed.

title_en: Top 100 chain stores have a new layout: scale exceeds 2 trillion, specialty stores are eye-catching.
body_en:
On June 18, the China Chain Store Association (CCFA) released the "2024 China Top 100 Chain Stores".

According to CCFA data, the overall sales of the top 100 chain enterprises in China in 2024 reached 2.13 trillion yuan, with a total of 257,200 stores, representing a growth of 4.9% and 13.5% respectively compared to 2023.

Companies such as Walmart (China), Juran Smart Home New Retail, Suning.com, Gaoxin Retail (Runfeng), Hema (China), Yonghui Superstores, Wumart Technology, Wangfujing, and Mei Yi Jia have maintained their leading positions. Walmart (China) topped the list with sales of 158.845 billion yuan.

In terms of changes in the list, five new companies including Wanchen Biology, Liangpinpuzi, West Asia and America, Juewei Food, and Guizhou Heli have entered the list. Hunan Mingming Busy made it to the top ten for the first time with sales exceeding 55 billion yuan. In terms of scale, the number of companies with sales exceeding 30 billion yuan increased from 21 in 2023 to 24 in 2024.

Comparing the lists from 2022 and 2023, companies like Harbin Central Red, Xingsheng Community, and Renrenle continued to decline in rankings and exited the top 100 in 2024. Renrenle announced the termination of its stock listing on June 5, 2025, due to consecutive losses.

In the 2024 Top 100 chain enterprises, there are 46 comprehensive retail stores, 23 supermarkets, 13 convenience stores, and 18 specialty stores.

From the list data, comprehensive retail enterprises face greater growth pressure. Only 19 companies saw year-on-year sales growth, with only 9 achieving growth in both sales and number of stores, while the rest performed poorly. Some former retail giants are being marginalized by e-commerce and new formats due to limited "positive expansion".

For example, in 2024, Suning.com and CR Vanguard saw a 14.1% and 23.1% year-on-year decrease in sales respectively, with a 7.0% and 18.3% decrease in the number of stores. Other leading comprehensive retail enterprises, such as Tianhong Technology and Yinzuo Group, are also facing varying degrees of contraction and adjustment under profit shrinkage.

In fact, the development of comprehensive retail enterprises has been hindered not only in 2024. The "2023 China Top 100 Chain Stores" showed that comprehensive retail enterprises were already facing sales difficulties. In 2023, Suning.com saw a 15.5% year-on-year decrease in sales, CR Vanguard saw a 9.7% decrease, and the number of stores decreased by 13.9%.

Comprehensive retail is characterized by its "large" format. When facing the rapidly changing consumer market, the lack of flexibility and difficulty in adapting the model to changes can lead to stagnation in development. With rising fixed costs such as labor and rent, the penetration rate of online sales is gradually increasing, leading to the closure of inefficient stores and the contraction of non-core areas for many comprehensive retail enterprises.

Previously, Peng Jianzhen, the president of the China Chain Store Association, pointed out that in the current economic cycle, comprehensive retail enterprises that are "not having a good time" need to pay attention to the decrease in customer traffic. This means that the absolute decrease in the number of customers represents whether the company's positioning, products, and services meet the needs of the target customers, and maintaining customer traffic is more important than maintaining the average customer spending.

It is worth noting that the data from the "2024 China Top 100 Chain Stores" list shows that supermarket enterprises are gradually improving.

Among the 23 supermarkets on the list, 12 saw a year-on-year increase in sales, with 6 companies including Hema, Jiajia Yue, and Century Lianhua achieving growth in both sales and number of stores.

Hema (China) saw sales exceed 75 billion yuan, a 27.1% year-on-year increase, with the number of stores exceeding 420, a 16.7% increase. Pandonglai saw sales exceed 16.9 billion yuan, a 58.5% year-on-year increase, showing outstanding performance.

The stable and positive sales trend is the result of breakthroughs in operations.

Some new chain supermarket enterprises (such as Hema, Pandonglai, etc.) focus on high-frequency categories (such as fresh food, cooked food, pre-made dishes, etc.), strengthen their local life service functions, and have gained strong user stickiness and high repurchase rates, improving their single-store operating capabilities. Pandonglai, with 13 stores, achieved revenue of 10.7 billion yuan and a net profit of 140 million yuan. Since its rise to fame, it has been a benchmark for many supermarkets to learn from.

Chen Liping, a professor at the Capital University of Economics and Business Consumer Big Data Research Institute, previously told 21st Century Economic Report that at present, value-creating supermarkets like Pandonglai are showing positive development trends and are expected to become mainstream in the future. This is mainly due to their direct procurement and self-owned supply chain system, which allows for a wide range of products in the supermarket at affordable prices, with excellent freshness. They also focus on on-site processing, providing excellent service. In the market environment of the rise of experiential economy, this innovative and differentiated business model meets the diverse needs of consumers.

In addition, convenience store enterprises overall continue to show a trend of growth in both sales and number of stores. However, comparing the lists from 2023 and 2024, well-known convenience store companies such as Mei Yi Jia, 7-Eleven, and Lawson saw a significant slowdown in sales growth, dropping from 20.1%, 30.0%, and 23.7% in 2023 to 3.1%, 19.7%, and 4.7% in 2024.

Convenience stores mainly provide temporary services that can be obtained immediately. Initially, both foreign convenience stores like 7-Eleven, Lawson, and local convenience stores like Bianlifeng and Mei Yi Jia, expanded their store networks and aggressively expanded into lower-tier markets through measures such as "brutal growth". However, due to saturation in expansion, rising operating costs, the impact of new retail formats, and consumer differentiation, convenience store enterprises have gradually entered a bottleneck period in their development.

Some of the new stores added to the Top 100 enterprises in 2024 come from convenience store companies. Analysts believe that in order for these companies to maintain stable growth and not fall behind, they need to focus on operational strategies, find new growth points, and adapt to market changes.

From the list data, specialty store enterprises in 2024 have the best operating conditions, becoming the new driving force of retail.

Whether it is in the pharmaceutical, beauty, maternity and baby, eyewear, or pet industries, overall sales and the number of stores have seen double-digit growth, highlighting the strong demand and high user stickiness in segmented markets.

Specifically, in the pharmaceutical chain field, Dashenlin has expanded its stores rapidly, with a 17.6% year-on-year increase compared to the previous year. Haiziwang has also performed well in the maternity and baby products sector, with sales exceeding 16.9 billion yuan in 2024.

In the vibrant snack industry, emerging discount stores have risen, not only impacting the market share of traditional supermarkets, but also having a profound impact on the business model of the entire industry. Hunan Mingming Busy Commercial Chain Co., Ltd. (including Snacks Busy and Zhao Yiming Snacks) made a breakthrough into the top 10 of the 2024 China Chain Store list, with a 132.7% year-on-year increase in sales and a 105.6% increase in the number of stores.

However, Zhu Danpeng, a Chinese food industry analyst, pointed out to the 21st Century Economic Report that the entire snack retail industry in China is facing significant problems in terms of store expansion and survival from the industry side. Secondly, the competition in the entire product pricing is very fierce, and companies also need to pay attention to the hidden dangers of vicious competition in the industry.

The "2024 China Top 100 Chain Stores" not only reflects the performance of various enterprises but also reflects the restructuring trend of the overall structure of the retail industry in China.

In the future, the competition among chain enterprises will increasingly rely on user operation capabilities, service experience, product accuracy, and technological support. At the intersection of consumption upgrading and rational return, those who can understand users, innovate continuously, will be able to occupy new industry highlands and maintain growth momentum. With the continuous development of the retail market, competition is becoming increasingly fierce. Specialty store chain retailers need to continuously improve their competitiveness to cope with the competition pressure from other retail formats and e-commerce platforms.
(Intern Xue Liying also contributed to this article)

The security of the supply chain of pharmaceutical excipients used in high-end formulations in China urgently requires the strengthening of technical innovation and industrial support for domestically produced pharmaceutical excipients. At the same time, ensuring the quality of clinical medication, reducing drug costs, and alleviating the pressure on medical insurance to a large extent also depend on the improvement of the quality of domestically produced pharmaceutical excipients.
