title_en: What kind of company? Can make "stingy" young people dig out a market worth billions.
body_en:
Dialogue with decision-makers "We are a group of heroes from Liangshan, doing practical things directly and decisively." This is how Zhang Ning, co-founder of HotMaxx, defined his team in an interview with the China Toy Association's All-Media Center, and it is the key to their ability to stand out in the fiercely competitive retail market. When inventory backlog became a "major problem" for brand owners, and traditional retailers were deeply mired in the quagmire of traffic competition, HotMaxx, in just 5 years, transformed from a one-day sales surge to 80,000 yuan in "accidental clearance sales," into a chain retail enterprise with nearly a thousand stores nationwide. What kind of business considerations are behind this? Is it the huge treasure hidden in the discount store industry, or did he keenly capture a new opportunity to solve the inventory problem for companies?

Zhang Ning's insightful views are as follows:
1. Consumers' enthusiasm for surprise discounts far exceeds their sensitivity to traditional low prices.
2. The generation of tail goods stems from brand innovation attempts, and HotMaxx's business model is essentially helping brands reduce the cost of innovation failures.
3. "Emotional satisfaction" is becoming the core variable driving consumer decision-making and continues to permeate all categories of the retail industry.
4. Enter the market with a symbiotic mindset to achieve a pain point closure at both ends of supply and demand.
5. New retail is actually a way to use technology to solve problems that traditional retail cannot solve.

The following is the full text of the dialogue (with deletions and modifications):
01. Entrepreneurial Origins
From the fire of clearance sales to the awakening of business cognition
China Toy Association: How did HotMaxx's business model initially emerge?
Zhang Ning: The market fluctuations at the beginning of 2020 caused a large backlog of inventory for brand owners and retailers. HotMaxx's founder, Gu Xiaojian, and the team keenly seized this business opportunity and opened the first discount store for near-expiry food products. What we didn't expect was that the sales on that day exceeded 80,000 yuan! Compared to the previous daily sales of 1,500 yuan, it was a world of difference. This unexpected event made us realize that consumers' enthusiasm for surprise discounts far exceeds their sensitivity to traditional low prices. Therefore, we discovered the market demand and created a unique shopping experience.
China Toy Association: What is the core competitiveness of HotMaxx's tail goods sales model compared to traditional retail models?
Zhang Ning: In the trend of the retail industry moving towards high quality and high cost-effectiveness, HotMaxx stands out with its tail goods sales model. Its core advantage lies in relying on brand goods to guarantee quality, achieving "high quality + low price" to the utmost extent at affordable prices for consumers. HotMaxx realized that the generation of tail goods stems from brand innovation attempts, and its business model essentially helps brands reduce the cost of innovation failures, providing consumers with high cost-effective goods and solving the problem of handling tail goods for brand owners, paving a unique and socially valuable path in the retail market.
02. From "Buying Things" to "Buying Emotions"
The consumption logic behind the hot sales of toys
China Toy Association: From the fire of clearance sales to systematic operation, what is the biggest cognitive shift?
Zhang Ning: I initially thought it was price-driven, but upon review, I found that when the shelves were cleared and the products were displayed in piles, consumers experienced a "treasure hunt shopping experience." We once conducted a test: the sales of the same trendy blind box in the limited-time discount area were three times that of the regular shelf. This made us realize that we must transform the randomness of surprises into replicable retail logic.
China Toy Association: Besides blind box categories, what other categories does HotMaxx sell? What are the main toy brands you cooperate with?
Zhang Ning: Most of the toys sold by HotMaxx are authorized contract near-expiry IP products. The main sales are Disney, Marvel, Harry Potter, Crayon Shin-chan, and other IP authorized products; in educational toys, the main sales are LEGO mechanical sets, TOPTOY Chinese building blocks, Bruco Ultraman armor, and other building puzzles.
China Toy Association: What considerations are there when choosing to cooperate with trendy toy brands? What principles do you follow?
Zhang Ning: HotMaxx mainly considers the market popularity, brand value, product competitiveness, supply chain stability, cooperation mode, brand fit, and consumer demand of trendy toy brands from multiple aspects.
China Toy Association: What is the expected proportion of trendy toys and baby products in the product structure?
Zhang Ning: We hold a strategic positive attitude towards the trendy toy and baby product categories, planning to increase the sales proportion of these two major categories to double digits in the future. To ensure supply chain stability and product safety control, this category will strictly select cooperation partners and only establish deep cooperation relationships with industry-leading big brands.
China Toy Association: How do you view the development trend of the toy industry, and what advice would you like to give to toy companies?
Zhang Ning: I believe that the current market's emphasis on the value of "emotional consumption" has become an industry consensus. The hot sales of toy categories reflect consumers' deep pursuit of emotional value in products. This demand is evolving into a "new rigid demand" for young groups. Against the backdrop of consumption upgrading, users' demand for products has surpassed the functional level and shifted towards long-term value exploration in dimensions such as emotional experience, social attributes, and self-expression. With the iteration of Generation Z's consumption concepts, "emotional satisfaction" is becoming the core variable driving consumer decision-making and continues to permeate all categories of the retail industry. This trend is not only reshaping the relationship between people and goods but also requiring retail companies to shift from being mere product providers to creators of emotional value.
Toy companies should keenly capture consumers' emotional needs, integrate emotions into design; increase innovation efforts, keep up with trends in intelligence and environmental protection, provide personalized services; actively seek cross-border cooperation, leverage well-known IP to enhance influence; optimize marketing, use social media to expand dissemination, and strengthen supply chain management to ensure product supply and establish a foothold in the market.
03. Technological breakthrough of the soft discount model
Reshaping the operational logic of tail goods retail
China Toy Association: Since its establishment, HotMaxx has developed rapidly and has established deep cooperation with over 1000 well-known brands at home and abroad. What unique strategies and advantages does HotMaxx have in expanding cooperation with brands that can attract many brands to choose to work with HotMaxx?
Zhang Ning: HotMaxx's core strategy focuses on helping brands reach young users. In response to the current situation of declining brand penetration rates in first-tier cities, it naturally presents goods to non-targeted young consumers through offline scenes. Its unique value lies in the fact that even if consumers are not specifically buying a certain type of product, they can complete their first trial through scene guidance, achieve large-scale exposure and penetration among young consumers in first-tier cities, and become an important channel for brands to connect with young users.
HotMaxx's core competitiveness is reflected in two advantages: first, relying on brand tail goods resources to form extreme cost-effectiveness, coupled with genuine quality assurance, significantly reducing the threshold for consumer decision-making; second, accurately grasping the emotional consumption attributes of toys. Most consumers enter the store with the intention of buying daily goods, but due to the attractive appearance and cost-effectiveness of toys, they are triggered to make impulse purchases, forming a habit of "picking up one item."
China Toy Association: HotMaxx's success has set an example for the discount retail industry. In your opinion, what are the aspects of HotMaxx's business model and operational experience that are worth learning from for other emerging discount store brands and traditional retail companies in transformation?
Zhang Ning: The operational logic of HotMaxx is fundamentally different from the traditional model of achieving "hard discounts" through low prices. The brand's core focus is on the soft discount model and tail goods management, with "solving industry common problems" rather than "competitive confrontation" as the underlying operating philosophy. The industry value of HotMaxx lies not in simply replicating a certain retail paradigm but in entering the market with a symbiotic mindset: by providing brand owners with tail goods digestion solutions, alleviating their inventory pressure and innovation trial and error costs, while creating a scene value of "high cost-effective shopping" for consumers, achieving a pain point closure at both ends of supply and demand. This path of "problem-solving-oriented" not only differentiates from the price game logic of hard discounts but also breaks out of the framework of traditional retail's traffic competition.
At the operational level, HotMaxx adopts a full buyout supply chain model, abandoning the traditional backend profit-sharing mechanism of channels, with all pricing decisions based solely on consumer real needs. I believe that this "decentralized" and highly transparent cost structure is more in line with the pursuit of "real cost-effectiveness" by the new generation of consumers and will become one of the mainstream trends in the future retail industry.
China Toy Association: The demand for discount retail by consumers is increasing, and more and more discount store brands are emerging in the market. How does HotMaxx maintain its leading position in the fierce competition and create differentiation competitive advantages?
Zhang Ning: The core lies in deepening the symbiotic relationship with brands, driving supply chain innovation and tail goods management efficiency through service. The long-term competitiveness of brands is rooted in the deep service capabilities to upstream suppliers. Only by continuously solving the tail goods handling needs in the innovation process for brands, providing efficient inventory digestion channels, can a stable high-quality product portfolio be built. This "exchange service for source" model has formed a positive cycle: serving the brand end, helping brands reduce the cost of innovation trial and error and release production redundancy through professional tail goods management capabilities, while reaching young consumer groups in first-tier cities, increasing the brand's penetration rate among non-core customer groups; feeding back to the consumer end, relying on genuine tail goods supplied by brands, attracting consumers with extreme cost-effectiveness and random "shopping" experiences, forming a consumer mindset of "having good goods without lacking traffic."
04. Future Retail: Integration of Technological Empowerment and Offline Experience
China Toy Association: How do you view the concept of "new retail"?
Zhang Ning: The essence of new retail is how to more effectively meet consumer needs. I recently heard an expert's opinion that there is no such thing as new retail, and I tend to agree. New retail is actually a way to use technology to solve problems that traditional retail cannot solve. For example, AI has significant advantages in dealing with price fluctuations, changes in inventory levels, and uncertainties in sales speed, which are problems that the human brain finds difficult to predict accurately.
Our company's significant investment in algorithms is to build such a competitive barrier. Our algorithms ensure the healthy circulation of goods, which is the key to our success. If the algorithm makes a mistake in pricing or allocation, leading to a backlog of goods in areas with poor sales, these goods will become a burden, hindering the circulation of new goods and ultimately affecting store operations. Therefore, our algorithms not only need to solve uncertainty problems but also ensure the efficient operation of our supply chain and sales channels.
China Toy Association: What do you think the future development trend of the retail industry will be?
Zhang Ning: Online channels will still occupy a core position, especially in purposeful goods such as standardized daily necessities, 3C products, etc., where efficient access and transaction efficiency are difficult to shake. However, at the same time, offline retail is showing signs of structural recovery, with some categories such as experiential consumption, instant goods, and emotional scene goods re-attracting market attention through innovative models. Traditional offline retail was previously passive due to lagging supply chain response and insufficient consumer insights, under the impact of e-commerce. But the market has now seen a batch of differentiated recovery typical cases: from Pinduoduo, Sam's "extreme cost-effectiveness + membership experience," to Miniso, Hema's "scene retail + supply chain innovation," to Pop Mart's "trendy toy IP + offline immersive experience," all demonstrating the iterative potential of offline retail. The future of viable offline models needs to focus on experiential value, emotional connection, and immediate satisfaction.
Conclusion: HotMaxx's business model and operational experience provide valuable reference for other emerging discount store brands and traditional retail companies in transformation. But more importantly, it shows us how companies can find their own development path through continuous innovation and optimization in a rapidly changing market environment. In this process, the application of technology, optimization of the supply chain, improvement of consumer experience, and deep cooperation with brand owners will all be key factors for success. At the end, let's consider: can HotMaxx's success be replicated in such a rapidly developing market? How will they continue to maintain their unique advantages in future competition? I believe the future will provide answers, and HotMaxx will continue to explore their endless possibilities. Written/Edited by: Han Weiling

title_en: Small factory, big order, AI has become the new "matchmaker"
body_en:
On the old machines with peeling paint, production plans written on whiteboards, and tea rooms with a strong smell of engine oil mixed in... Among the 6 million manufacturing companies in China, there is a type of "small workshop" that has few employees, small scale, average environment, lacks publicity, but is large in number and wide in coverage, like capillaries supporting many nodes of the supply chain.

When buyers are worried about not finding quality suppliers, when small and medium-sized manufacturers are struggling with order acceptance and lack of customers, a transformation driven by AI technology is breaking down barriers of geography, language, and information, awakening the long-buried manufacturing capabilities.

Digital "matchmakers" help supply and demand shake hands
An injection molding factory from Wuhu, Anhui, used to struggle with a lack of orders in the early days of its business. By chance, they came into contact with the digital platform focusing on industrial components - Haizhi Online, and since then became its loyal "fans". With the help of this platform, the factory successfully established stable cooperation with more than ten customers, and its annual output value grew from zero to 6 million yuan.

From the perspective of the entire component market, over 80% of components are non-standardized. Producing a car requires tens of thousands of parts, producing a mobile phone also requires thousands of parts, the vast majority of which are non-standard components. When product designs change, components need to be customized again, and small and medium-sized factories generally face the pain points of order acceptance difficulties and inconsistent income.

"The characteristic of the non-standard component market is that the buyer defines the product, with many technical details, but the buyer cannot access the production process. Once there are errors or misunderstandings in the information transmission process, it may lead to many risks," said Liu Haitao, Vice President of Haizhi Online.

Therefore, communication between buyers and sellers is crucial. At Haizhi Online, journalists saw an "image search" AI tool, which, by uploading drawings into the system, can turn "finding a needle in a haystack" into precise navigation, quickly matching several drawings with high similarity and factories that have produced similar parts. "The operation is very similar to Taobao's image recognition," Liu Haitao said.

An intelligent quotation system that can price in one minute and place an order in three minutes, an online collaboration system that automatically annotates processing key points on drawings... At Haizhi Online, there are many such intelligent AI tools. This is made possible by the support of large-scale model technology, which, with the help of millions of historical drawings, has created the first truly deployed large-scale model in the industrial field, breaking through the recognition difficulties of 2D drawings and saving over 60% of time.

To further improve transaction efficiency, based on on-site inspection experience, Haizhi Online has also built two databases covering over 700,000 factories and more than 200,000 buyers. Different types of factories and buyers from around the world are analyzed and standardized into hundreds of tags, including production equipment, process level, production capacity, and other dimensions, enabling quick matching in seconds. "Person-to-person" matching has also become possible, as the platform can recommend more suitable partners based on the actual characteristics of the account users, such as recommending buyers from the same hometown to factory owners who are not fluent in Mandarin.

In addition to independently developing AI tools, Haizhi Online actively collaborates with technology companies in the industrial artificial intelligence field, with the platform providing data and transaction scenarios, while other companies provide algorithm development capabilities, jointly promoting the deep development of large-scale model technology. Recently, Haizhi Online announced a cooperation agreement with Xuelangyun, aiming to improve the speed and quality of extracting key elements such as shapes and dimensions from drawings, creating more accurate large-scale models for component processing parameters.

AI "scouts" driving "cross-border breakthroughs"
"Look at the wheels of this organ transplant box, its original production factory was a toy car wheel factory on the verge of bankruptcy. After being found through image search, it went through two leaps. The first time, it became the knob of the largest industrial camera manufacturer in the United States; the second time, it became the wheel of the organ transplant box," shared She Ying, founder of Haizhi Online, with a reporter from China Electronics News.

There are countless examples of such "counterattack" cases of cross-border production. A part originally used for cosmetic tools transformed into an important component for a medical company's blood pump; a factory that used to make inner cups for thermos flasks now supplies water storage equipment inner cups for the aviation industry; a factory engaged in gas stoves and lighters production, whose biggest dream was to produce lighters for large companies, can now produce diesel engines...

In the past, many factories possessed unique skills but were unaware of them, used to working hard in familiar territories without realizing that their capabilities were far beyond that. Buyers also had no way of knowing that in these seemingly ordinary or even somewhat rudimentary workshops, parts that passed strict inspections could be produced.

The significance of digital platforms like Haizhi Online is to provide a better development path for the transformation and upgrading of small factories. Factories no longer need to be evaluated based on which industry they belong to, or passively wait for introductions from acquaintances, but can define their capabilities based on bottom-level processes, allowing factories to be discovered accurately based on their own strengths.

Through various AI tools, combined with two large databases, complex drawings can be accurately interpreted, further breaking down the processing requirements, equipment parameters, material requirements, and other key processing points, and automatically matching factories with the same manufacturing processes in the system. Small and medium-sized factories that were previously on the periphery of the supply chain have gained more exposure opportunities through the platform, enabling them to enter high-value-added industries and move closer to core industries.

Some factories, with the assistance of AI technology, have transformed suppliers into buyers, pushing more factories to integrate into the industrial chain. A metal manufacturing company in Guangzhou, through the Haizhi Online platform, integrated resources from surrounding factories, shared orders with other factories, formed a collaborative manufacturing network, significantly improving order acceptance capabilities, with 70% of its output value coming from collaborative manufacturing.

Intelligent engines driving enterprises overseas
A small factory owner with equipment, processes, and experience, but who happens to not understand English, may one day receive an order from overseas. Due to not understanding the client's language and not being able to read English drawing annotations, he may need to spend a lot of time and effort, and may even miss the opportunity for cooperation.

Language may be a common problem encountered by many small and medium-sized factories when going overseas. With the help of digital platforms, factories that were originally clueless about international business may now have the confidence to engage with the world. Currently, Haizhi Online's trading platform has AI intelligent translation capabilities in 27 languages, and the company is also focusing on developing online audio and video translation services, suitable for complex scenarios such as technical exchanges and product demonstrations between multinational factories. This means that even if a factory owner in China does not speak Spanish, they can still conduct business negotiations and production discussions with Latin American customers through the platform, smoothly entering the international business arena.

Not only does this help Chinese companies "go global," but it also achieves "bringing in." Overseas buyers who were originally skeptical of Chinese manufacturing, through the platform, can intuitively feel the hard strength of Chinese factories in terms of price, efficiency, and service, prompting them to move from observation to placing orders, eventually becoming regular customers, driving more international orders to China. "As long as you take overseas buyers to see Chinese factories, the success rate of placing orders is 100%," She Ying said.

With the support of the Haizhi Online platform, many small and medium-sized factories have successfully crossed mountains and seas to reach the global market. A factory in Qingdao with an annual output value of 2 million yuan, by connecting with overseas customers through the platform, can now secure over 1 million yuan in foreign trade orders every year; a factory in Suzhou, after cooperating with the platform, quickly opened up the international market, reaching deals with 40 large and small buyers globally, doubling the value of overseas orders.

Technology continues to evolve, but the mission of solving problems remains unchanged. In the face of the increasingly close integration of manufacturing with artificial intelligence technology, Liu Haitao believes that the biggest problem with applying artificial intelligence technology to industry is that those who master the technology may not necessarily understand industry, manufacturing, or the market. "Developing based on imagined needs without actual industrial work experience is like working in isolation," he said. "We need to think about in what scenarios we can truly unleash the real value of artificial intelligence."

The goal of AI technology development is not to show off, but to respond to the pain points and needs of the industry in real business scenarios. "The goal is not to use artificial intelligence, but the business results obtained after using it are the focus," Liu Haitao said. "First, in some highly digitized scenarios, let industrial enterprises start using artificial intelligence, then promote the resolution of detailed issues in some detailed scenarios, gradually accumulating into a fully digitized end-to-end process."

As of July 2024, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has promoted the establishment of more than 1,780 public service institutions for small and medium-sized enterprises covering national, provincial, municipal, and county levels, with a coverage rate of administrative regions at the city level and above reaching 84%. With the support of national policies and the blessing of new-generation information technologies such as artificial intelligence, more fair, efficient, and intelligent digital platforms are continuously integrating into industries, significantly accelerating the pace of digital transformation for small and medium-sized enterprises, effectively assisting in the development of specialized, refined, and new industries.

title_en: Stock prices have surged by 200% in the past two months, while the main business of Yongan Pharmaceutical continues to "bleed".
body_en:
In just two and a half months, the stock price of Yongan Pharmaceutical (002365.SZ) soared from 9 yuan to 28 yuan, with a cumulative increase of over 200%.
As of the close on June 19, Yongan Pharmaceutical's price-earnings ratio (TTM) was as high as 261 times, far exceeding the average price-earnings ratio of 32 times for the pharmaceutical manufacturing industry. However, the taurine price that supported this market surge has fallen from a peak of 25,000 yuan/ton in May to 16,000 yuan/ton.
Currently, Yongan Pharmaceutical still faces the dual challenges of "bleeding" in its main business and whether its new business can continue. From 2022 to 2024, the company's revenue has fallen by 42.6%, with a loss of over 4 million yuan in the first quarter of this year.
Stock price surged 200% in 2 months
Since the market started in April, Yongan Pharmaceutical has experienced three waves of increases, with the stock price rising from less than 9 yuan to a high of 29.19 yuan, with a cumulative increase of up to 224%. After experiencing a new round of increases, Yongan Pharmaceutical hit the limit down on June 19, closing at 25.44 yuan per share.
The core logic of the market speculation on Yongan Pharmaceutical revolves around the "supply-demand gap" of taurine. In April 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) required taurine to be added to infant formula and pet food. As China accounts for 90% of global production capacity and faces domestic environmental production restrictions and overseas competitors shutting down, the supply shortage has worsened.
According to Yongan Pharmaceutical's 2024 annual report, the company's current taurine production capacity is 58,000 tons per year, accounting for around 50% of the market share, with most of the company's taurine products exported worldwide, with overseas revenue accounting for 60.23% in 2024.
Market analysts said that there are no companies in the U.S. that produce taurine on a large scale domestically, relying entirely on imports, with China accounting for over 90% of the supply, directly driving export demand. There are even market rumors that taurine prices have surged several times.
Affected by the above news, Yongan Pharmaceutical started an upward trend in April, recording its first limit up on April 8, followed by a brief pullback, and then recording 6 consecutive limit up days from the 21st to the 29th, with the stock price quickly rising to 14.34 yuan.
On the evening of April 29, Yongan Pharmaceutical issued a reply to the abnormal stock price movement report, stating that recent rumors circulating on the internet about "taurine prices surging several times" were found to be untrue by the relevant departments of the company, and the next day Yongan Pharmaceutical hit the limit down.
On May 5, Yongan Pharmaceutical announced that its actual controller and chairman, Chen Yong, was under investigation and placed under investigation. Yongan Pharmaceutical hit the limit down again on the 6th.
However, even with the actual controller being investigated and placed under investigation, Yongan Pharmaceutical only briefly adjusted for less than 7 trading days, with the stock price falling to around 10 yuan, and then hitting the limit up again on May 14 to start the next round of increases, recording 7 consecutive limit up days in 11 days, with the stock price reaching 24.63 yuan, a 146.3% increase.
The reason for this round of speculation is that, in addition to its main taurine business, Yongan Pharmaceutical's attempts in the health product sector have also attracted market attention. The solid functional beverage "Yijianeng" launched by its subsidiary is selling well on platforms such as Taobao, Douyin, Pinduoduo, JD.com, and Kuaishou, with a total of 25,000 orders from May 12 to 18, with a daily average increase of 60%. However, according to Yongan Pharmaceutical's 2024 annual report, its health food revenue was 103 million yuan, accounting for only 12.37% of its total revenue.
After a brief pullback from May 29 to June 5, Yongan Pharmaceutical rose again, hitting a new high of 29.19 yuan per share on June 17, and finally hitting the limit down on the 19th.
Behind the sharp rise in Yongan Pharmaceutical's stock price is speculative capital taking over, with data from the Dragon and Tiger List showing that individual investors have been on the list 25 times in the past two months. "Lhasa Group", Yongxing Securities Ningbo and Yuanlu, Dongguan Securities Nanjing Branch, and Lianchu Securities Shanghai Songlin Road and other speculative seats have frequently appeared to boost the stock price.
According to the details of the top ten shareholders disclosed in the 2024 annual report, well-known "bullish" Wang Chenghua also participated, with a new holding of 4.030467 million shares, accounting for 1.37%, becoming the fourth largest shareholder.
Main business continues to "bleed"
Behind the over 200% surge in stock price, Yongan Pharmaceutical is experiencing a dual situation of "ice and fire" in its operational dilemma. With continuously deteriorating financial data, shrinking core business, and management turmoil, the fundamental crisis of this taurine leading enterprise contrasts with the frenzy in the secondary market.
Disclosure data shows that from 2022 to 2024, Yongan Pharmaceutical's revenue plummeted from 1.462 billion yuan to 839 million yuan, a cumulative decline of 42.6% over three years. In 2023, a 33.48% drop in revenue directly plunged Yongan Pharmaceutical into a deep loss. Although in 2024, it achieved a net profit of 61.766 million yuan through cost control.
The return to profit was not sustained. In 2025, the company's performance deteriorated further, with first-quarter revenue falling to 171 million yuan, a 12.96% year-on-year decline; a net loss of 4.3672 million yuan, a staggering 115.23% year-on-year decline.
As the core business accounting for 75.67% of total revenue, the company's taurine segment had revenue of 635 million yuan in 2024, a 4.14% year-on-year decline. In a situation of increasing volume and falling prices, although sales volume increased by 16.32%, the average selling price fell, directly leading to a drop in gross profit margin from 29.4% in the previous year to 24.02%.
In May of this year, there were market rumors of a surge in taurine prices. According to data from commodity pricing websites, taurine prices briefly rose to a peak of 25,000 yuan/ton in the first five days of May, but have since fallen back to the normal price range of 16,000 yuan/ton. The uncertainty remains as to whether taurine prices will continue to rise in the future.
To reverse the downturn in the taurine business, Yongan Pharmaceutical is expanding its presence in the C-end of the health sector through its subsidiary Yongan Kangjian's Yijianeng product. Yongan Pharmaceutical stated on an interactive platform that its subsidiary Yongan Kangjian's Yijianeng self-owned brand product was officially launched and operational by the end of 2024. In terms of channel expansion, in addition to online sales, Yongan Kangjian's Yijianeng products have begun to be stocked in some chain pharmacies in certain regions and promoted at the end, continuously strengthening the brand's consumer end layout.
However, the proportion of the above business is still relatively small. In 2024, Yongan Pharmaceutical's health food revenue was 103 million yuan, accounting for only 12.37% of its overall revenue.
The performance crisis has not been alleviated, and management turmoil has followed. On May 5, 2025, the company announced that its actual controller and chairman, Chen Yong, was under investigation and placed under investigation by the Supervisory Committee of Hefeng County, Hubei Province. Although the board of directors promptly appointed his son, Chen Zidi, to act on his behalf the next day, the market responded with a limit down.
In the frenzy of stock price speculation spurred by rumors of a surge in taurine prices, Yongan Pharmaceutical's fundamental crisis has come to the surface. When the tide recedes, this company, deeply mired in performance quagmire and management turnover, will need further observation to see if it can rescue itself.

title_en: The "triple gate" of China's AI glasses super prosperity.
body_en:
"Lucky, pay XX yuan," said the user wearing Rokid Glasses, and Rokid Glasses recognized the Alipay payment code. Then, the user said "confirm payment," and the payment could be completed without the need for any operation on the phone.
On June 17th, Rokid announced that smart glasses can now be used for payments, and the scene described above became a part of daily life. This event expanded the use cases of smart glasses, indicating a shift from just "seeing" to "using," further expanding the range of applications.
Since the beginning of this year, smart glasses have become one of the hottest consumer electronics products. In May alone, there were over 10 new smart glasses models launched. Manufacturers such as Rebird, Xreal, and Liweike all released their new products.
Apart from terminal manufacturers, upstream companies are also gearing up. On June 11th, Qualcomm even released the Snapdragon AR1+Gen 1 for smart glasses, which includes a built-in neural processing unit capable of running small language models on the edge. With the entry of companies like Qualcomm and Google, the standardization of systems and chips has been further promoted, pushing smart glasses towards a more lightweight transformation.
With so many products available, there is bound to be one that meets the needs of consumers. The audience for smart glasses is gradually expanding from tech enthusiasts to a more mainstream user base, and the smart glasses market is rapidly growing.
According to IDC, the global smart glasses market shipped 1.487 million units in the first quarter alone, an 82.3% year-on-year increase. In China, the shipment of smart glasses reached 494,000 units, a 116.1% year-on-year increase.
Under the thriving market, some trends different from consumer electronics are quietly emerging. If smart glasses are to be used in more scenarios and reach a wider consumer base, lightweight and aesthetics are key, even more important than intelligence. Secondly, smart glasses can meet the needs of people with myopia, making offline traditional glasses sales channels a significant growth point for the industry.
Currently, the global smart glasses market is still dominated by Meta, with a focus on the US market and a growing presence in Western Europe. The domestic smart glasses market is more like a battle among various players, aptly described as the "Battle of a Hundred Glasses."
Data shows that in the first quarter of China, the market for audio and audio recording glasses shipped 359,000 units, a 197.4% year-on-year increase. Among them, audio glasses products are the main focus, with major players including Xiaomi, Huawei, and Jiehuan. The launch of Rebird's new product V3 in the first quarter significantly boosted the growth of the audio recording glasses market.
"Domestic manufacturers' products are mostly benchmarked against Ray-Ban Meta," said a smart glasses manufacturer's design director to reporters.
"Compared to Meta, there are no obvious technological barriers in the supply chain in China. It's more about what kind of play the manufacturers can make on the glasses, fully utilizing the camera function for AI interaction and practical value. Whether Meta's play and ignition path can be replicated in China remains to be seen in the market," said IDC China's research director Pan Xuefei in an interview with 21st Century Business Herald.
One obvious change is that in the past two quarters, the focus of the Chinese AR/VR market has gradually shifted towards the AR (transparent or semi-transparent binocular display, supporting 3D object manipulation) & ER (capable of displaying 3D digital images and the external world simultaneously) market. In the first quarter, the AR&ER market shipped 86,000 units, accounting for 63.8% of the market share, with a year-on-year growth of 64.0%. Xreal, Rebird, and Xingji Meizu have jointly driven market growth.
As the market for viewing glasses becomes saturated and growth slows down, lightweight glasses are providing new consumer applications such as light sports and health, light business travel, etc., giving the AR/ER market new opportunities.
Public information shows that the Rokid Glasses, weighing only 49g, has already received orders for over 250,000 units worldwide and will begin delivery at the end of June.
In response to this phenomenon, IDC China analyst Ye Qingqing analyzed that lightweight glasses for the consumer market have a wider range of applications and lower user thresholds. Compared to traditional glasses/headsets devices with entertainment and audiovisual scenes as the core, the commercialization path is clearer and faster, making it easier for manufacturers to enter the market, thus significantly leading the growth ahead of other forms of products.
It is worth noting that the growth of the lightweight glasses market is also benefiting from the rapid development of large models. Models such as Tongyi Qianwen, DeepSeek, and Wenxin large models are the mainstream underlying models for AI glasses products at present.
Leveraging large models not only enhances the semantic understanding and contextual processing capabilities of smart glasses but also improves the multimodal interaction capabilities in speech and vision, making glasses truly AI glasses.
It is expected that from June 2025 to the end of the year, more manufacturers will launch smart glasses in China. With the support of large models, smart glasses will bring more graphic interface expandability and playability to glasses-shaped devices with lower market thresholds.
The development of AI glasses not only requires mature large models but also strong hardware support and battery life.
Among them, there has long been a dilemma known as the "impossible triangle": lightweight, high performance, and long battery life are difficult to achieve simultaneously. How to balance the relationship between the three, different manufacturers have different considerations, which is also one of the challenges in mass production of smart glasses.
Will, the founder of Even Realities, mentioned in a sharing session that smart glasses are generally understood as "smart + glasses," but the key issue is the proportion of intelligence and glasses. Currently, most people wear traditional glasses, and for the next generation of smart products, the question is whether to significantly increase the proportion of intelligence from the beginning or gradually penetrate. This is the starting point that needs to be considered. "In our view, the proportion of intelligence should not exceed 40%," Will pointed out.
The implication here is that glasses should not sacrifice aesthetics and comfort for intelligence.
"From the perspective of traditional glasses manufacturers, functionality, stylish appearance, and comfort are all indispensable. Our goal is to create a pair of smart glasses that are both practical and in line with fashion trends, which can be paired with different sunglasses or optical lenses, complementing the individual's face shape and overall style. The designed glasses should not cause too much burden during wear," the design director mentioned above told reporters.
Using stronger and more integrated chips helps achieve the lightweight and low power consumption of smart glasses, as no consumer wants to be burdened by glasses pressing on their nose.
Taking the core control chip as an example, the Qualcomm Snapdragon AR1 is the first choice for flagship models of many manufacturers, with significant advantages in image signal processing and AI computing power, making it a popular choice among many AI glasses manufacturers for their flagship products.
In addition, some manufacturers have adopted the UNISOC W517 chip, such as the AI camera glasses from FlashExtreme. However, after the launch of these AI glasses, user feedback has not been positive, with complaints about Bluetooth connectivity and power consumption.
"Based on the current conditions, combining software application ecology with hardware functionality trade-offs, manufacturers can temporarily allocate some computing power to smartphones and the cloud for collaboration to reduce the burden on glasses, balancing weight, battery life, product usability, and playability," suggested Pan Xuefei.
Currently, smart glasses are more of a supplement to the mobile phone scene, with hopes for the future that tasks such as calling a taxi or navigation can be completed through glasses without the need to take out a phone.
The growth of the audio and audio recording glasses market in the first quarter of 2025 partly came from the expansion of offline channels. IDC data shows that the retail channel shipment volume of audio and audio recording glasses in China in the first quarter increased by 75.3% year-on-year.
This is because smart glasses are more in line with human senses, providing the most natural way of interaction, and are more similar to traditional glasses in terms of appearance, weight, and price.
In addition, Pan Xuefei analyzed that myopia glasses require the introduction of a lens matching process that demands professionalism. Currently, the smart glasses market is still dominated by technology companies, which is a relatively weak point. This is also why the market is seeing more cooperation with traditional glasses channels.
Previously, reporters from 21st Century Business Herald visited several physical eyewear stores in Shenzhen and found that some chain eyewear brands have set up smart glasses sections, with prices ranging from hundreds to thousands of yuan.
Taking Dr. Glasses (300622.SZ) as an example, the company revealed on its investor interaction platform that it has already partnered with brands such as Xingji Meizu, Rebird Innovation, XREAL, Jiehuan, Liweike, and Rokid in the smart glasses business.
IDC believes that for AR/VR products, smart hardware manufacturers and traditional eyewear manufacturers have more advantages in offline channels. The entry of new players has further intensified the channel competition pressure on technology innovation manufacturers, prompting the entire AR/VR market to shift from focusing on online to a diversified full-channel layout.

title_en: Why is it difficult for express packaging to "lose weight"?
body_en:
Xinhua News Agency "Xinhua Viewpoint" reporter
The corrugated cardboard box is wrapped with difficult-to-tear tape, and the packaging box contains a large number of bubble bags, foam plastics... Many people will encounter this "nested doll" style packaging when receiving express delivery.
Why is it difficult for express packaging to "lose weight"? How to promote the industry to achieve green transformation? "Xinhua Viewpoint" reporter conducted an investigation.
"Nesting doll" packaging, pungent odor, surge in garbage
Mr. Xu from Chengdu, Sichuan Province, purchased a mini CD player online. The size of the product is not large, but the package size is twice the size of the product, filled with bubble bags. "I understand that the merchant wants to protect the product, but these fillers not only take up space but also make it difficult to dispose of." Mr. Xu said.
The investigation found that some merchants will stack films, nets, and other materials in the packaging; some merchants will place a large number of ice packs, moisture-proof pads, and other "functional" packaging materials in the express delivery.
Previously, the Shaanxi Survey Team of the National Bureau of Statistics conducted a survey of 462 consumers in 20 cities and counties in the province, of which more than 64% of consumers believed that there was too much tape winding in express packaging, more than 33% of consumers believed that there were too many fillers in express packaging, and more than 32% of consumers believed that express packaging was too large.
To reduce costs, some merchants choose low-quality tapes, plastics, and cardboard for packaging. In some areas where express delivery is concentrated, even wearing a mask, you can smell a pungent odor.
The indoor air quality standard that will be implemented on February 1, 2023, stipulates that the one-hour average concentration of formaldehyde indoors should not exceed 0.08mg/m3. Reporters randomly tested five express stations in Changchun, Jilin with a formaldehyde concentration detector, and after staying for only a few minutes, the formaldehyde concentration value displayed on the detector quickly exceeded this standard, with some values even seven times higher than the standard.
Excessive packaging also leads to a surge in waste.
At a waste sorting center in Beijing, reporters saw classified garbage placed in rows. The person in charge of the center said that this garbage mainly comes from multiple communities, and about 60 tons of recyclables are sent to the center every day. The proportion of express packaging paper made mainly of yellow cardboard is increasing, and it has now exceeded 60%.
Wang Qi, academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, said that with the continuous increase in the annual business volume of express delivery in China, a large amount of paper and plastic waste is generated every year, and the total amount of express packaging waste in China in 2023 is close to 20 million tons.
Why is it difficult to "lose weight" and "go green"
Why is it difficult for express packaging to "lose weight"?
The person in charge of an express delivery company told reporters that more than 95% of the goods packaging responsible for delivery by the company is handled by platform e-commerce, and many e-commerce platforms either focus on enhancing brand premiums and unboxing experiences or avoid damage to goods during transportation, generally putting effort into packaging, leading to excessive packaging.
Zhang Tao, an e-commerce seller engaged in food processing, told reporters that if the goods are not "properly" packaged, they may be damaged or crushed during transportation, and consumers often complain or give negative reviews when they receive them. "It costs more to resolve these complaints and negative reviews, so it's better to over-package before sending them out," he said.
Some consumers also have requirements for packaging when purchasing goods. "When buying gifts like lipstick, perfume for friends, some buyers will ask to put the gifts in large gift boxes or shopping bags, creating a romantic atmosphere on the one hand, and also allowing the other party to feel the level of care." Li Min, an e-commerce seller engaged in cosmetics sales, admitted.
The newly revised "Interim Regulations on Express Delivery" will be implemented from June 1 this year. The regulations propose to encourage companies operating express delivery services and senders to use environmentally friendly packaging materials that are degradable and reusable.
"Compared with traditional corrugated cardboard or tape packaging, the cost of environmentally friendly material packaging boxes is often twice as high or even higher. The extensive use may weaken the price competitiveness of merchants." A person in charge of an express delivery station admitted.
In addition, e-commerce platforms assess merchants based on sales volume, positive review rate, and express delivery efficiency, without giving much weight to the environmental friendliness of express packaging, so most merchants do not have much motivation to use environmentally friendly materials for express packaging.
In terms of green recycling, the revised "Interim Regulations on Express Delivery" propose to encourage the setting up of packaging material recycling facilities in express business premises, enterprise units, residential communities, and other appropriate places.
Reporters visited 20 express business outlets and express stations in Changchun, most of which have green recycling bins, designed to promote the reuse of more express boxes.
However, reporters found that most of the recycling bins were either idle in the corner or filled with miscellaneous items or garbage, and the number of bins that could truly serve their purpose was limited. In addition, many consumers do not unpack at the site of the express station, and some express boxes that could be recycled are eventually thrown into the trash.
"The recycled cardboard boxes will be properly stored and provided free of charge to sending customers for reuse, but there is not much publicity about this, and many people still do not understand." Express deliveryman Zhao Zijun said.
Achieving green and reduced express delivery requires full-chain management
The governance of excessive express packaging involves multiple links such as production, use, recycling, and disposal, and joint efforts along the entire chain are the key to achieving both symptomatic and fundamental treatment.
Many express delivery companies are taking a series of measures to give express packaging a "makeover."
Cainiao has increased the overall box fullness rate by 18% and reduced the number of box types by 11% through algorithm design and refined operation to match the size of the cardboard boxes. "For example, we customize gift boxes for some companies, recommend the best box type through intelligent box design algorithms, combine packaging with logistics boxes, and reduce the use of plastic materials." Yuan Liu, responsible for global supply chain green technology products at Cainiao, said.
Biodegradable and environmentally friendly stone plastic boxes made from waste stone materials are the new packaging boxes that ZTO Express is currently piloting. "These packaging boxes are relatively expensive, and we are promoting the intelligent construction of warehouses, applying a series of equipment to reduce logistics costs." Xu Yonggui, head of the brand department of ZTO Cloud Warehouse Market, said.
The network outlets are key to forming a closed loop for governance, and promoting express packaging to "lose weight" and "go green" requires cultivating awareness of delivery and recycling.
Zhejiang University has set up "Green Box" express packaging recycling devices at all 14 sites. "Take the Baisha Mail Delivery Service Station at Zijingang Campus as an example, more than 200 express packages are recycled and reused here every day." Yao Xin, secretary of the Party Committee and chairman of the Logistics Group of Zhejiang University, said that after nearly 10 years of daily guidance and green activities, recycling and reuse of cardboard boxes has become a routine operation at the service station.
Xu Yong, vice chairman of the Express Logistics Branch of the China Communications and Transportation Association, said that relevant departments should strengthen supervision, investigate and rectify factories that produce unqualified and environmentally unfriendly packaging materials from the source, and prevent packaging materials that do not meet requirements from entering the market.
"To achieve green and reduced express delivery, clear responsibilities need to be assigned to producers, e-commerce platforms, express logistics, and other responsible entities." Zhao Guojun, director of the Postal Development Research Center at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, said that further coordination with relevant departments can bring e-commerce platforms and packaging material manufacturers together as responsible entities for strict regulation.
"Many consumers do not trust simple packaging, and the level of concern for green packaging also needs to be raised." Zhao Guojun said that it is necessary to enhance consumers' awareness of green and reduced express packaging and promote companies to make changes, designing packaging solutions that can enhance protection and are relatively lightweight based on the characteristics of different products and transportation environments. (Xinhua News Agency, Beijing, June 19)

title_en: Postal Savings Bank of China Henan Branch: Financial vitality nourishes the Central Plains, rural revitalization writes a new chapter.
body_en:
In the summer season, the Central Plains are a scene of abundant harvest and busy activity.
Rural revitalization, financial leadership. In 2025, the Central Committee issued Document No. 1, proposing to promote financial institutions to increase funding for rural revitalization.
Vigorously carry out the "hundreds of counties, thousands of towns, and tens of thousands of villages" deep service action, deepen political and financial cooperation, explore rural industrial needs, optimize social service models... During the critical period of summer harvest and planting, the Postal Savings Bank of China Henan Branch focuses on financial support for rural revitalization, continuously innovates financial products and services, uses financial "living water" to accurately "irrigate" the fields, and escorts the production during the "three summers" and the development of rural characteristic industries.
More convenient, political and financial cooperation enables comprehensive funding connection
"Thanks to the Postal Savings Bank's loan of 300,000 yuan, I have enough funds to carry out the next planting work." Although many days have passed, on June 4th, when talking about the "political and financial exchange meeting" she attended last month, farmer Guo still expressed gratitude.
The "political and financial exchange meeting" mentioned by Guo is called the "Political and Financial Cooperation, Promoting Rural Revitalization" launch meeting, held in the conference room of the Grape Frame Township Government in Lankao County on the morning of May 15th. The exchange meeting was jointly organized by the Postal Savings Bank Lankao County Branch, the Lankao County Development and Reform Commission, and the Grape Frame Township Government.
At the meeting, the staff of the Postal Savings Bank Lankao County Branch used simple language to introduce the bank's loan business and process to the participating farmers. Especially after understanding everyone's funding needs, the staff conducted on-site credit assessment for more than a dozen farmers and granted nearly 5 million yuan in credit.
"I never thought that the loan would be approved on the spot." Guo said she is a large-scale planter in Grape Frame Township, with 300 mu of land under contract for large-scale sweet potato planting. She also built a 500 cubic meter cold storage for storage and staggered sales.
After the sweet potato planting work started in April this year, her expenses gradually increased: land leasing fees, hiring farmers for field management fees, purchasing organic and chemical fertilizers. In addition, there were also fees for renting agricultural machinery, with a funding gap of about 300,000 yuan.
Recommended by the village committee, Guo participated in the "political and financial exchange meeting." At the meeting, the staff carefully guided her to fill out the relevant information, completed a pre-credit assessment of 300,000 yuan for the "industrial loan" within 5 minutes, and the loan funds were credited on the same day. After the funds were in place, Guo promptly paid the labor costs of her fellow villagers, purchased fertilizers, and booked agricultural machinery services to ensure the smooth progress of sweet potato planting.
Leading at the county level, promoting at the township level, and rooting in the countryside, the Postal Savings Bank Henan Branch has established a hierarchical joint system with county, township governments, and village-level organizations, building a universal financial service network, clearly assigning responsible management personnel and village customer managers, holding township and village promotion meetings irregularly, increasing the frequency of door-to-door visits to promote financial knowledge... Continuously promote financial services to rural areas, unblocking the "last mile" of financial services for the masses.
Currently, the Postal Savings Bank Henan Branch's "hundreds of counties, thousands of towns, and tens of thousands of villages" deep service action has covered all counties and major townships in the province, holding nearly ten thousand village promotion meetings. As of the end of April 2025, the bank's agricultural loan scale reached 190.3 billion yuan, with nearly 45 billion yuan already disbursed this year.
More professional, tailored to help characteristic industries thrive
In June, Zhecheng is seamlessly transitioning from summer harvest to summer planting. In the intercropped fields, after harvesting wheat, they immediately start transplanting peppers, and the straw left in the ground becomes fertilizer for the pepper plants.
Unlike the busy fields, the pepper market in Zhecheng is a bustling scene: piles of bright red dried peppers, trading stalls buzzing with activity, and farmers looking at the constantly flashing numbers on the electronic settlement screen with joy on their faces.
Mr. Cao has been operating in the pepper market for many years, with an annual turnover exceeding 20 million yuan. To expand the scale of procurement and storage, he planned to finance from the bank. Thinking that with an annual turnover of over ten million yuan, he could easily get a bank loan approved, he encountered the problem of "flowing accounts."
It turned out that the bank required Mr. Cao to provide bank statements, but Mr. Cao had been manually recording his purchases and transactions for many years, and daily settlements were made through various methods such as WeChat, Alipay, and bank transfers. When organizing credit materials, it was not only time-consuming and laborious but also prone to omissions and errors.
"I no longer have to worry about keeping accounts in the future. With a light tap on my phone, everything is clear and transparent. 'Jiaoyitong' has been a great help to me!" Mr. Cao said happily.
The "Jiaoyitong" platform is a special service tailored by the Postal Savings Bank Henan Branch after in-depth research on the development of the Zhecheng pepper industry, meeting the financial needs of industry associations, large purchasers, and cooperatives. This platform has functions such as transaction settlement, fund supervision, and data statistics, providing full-chain financial support for the pepper industry in Zhecheng County.
This is just a glimpse of the bank's service to local industry development. The Postal Savings Bank Henan Branch focuses on "small and beautiful, beautiful and excellent" rural characteristic industries, according to the "one industry, one plan" approach, tailoring exclusive business plans for characteristic industry clusters and leading enterprises within its jurisdiction based on the operating characteristics, financial needs, and funding cycles of rural industries, matching loan elements such as quotas, interest rates, and repayment methods.
The Postal Savings Bank Lankao County Branch has launched special products such as musical instrument industry loans to provide strong financial support for the musical instrument processing industry in Lankao; the Postal Savings Bank Taiqian County Branch actively supports the local down industry, helping a small business that used to collect duck and goose feathers on the streets grow into a characteristic industry; the Postal Savings Bank Zhoukou City Branch, based on industrial loans, has innovatively launched products such as "land transfer loans" and "cattle breeding loans" to inject financial vitality into the development of local county-level characteristic industries.
When industries thrive, the economy thrives, and when the economy thrives, rural areas thrive. Focusing on weak areas of inclusive finance development in the province, the Postal Savings Bank Henan Branch's various branches actively cooperate with local agricultural departments and industry associations to provide special financial services for grain production, characteristic industries, agricultural product processing, etc., effectively matching financial resources with rural industries, continuously improving business efficiency, and truly enabling customers to "walk less and get money faster."
In the future, the Postal Savings Bank Henan Branch will continue to deepen the "hundreds of counties, thousands of towns, and tens of thousands of villages" deep service action, through political and financial cooperation to comprehensively connect funding needs, tailor support for characteristic industry development, optimize business processes through digital empowerment, deeply cultivate key areas, continuously innovate products, and enhance service levels, accelerating the creation of the main force for rural revitalization.
Growing together with rural areas, developing together with industries, and prospering together with farmers. The Postal Savings Bank Henan Branch will always adhere to the original intention of serving agriculture, rural areas, and farmers, painting a magnificent picture of rural revitalization with the brush of finance.

title_en: International Business Daily: 618 battle report data released, is the "temperature difference" bigger this year?
body_en: As of 23:59 on June 18, 2025, JD's 618 set a new record, with the number of orders increasing by over 100% year-on-year, and the overall order volume of JD's online retail business, offline formats, and JD Takeout exceeding 2.2 billion orders. During 618, the number of daily active users on the JD app reached a historic high. The scale and growth rate of the 3C and home appliance categories remained industry leaders, while the fashion and beauty, and daily necessities categories led the industry in growth. The diverse formats resonated together, driving strong growth in orders for millions of offline stores, with JD's live streaming sales volume increasing by 285% year-on-year. As of 24:00 on June 18, the simplified 2025 Tmall 618 saw record user scale and activity, with efficient growth in brand transactions throughout the entire cycle. Transactions for 453 brands on Tmall 618 exceeded one billion, a 24% year-on-year increase. Brands such as Apple, Midea, Haier, Xiaomi, Huawei, Genki Forest, Nike, Gree, FeiLe, Vivo, Pechoin, Adidas, L'Oreal, and others firmly held their place in the "billion club" of Tmall 618. Every time a major promotion ends, there is always a report card to summarize the original intention, but I don't know how everyone views it (feel free to leave a comment). Following 618 for almost 10 years, I feel like I'm getting more and more "temperature difference" (because I really "don't have time" to shop... luckily I placed an order early and feel like I didn't lose a billion). However, through the month-long "hype" on various platforms, we can still smell the gunpowder of this year's 618 and see where the new focus of the platforms is. At the 618 Media Open Day held by JD on June 18, various business leaders from JD took turns to passionately talk about data and trends. Overall, this year's 618, based on being "good and cheap," JD provided users with a comprehensive experience upgrade through greater discounts, guaranteed quality, better services, more interesting gameplay, and wider coverage. Under this promotion, Chinese brands are accelerating their rise, releasing vitality in the sinking market, and witnessing explosive growth in instant retail and life service consumption, with highlights in consumption data. 618 has become a strong booster for consumption growth and industry development. JD stated that this year's 618 consumption trends have changed again, showing four significant characteristics: First, the AI wave has driven high attention to AI-related products, while national trend products are more favored by consumers. Under the dual drive of "technology + traditional culture," over 70% of the top 100 brands in terms of popularity during 618 are Chinese brands, with searches for "AI elements" and "intangible cultural heritage elements" products increasing by over 120% and 270% year-on-year, respectively. Second, the consumption vitality in the sinking market is strong, with orders in county and rural areas increasing by over 130% year-on-year, and the number of users increasing by over 140% year-on-year. Nanchang County in Nanchang City and Chengwu County in Heze City have become the areas with the strongest consumption power and the strongest growth in consumption power during JD 618. In addition, as of now, JD's group buying stores have landed in Hefei, Beijing, and Suqian, with a total coverage of users increasing by 34 times year-on-year. Third, instant retail is booming, with JD Takeout's daily order volume exceeding 25 million, and over 1.5 million high-quality dining establishments joining. JD Fresh's online orders increased by over 150% year-on-year, sales of JD Fresh's own brand products increased by 340% year-on-year, and the recently launched "6.18L Pilsen Original Beer" and the "Fengyou Exploding Soft Candy" co-branded with Longhu are selling like hotcakes. Lastly, there is a significant growth in life service consumption, with the turnover of JD's self-operated housekeeping services exceeding one billion, and orders for self-operated home appliance cleaning and laundry increasing by 211% and over 10 times year-on-year, respectively. JD has 120,000 full-time delivery riders and nearly 300,000 professional technicians, including car maintenance technicians, home appliance engineers, and housekeeping cleaners, ready to respond to user needs at any time. Additionally, this year's 618 saw a significant increase in subsidies, with the addition of national subsidies for trade-ins and JD Takeout's billion-yuan subsidy for the first time, combined with various other benefits, allowing each person to receive over 6180 yuan in subsidies per day, achieving "more subsidies on top of savings." Sales of mobile communications, home appliances, and food and seasoning products increased by 88%, 161%, and 138% year-on-year, respectively. In the price range of 4000 to 6000 yuan, the transaction volume of mobile phones increased by 50% year-on-year, while the transaction volume of AI notebooks and 100-inch TVs increased by 151% and 260% year-on-year, respectively. Tmall focused on two main aspects of effectiveness: "simplifying the rules of major promotions, lowering the threshold for participation, and unleashing consumer vitality" and "deepening the anti-internal competition process through mechanism adjustments to help businesses improve quality and efficiency." In the former, during this year's 618, Tmall eliminated complex discount models such as "spend X get Y" and only set an official gameplay of "official discounts" combined with large coupons, with basic discounts starting at 15% off and a maximum discount of up to 50%. On top of the discount, consumers could stack additional benefits such as 88VIP coupons, industry category coupons (beauty coupons, fashion coupons, etc.), and live streaming room red envelopes. This made transactions simpler and the benefits for consumers more direct. By May 26, during the first phase of Tmall 618, the total transaction volume of categories participating in national subsidies such as home appliances, home furnishings, and mobile electronics increased by 283% compared to last year's Double 11, with 40 brands including Midea, Haier, Karcher, and Genki Forest achieving transactions exceeding one billion. This drove double-digit year-on-year growth in overall transactions for industries such as home appliances, home furnishings, home decor, and 3C electronics, with over 3000 brands doubling their transactions year-on-year, unleashing strong consumer vitality. In the latter, as the rules of 618 were simplified and price differentials were squeezed out, the way forward for brands was to reconstruct their value dimensions. On the product side, there needs to be a focus on technological differentiation, while on the user side, an emotional connection needs to be established to transform consumers from buyers to participants. On the channel side, there needs to be a focus on refined operations, abandoning mass coverage and focusing on deep services for high repeat-purchase customer groups. The platform's traffic allocation mechanism is shifting from "the lowest price wins" to "the best wins more," and brands need to use their product innovation capabilities and ability to meet consumer demands to achieve growth. During 618, brands that were early to market with new products on Tmall saw a concentrated effort. In the month leading up to 618, nearly 40,000 brands launched 1.09 million new products on Tmall. During 618, over 200 "super new products" from top brands were launched on Tmall, with the number of "super new products" increasing by 90% year-on-year. In addition, Taobao is focusing more on the battlefield of instant retail. It was announced on May 26 that during 618, Taobao Flash Sale and Ele.me jointly announced that the daily order volume had exceeded 40 million. This was less than a month after the official launch of Taobao Flash Sale. Data shows that the order structure of Taobao Flash Sale has significantly expanded to cover all categories, with non-beverage products accounting for 75% and orders for non-food categories growing far beyond expectations. Instant retail business brings higher user activity. Alibaba's financial report for the fourth quarter and full year of the 2025 fiscal year revealed that in the long run, Taobao Flash Sale will bring benefits to Taobao in terms of user activity and user scale. Tmall's 618 spot sales began, and Taobao Flash Sale announced an increase in free milk tea giveaways, with a million cups given away on the first day of 618; during this time, a variety of activities were launched for different festivals, such as free flowers on 520, free zongzi on Dragon Boat Festival, and free hamburgers on Children's Day. The free giveaway series has become a signature activity of Taobao Flash Sale. Instant retail also brings new business growth for merchants. During 618, Xidesheng opened a store pickup service on Taobao Flash Sale, with daily GMV exceeding 3 million yuan on the fourth day; Decathlon's overall daily order volume on Taobao Flash Sale doubled compared to the previous month. On Mother's Day, Taobao Flash Sale launched a free flower promotion, driving a doubling of transactions for 8625 flower shops year-on-year. Among the flower merchants on Taobao and Tmall that have transitioned from offline to online, nearly 20% saw a doubling of transactions, bringing new customers to the local scene.
