title_en: Talent development chain empowers e-commerce value chain.
body_en:
The RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement) initiated by the ten ASEAN countries officially took effect in 2023 in the 15 member countries. The agreement aims to promote regional economic development and cultural exchange. With the rapid development of global trade, RCEP has become a major cooperation platform for the "Belt and Road Initiative," playing a positive role in supporting the free trade system of cross-border e-commerce in countries along the route, maintaining the stability of regional industrial chains, and promoting the high-quality development of cross-border e-commerce in China.
RCEP's strategic drive and the current demand for cross-border e-commerce talent
Data shows that the annual growth rate of the cross-border e-commerce market in Southeast Asia among RCEP member countries has exceeded 25%, while markets in Central Asia, Central and Eastern Europe still have huge room for expansion. In this context, cross-border e-commerce language service talents have become a key link connecting Chinese enterprises with overseas markets. These talents need to have bilingual communication skills, cross-border professional skills, cross-cultural understanding, and be able to serve as communicators for economic and trade cooperation and disseminators of Chinese cultural values.
However, the current talent development faces multiple challenges. At the level of industry-education integration, cooperation between schools and enterprises remains superficial, teaching content is disconnected from job requirements, and there is a lack of real project practice; at the level of cultural education, the curriculum system generally overlooks cultural differences among RCEP member countries, such as religious customs in ASEAN countries, business etiquette in Japan and South Korea, etc.; at the level of knowledge system, there is a tendency to prioritize language skills over cultural logic, making it difficult for talents to cope with complex cross-border scenarios. For example, some cross-border e-commerce product detail pages have caused local consumers to resist due to cultural taboos not being considered during translation, directly affecting the effectiveness of the company's overseas expansion. Therefore, building a scientific training model has become an urgent need for industry development.
Innovative practice of the "Chinese + Cross-border Professional Skills" training model
Huzhou Vocational and Technical College integrates language education and vocational education resources based on the theory of situational education and work-based learning theory, constructing a "Chinese + Cross-border Professional Skills" talent training model. It builds a three-dimensional training structure of "structure-function-context" to help students improve their abilities in real work situations. Taking Amazon platform operation teaching as an example, teachers first help students master product description translation skills through language courses (structure), then let students know how to adjust the copy based on the consumption habits of the target country through case analysis (function), and finally apply what they have learned in simulated store operations (context) to help students form a "learn-practice-use" closed loop. Specifically, there are the following training paths.
Building a "1+N+X" three-level training framework. This framework is based on the core culture of the enterprise. "1" represents the enterprise's mission, vision, and values, such as Alibaba's mission of "making it easy to do business anywhere in the world," which is the soul of the training framework. "N" refers to personalized training programs based on the "MVV" of different enterprises, such as developing training programs focusing on the Russian-speaking market for enterprises like "AliExpress" and designing special courses for the Southeast Asian market for brands like Lazada. "X" represents a cross-cultural training system that customizes content based on cultural differences among RCEP member countries - emphasizing business etiquette details for the Confucian cultural circle (Japan, South Korea, Singapore), focusing on religious taboo training for the Islamic cultural circle (Malaysia, Indonesia), and emphasizing workplace communication habits for the Christian cultural circle (Australia, New Zealand).
A cooperation case between a cross-border e-commerce company and a school shows that this framework has shortened the internship adaptation period from 3 months to 1 month, increased the accuracy of product translation by 40%, and reduced customer complaint rates by 25%. In the specific implementation, companies need to involve senior practitioners in course design, transforming real work processes into teaching modules, such as optimizing the case analysis course "Amazon online product detail page design" into three teaching units: keyword analysis, selling point refinement, and cultural adaptation.
Innovative multi-domain collaborative training model. Adopting a three-dimensional training path of "online + offline" and "domestic + overseas." Online, virtual operations are conducted using cross-border e-commerce simulation platforms (such as Eclac), where students can process orders from different countries and the system automatically provides feedback on cultural adaptability scores; offline, joint school-enterprise training bases are established to introduce real projects from companies, such as providing product detail page translation services for small businesses in Southeast Asia. In terms of international cooperation, joint training programs are conducted with schools in each member country, with students studying language and professional knowledge domestically for the first two years and then studying local business culture in the target country for the third year while participating in internships at local companies.
Taking the "Cross-border E-commerce English" course as an example, the teaching content is restructured according to the "pre-sale - in-sale - after-sale" process: in the pre-sale stage, students learn market research English, analyzing how Thai consumers prefer to express their preferences for green products; in the in-sale stage, they practice translating product detail pages, meeting the strict requirements of Japanese consumers for detailed descriptions; in the after-sale stage, they simulate dispute resolution, mastering the special requirements of Korean customers for apology etiquette. This scenario-based teaching helps improve students' employment rates and the satisfaction of employing companies.
Development and application of a dynamic teaching material system. The school has established a "research - practice - development - evaluation" iterative mechanism for teaching materials. First, the school surveyed 50 "going global" companies, identified 12 typical tasks in cross-border e-commerce language services (such as exhibition negotiations, customs declarations, social media marketing, etc.), and distilled 86 core skill points. Then, teachers integrated these skill points into the curriculum, with each unit including a "cultural tips" module, such as adding details on "Vietnamese taboos" and "Indonesian prayer time arrangements" in the Southeast Asian market chapter. Supplementary online micro-courses have been developed, allowing students to scan QR codes to watch videos of Malaysian business negotiations for situational imitation.
In the use of teaching materials, teachers have established a three-dimensional evaluation system: language application abilities are assessed through role-playing in physical classrooms, knowledge mastery is analyzed through correct answer rates in online learning, and skill transfer effects are measured through order conversion rates in cross-border platform practices. After using these teaching materials, a vocational college saw a significant improvement in students' performance in the national cross-border e-commerce skills competition, and companies reported a significant enhancement in interns' cultural adaptation abilities.
Value breakthroughs and future optimization directions of the training model
This training model fills three major gaps in current talent development: cultural cognitive gap (such as resolving marketing mistakes due to religious differences), skill connection gap (such as shortening the adaptation period from the classroom to the workplace), and value dissemination gap (such as conveying Chinese brand concepts through language services). Data from a certain cross-border e-commerce talent service agency shows that graduates trained in this model have cross-cultural communication ability scores 2.3 levels higher than those trained in traditional models, leading to an 18% increase in overseas customer repurchase rates on the platform.
In the future, schools plan to optimize the model in two ways. First, by integrating digital technology, they will develop an AI-based cross-cultural communication training system to enhance adaptability through interactive simulations with virtual clients; second, they will expand into minor language directions, building a diverse training system of "English + minor languages + professional skills" to meet the demands of languages such as Thai and Vietnamese in RCEP member countries.
As the markets of RCEP member countries deepen, this model will provide a more solid talent support for building an Asia-Pacific economic community, helping Chinese enterprises achieve higher-quality "going global" in the global value chain.
(Author's unit is Huzhou Vocational and Technical College)

title_en: 60,000 taxis will increase "online hailing" prompts.
body_en:
"Why do taxis keep waving their hands when they haven't picked up any passengers?" This is a question often asked by many citizens, especially elderly passengers, when trying to hail a taxi. In the future, citizens can determine whether these taxis have accepted an online booking or are refusing passengers by looking at the "online booking" indicator light on the vehicle.

According to the Municipal Transportation Commission, the city is gradually upgrading the light panels of 60,000 taxis equipped with intelligent terminals, adding an "online booking" display mode, with plans to complete the upgrade by September this year.

On June 16, a taxi in Chaoyangmen displayed an "online booking" indicator light. Intern Luo Zengjia photographed.

Current situation investigation

Passengers complain that taxis keep driving past, drivers have something to say

At 11 a.m. on June 12, in front of the Dongdan campus of Peking Union Medical College Hospital, a dozen elderly people stood scattered on both sides of the bus stop and intersection, constantly waving their hands trying to flag down a taxi, but to no avail. During this time, many taxis passing by had no passengers.

This scene is not uncommon. Observations by reporters around several hospitals and commercial areas found that when passengers waved for a taxi, some "empty" taxis often drove straight past. Especially for the middle-aged and elderly groups, who are not familiar with online car-hailing platforms, they often find themselves in the embarrassing situation of being unable to hail a taxi on the road.

When it comes to this topic, taxi drivers feel very wronged. Many taxis that appear to be "empty" are actually accepting orders from online platforms.

With the vigorous development of online car-hailing services, the mode of accepting orders by taxis has undergone significant changes. "If we don't connect to the platform and rely solely on hailing orders, our income will be greatly affected," one taxi driver admitted. "It's not that we don't want to stop, it's that once we accept an online booking, we simply can't stop." It is understood that most drivers are connected to multiple platforms, and platform dispatching has become their main way of getting jobs.

During interviews, many drivers stated that compared to picking up passengers on the roadside, the efficiency of "calling a car online" is higher. Of course, if there are no orders from the platform, they are also willing to pick up passengers hailing on the roadside.

Transportation Department

Displaying "online booking" already has a task

According to the Municipal Transportation Commission, the original light panels of cruising taxis (indicating vacant, occupied, or out of service) have been modified. After the modification, the city's taxi management department will integrate data with online taxi-hailing platforms such as Didi and Gaode, taxi dispatch centers, and vehicle-mounted intelligent terminals to automatically display the words "online booking" on the light panel when a cruising taxi accepts an online booking, making it easier for passengers to identify the vehicle's operational status.

Currently, some taxis have a small electronic display screen installed on the inside of the front windshield, with the words "online booking." This indicates that the taxi already has a task and is going to pick up passengers who have booked online.

The transportation department stated that since June 2024, the city has been gradually upgrading the light panels of 60,000 taxis equipped with intelligent terminals, adding an "online booking" display mode to make it easier for passengers to know the operational status of taxis. Currently, there are still some vehicles that cannot display this status due to not having an intelligent terminal installed, and plans are in place to complete the vehicle updates by September this year to achieve the "online booking" status display.

Standardizing operations

Taxis displaying "vacant" should stop to pick up passengers

It is reported that this light panel upgrade is achieved through real-time data sharing and software upgrades of vehicle-mounted intelligent terminals, without involving hardware modifications or changing light fixtures. The "online booking" mode is automatically controlled by the backend software system, changing automatically based on the status of the vehicle accepting orders from online platforms such as Didi and Gaode, without the need for manual operation by the driver.

In addition, the transportation department will standardize driver operating behavior, requiring drivers to actively respond and stop to pick up passengers when they are displaying a "vacant" status on the taxi.

This report was written by Sun Hongyang, with contributions from intern Liu Yujie.

title_en: 21st Dialogue | HKEX CEO Charles Li: "Solving hand in hand", Chinese concept stocks returning to Hong Kong "definitely acceptable"
body_en:
Since the reform of the listing system by the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018, 33 Chinese concept stocks have listed in Hong Kong, accounting for over 70% of the total market capitalization of all Chinese concept stocks listed in the United States. As 2025 approaches, the Hong Kong IPO market continues to rebound. Against the backdrop of tense Sino-US geopolitical relations, an increasing number of Chinese concept stocks are considering listing in Hong Kong.

Concurrently, whether the Hong Kong Stock Exchange will relax the market capitalization threshold and dual-class share structure restrictions for Chinese concept stocks listing in Hong Kong has become a focal point of market attention. Market analysis indicates that among the 27 Chinese concept stocks listed in the US with market capitalizations exceeding US$1 billion, 22 companies have equity structures that do not comply with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange's regulations.

In April, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po revealed that he had instructed the Securities and Futures Commission and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange to be prepared, stating that if Chinese concept stocks listed overseas wish to return, Hong Kong must be made their preferred listing destination.

"Our consistent attitude is that we want high-quality companies to list in Hong Kong. Every company has its uniqueness, and if they need some flexibility to overcome certain issues, we will work hand-in-hand with them to resolve them," said Hong Kong Stock Exchange CEO Bonnie Chan Yick-ting in an exclusive interview with a reporter from 21st Century Business Herald.

She admitted that to better serve the real economy with finance, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange regularly reviews its listing rules. "As long as there is market demand, we must study it. This is the spirit of 'people, goods, and venue' that we advocate."

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting. File photo

The return of an increasing number of Chinese "giants" to list in Hong Kong has undoubtedly injected new vitality into Hong Kong's capital market. However, some industry insiders are concerned about whether these large-scale enterprises will face issues such as insufficient trading activity and suppressed stock prices after returning to Hong Kong, thereby affecting the overall market liquidity.

In response, Bonnie Chan Yick-ting firmly stated, "Hong Kong is an open market, and there is no need to question whether we can handle it. The answer is 'we can definitely handle it.' As long as the companies are outstanding enough, and as long as they are favored by investors, funds will flow in continuously from all directions."

According to statistics, in the first five months of this year, 27 Hong Kong stocks were listed through IPOs, raising a total of HK$77.346 billion, nearing last year's full-year level.

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting stated that the liquidity in Hong Kong's new stock market is very ample. Over the past decade, cumulative financing has exceeded US$300 billion (approximately HK$2.35 trillion), ranking first globally. In the first five months of 2025, the average daily trading volume in the Hong Kong securities market was HK$242.3 billion, more than double that of HK$110.2 billion in the same period last year.

This year, the Hong Kong market has successfully welcomed the listing of several large new stocks. These companies have shown high trading activity after listing, dispelling market concerns about insufficient liquidity for "giant" enterprises.

At the same time, the performance of Hong Kong's refinancing market has also been impressive. As of June 6, 2025, the cumulative refinancing volume this year has reached US$25.9 billion (approximately HK$203.3 billion), more than double the IPO fundraising amount in Hong Kong during the same period.

To continuously enhance the attractiveness and competitiveness of the Hong Kong market and thus improve overall liquidity, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange has launched a series of innovative initiatives in recent years. Among them, the "FINI" (Fast Interface for New Issuance) system launched in 2023 is a key component. This system aims to shorten the settlement cycle for new shares, significantly reducing it from the traditional "T+5" to "T+2." The shortening of the settlement cycle means an increase in capital turnover efficiency, which can effectively reduce market risk and attract more international investors to participate in new stock subscriptions, thereby further enhancing the liquidity of the new stock market.

Since the beginning of this year, Hong Kong stock liquidity has significantly improved, leading to a substantial narrowing of the A-H share price gap. This has also prompted leading A-share companies to more actively consider listing in Hong Kong. The recent listing of CATL, a leading new energy company in mainland China, in Hong Kong has pushed this trend to a climax, setting the record for the largest IPO financing globally this year.

"For companies with overseas expansion plans, listing in Hong Kong not only provides a financing platform but also facilitates their overseas mergers and acquisitions, equity incentives, and other activities. By listing in Hong Kong, companies can use Hong Kong stocks as consideration for overseas acquisitions, thus avoiding the pressure of relying solely on cash payments," said Bonnie Chan Yick-ting. "If a company is listed simultaneously in the A-share and Hong Kong markets, the trading activity in the Hong Kong market will also drive the trading volume in the A-share market, achieving a virtuous cycle."

In 2024, the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) introduced five capital market cooperation measures with Hong Kong and has continued to optimize the filing process for companies listing overseas. These policies provide a more convenient and efficient channel for mainland companies to list in Hong Kong, reducing compliance costs and time for these companies, thereby stimulating more enthusiasm for companies to choose the A+H model.

Meanwhile, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange's own continuously optimized listing mechanism also provides a convenient financing environment for mainland companies. It is reported that last year the Hong Kong Stock Exchange lowered the market capitalization threshold for specialist technology companies and jointly optimized the approval process timetable for new listing applications with the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission. In early May this year, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange officially announced the launch of the "Tech Company Fast Track."

According to a report by CICC, since the listing of Midea in Hong Kong in September last year, eight A-share companies have listed in Hong Kong, with IPO financing totaling HK$98.11 billion, including industry leaders like Midea and CATL. According to the CSRC's filing information and listed company disclosures, nearly 50 more A-share companies plan to list in Hong Kong, with 23 having already completed the filing or submitted their materials.

On June 10, the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council issued the "Opinions on Deepening the Shenzhen Comprehensive Reform Pilot and Further Deepening Reform and Innovation to Expand Opening-up" (hereinafter referred to as the "Opinions"), which allows companies in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area listed on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong to list in Shenzhen. The Shenzhen Stock Exchange is expected to welcome "H+A" listed companies.

In response, she jokingly said, "The A+H model is not a competitor to A-shares, but a supplement to A-shares. The two can form a virtuous interaction and jointly expand the 'cake' of the capital market. As long as it plays a complementary role, it is a good thing."

Since the beginning of the year, with DeepSeek leading the narrative of China's asset revaluation, the Hong Kong stock market has shown a unique performance. With a year-to-date gain of over 20%, Hong Kong stocks have led major global stock markets. Inflows of southbound and international capital into Hong Kong stocks have become the main driving force for the market's upward trend this year.

"The emergence of DeepSeek in January this year has allowed the market to re-evaluate Chinese concept stocks," Bonnie Chan Yick-ting said with a smile. "The market is undergoing a 'treasure hunt' process, with investors deeply researching and uncovering high-quality Chinese assets."

The stable development of the Chinese economy and the series of economic stimulus policies issued by the state have greatly boosted investor confidence in the Chinese capital market and Chinese assets. At the same time, she believes that the global trend of "de-dollarization" is intensifying, reshaping the capital market. "With the decline in global interest rates and the improvement of market sentiment, funds are seeking new allocation directions. We observe that many international investors are re-evaluating their portfolios, beginning to seek investment targets beyond dollar assets, and considering shifting some funds from more volatile markets to markets with greater growth potential."

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting pointed out that global asset reallocation will be a long-term process. Undoubtedly, this will bring new opportunities for non-dollar assets, including Hong Kong stocks.

It is worth noting that international capital is also "voting with its feet." Taking CATL's H-share listing as an example, its international placement accounted for 92.5%, including overseas institutions from 15 countries and regions such as the Kuwait Investment Authority (a Middle Eastern sovereign wealth fund), Mirae Asset Global Investments, UBS Asset Management, and Oaktree Capital, with 23 top international cornerstone investors subscribing.

"21st Century": Everyone is very concerned about the "Tech Company Fast Track" recently launched by the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. What is the overall application situation?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: "The Tech Company Fast Track" was launched on May 6th, primarily to support the nation's overall strategy of promoting technological innovation. Over the years, from Chapter 18A to Chapter 18C, we have aimed to better serve companies by providing them with tailored listing rules. Some companies, due to their highly innovative nature, may sometimes be uncertain if they can meet our listing requirements. By opening this fast track, we provide them with a channel to engage with us directly at an earlier stage, offering one-on-one pre-listing guidance.

This has also opened a confidential submission channel, and the market reaction has been particularly positive. Since its launch, many companies have made inquiries. Our listing department colleagues ensure a preliminary response within five working days, holding meetings with companies. Currently, under Chapters 18A and 18C, over 20 companies have expressed their intention to proceed, which I believe is a good result.

"21st Century": Is this reaction in line with or beyond your expectations?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: Investors are clearly very enthusiastic about technology and tech companies right now. For example, the leading companies that have recently listed saw very high-quality institutional investors place orders during their offerings, including many long-term funds and sovereign funds. Subsequently, funds from the Middle East and Europe have gradually joined.

When I recently met with foreign investors, they particularly liked two sectors in China: one is tech companies, and the other is new consumption. New consumption is also very hot right now, with examples like milk tea, Labubu, and the upcoming IPO of Haitain Soy Sauce. In the future, quite a few companies will be coming to the market successively.

"21st Century": What were your gains and feelings from your recent trip to the Middle East with the Chief Executive of Hong Kong? Besides opening an office in Riyadh, how will the Hong Kong Stock Exchange further facilitate financial connectivity between Hong Kong and the Middle East in the future?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: Every time I return from the Middle East, many media outlets ask me the same question – when will Middle Eastern companies list here? I think it will take some time to brew. The Hong Kong Stock Exchange has a longer history and a larger number of listed companies, over two thousand. However, Middle Eastern exchanges are still at the stage of having one to two hundred listed companies, reflecting that some local enterprises still need to go through a development process.

Although there are no Middle Eastern companies directly listing yet, both sides have listed each other's assets as underlying assets for ETFs. Hong Kong listed a new ETF in May, with "Sukuk" (Saudi Islamic Bonds) as the underlying asset. The Hong Kong Stock Exchange has listed two ETFs with Saudi assets as the underlying, and correspondingly, the Saudi Stock Exchange has listed two ETFs tracking Hong Kong stocks, with good trading performance.

Our work must continue, and we must continue to promote to local companies. However, this time in the Middle East, I spent more time digging for investors. I found that they (Middle Eastern investors) are actually quite knowledgeable. They discussed "Connect" with me and are aware of our latest developments and optimization plans.

"21st Century": Is this because the world is facing the same problems?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: You are absolutely right. Recently, whether it's the Middle East, Europe, or the US, global investors are facing the same task. When people perceive that the US market is highly volatile and unstable, and when the US experienced a "triple kill" of stock, bond, and currency markets for a period, many dollar asset fund managers are re-planning whether to adjust their fund allocations. In this scenario, where can they diversify their investments? Where should they place their assets? This is actually a difficult question. Because the US dollar asset market is a huge entity, their biggest problem is "not being able to fit it all in." Recently, why have our Hong Kong stocks, for example, had such good IPO performance? It is precisely because at the time they were making decisions, we launched these reasonably sized, highly compatible, and excellent IPOs.

In addition to the primary market, from the beginning of the year until now, our secondary market rights issues have also been very hot. There have been several rights issues exceeding US$5 billion, such as for Xiaomi and BYD. Recently, China Ping An issued US$1.5 billion in zero-coupon convertible bonds, and all the news I've heard indicates they are sold out.

"21st Century": Commodity trading is an important part of the financial market. China is the world's largest importer and consumer of commodities. Against this backdrop, with the approval of LME Hong Kong warehouses, what are the future plans for the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in building a commodity ecosystem?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: This is the first step. LME announced last year that it would conduct a feasibility study, and now, in less than a year, we have approved seven warehouses. Why has this been able to move forward? It's mainly because we are serving offshore users and companies. Why were we so fast? It proves there is indeed demand. Starting with warehouses, we can gradually build an ecosystem. Because warehouses are opened, there will be demand for logistics, trade finance, and transaction-related financial services around them. The next step is to explore products, such as commodity-related financial products, securities products, futures, etc. I think the potential here is quite significant.

"21st Century": Do you see any inherent connection between this and the recent hot commodity market?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: There is a popular saying in mainland China recently called "people, goods, and venue." "People, goods, and venue" can actually be applied to my business. I operate a platform, which is financial infrastructure. So I need "people," meaning "participants." Whether you are a company, an individual, or an investor, you are my "participant." "Goods" are my products. If you go to a supermarket, the shelves must be well-stocked. If we are to get a piece of the pie in the de-dollarization process, we must match and align with what the US has. Finally, "venue" is what we have always talked about: in all transaction processes, whether the procedures, workflows, and platforms can provide users with the ultimate experience is very important. Therefore, we introduced normal trading services during adverse weather last year, and we will soon introduce the minimum price change unit for stock trading, as well as the southbound RMB counter, etc. These are all aimed at providing users with the best experience in our "venue."

"21st Century": How do you understand financial services for the real economy, and how does the Hong Kong Stock Exchange practice this in its business?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: When we review listing rules, we are essentially following a path of continuous evolution and rule adjustment to keep up with economic changes. I have been in this field for over thirty years, starting in 1993. At that time, companies listing in Hong Kong from mainland China were large state-owned enterprises, such as the "three oil companies" and telecommunication companies. This was followed by the "Big Four" state-owned banks, then asset management and insurance companies, and later private enterprises. More recently, since 2018, we have seen new economy and biotechnology companies.

For instance, the idea behind Chapter 18C came from discussions with leaders in private equity and venture capital. They needed exit channels after three to five years of investment, so we designed the rules in advance. I remember during the first year of 18C's launch, when IPOs were relatively sluggish, people constantly asked me when 18C would be implemented. I knew in my heart that it would happen eventually, it was just a matter of time.

I need to accurately know what the next batch of "little giants," "big giants," and "giants" will be. What do they need? What are their characteristics? What are their funding requirements? Why have we gone from strictly requiring profitable companies to relaxing it to non-profitable enterprises, and then to companies with no revenue? I can create a set of inclusive listing rules, but while being inclusive, we maintain quality.

"21st Century": Since the listing system reform in 2018, as of the end of March 2025, 33 "Chinese concept stocks" have returned to Hong Kong. It is understood that there are about twenty to thirty Chinese concept stocks that meet the criteria but have not yet dual-listed or secondary-listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. What preparations has the Hong Kong Stock Exchange made in advance to welcome this wave of Chinese concept stock returns?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: The return of Chinese concept stocks is not a new phenomenon. In 2021, due to accounting ledger issues, the number of returning companies was only around thirty. However, their market capitalization was very large, accounting for nearly 70%-80% of the total market capitalization of all Chinese concept stocks listed in the US. Our consistent attitude is that every company has its uniqueness, but it must be a high-quality company. If they need flexible handling to overcome their unique problems, we will work hand-in-hand with them to resolve the issues on a case-by-case basis.

This wave of Chinese concept stock returns is driven not only by pressure from the US market but also by the inherent attractiveness of the Hong Kong stock market. After Alibaba converted to a dual primary listing and was included in "Stock Connect" in September last year, its stock price and liquidity saw significant improvements. This in itself is very attractive, and as a result, many companies are actively approaching us. We have also recently observed that the trading of some returning Chinese concept stocks is gradually shifting towards Hong Kong. Recently, many investors ask me about ADRs and if we can handle them. I tell them not to worry. (Their implied meaning is that if you can handle them, I will move my trading venue here.)

"21st Century": There has been some discussion recently about the market capitalization threshold for companies with weighted voting rights, voting rights, and other details. Will the Hong Kong Stock Exchange further relax these?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: The Financial Secretary revealed a hint during the budget speech, saying that the Hong Kong Stock Exchange and the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission will conduct a relatively comprehensive review of listing rules this year. In fact, regardless of the context of Chinese concept stock returns, we will review our listing rules. Whether it's about weighted voting rights, how to better serve the real economy, or the aforementioned technology companies, we are constantly thinking about it. As long as there is market demand, we must study it. This is the spirit of "people, goods, and venue."

"21st Century": You mentioned that some investors asked you if you could handle it, is it because investors are also concerned about market liquidity?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: Liquidity has never been an issue. Firstly, for primary market IPOs, the recent IPO of CATL was US$5.3 billion, and Midea was US$4.6 billion last year. We have extensive experience with IPOs of this scale. Hong Kong is, after all, an open market. Don't ask me if we can handle it or not; we certainly can. Because as long as the companies are good enough, and as long as they are transactions and investment targets favored by investors, funds will flow in from all directions at any time.

Secondly, in the secondary market, the average daily trading volume in 2023 was HK$100 billion, HK$132 billion last year, and HK$240 billion this year. Since the implementation of measures in September last year, there has been a strong rally. We broke records three times in two weeks, with the highest daily trading volume reaching HK$620 billion. This indicates that we have sufficient depth as a capital market, we can cope, and we have the technical capability to maintain it.

"21st Century": The Hong Kong Stock Exchange had very good performance in the first quarter of this year, and its stock price performance was also outstanding. How sustainable do you think this rally in Hong Kong stocks is from a market perspective?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: This time is a bit different. Since the emergence of DeepSeek in January, everyone has begun to re-evaluate Chinese concept stocks. They are truly on a treasure hunt now, so this rally is relatively long-lasting. From January to now, trading volumes have generally remained at historical high levels.

In addition to this rally not being policy-driven but fundamentals-driven, there is also the backdrop of de-dollarization. Dollar assets are a behemoth, and this adjustment is ongoing, with considerable incremental flows. I believe that foreign investors are unlikely to remain steadfast in putting all their money into US stocks, US assets, and the US dollar. They will inevitably consider risks and need to diversify.

"21st Century": A+H shares are also a focus of market attention. Why are so many A-share companies listing in Hong Kong recently?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: Through some analysis, we found that many A-share companies choosing to list in Hong Kong in the past period were mainly seeking an offshore financing platform to support their international expansion plans. If a company plans to undertake overseas acquisitions or mergers, it can use its Hong Kong stock as consideration for the transaction, which is more convenient and flexible.

In addition, many companies wish to attract top scientists and engineers globally and use equity incentives. The Hong Kong market provides relatively practical tools for this. All these factors lead them to believe that the H-share market in Hong Kong can be an effective supplement for A-share companies' overseas development. At the same time, we have also noticed that if a company is listed simultaneously in the A-share and Hong Kong markets, the trading activity in the Hong Kong market will also drive the trading volume in the A-share market, achieving a virtuous cycle.

There is a misunderstanding in the market that mainland exchanges and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange are in competition. This is not the case. In fact, we should strive to continuously expand the size of the "cake." Even exchanges in Southeast Asia are seeking cooperation with us because Hong Kong has rich listing resources and liquidity advantages, and they hope to leverage our market liquidity to revitalize their stock markets. Therefore, we are increasing our efforts to consider how to cooperate with regional exchanges.

"21st Century": The Shenzhen Stock Exchange recently stated that it welcomes Greater Bay Area companies listed in Hong Kong to list in Shenzhen. What are your thoughts on this?

Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: This statement first appeared in reports in 2024 and is not new. We have repeatedly handled the interworking and exchange between A-shares and H-shares, whether it is A-shares converting to H-shares or H-shares converting to A-shares. I am very familiar with the relevant schemes. This primarily depends on the company's own needs: A-share companies may need to use overseas platforms to expand their international business, or companies listed in Hong Kong may need to expand their business layout in the mainland market. These are all normal considerations. Regardless of the method adopted, as long as it can achieve complementarity, it is worth trying. We need to continuously enrich our product lines and offer more choices to attract more investors.

title_en: Bubble Mart AB side: Explosive sales and hidden capital flows.
body_en:
Recently, Pop Mart has been taking frequent actions, and the commercialization of IP is accelerating comprehensively. On June 10th, a first-generation collectible mint LABUBU was sold for a high price of 1.08 million yuan at the Yongle 2025 Spring Auction, immediately sparking a market frenzy. From the proliferation of counterfeit goods, scalpers rushing to buy, to the sell-out of the new store in Hangzhou, LABUBU's popularity continues to rise.

Against this background, Pop Mart is rapidly advancing its diversification strategy. On June 13th, Pop Mart's independent jewelry brand POPOP opened its first store in the luxury gathering Shanghai Grand Gateway Plaza. On June 14th, POPOP's first store in Beijing officially opened at the China World Trade Center. "We have always hoped to expand more possibilities through different categories, and jewelry is a very important category that we have been trying." Wang Ning, Chairman and CEO of Pop Mart International Group, said at the opening ceremony of POPOP's first store in Shanghai. It is not difficult to see that Pop Mart is trying to explore more diverse IP monetization.

On June 16th, Uniqlo announced the launch of a new collaborative series featuring Pop Mart's THE MONSTERS IP as the theme.

"The popularity of LABUBU is not only due to luck but also to Pop Mart's operational strategy. From the release of the March financial report to subsequent new product launches, flash events, and a series of actions, there is coherence," said Guo Yulian, General Manager of Mighty Jaxx China, in an interview with 21st Century Business Herald.

However, behind the frenzy of Pop Mart, the capital market presents a different picture. Since 2024, major shareholders including founder Wang Ning have started intensive reductions, especially in May this year when Fengqiao Capital cleared its entire pre-listing holdings, triggering a strong market reaction. This capital move contrasts sharply with the company's high-profile market performance.

This contrast has led to renewed doubts in the market about Pop Mart's continued innovation capabilities: How long can the heat of LABUBU be sustained? Can the company replicate the next explosive IP? These questions that have existed since the Molly era have been answered by Wang Ning multiple times. However, the market continues to question and inquire.

On June 17th, Pop Mart's stock price fell all the way, closing down 6.04% on the Hong Kong stock market, with a market value evaporating by about 22.3 billion Hong Kong dollars (about 20.4 billion yuan).

In just one week, Pop Mart continued to dominate social media.

On June 10th, the world's only mint LABUBU was sold for 1.08 million yuan at the Shanghai Yongle Spring Auction, while the limited edition brown LABUBU was sold for 820,000 yuan, breaking the record for toy auction prices. On the night of June 12th at 10 o'clock, Pop Mart released a series of new products online on its mini-program and official flagship store. There were queues in many places to buy blind boxes, and videos circulating on social platforms showed disputes over buying Pop Mart blind boxes. On June 15th, the new Pop Mart store in Xixi Tianjie, Hangzhou, opened, and it was reported that due to scalpers "grabbing boxes," the products were sold out within two hours, and the store had to close urgently.

However, the issue of scalpers has always been criticized by the public, and behind this is the high premium in the second-hand market. For example, the LABUBU and VANS collaboration released in 2024 for 599 yuan has been speculated to 31,999 yuan in the second-hand market, with a premium of over 52 times.

Not only is there a frenzy of buying in the domestic market, but the overseas market is also very lively. The offline Pop Mart store in South Korea also caused disputes due to crowded buyers queuing. In May of this year, due to high demand, there was even a "fight" incident at the Westfield Stratford City shopping center in London, UK. Due to the increased safety risks, Pop Mart has announced the suspension of LABUBU sales in the UK and plans to remove the product from all UK stores by June.

A deeper analysis of the logic behind the popularity of LABUBU shows that celebrity endorsements are just surface factors. Senior observers in the toy industry pointed out, "Different from imitators who simply rely on celebrity endorsements, LABUBU has successfully shaped a high-end image - it is seen by consumers as the 'Beverly Hills luxury brand,' and this brand tone is difficult to replicate."

However, behind the popularity of LABUBU, the issue of counterfeit goods is becoming a shadow. From the enforcement situation, Shanghai Pudong Airport Customs found 5,961 "fake Pop Mart" items without authorization to use the "POP MART" logo when inspecting a batch of express parcels, which infringed on the "POP MART" trademark, and the relevant products have been detained by customs. Reports of cases from local police and factories in Yiwu also show that the counterfeit goods industry chain has formed a large-scale operation. These acts of infringement not only harm the brand's interests but also reflect the chaos in the market under the frenzy.

Under the wave of LABUBU craze, more and more consumers are joining in.

"I have bought many products from Pop Mart, covering various IPs from blind boxes to action figures. Previously, my friends were not interested in this at all, but after LABUBU became popular, some friends asked me how to buy, I think they are just following the trend," said 90s-born Weiwei to the reporter.

Another new LABUBU fan, Xiaoyou, said, "It's cool to carry it out, and hanging LABUBU will attract a lot of attention."

"LABUBU has indeed spread toy culture to a deeper and wider level, and has also shown Asian designers to the overseas market," Guo Yulian analyzed, "The market will fluctuate, the wave in 2019 opened up the Chinese toy market for Pop Mart, and now LABUBU is the key to pushing Chinese toy culture to the overseas market." 

According to data from Taotian's "618" event, the entire toy industry has seen explosive growth. As of June 12th, six merchants in the toy industry had a total transaction amount exceeding one billion, nearly a hundred merchants had a total transaction amount exceeding tens of millions, 16 single products had a total transaction amount exceeding tens of millions, nearly 800 single products had a total transaction amount exceeding one million, and over 2,400 Taotian toy stores achieved a year-on-year triple-digit growth in total transaction amount, with the number of merchants with a total transaction amount exceeding one billion and the number of single products with a total transaction amount exceeding tens of millions surpassing the entire "618" cycle last year.

At the same time, this year, many companies such as Kayout, Brucoco, and 52TOYS have been rushing to IPO. "Overall, the market sentiment is quite good," Guo Yulian further pointed out, "The frenzy in the domestic market comes in waves, and Pop Mart has set the rhythm well in this wave of LABUBU. But I believe that these trend-following buyers will not repurchase after the heat of LABUBU dissipates. After the tide recedes, the buyers will still be the same, with some increase in numbers, but toy culture is not a demand of the mass market."

Many interviewees also hold similar views, believing that the toy market will return to rationality, and high heat is not sustainable. A person who transitioned from the toy industry told the reporter, "The toy field is too narrow."

However, taking advantage of this wave of popularity, Pop Mart has not been idle. The new jewelry brand POPOP opened by Pop Mart is also booming.

The jewelry store offers products from various popular IPs, such as Molly, DIMOO, CRYBABY, LABUBU, Twinkle Twinkle, Hirono, SKULL PANDA, etc. It is reported that the LABUBU, Hirono, and Molly series, which are popular in Beijing stores, have been sold out, especially the LABUBU bracelet is about to be sold out.

"This jewelry store is aimed at converting loyal IP fans, rather than competing for traditional jewelry store customers," said Guo Yulian, General Manager of Mighty Jaxx China, in an interview with 21st Century Business Herald. "Pop Mart's move is not to expand its customer base outside the circle but to dig deeper into its own consumer base. By exploring the consumption power of fans through different product lines, functions, pricing, etc., Pop Mart is tapping into the consumption power of fans."

She further explained, "Artistic IPs like LABUBU can give fans more emotional resonance, and fan loyalty is relatively high. Because everyone supports a real person, it's a bit like a fan circle. Ordinary consumers see LABUBU as if it came out of nowhere, but in reality, its creator Long Jiasheng has been deeply involved in the toy circle for a long time. He has been interacting with consumers for over a decade, so when new fans enter the scene, there are stories to look back on."

Not only the jewelry store, in February of this year, the global first store of Hirono Xiao Ye landed in Shanghai's Central Plaza; in May, Pop Mart's global first collection store POP MART COLLECTION landed in Chengdu SKP.

The heat of LABUBU can also be seen in surrounding sales. According to official data from Taotian, in May, the search volume for "LABUBU doll clothes" exceeded 500,000 times, with a total transaction amount exceeding one million yuan, an increase of over 100% compared to April. At the same time, derivative products such as "LABUBU protective case," "LABUBU display box," and even "LABUBU safety seat" have rich supply on Taobao.

The market's frenzy and soaring stock prices, but on the other hand, shareholders have quietly reduced their holdings. In October 2024, there was a relatively intensive wave of reductions, including Wang Ning. Data from the Hong Kong Stock Exchange shows that Pop Mart's major shareholders GWF Holding, Pop Mart Hehuo Holding Limited, Pop Mart Director Si De, and Wende have all reduced their holdings of Pop Mart shares.

Among them, GWF Holding is fully owned by UBS Trustees (B.V.I.) Ltd., a trust of Pop Mart founder Wang Ning, and Pop Mart Hehuo Holding Limited is 40.96% owned by Wang Ning. Through the combined reduction of 21.7 million shares by these two companies, Wang Ning cashed out approximately 1.562 billion Hong Kong dollars.

In May of this year, Fengqiao Capital cleared all its holdings of Pop Mart shares purchased before listing, attracting widespread attention in the market. According to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange's equity disclosure, Fengqiao Capital sold 11.91 million shares in three large transactions from April 30th to May 7th, cashing out a total of 2.267 billion Hong Kong dollars.

Perhaps due to this impact, Pop Mart's stock price has been under pressure. The stock price of Pop Mart, which has been soaring all year, fell by a cumulative 6.77% from April 30th to May 7th. Even a year earlier, Fengqiao Capital founding partner Tu Zheng had already started reducing his holdings of Pop Mart.

In May 2024, Tu Zheng reduced his holdings of 16 million shares of Pop Mart at a price of 35.1 Hong Kong dollars per share, cashing out approximately 562 million Hong Kong dollars. In October 2024, Tu Zheng once again reduced his holdings of 5 million shares of Pop Mart at a price of 58.8 Hong Kong dollars per share, cashing out approximately 294 million Hong Kong dollars.

However, it is worth mentioning that in June of this year, Citi reiterated its buy rating on Pop Mart, raising its target price from 162 Hong Kong dollars to 308 Hong Kong dollars. Citi believes that Pop Mart's iconic IP is gaining increasing global recognition, and its diversified IP strategy should lay the foundation for long-term sustained growth, while the launch of new products may also become a short-term catalyst.

However, the continuous reduction of holdings by shareholders has once again raised doubts about whether Pop Mart can continue to launch popular IPs.

"The current valuation is a bit high, but this is related to the overall environment," Guo Yulian believes that the value of Pop Mart lies not in how hot LABUBU is but in continuously creating the next "LABUBU." "Pop Mart is actually a platform, and as it develops and grows, more artists are willing to sign with Pop Mart and operate their IPs, creating a positive cycle. This also allows Pop Mart to continue discovering high-quality IPs and operating them, and of course, it may take a few more years to create another 'LABUBU,' but it is worth looking forward to."

(Author: Yi Jiaying Editor: Bao Fangming)

title_en: The province's campaign to protect minors has been launched.
body_en:
This newspaper, Taizhou, June 17th (Reporter Chen Jiuren) On the 17th, the province-wide publicity month for the protection of minors and the promotion of child-friendly activities, "Protecting Minors in Zhejiang and Warming Children's Hearts," was launched in Taizhou. This is the first publicity month event after the implementation of the "Zhejiang Province Regulations on the Protection of Minors," aiming to jointly create a good social environment conducive to the healthy growth of minors.
At the event, the top ten "small and warm" public welfare projects for children, such as the Alibaba Youth Cloud Assistance Program and the "Hello Taizhou" mobile children care project, were announced. A cooperation agreement was signed for the construction of a collaborative community for psychological health services for families, schools, communities, and medical institutions under the theme of "Warming Children's Hearts." The Children's Observation Team also issued a proposal for the construction of child-friendly cities.
The protection of minors is a systematic project. In order to carry out the publicity and implementation of the regulations, the provincial government's Women and Children's Work Committee has taken the lead in promoting legal publicity through activities such as entering villages (communities), households, schools, hospitals, enterprises, and key locations, forming a working pattern led by the government, with the participation of various groups and the entire society. For five consecutive years, Taizhou has included projects for caring for the growth of young people in the city government's livelihood projects, taking the lead in implementing a system for preventing harm to minors in the province, and issuing the country's first white paper on mandatory parenting education. With the construction of a national child-friendly city as the link, a full-chain, full-cycle, and full-coverage protection scene for minors is being created.

title_en: The situation in the Middle East is deteriorating, but the overall market remains stable.
body_en:
Wei Jun
The situation in the Middle East has deteriorated, with Asian stock markets generally falling on Tuesday. The Hong Kong stock market rose initially and then fell, opening high in the morning and rising to 24,131 points, an increase of about 71 points. It later dropped to 23,880 points before the close, a decrease of 188 points, closing at 23,980 points, down 80 points or 0.34% for the day, with a reduced turnover of 202.144 billion yuan. However, the Hang Seng Index is still above the 20-day moving average of 23,723 points, and the consolidation at high levels led by institutional investors remains unchanged.
Except for the Utilities Index, all sector indices of the Hang Seng Index softened. The recently strong Financials Index also fell by 0.7%, facing greater pressure. In terms of active stocks, the recently strong stock, Meituan (9992), showed a significant pullback, falling by 6% for the day with a turnover of 6.238 billion yuan; Alibaba (9988) rose by 1.68%, performing well with a turnover of 6.875 billion yuan.
There was a net inflow of 6.302 billion yuan from Northbound funds, marking the 15th consecutive day of net inflows. China Construction Bank (0939) continued to see a net inflow of 1.122 billion yuan, while Alibaba saw a net inflow of 599 million yuan. In the comprehensive enterprise sector, CITIC (0267), Beijing Enterprises (0392), and Shanghai Industrial (0363) performed well against the market trend, rising by about 1.4% to 1.6%, as Northbound funds continue to favor the value rebound of central and state-owned enterprises.
Data shows that Hong Kong's IPO fundraising of 108.7 billion Hong Kong dollars in the first half of the year topped the global rankings, and the market anticipates a continued strong trend in the second half of the year. Sany Heavy Industry (600031.SH), which submitted an application to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on May 22, is expected to boost demand from international investors in the engineering machinery sector. Its subsidiary, Sany International (0631), has shown strong performance in recent weeks and can be accumulated in stages during market adjustments.
Sany Heavy Industry to be listed in Hong Kong
Sany Heavy Industry is a private enterprise (with a market value of 152.8 billion yuan in A-shares as of yesterday's closing), holding a 66.36% stake in Sany International (with a market value of 22 billion yuan as of yesterday's closing). Sany Heavy Industry is the third largest globally and the largest in China in the engineering machinery sector, focusing on the research, development, manufacturing, and sales of machinery products such as excavators, concrete machinery, cranes, piling machinery, and road machinery.
Since the beginning of the year, the export of engineering machinery has been in a growth period, with emerging economies in the Middle East, Central Asia, and Latin America vigorously improving infrastructure. Additionally, the demand for infrastructure repair due to geopolitical military conflicts is favorable for the growth of engineering machinery orders.
Sany International recently announced that as of the end of March this year, the unaudited attributable profit to the owners of the parent company increased by 23.2% year-on-year to 635 million yuan (RMB, the same below). Revenue increased by 14.6% year-on-year to 5.876 billion yuan. The group stated that the comprehensive implementation of globalization, digitalization, and low-carbon strategies has significantly increased the revenue of the group's port machinery, oil and gas equipment, silicon energy products, and overseas mining truck revenue. In addition, the acquisition of the lithium energy business completed in July last year has brought new sources of income. The group pointed out that the comprehensive implementation of digital operations, the implementation of measures to improve quality and efficiency, reduce costs, and control expenses, have increased the gross profit margin of excavators, port machinery, oil and gas equipment, and silicon energy products.
Sany International retraces, suitable for accumulation in stages
Sany International closed at 6.81 Hong Kong dollars yesterday, down by 1 cent, with a turnover of 80.2 million yuan. The stock has risen from the 5 yuan level to a recent high of 7.08 yuan in the past two months, a cumulative increase of over 40%. The current price-earnings ratio is 18.6 times, the forecasted price-earnings ratio is 9 times, the dividend yield is 4.2%, the price-to-book ratio is 1.69 times, and the valuation is not considered expensive. It is suitable for accumulation during retracements, with a target price of 7.50 yuan.
The opinions expressed in this article are those of the author and do not represent the position of the newspaper.

title_en: Zhejiang Consumer Protection Commission interviewed multiple platforms.
body_en:
Hangzhou News (Reporter Shi Benyun) In response to the issue of a high piracy rate of 35.8% in platform online book purchases discovered in the previous investigation (see "Some Platform Self-operated Stores Actually Selling Pirated Children's Books" on page 1 of China Consumer News on June 4), the Zhejiang Consumer Rights Protection Committee held a meeting on June 13 to report the relevant information of the piracy book consumption investigation. Representatives from platforms such as Douyin, JD.com, Taobao, Tmall, Pinduoduo, and WeChat Video attended the meeting and responded to the issues raised in the report.

On the eve of this year's Children's Day, the Zhejiang Consumer Rights Protection Committee, in collaboration with the Zhejiang Children's Publishing House, conducted a special investigation on pirated books, involving multiple platforms such as Douyin, JD.com, Taobao, Tmall, Pinduoduo, and WeChat Video. A total of 478 children's literary books published by the Zhejiang Children's Publishing House were purchased, and after verification by the publishing house, 171 pirated books were found, resulting in a piracy rate of 35.8%.

The relevant person in charge of the Zhejiang Children's Publishing House revealed the harm of pirated books to the entire industry at the meeting, calling on major platforms to increase penalties for selling pirated works, establish stricter copyright protection mechanisms, strengthen piracy complaint handling, and curb the circulation of pirated books from the source.

The relevant person in charge of the Zhejiang Consumer Rights Protection Committee proposed three opinions on strengthening the governance of pirated books on platforms: first, to raise awareness. Pirated books seriously disrupt the order of the publishing market and threaten the physical and mental health of minors. Platforms should enhance their awareness, take proactive measures to govern, shift from post-punishment to preventive measures in piracy governance, truly prioritize consumer rights protection, and have a "zero tolerance" policy towards pirated books. Second, to improve platform rules. Platforms should carefully review relevant laws and regulations such as the E-commerce Law, examine whether current platform rules meet regulatory requirements and governance needs, and whether there is a gap with the expectations of the people. They should further refine and improve regulations related to book review, violation handling, etc., and strengthen the responsibility of the platform. Third, to explore long-term mechanisms. It is suggested that relevant platforms work together with publishing houses to explore long-term governance mechanisms for pirated books, establish a "green channel" with publishing houses, promptly respond to and effectively handle complaints related to pirated books, strengthen monitoring and governance of abnormal behaviors such as low-price sales and shell operations, and form a joint force to combat pirated books.

Next, the Zhejiang Consumer Rights Protection Committee will continue to monitor the governance of pirated books on platforms and conduct "look-backs" as needed, striving to create a safe and trustworthy online book purchasing environment for consumers. At the same time, it will further unite the forces of publishing houses, platforms, and other parties to promote collaborative governance of pirated books, and build a solid copyright protection barrier to promote the high-quality development of the cultural industry.

title_en: Zhejiang Yongkang helps foreign trade enterprises reduce costs and burdens.
body_en:
In response to the changing global trade market environment this year, the Market Supervision Bureau of Yongkang City, Zhejiang Province, has recently focused on the pain points of foreign trade enterprises, opened up new paths for internal trade, and fully supported enterprises in reducing burdens, increasing efficiency, stabilizing orders, and expanding markets.

Proactively building an e-commerce platform for external sales to internal sales, expanding the sales channels for foreign trade enterprises. The bureau relies on the JD platform's billion-yuan special procurement plan to build the "Hardware Foreign Trade Excellent Products for Internal Sales" platform, and has successively held events such as the Tmall Home Yongkang Industrial Belt Selection Conference and the Taobao Flash Sale Special, promoting the launch of a special exhibition area for "Source Factory Excellent Products · Export Quality" on the 1688 platform.

Actively constructing a cross-border testing and certification system to facilitate the circulation between domestic and foreign markets. The bureau utilizes the National Hardware Tools and Category Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Center and Quality Station to open a "CCC Certification Testing" green channel for electric tools, and introduces convenient measures such as "institutional errands" and "shared laboratories" to simplify the certification process for products transitioning from export to internal sales, saving operating costs for foreign trade enterprises.

Strengthening intellectual property protection to stimulate the transformation momentum of enterprises. The bureau relies on Zhejiang's first Hardware Industry Intellectual Property Fast Maintenance Center to develop a "fast pre-examination" channel for appearance patents, providing one-on-one filing guidance for key foreign trade enterprises to accelerate the transformation of their innovative achievements. Since the beginning of this year, it has helped 67 key foreign trade enterprises to handle patent fast pre-examination filings, with the average authorization time compressed to 5 working days, a 90% reduction compared to the conventional process.

title_en: Notice on holding the 2024 Academic Annual Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association (Second Round)
body_en: Relevant units: Pharmaceutical excipients are an important foundation in China's pharmaceutical industry, and are one of the key factors determining the quality of generic drugs and the high-quality development of innovative formulations. The security of the supply chain of pharmaceutical excipients used in high-end formulations in China urgently requires the strengthening of technical innovation and industrial support for domestically produced pharmaceutical excipients. At the same time, ensuring the quality of clinical medication, reducing drug costs, and alleviating the pressure on medical insurance to a large extent also depend on the improvement of the quality of domestically produced pharmaceutical excipients. In line with the principle of "promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new productive forces of the pharmaceutical industry," the "2024 Annual Academic Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association," organized by the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association, is scheduled to be held in Hefei, Anhui Province from November 8th to 10th, 2024. This academic conference will feature conference reports in the fields of materials science related to pharmaceutical excipients, innovative drugs, and innovative formulations, analyzing the development difficulties and innovations of pharmaceutical excipients; inviting authoritative experts to deeply discuss the in vivo processes of pharmaceutical excipients and drug delivery carriers, as well as the improvement and innovation of excipient quality. The conference will set up expert venues and young scholar sub-venues on the themes of "Pharmaceutical Excipients, Packaging Materials, and Drug Delivery Devices," "New Materials, New Carriers, and Innovative Formulations," and "Pharmaceutical Excipients and Innovative Drugs," promoting the wide participation of enterprises, academia, and young scholars to jointly focus on the technological innovation and industrial research and development of pharmaceutical excipients. title_en: LC: 800G optical module drives market recovery in Q2 2025.
body_en: Official WeChat Official Weibo Recently, LightCounting released the "June 2025 Quarterly Update Report on the Optical Communication Market." The report predicts that although the market performance was flat in the first quarter, optical module sales in the second quarter will increase by 10% compared to the previous quarter, with the main growth coming from 800G Ethernet optical modules (as shown in the chart). The 1.6T optical modules, not reflected in the chart, will also be shipped for the first time, contributing a small amount of revenue to the market. As Amazon and Meta shift to higher-speed modules, sales of 400G Ethernet modules will decline. Sales of 400G and 800G active optical cables (AOC) also remain strong. In addition, DWDM, FTTx, and wireless front-haul (WFH) optical modules rebounded after a seasonally slow first quarter, driving market growth in the second quarter. However, the telecom market is not expected to significantly recover. In the first quarter of 2025, the top 15 global telecom service providers (TSPs) saw flat revenue, but capital expenditures decreased by 5% year-on-year. The three major Chinese operators - China Mobile, China Telecom, and China Unicom - have all announced cuts in capital spending this year, with the total expenditure of the three companies in 2025 amounting to $39.8 billion, a 10% decrease from 2024. Leading operators in revenue growth in the first quarter of 2025 include Softbank (7% year-on-year growth), Deutsche Telekom (3% growth), and China Unicom (3% growth). In contrast, Telecom Italia saw a 19% year-on-year revenue decline, while Telefonica saw a 12% decline, mainly due to selling businesses to focus on core assets. M&A activity is becoming increasingly active, with U.S. telecom operators acquiring fiber assets, while European operators are optimizing their layouts by divesting non-core businesses. In terms of technology giants, Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle all significantly increased their spending in the first quarter of 2025 compared to the same period last year. Among them, Oracle's spending soared by 233% year-on-year, but it is the smallest in scale among the top five companies - with spending of less than $11 billion for the full year of 2024, while Meta and Amazon were $39 billion and $83 billion respectively. Oracle's first-quarter spending reached $5.6 billion, exceeding 50% of its full-year spending in 2024. Alibaba's first-quarter revenue was $32.5 billion, a 5% year-on-year increase, but a 17% decrease from the previous quarter. The company announced that it will invest over 380 billion yuan (approximately $53 billion) in AI infrastructure construction over the next three years. Baidu's revenue was $4.5 billion, a 3% year-on-year increase, but a 5% decrease from the previous quarter, with spending of $398 million, a 41% year-on-year increase and a 23% quarter-on-quarter increase. Tencent's revenue was $24.7 billion, a 12% year-on-year increase, a 3% quarter-on-quarter increase, with spending of $3.7 billion, an 89% year-on-year increase, but a 36% quarter-on-quarter decrease.
