title_en: Guangzhou will strengthen policy guidance and capital support in key areas such as AI.
body_en:
Guangzhou will strengthen financial support for market entities in the fields of artificial intelligence and low-altitude economy.
On June 17, Guangzhou held a press conference for the 11th Guangzhou International Investment Conference. The 11th Guangzhou International Investment Conference will be held from June 26 to 27. As of June 16, more than 800 guests have registered to attend, including senior executives from Fortune 500 companies, central enterprises, and the top 500 Chinese companies, as well as representatives from enterprises in new productive sectors such as artificial intelligence, low-altitude economy, new energy storage, biomedicine, high-end equipment, and clean technology.
Currently, Guangzhou is focusing on building a "12218" modern industrial system, including 15 strategic industrial clusters, 6 future industries, and 8 modern service industries, and has established 5 key industrial development offices. Yang Xiaoyan, Deputy Director of the Development and Reform Commission of Guangzhou, stated at the meeting that Guangzhou will introduce a "package" of policies in the field of artificial intelligence and low-altitude economy.
In terms of artificial intelligence, Guangzhou will introduce special policies for the development of the artificial intelligence industry, innovatively launch "four vouchers linkage" including computing power vouchers, data vouchers, scenario vouchers, and model vouchers to reduce the research and development operating costs of market entities. At the same time, Guangzhou will establish an artificial intelligence industry investment fund, focusing on algorithm research and development, computing power infrastructure, industry applications, and providing full-cycle financing support to market entities through "angel investment + VC follow-up + Pre-IPO relay".
In the low-altitude economy sector, the focus will be on building a "full-cycle service" ecosystem. By constructing a low-altitude industry fund matrix, mobilizing social capital to focus on research and development, manufacturing, and operational services, enterprises will be provided with a full chain of financial support including equity financing, debt financing, and listing incubation. Additionally, Guangzhou will accelerate the issuance and implementation of the "Measures for Promoting the High-Quality Development of the Low-Altitude Economy" to strengthen policy support in areas such as research and development, manufacturing, and airworthiness certification. In terms of infrastructure construction, efforts will be made to accelerate the construction of "1+5+100" low-altitude take-off and landing sites and new infrastructure projects such as low-altitude intelligent networking.
Reporters learned that Guangzhou is strengthening policy guidance for key industries, formulating and implementing a batch of special policies for intelligent connected new energy vehicles, specialty semiconductor processes, biomedicine, and other industries. The city is also enhancing carrier support, nurturing and constructing the first batch of 10 characteristic benchmark industrial parks, and is preparing to launch the second batch of parks soon. Furthermore, capital support is being strengthened through the establishment of industrial development funds and the promotion of activities such as the "Gathering Chain in Guangzhou, Setting Sail in the Bay Area" strategic industrial cluster supply and demand docking, and the "One Month, One Chain" investment and financing service for specialized and innovative enterprises.
Wang Yuyin, Deputy Director of the Industrial and Information Technology Bureau of Guangzhou, stated that from January to April this year, industrial investment in Guangzhou increased by 15% year-on-year. In terms of attracting leading enterprises and major projects, advanced manufacturing projects such as TCL Huaxing T9, Zengxin, Rongjie Lithium Battery, Gaojing Solar, and Maisheng Medical have been successively constructed and put into operation. In addition, Guangzhou is strengthening the attraction of industrial chains. In recent years, efforts have been made to stabilize, supplement, and strengthen the automotive industry chain, attracting a number of core automotive component companies such as Continental Electronics and Beixin LiDAR. Since 2024, 64 new projects have been connected to the automotive industry chain, with 40 signed contracts and an expected total investment exceeding 18 billion yuan, driving the establishment of the "Huawang Automobile" project in cooperation with Guangzhou Automobile Group and Huawei in Nansha. By relying on leading enterprises such as Guangzhou Pharmaceutical, Lejin, and Yuexin, a group of upstream and downstream enterprises have been gathered, focusing on local high-quality medical resources, attracting a group of high-quality enterprises such as Aoluxin and Dongze Medical to settle in, and building a good ecosystem of close cooperation between upstream and downstream enterprises and the development of large, medium, and small enterprises. From January to April this year, Guangzhou added more than 300 industrial projects with a total planned investment exceeding 76 billion yuan.
According to Han Zhenxiang, Deputy Director of the Guangzhou Municipal Bureau of Commerce, from January to April this year, Guangzhou introduced 625 new industrial investment projects with a total expected investment of 161.5 billion yuan, including 70 projects with investments or revenues exceeding 1 billion yuan. The total investment in manufacturing projects in the city accounts for over 50%. The total investment in domestic projects in the city ranks first in the province. There were 2,664 newly established foreign-funded enterprises, an increase of 14.9%, with actual foreign investment of 11.54 billion yuan, showing growth in both the number of new foreign-funded enterprises and the actual use of foreign investment. Strategic cooperation agreements have been reached with large enterprises such as the Investment Promotion Bureau Group, Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China, and Tencent, and investment projects from companies such as Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Pengrui Li, Ant Group, Hikvision, and Douyin have been successively implemented.
In the first half of the year, Ant Group's "Dual Centers" and Douyin's South China Innovation Base settled in Haizhu District, Guangzhou, which has already attracted numerous platform companies. Yang Xiao, Deputy District Mayor of the district, mentioned that in addition to Ant's "Dual Centers" and Douyin South China, this year the district also landed a batch of new projects for the first time, including Kuaishou E-commerce, Hellobike Smart Driving, and Shanghai Douyin E-commerce. Starting in 2021, Haizhu District took the lead in establishing the country's first artificial intelligence large-scale model application demonstration zone, with 17 models approved, covering education, transportation, language, and other fields, ranking first in the province. At the same time, Haizhu District has implemented an industrial ecological prosperity plan, nurturing 65 backbone enterprises in the new generation information technology industry with a value of over 100 million yuan, forming a situation of "leading the head, supporting the backbone, and prospering the small and medium-sized enterprises".
Chen Chao, Secretary-General of the Guangzhou Development Zone Management Committee, stated that the Guangzhou Development Zone is improving the investment and financing system of "state-owned enterprise investment + industrial fund guidance + social capital", establishing a 5 billion yuan science and technology innovation mother fund. A scene "opportunity list" has been established, relying on the annual construction volume of over 200 billion in the entire region to accelerate the creation of industrial application scenarios for artificial intelligence, unmanned driving, hydrogen energy storage, low-altitude economy, and other industries.
From January to May, the Guangzhou Development Zone and Huangpu District signed 170 new high-quality projects; the total investment under agreement reached 93.3 billion yuan, an increase of 13%. This includes the hundred-billion-yuan project of the Tibet-Guangdong DC, as well as six billion-yuan projects such as GAC Flying Car. Manufacturing projects such as the headquarters base of Siyuan Shares and the high-performance composite material base of Jinfahao have successively started construction. The actual utilization of foreign capital in the district was 869 million US dollars, accounting for 47% of the total in Guangzhou. The number of newly registered business entities exceeded 35,700, a significant increase of 73.9%, with the total number of business entities exceeding 300,000 for the first time.

title_en: "Three fees in one" are collected with water in Zunyi City to improve the efficiency of garbage disposal fee collection.
body_en:
Report (Correspondents Lu Lihua, Zhang Ji, Xiao Jun) "Before, we had to go to the window to pay the garbage disposal fee, now it is deducted together with the water bill, which is much more convenient." On June 12, Zunyi citizen Ms. Wang opened her phone and found that in addition to the water and sewage treatment fees, there was also a urban garbage disposal fee when she paid her water bill through the "Guizhou Taxation" WeChat public account. Ms. Wang is very satisfied with this convenient payment method.

In the past, the urban household garbage disposal fee was collected by multiple departments, with inconsistent standards, making collection difficult and costly. To solve this problem, in January 2024, under the guidance of the Guizhou Provincial Taxation Bureau of the State Administration of Taxation, the Zunyi Taxation Bureau proposed the "collected with water" model - the garbage disposal fee is collected by the water supply enterprise, achieving the combined collection of "water fee + sewage treatment fee + garbage disposal fee".

To ensure the smooth implementation of the combined collection of the three fees, the tax department of Zunyi City leveraged its own advantages, provided support in setting the fee standards and data provision, and after extensive consultation and holding public hearings, issued new standards for the urban household garbage disposal fee in the central urban area of Zunyi City. At the same time, the tax department signed a commission collection agreement with the water supply company, clarified the requirements related to the collection process, and carried out policy publicity and interpretation through government websites, news media, community outreach, etc., to ensure that payers understand the policy and know how to operate.

Since the implementation of the collected with water model, the amount of urban household garbage disposal fees collected in the central urban area of Zunyi City has significantly increased, collection costs have decreased, and cases of under-collection and mismanagement have been effectively improved. At the same time, the payment method is more convenient than before, residents can "pay with one click" through online channels such as WeChat, Alipay, and Qian Nong Yun.

"The collected with water model not only improves the efficiency of tax collection and management, but also promotes the enhancement of public environmental awareness, maximally implementing the principle of 'polluter pays', and further demonstrating the fairness of payment." said Kang Ying, Director of the Non-Tax Revenue Department of the Guizhou Provincial Taxation Bureau.

title_en: Build a "bridge" for African youth to start businesses in China.
body_en:
Not long ago, energy storage products from a new energy company in Changsha, Hunan, crossed the ocean to the Republic of Mali (hereinafter referred to as "Mali"), bringing light to the local people. In addition to a container of products, the company is also establishing a presence in the capital of Mali, Bamako, and will use its industrial park as a pilot project to build a complete solar power system, gradually expanding to surrounding rural areas.

This project, which has attracted the attention of the people of Mali, would not have been possible without the efforts of Aboubacar Garba KONTE, the head of the incubation station of the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base in Mali.

On June 13, at an important special event of the 4th China-Africa Economic and Trade Expo, the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Dialogue, Konte was named an expert of the "Hunan Xiangjiang New Area-China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base Think Tank." This is a recognition of his contributions to China-Africa economic and trade cooperation.

In 2016, Konte came to Beijing University of Science and Technology to pursue a Ph.D. in management. At that time, he never imagined that this period of study would completely change his life trajectory, and even bring new hope to his homeland in Africa.

During his studies, Konte visited a Chinese solar factory. In the factory, rows of solar products were shining brightly in the sunlight, and workers were assembling new energy products. This scene deeply impressed him, "The most abundant resource in Africa is sunlight, but my hometown is plunged into darkness due to a lack of electricity."

Only less than 5% of the population in Mali can have stable electricity, and the electrification rate in rural areas is as low as 20%. At night, many children can only do their homework by candlelight, and hospitals sometimes cannot operate normally due to power shortages. Konte realized that solar energy could be one of the key elements to change the lives of African people.

In 2022, after graduating with a Ph.D., Konte did not choose to return to his home country for employment, but instead went to Guangzhou and established a technology transfer company, hoping to introduce China's clean energy technology to Africa. However, the road to entrepreneurship was not smooth - policy coordination, fundraising, market promotion, each step was full of challenges.

Two years ago, he walked into the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base in Hunan Xiangjiang New Area for the first time, and the atmosphere here impressed him. "This place not only provides office space, but also connects with Chinese companies, applies for policy support, and even helps foreign entrepreneurs solve the problem of their children's education!" In just a few months, he decided to move his company and family from Guangzhou to Changsha.

The China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base provided him with an expert apartment, assisted in business registration, and even helped his children contact an international school. With no worries, Konte began to push forward his "African Solar Plan." With the help of the base, he visited more than 10 new energy companies in Changsha and eventually reached a cooperation agreement with a solar technology company in Hunan.

"Our goal is not only to sell products, but to empower Africans with technology for sustainable development," Konte said. Today, he frequently travels between China and Mali, coordinating with the Chinese supply chain while negotiating with local governments and chambers of commerce on landing matters. In addition to cooperation in new energy, he has also introduced sesame from his hometown to the Chinese market.

Konte's story is a microcosm of the struggles of many African youth in China. Leading the way for these African youth to start their businesses in Hunan is the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base created by the Hunan Xiangjiang New Area.

Currently, the base has established contacts with over 200 government agencies, chambers of commerce, and companies from more than 50 African countries, supporting the incubation and cultivation of many African youth entrepreneurship projects. The base team follows up on projects through online and offline research, face-to-face meetings with key project companies, and covers various fields such as economy and trade, agriculture, culture, education, energy, and healthcare; hosting nearly 80 online and offline events related to China-Africa cooperation, including the China (Changsha)-Nigeria Investment and Trade Promotion Conference, with an average of cross-border "business matchmaking meetings" every week.

As the results of China-Africa youth innovation and entrepreneurship gradually emerge, the base is attracting more and more attention, becoming a "super hub" for resource connection.

"A lot of African agricultural products are very attractive in China, with a sense of mystery, so smooth channels are crucial," said Lei Ting, head of the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base. In the tide of China-Africa cooperation, such "bridges" are becoming increasingly important.

During the 2022 "Double 11" period, the base, together with the United Nations International Trade Center and Alibaba Group, launched the "Digital Village" project plan, importing a batch of high-quality coffee beans from countries such as Rwanda and Ethiopia in Africa, roasting them domestically, and then making them into drip coffee. In just two minutes in the live broadcast room, nearly 20,000 boxes of this coffee were sold, making the farmers in the country of origin ecstatic.

There is a medical equipment manufacturing company in Hunan Xiangjiang New Area that mainly produces oxygen equipment for hospitals, which has attracted the interest of customers in Algeria. However, due to the long distance between the two parties and the lack of face-to-face meetings, there was some hesitation when it came to discussing orders.

In 2023, the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base invited a counselor from the Algerian Embassy to visit Hunan and inspect this company. In the presence of the counselor, the company's head connected via video with a buyer from Algeria, confirming the reliability of the cooperation and facilitating the project.

Today, the office of young entrepreneurs from Algeria in the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base is thriving.

It is reported that there are more than 20 young people from 8 countries currently stationed at the base, a considerable number of whom started their businesses after studying in China, as well as some young people recommended by various African embassies and some young people from Africa who have already had economic and trade exchanges with China. After several years of cooperation, the base has successfully landed more than 30 projects.

"These (African youth) come to China with dreams, and then bring China's technology, experience, and friendship back to Africa. And Changsha, with its open policies and inclusive environment, has become their first choice," Lei Ting said.

title_en: Farewell to low-price internal competition, 618 can go further · Chongqing Daily Digital Newspaper
body_en:
In 2025, the 618 shopping festival arrived earlier than before, kicking off on May 13th. In addition to being labeled as the "longest promotion in history," this year's 618 holds another special significance - it is the first 618 after the country clearly set the tone of "anti-internal competition."

Looking back, 618 can be seen as a typical example of internal competition. In the early years, e-commerce platforms used discounts to attract customers and rapidly expand their user base in order to seize market share. As more platforms entered the market, the competition for low prices continued to intensify, with some platforms requiring merchants to offer the "lowest price on the entire network" and even engaging in "either-or" exclusive competition. At the same time, the complex and cumbersome rules of discounts and the endless pre-sale routines not only exhausted consumers' patience but also further exacerbated internal competition within the industry.

When the early dividends dried up, 618 finally reached a standstill. Among those most exhausted were the merchants - on one hand, engaging in low-price competition inevitably compressed profit margins; on the other hand, those with high traffic prices won, and the threshold for participating in major promotions continued to rise. In this situation, merchants were making less and less money, either cutting back on quality and service to maintain a low-price advantage, or "raising prices first, then discounting." As a result, consumers' shopping experience was no longer guaranteed, and the attractiveness of major promotion events was greatly reduced.

At this stage, 618 has fundamentally relied too much on exchanging growth for low prices, leading the industry into a zero-sum game. In fact, this kind of inefficient and repetitive "internal competition" has become a major obstacle to China's current economic transformation and upgrading. Therefore, last year's Central Political Bureau meeting and other meetings clearly called for the rectification of "internal competition," and this year's National People's Congress even included "comprehensively rectifying 'internal competition'" in the Government Work Report, demonstrating the decision-makers' firm determination to combat internal competition.

From a macroeconomic perspective, China is currently in a critical period of transition from old to new driving forces. Against this backdrop, the development model relying on low prices and scale expansion has reached its limit and urgently needs to shift towards innovation-driven and quality improvement. For example, last year's 618, although the promotion period was extended to nearly a month, experienced negative growth for the first time in 16 years. This market feedback is a strong warning against past strategies. If companies invest a large amount of resources in price wars rather than cultivating core competitiveness, it will inevitably lead to the industry lingering in low-level and repetitive competition, hindering the optimization and upgrading of the entire economic structure.

When faced with challenges, one must seek change. This year's 618 marks a turning point. In terms of activity rules, Taobao has changed from "cross-store discounts" to "official discounts"; in terms of platform relationships, JD Logistics has integrated with the Taobao system, and Taobao fully supports WeChat Pay... Platforms are no longer simply competing on low prices but are focusing on improving service efficiency and promoting resource sharing, reducing the tense competition and reshaping the ecosystem together. These changes are not only an active exploration of sustainable development models under policy guidance but also reflect the e-commerce industry's positive response to changes in market demand.

618 should serve as a mirror, allowing every industry to see its past and future. Take the food delivery industry, for example - the "money-burning war" between platforms is very similar to what 618 used to be; in addition, the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers recently issued a proposal explicitly opposing the disorderly "price war" among car companies. This indicates that the phenomenon of low prices, low quality, and low-level competition still exists, and there is still a long way to go in rectifying "internal competition." This not only requires consensus within the industry but also relies on a combination of loosening and tightening, comprehensive governance, and multi-party efforts to build a new paradigm of healthy competition.

By bidding farewell to low-price internal competition, we can go further. In the market, competition will never end, but good competition will elevate the industry rather than drag it down like a vortex. When we call for letting go of the obsession with low prices, we are actually calling for a return to values. Competing on value will inevitably be more challenging than competing on price, but success in this area means technological iteration and industry-wide advancement. Remember, falling downward may be fast in the short term, but it leads to the abyss; climbing higher, no matter how high the mountain, will eventually lead to the summit.
