title_en: "Double engine" drives this shopping festival (picture)
body_en:
The annual mid-year shopping festival, "618," is in full swing, with online and offline promotions battling for over twenty days. When "low prices" become the norm, this year's "618" sees new, attention-grabbing phenomena emerging beyond price wars: "export-to-domestic" goods and "new national brands" are powerfully taking center stage, becoming new engines to drive consumption growth. This annual consumer feast is quietly evolving into an important window to observe China's industrial transformation and domestic demand potential.

Pressure Forces Change
Foreign Trade Enterprises' "Internal Circulation" Breakthrough Battle

The U.S.'s tariff hammer, coupled with the uncertainty of the global trade environment, has sent a chilling wave through many Chinese foreign trade enterprises that have long relied on overseas orders. Returning to the vast domestic demand market has become their inevitable choice to seek survival.

■ Case 1: The "Dual Circulation" Path of "Carpet Town"

Cuihuangkou Town in Wuqing District, Tianjin, a small town of less than 100 square kilometers, once accounted for half of the country's carpet production, truly earning its title as "Carpet Town." Over 1,200 carpet enterprises form the industrial cornerstone of the town, with hundreds of large-scale enterprises focusing on overseas markets. However, U.S. tariffs exceeding 30% have put immense pressure on enterprises primarily exporting to the U.S.

Liu Mingjun, born in the 1980s and the third-generation head of a family carpet business, deeply understands this: "Exporting to the U.S. is on a 'lifeline,' and foreign trade business is mainly in a wait-and-see mode." Under these circumstances, the "walking on two legs" strategy that the enterprise has adhered to for years has become a key support, providing a solid buffer for the domestic sales team that has been deeply cultivated for many years. At the same time, Liu Mingjun is actively expanding into markets such as the Middle East, Russia, and Southeast Asia, and is responding positively to the government's plan to participate in an exhibition in Russia in September: "We will definitely go, we must break into new markets!"

The carpet industry affects the livelihoods of 54,000 people in Cuihuangkou Town, with nearly half of the population directly or indirectly employed. Carpet output value accounts for one-fifth of the town's GDP, with exports contributing nearly half. Under pressure, departments at all levels, from the municipal to the town, have acted swiftly: intensively organizing "export-to-domestic" matchmaking meetings, forming groups to explore emerging markets like Vietnam and Thailand, and establishing centralized procurement companies to reduce raw material costs... Government-enterprise synergy is injecting momentum into the industry.

However, "transitioning to domestic sales" is by no means a simple switch of sales channels. Liu Mingjun highlights the key challenge: "Consumer preferences vary greatly across countries. The U.S. favors thick and durable washable carpets, Saudi Arabia prefers vibrant ethnic patterns, while the domestic market favors soft-touch imitation cashmere carpets." The gap in categories, materials, and colors means products need to be deeply reimagined. For this reason, her enterprise firmly implements a "dual circulation" strategy: on one hand, actively expanding domestic demand; on the other hand, never lightly giving up on the overseas markets cultivated for many years.

Chen Chenggong, secretary-general of the Cuihuangkou Town Chamber of Commerce, stated that this year the town government has meticulously planned a series of professional sales training sessions for e-commerce platforms, attracting the deep participation of platforms such as Pinduoduo Overseas Edition (TEMU), JD.com, and Taobao. At the same time, export enterprises are accelerating their transformation, shifting to diversified business strategies of "online + offline" and "domestic + international" to enhance their risk resistance. "Resilience is etched in the DNA of Cuihuangkou's carpet industry; through a century of storms, we always find new paths," said Chen Chenggong.

■ Case 2: The "Internal and External Cultivation" Balancing Act of the "Hometown of Silk Flowers"

A similar transformation story is unfolding in another characteristic industrial cluster in Wuqing District, Tianjin—the artificial flower industrial cluster in Caolizi Town.

Caolizi Town is a well-known "Hometown of Silk Flowers," with an industrial scale accounting for about one-third of the national total and an annual output value of nearly 2 billion yuan. Of the town's 28,000 residents, over 15,000 are engaged in silk flower production. Previously, 90% of silk flowers from Caolizi Town were exported overseas. Today, this flower is writing a new chapter of "internal and external cultivation."

Wang Wenlong, manager of Meiyu Craft Flower Co., Ltd. in the town, told reporters: "During '618,' our sales indeed increased significantly compared to usual. The domestic market shows signs of recovery this year, and we actively participated in the major promotions of various platforms."

Wang Wenlong's enterprise is deeply involved in the entire artificial flower industry chain, covering raw materials, production, agency, and online sales. He admitted that the company's strategy is to "grasp both hands equally firmly": on one hand, making great efforts to develop the domestic market; on the other hand, never giving up on the export market. He crunched the numbers: the company focused on domestic sales at its inception, then gradually opened up international markets. Currently, the sales ratio of domestic to export has stabilized at 4:6. "'Meiyu Craft Flower' will do its utmost to maintain and develop in both markets," Wang Wenlong emphasized. With advantages such as timely supply and low defect rates, the company's own brands are quite popular on Alibaba International Station and domestic trade platforms, with annual sales stable at around 100 million yuan.

However, Wang Wenlong has also keenly observed changes in the domestic e-commerce ecosystem: "The enthusiasm of buyers and sellers on platforms for big promotions seems to be less intense than in previous years. There are online live streams every day, and discounts are available at all times. The 'scarcity' of major promotions is diminishing." This suggests that foreign trade enterprises transitioning to domestic sales need not only adapt to product differences but also profoundly understand the rapidly iterating domestic e-commerce gameplay and consumer psychology.

National Subsidies Fuel Fire
Some National Brands Explore "All-Time Low Prices"

A significant change in this year's "618" is the strong intervention of national-level "trade-in" subsidies (hereinafter referred to as "national subsidies"). Building on last year's coverage of 8 major categories including washing machines, televisions, and air conditioners, the national subsidy categories have been significantly expanded this year, adding more items such as mobile phones and digital products, smartwatches (and bracelets), microwave ovens, water purifiers, and dishwashers, further activating consumers' enthusiasm for upgrades and becoming an accelerator for "new national brands" to "break out."

Taobao Tmall stated that the national subsidy categories covered on its platform exceed 1,600, including 12 major categories of home appliances, mobile phones and digital products, smart wearables, as well as smart home, home improvement, and other newly added categories. At the same time, Taobao Tmall has undertaken the online distribution of national subsidies for 29 provinces and cities across the country, becoming one of the platforms with the widest coverage, attracting over 150 million visits to national subsidy products daily.

The "national subsidy + platform subsidy" combination has brought consumers unprecedented benefits. In social media feeds, shopping tips like "for the price of a wool coat, you can buy a quite good air conditioner" are widely circulated.

With multiple subsidies superimposed, prices of domestic big-brand popular home appliances have collectively "plummeted," with some categories experiencing "all-time low prices." Taking air conditioners as an example, the subsidy intensity has significantly increased: from a limit of one unit per household last year to three units this year, with a maximum subsidy of 6,000 yuan. This has directly stimulated consumption: Haier's energy-saving 1.5 HP split air conditioner: original price 2,799 yuan, now 1,486 yuan (about 5.3 fold); Midea's Cool Gold air conditioner: original price 2,499 yuan, with national subsidy and "618" discounts, the final price is 1,559 yuan; TCL's 1.5 HP new-level heating and cooling air conditioner: original price 2,499 yuan, with national subsidy and "618" discounts, the final price is only 1,199 yuan (about 4.6 fold)...

Many consumers in Tianjin took this opportunity to replace all their home air conditioners. Ms. He, a resident of Nankai District, not only replaced her own air conditioner but also successfully persuaded her mother-in-law to do the same: "The new air conditioner not only has a simple and attractive appearance but, more importantly, is more energy-efficient."

On the JD.com platform, the effect of national subsidies is equally significant. The transaction amount for categories such as domestic tires, automotive maintenance supplies, and repair and modification parts increased by over 30 times year-on-year, while the transaction amount for electric bicycles increased by 300%. Domestic new energy vehicle-related categories have grown rapidly, with transaction amounts for automotive charging equipment increasing by 10 times year-on-year. Policy dividends are precisely irrigating key areas of green consumption and industrial upgrading.

Minor Flaws Remain: Pain Points in Experience Persist

Although national subsidies have effectively boosted consumer enthusiasm, the convenience of policy implementation and the user experience of platform functions still have room for improvement, creating some discordant notes amidst the "618" fervor.

Ms. Lü, who lives in Hexi District, wanted to buy a Dongling dough mixer during "618." She saw on the Taobao flagship store's main image that the "618 price was about 624 yuan" and added it to her cart in advance. However, when she placed the order after the promotion began, the checkout page consistently showed 714 yuan, no matter how she tried. After consulting customer service, she received a complex operating guide: she needed to claim the subsidy first, place a separate order, and finally use "UnionPay QuickPass" to pay. Ms. Lü, who is not accustomed to using "UnionPay QuickPass," switched to the same product on JD.com and found that it also required "UnionPay QuickPass" and the price remained unchanged. After several unsuccessful communication attempts, Ms. Lü was ultimately dissuaded by the cumbersome process and decisively chose to forgo the national subsidy, purchasing it for 619 yuan from a distributor on Taobao. "The policy is good, but the operation is too troublesome. I hope the process can be simpler and more intuitive," Ms. Lü said helplessly.

Ms. Liu, who lives in Hedong District, was troubled by the platform's "intelligent" recommendations. She found that a fish oil product she had browsed was "automatically" added to her shopping cart multiple times without her initiating it. "I just browsed it, I didn't intend to buy it, but the product was forced into my cart. This kind of 'forced addition' feature is too 'rogue'!" Despite multiple complaints to the platform, the problem recurred, severely affecting her shopping mood. This reflects the need for a better balance between platforms pursuing conversion rates and respecting user choice.

National Brands Rise
Time-Honored Brands Renewed and High-Quality Domestic Products Popular

While "high-quality foreign trade products" accelerate domestic sales, a group of "time-honored brands" carrying national memories and new national brands that have risen through their strong capabilities have also shone brightly during this "618," demonstrating strong brand appeal and market competitiveness.

As the first national bicycle brand in New China, "Flying Pigeon," a name carrying the memories of generations, is attracting more and more young followers.

On JD.com's Flying Pigeon official flagship store, a popular mountain bike has received over 50,000 positive reviews. The platform's "Billion Subsidy" is unprecedented: the daily price of 914 yuan is reduced by 166 yuan, with the final price only 748 yuan. User reviews are filled with praise such as "good quality, low price," "cool appearance is stunning," and "old brand's cost-effectiveness is excellent." Another JD.com self-operated Flying Pigeon smart electric bicycle priced at 999 yuan even became the sales champion in the sub-1000 yuan price segment.

The bicycle industry is one of Tianjin's representative industries in its export-oriented economy. Public data shows that in 2024, Tianjin's bicycle export volume and export value both accounted for over 30% of the national share, ranking first in national bicycle exports for 12 consecutive years since 2013. Jinghai, Tianjin, is known as the "Capital of Chinese Bicycles and Electric Bicycles," and Wangqingtuo Town in Wuqing District is a well-known industrial base, with brands like Flying Pigeon and Fujida enjoying fame at home and abroad.

A responsible person from an electric bicycle enterprise in Tianjin revealed to reporters that the tariff war has indeed affected the export of domestic bicycles to the U.S. However, fortunately, the company's layout in markets such as Southeast Asia, Europe, and South America is relatively balanced, and the overall pressure is bearable. More encouragingly, with the stabilization of the domestic consumption market and the deepening of the concept of green and low-carbon travel, the domestic bicycle sales market is showing strong growth momentum, thanks to the precise reach of online platforms. Data released by the digital freight platform Yunmanman on World Bicycle Day confirms this: Tianjin is the undisputed "King of Bicycles," with the highest shipping volume nationwide; the top five regions receiving Tianjin bicycles are Shandong, Xinjiang, Guangdong, Guangxi, and Hunan, reflecting the abundant vitality of the internal circulation.

The charm of national brands is not limited to nostalgia. In an era of increasingly rational consumption, high cost-performance and high-quality domestic products are becoming consumers' "favorite."

In the scorching summer heat, domestic pure silk clothing sales on various e-commerce platforms are exceptionally popular. Multiple brands from Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Shanghai have sold out. Consumer reviews are practical and direct: "I used to blindly trust international big brands, with a chemical fiber shirt costing thousands or even tens of thousands of yuan. Now I buy domestic brands, 100% pure silk, with good design and workmanship, for only a few hundred yuan. It's amazing!" This shift from blindly pursuing "foreign brands" to recognizing the "quality-price ratio" of domestic products provides a solid consumption foundation for the rise of national brands.

Similarly, Tianjin's "time-honored brands" like Yumaojing Children's Cream, as well as a batch of emerging domestic skincare and cosmetics brands, have become new favorites among beauty enthusiasts with their "conscientious prices" and "high cost-performance." After trying them, consumers exclaimed, "National brands are truly amazing" when comparing them to expensive international brands.

Platform Competition

From "High-Quality Foreign Trade Goods" to "National Brand Bestsellers"

The accelerated shift of foreign trade enterprises to domestic sales has triggered an unprecedented resource competition among e-commerce platforms. More than a dozen leading platforms, including Alibaba, JD.com, Pinduoduo, Douyin, and Kuaishou, have all invested heavily, making "export-to-domestic" goods and new national brands strategic high ground, with unprecedented investment intensity.

Platforms are providing resource tilting with real money to build "moats":

JD.com has launched a 200 billion yuan special support plan covering traffic, logistics, finance, and services, focusing on supporting foreign trade enterprises, industrial belt merchants, and "time-honored brands."

Pinduoduo's "hundred billion yuan support" focuses on cross-border small and medium-sized merchants transitioning to domestic sales, providing special subsidies, traffic support, and operational guidance.

Douyin E-commerce has launched a "Special Support Plan for High-Quality Foreign Trade Goods" with remarkable results. According to its disclosure, from April 16th to May 9th, the transaction value of domestic brands participating in this plan exceeded 430 million yuan, with live streaming sales contributing over 300 million yuan.

Kuaishou E-commerce has established a "High-Quality Foreign Trade Goods" special assistance team and released multiple measures: opening green channels for entry, tilting exclusive traffic and subsidies, creating hot topics, short video seeding, influencer live streaming sourcing, and setting up "National Brand Category Days" to comprehensively promote the transformation of "High-Quality Foreign Trade Goods" into "National Brand Bestsellers."

In addition, Meituan has launched five measures to pave the way for foreign trade enterprises; Baidu is using AI technology to help millions of enterprises develop domestic sales; Hema has opened a 24-hour green channel; and JD Seven Fresh has launched the "Quality Merchant Plan"...

"Direct procurement of orders," "exclusive traffic," and "supply-demand matching" have become standard actions for platforms supporting foreign trade transitions to domestic sales. A "positioning battle" for high-quality foreign trade supply chains has fully escalated. Platforms are not only responding to the national "dual circulation" strategy but also valuing the R&D capabilities and strict quality control standards that foreign trade enterprises have accumulated over many years. Zhuang Shuai, a specially appointed researcher at the E-commerce Research Center of the eNet Research Institute and founder of Bailian Consulting, analyzed: "The manufacturing capabilities that have long served European and American markets can precisely fill the supply gap in China's mid-to-high-end consumption. These high-quality supply chains are core resources for platforms to upgrade their product pools and attract high-end users."

Platforms also know well that not all foreign trade enterprises can easily "turn around." "Insufficient e-commerce experience, inventory backlog, and difficulty in acquiring traffic" are the three common pain points faced by foreign trade enterprises. Therefore, platforms are offering "nanny-style" services to solve their transformation challenges.

Foreign trade industrial belts in Ningbo, Linhai, and Cixi in Zhejiang have been suffering from a decrease in orders since last year. Deep cooperation with e-commerce platforms during "618" has brought them a turning point. The shipment volume of products such as garment steamers, fans, and vacuum cleaners has significantly increased. Some platform e-commerce teams have even taken on the entire sales and fulfillment chain for some enterprises, including product selection, online operations, marketing promotion, logistics and distribution, and customer service and after-sales, allowing foreign trade enterprises lacking domestic e-commerce experience to "travel light."

The case of Yangzhou Shuguang Toothbrush Factory is quite representative. This old enterprise with annual exports exceeding 200 million yuan faced a crisis of three production lines potentially shutting down due to a sharp drop in foreign trade orders under the impact of the tariff storm. After JD.com's Jingxi self-operated team intervened, they developed a new "soft-bristled toothbrush" category based on big data analysis of domestic consumption trends and precisely targeted consumers in third- and fourth-tier cities. The enterprise负责人 remarked: "The platform's data and channel empowerment have allowed us to find a breakthrough in domestic sales. We are now setting a domestic sales target of 100 million yuan and plan to develop more 'Chinese-flavored' products that meet domestic demand in the future."

According to data from the Ministry of Commerce, since April, e-commerce platforms have, through eight major measures such as direct procurement of orders and setting up foreign trade zones, attracted over 3,100 foreign trade enterprises, with sales in special zones exceeding 1.1 billion yuan and platform direct procurement reaching tens of billions. The platform's role as a main battlefield in assisting foreign trade to transition to domestic sales is becoming increasingly prominent.

Expert Opinion:
Deep Cultivation Leads to "Long-Term Popularity"

The acceleration of foreign trade enterprises returning to the domestic demand market is a strategic adjustment under multiple pressures and a reflection of China's economic resilience and domestic demand potential. Experts believe that this process is fraught with both opportunities and challenges, posing higher demands on enterprise capabilities.

"The return of foreign trade enterprises to the domestic demand market is essentially an inevitable choice under multiple pressures such as rising export costs and shrinking overseas orders caused by Sino-U.S. tariff barriers," Zhuang Shuai pointed out incisively. However, for foreign trade enterprises that have long relied on the large-order overseas model, transitioning to domestic sales means all-around challenges:

1. Production Mode Conflicts: The contradiction between large-scale production for European and American orders and the domestic demand for small-batch, multi-batch, and fast-response flexible production.
2. Channel Cost Pressure: The high traffic costs and payment term pressures on domestic e-commerce platforms may significantly squeeze enterprise profit margins.
3. Standard Conversion Barriers: In fields such as food and home appliances, different domestic and international quality, safety, and certification standards need to be navigated, increasing compliance costs.
4. Brand Recognition and Marketing: Many foreign trade OEM enterprises lack domestic brand recognition and need to build brand image and marketing systems from scratch.

Bao Yuezhong, Chairman of Baum Consulting, emphasized: "Platform and policy support and endorsement can play a certain role, but the key is for enterprises to proactively seek change and not 'wait for, rely on, or ask for.' Enterprises familiar with international markets must quickly settle down to study the characteristics of domestic market demand, e-commerce channel rules, and supermarket channel gameplay. Cooperation is two-way, and the cultivation of the enterprise's own internal strengths is crucial."

Moreover, the large-scale return of foreign trade enterprises to domestic sales also serves as a "shot in the arm" for local enterprises, creating a significant "catfish effect."

Zhuang Shuai analyzed: Foreign trade goods generally adhere to the high-quality standards of exports to Europe and America. At the same quality level, their prices are more competitive, raising the quality benchmark for the domestic market. In addition, the mature after-sales service systems of foreign trade enterprises are being brought into the domestic market, helping to raise the overall consumption service level. At the same time, novel product categories, such as outdoor equipment, smart home appliances, and distinctive small home appliances, which were previously mainly exported, are accelerating their entry into the domestic market, enriching consumer choices. All these factors will force local enterprises to accelerate product iteration and improve service quality, promoting overall industrial upgrading.

The smoke of "618" will eventually dissipate. The grand transformation from "high-quality foreign trade goods" to "national brand bestsellers" is by no means achievable in a single promotional event. It tests the enterprises' deep cultivation ability to understand the local market, reshape their product systems, build brand power, and optimize their supply chains; it tests how platforms can more accurately match supply and demand, empower merchants more efficiently, and serve consumers more friendly; it also tests how policies can be implemented more smoothly and more effectively stimulate market vitality.

—Whoever can transform "bestsellers" from "618" into sustained "long-term popularity" will win a broader future in the new chapter of China's high-quality economic development. Opportunities and challenges coexist, and deep cultivation leads to far-reaching achievements.

title_en: Dairy and Baking Synergistically Drive Yiming Foods' Steady Performance Growth
body_en:
By reporter Wu Jixia
Trainee reporter Wang Nan
On June 16, Zhejiang Yinming Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Yinming Food") held its 2024 Annual and First Quarter 2025 Performance Briefing. During the briefing, the company's management engaged with attendees on issues of concern to investors.
At the performance briefing, Zhu Lifu, Chairman of Yinming Food, stated: "In 2024, the company closely follows consumption trends and understands consumer needs, persisting in building brand connotations centered on freshness and health. We are launching more trustworthy, delicious, and fashionable products and services, focusing on brand tags such as 'nutritious breakfast at your doorstep,' 'healthy relay meal for young white-collar workers,' and 'Starbucks for kids.'"
Over the past year, under the guidance of its fresh and healthy strategy, Yinming Food has continuously advanced brand upgrades and business format expansion, with stable and increasing operating performance. The company achieved an annual operating revenue of 2.751 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 4.09%. Net profit attributable to shareholders of the listed company reached 28.9438 million yuan, a year-on-year increase of 30.16%.
Yinming Food has taken the lead in revolutionizing consumption methods such as the "School Children's Milk Program," "Milk Delivery to Home," and "True Fresh Milk Bar." Through its "Central Factory" and "Chain Stores" combined "Dairy + Baking" chain store sales model, it has formed a comprehensive business scale that is more competitive than traditional single dairy or baking enterprises.
Public data shows that as of the first quarter of 2025, Yinming Food had a total of 1897 operating stores. Among these, there were 1407 franchised stores and 490 directly operated stores, with 10 stores signed and awaiting opening. Compared to 2024, the number of operating stores decreased by 71.
In response, Lin Yilei, Secretary of the Board of Directors of Yinming Food, told a reporter from Securities Daily that the net decrease in stores in the first quarter was mainly due to structural optimization. On one hand, the company adheres to a "quality-first" expansion strategy, actively closing some stores whose operational efficiency did not meet expectations. On the other hand, some stores chose to exit in an orderly manner due to lease expiration or the non-renewal of franchise contracts.
In terms of product strategy, Yinming Food promotes a strategy of large single products based on scenarios.
Concurrently, Yinming Food is resolutely advancing its large single product strategy. For example, its Jersey milk topped the sales chart for single products on the Tmall platform from May to June 2024.
Yinming Food is also actively exploring the development of new business formats, focusing on creating a composite business format of "milk bar + light catering," steadily expanding product lines such as pizza and coffee, and gradually forming a cooperation network in channels like group catering. Although the new brands are still in the trial stage, their recognition and penetration among young consumers and office white-collar workers are continuously increasing, laying the foundation for the formation of a second growth curve in the future.
Zhu Lifu told a reporter from Securities Daily that Houbi Pizza and Yicheng Coffee, as important extensions of the company's strategy, are currently steadily advancing their incubation and channel integration. As of now, "Houbi Pizza" is sold in approximately 400 stores, and "Yicheng Coffee" covers 105 milk bar channels. It has also achieved point-of-sale landings in B-end scenarios such as office buildings and medical institutions.
Entering the first quarter of 2025, Yinming Food continued to maintain its performance growth. The company achieved an operating revenue of 654 million yuan, a year-on-year increase of 1.75%. Net profit attributable to shareholders of the listed company reached 13.3067 million yuan, a year-on-year increase of 28.38%.
Looking ahead, Zhu Lifu stated that the company adheres to the goal of "building China's leading milk bar chain brand and a leading enterprise in fresh and healthy food." It will focus on its core businesses of dairy and baking, develop core products such as Jersey milk, organic milk, and functional baked goods, increase the proportion of new product sales, create more healthy products with explosive potential, and drive long-term revenue growth.

title_en: "In the heart there is love, in the hands there is AI" - they who have been changed, and they who change.
body_en:
What does the encounter between rural women and digital technology mean?
Ma Xuemei from Wangtuan Town, Tongxin County, Ningxia, said: "Thanks to the good policies of the country, the 'Go, Mulan' project saved me and my children."
Zhao Xinyuan from Boxing County, Shandong, said: "The 'Women in New Agriculture' support program has provided a new stage for rural revitalization for returnee female entrepreneurs like us."
Zhu Xiaoling from Yijun County, Shaanxi, said: "I am a farmer and an AI trainer. The 'AI Bean Project' has changed my life and also changed my hometown."
All of this stems from a "handshake" in 2023.
In June 2023, the "Intelligent and Beneficial Women" public welfare project jointly launched by the China Women's Development Foundation and the Zhejiang Ant Public Welfare Foundation officially started, launching a series of projects including the "Go, Mulan" women's public welfare insurance project, the "Women in New Agriculture" support program, and the "AI Bean Project," exploring a new path of "digital technology + public welfare."
By the end of 2024, the project had invested a total of 64 million yuan, benefiting more than 2.7 million women and families in difficulty.
Now, the eagerly awaited good news has come again. The "Intelligent and Beneficial Women" public welfare project has ushered in an upgrade in strategic cooperation. As more and more women benefit from the "Intelligent and Beneficial Women" project, as their lives are changed by digital technology, they will also firmly grasp digital technology in their hands and catch the fast-moving train of the times.
Digital technology + public welfare, with results
On May 23, the strategic cooperation upgrade event of the "Intelligent and Beneficial Women" public welfare project jointly launched by the China Women's Development Foundation and the Zhejiang Ant Public Welfare Foundation was held in Beijing.
It is understood that although 2025 is the third year of the "Intelligent and Beneficial Women" public welfare project, it is the seventh year that the China Women's Development Foundation and the Ant Group have jointly carried out public welfare projects and cared for and supported women in underdeveloped areas. Love has gathered, allowing women in underdeveloped areas to receive medical and employment support, and women and families who have suffered losses in major disasters have also received economic assistance.
"Along the way, we have witnessed many touching stories and seen many real changes. Women who were once trapped in the shadow of illness have regained confidence in life, sisters who stayed in the countryside have mastered digital skills to achieve economic independence, and female entrepreneurs have led more people onto the path of prosperity," said Du Rui, Chairperson of the China Women's Development Foundation.
Protecting the physical health of women in underdeveloped areas, providing scholarships for women in difficulty, the "Go, Mulan" public welfare project was born. As of now, it has raised more than 230 million yuan, covering 62 counties in 18 provinces, and nearly 5.6 million impoverished women have received project guarantees.
Caring for the healthy growth of families in difficulty, helping grassroots implement the "Love Mom" pairing assistance task, under the guidance of the All-China Women's Federation, the China Women's Development Foundation launched the "Love Warms Every Home" public welfare action in 2024, which has landed in 119 counties in 31 provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities, and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, establishing 119 teams of more than 5,000 loving mothers, providing care and support services to 12,200 families in difficulty, benefiting nearly 2 million people.
Supporting rural women in underdeveloped areas in employment and entrepreneurship, the "AI Bean Project" tailored for them, helping them engage in various businesses such as finance, unmanned driving, customer service, and medical care through mastering digital technology, truly providing them with the opportunity to "have a brilliant life and make their dreams come true." By the end of 2024, the "AI Bean Project" had carried out digital empowerment training and employment assistance for women in 16 districts and counties in 7 provinces including Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Guizhou, training a total of 9,922 people, with 7,508 people passing the assessment and earning an average monthly income of 3,000-4,000 yuan. At the same time, the "Women in New Agriculture" support program, officially launched in 2024, will also create new opportunities for rural women to make contributions and achievements in the characteristic industries of the countryside.
Public welfare always has a warm background, and now, with the support of digital technology, this warmth from the "family" can reach the hearts faster.
Digital technology + public welfare, efficient
"I didn't expect it to be so fast and convenient." A claim of 20,000 yuan relieved Ma Xuemei of the economic pressure when she was ill, and the claim speed of 5 hours made her both surprised and delighted. "Being sick is like racing against the disease. The efficient operation of this system has bought me time." Ma Xuemei still remembers the moment she received a bank account message while lying in the hospital bed, tears flowing uncontrollably. Ma Xuemei looked at the message over and over again, filled with endless gratitude.
Ma Xuemei said, "Go, Mulan" not only reduced the economic burden on her family in terms of medical care, but her daughter also received thousands of yuan in assistance for three consecutive years through the application process. The "family" system also fought for her "two-cancer special assistance" and enjoyed temporary assistance and "low-income support" policies.
Now, Ma Xuemei's condition is under control. In addition to her work, she has also become a "spokesperson" for "Go, Mulan," often sharing her story and bringing hope to sisters in similar difficulties.
In the operation of the "Go, Mulan" project, the application of digital technology allows more "Ma Xuemei" to receive help more efficiently.
It is reported that the "Go, Mulan" project uses front-end image recognition, AI intelligence, and blockchain technology in the insurance and claims process, not only improving the efficiency of project implementation but also enabling the project to expand coverage to counties and benefit more impoverished women in underdeveloped areas with public welfare insurance.
On this point, Ma Xuelian, Vice Chairman of the Women's Federation of Dongxiang Autonomous County, Gansu, and also the liaison officer when the "Go, Mulan" project landed in Dongxiang Autonomous County, has deep feelings.
"Over the years, I have witnessed the tremendous changes that the 'Intelligent and Beneficial Women' project has brought to Dongxiang women." Ma Xuelian said excitedly, "One family after another has rekindled hope, and Dongxiang women have regained their smiles. They have not only successfully fought against diseases but have also gained a precious strength in this process, supporting them to bravely pursue their dreams and strive for self-improvement."
Digital technology + public welfare, with a future
At the junction of the Guanzhong Plain and the Loess Plateau in northern Shaanxi, there is a group of rural women who, during busy farming seasons, work in the fields, husking corn and fertilizing; during idle farming seasons, they sit in offices, completing a series of AI training tasks on computers.
Zhu Xiaoling is one of them. In July 2024, Zhu Xiaoling participated as an AI trainer in the first phase of the company's vocational skills level certification exam and passed. "The certificate is an affirmation of my work. With a skill, I have confidence to go further in this industry," Zhu Xiaoling said.
All of this is thanks to the landing of the "AI Bean Project" public welfare project in Yijun County.
With the development of digital technology, the digital economy has become the core engine driving economic growth, social progress, and technological innovation. What development opportunities can women seize from this? With this question in mind, the "AI Bean Project" public welfare project was born.
Over the past five years, with the support of grassroots governments, the "AI Bean Project" public welfare project has provided free training in new digital technology skills for economically disadvantaged women with basic education levels who have returned to, entered, or stayed in rural areas, and through a series of assistance such as assessment, application, and stable employment, it has helped economically disadvantaged women in rural areas achieve high-quality employment "at their doorstep." "Statistics show that women entrepreneurs in the Internet field account for 55%. But we also see that in underdeveloped areas, women still face a digital divide, with limited resources and technological barriers becoming stumbling blocks on their path forward," Du Rui said. "The upgrade of the 'Intelligent and Beneficial Women' project, with precise efforts in improving women's digital literacy, researching scientific research topics, and building a global cooperation and exchange platform, is of great significance and far-reaching impact. This is not only a precise response to the needs of women but also a mission to fulfill social responsibility."
In the future, the upgraded "Intelligent and Beneficial Women" project may help more women improve their digital literacy, seize opportunities in the digital economy wave, realize their self-worth; bring more warmth and hope to families in difficulty, ensure women's rights, make life more colorful, and make life happier. (According to "China Women's News")

title_en: The Chinese Culinary Association held a quarterly work meeting of the Food Safety Research Group.
body_en: On the afternoon of June 10th, the quarterly work meeting of the Food Safety Research Group of the China Cuisine Association was successfully held at the association. Food safety management personnel and related representatives from chain brand catering enterprises such as Yum China, Haidilao, Starbucks, McDonald's, Luckin Coffee, Dicos, Meituan, and Ele.me attended the meeting. Wang Xuelian, Deputy Director of the Catering Department of the Beijing Municipal Market Supervision Administration, attended the meeting and delivered a speech, while Wu Ying, Vice President of the China Cuisine Association, also attended the meeting. Wu Ying, Vice President of the China Cuisine Association, and Wang Xuelian, Deputy Director of the Catering Department of the Beijing Municipal Market Supervision Administration, delivered speeches. The meeting focused on discussing the "Draft Regulations on the Supervision and Management of the Implementation of Food Safety Main Responsibility by Chain Catering Enterprises," and listened to the opinions and suggestions of participating enterprises. Wang Xuelian, Deputy Director of the Catering Department of the Beijing Municipal Market Supervision Administration, fully exchanged views with representatives of participating enterprises to understand the effective measures and methods of chain catering enterprises in implementing food safety main responsibility. At the same time, the meeting summarized the work of the Food Safety Research Group in the second quarter in food safety risk discussions, legal research, standard construction, etc., and reported the focus of the next quarter's work to member units of the Food Safety Research Group, including the release of good food safety case studies, standard construction, and other work. Representatives of participating enterprises expressed professional opinions on related topics.

title_en: How did the small water town become the "top stream" in Shanghai?
body_en:
Reporter Chen Jialin
Last weekend, it was rainy and overcast. Driving into Hemu Village in Zhaoxiang Town, Qingpu District, the wheels rolled over the wet asphalt road. One moment, the view outside the car window was a cityscape with towering buildings; the next moment, vast fields and countryside scenery came into view. This seemingly inconspicuous village, traversed by the Xujing River, has more than 20 shops on both sides, forming a winding "Hemu Water Street," nurturing a unique rural economic format.
Searching for "Hemu Village" on social platforms yields thousands of related shares, and many citizens and tourists drive from the city to visit. Located in the outskirts of Shanghai, how did a less than 300-meter water street become a new internet sensation? How did Hemu Village grasp the "traffic password" and become a "top stream" in Shanghai and a "model room" for rural revitalization? The reporter visited the site and made some observations.
Riverside courtyards are fully occupied
If the seamless transition from the city to the countryside momentarily confuses people, then the moment when Hemu Water Street (see Figure 4) comes into view can truly be described as a relaxing experience.
Amidst the flowing water, the white walls and black tiles of the houses blend with the lush greenery; parasols and tables and chairs are placed by the riverbank, with some people "lying flat" to rest; next to the Seven-Colored Magpie Bridge, several aunts and uncles are enthusiastically posing for photos; strolling along the riverbank, there are groups of tourists walking together. The misty Hemu Water Street, although not as popular as a sunny day, exudes a sense of leisure and poetry.
Walking further in, the riverside courtyards are each more "exquisite" than the last. Around 1 p.m., the restaurant "Hetian Mushi" is still bustling. With its wooden doors wide open, the spacious courtyard is filled with flowers, plants, and greenery. Jujube trees, pomegranate trees, and persimmon trees stretch their branches, and lanterns representing the twenty-four solar terms hang under the eaves; walking past the smoke-filled bluestone slabs, one can choose a bamboo chair and low table to sit around, drink coffee, chat, enjoy delicious food, and have a dog playing at their feet.
Despite the unfavorable weather, the courtyard is still full. 36-year-old Ms. Wang, who lives in Xujing, came with her husband and two-year-old daughter, ordered a Mexican burrito and pasta, and enjoyed a leisurely outdoor time, "Our family are regulars here. We have been coming almost every other week since our daughter was six months old, and we stay for most of the day." Ms. Wang said that what attracts her most to the water street is the outdoor environment, which is especially suitable for family outings. She plays with her daughter and pets, while her husband goes to the riverbank with a net and bucket to catch fish. Occasionally, they catch rare species and put them in the fish tank at home.
Not only local residents of Qingpu, but also many citizens from the city come to visit the water street. In less than a 5-minute walk, the tea and coffee house Sanmao Xiaoyuan is also bustling. Qi Zhenyi, in his sixties, holds an electric guitar and has started a small "concert" with a few aunts and uncles: order a pot of tea and snacks, and sing thirty to forty songs from morning till now. "We live in Xuhui District and came here on a friend's recommendation. Different from the hustle and bustle of the city, the environment here is quiet and peaceful. Drinking tea, chatting, playing music, we are very happy." Qi Zhenyi said.
Less than 300 meters, each step brings a surprise. Men, women, old, and young can all find enjoyment at the water street. This scene makes people sigh: is this still the countryside in our memories? On social platforms, Hemu Village is called the "outlet's backyard." Dong Chunhui, the secretary of the village party branch, told the reporter that this is thanks to Hemu Village's superior geographical location - adjacent to the Dahongqiao Business District, only a hundred meters from the Qingpu Outlet Shopping Center, and not far from the Jiasong Middle Road Station on Metro Line 17 to the northwest.
In addition to outstanding location conditions, the lively atmosphere of Hemu Village can also be traced back further: in the 1920s during the era of waterway transportation, there was a market at Luyu Bridge in the Xujing River basin, with streets built along the river, houses standing by the water, and bustling commercial activities.
In 2021, nearly a hundred years later, due to the remarkable achievements in beautiful rural construction, Hemu Village became the third batch of demonstration villages for rural revitalization in Shanghai. "With the improvement of hardware, how to promote upgrading and attract industries has become our new focus." Dong Chunhui told the reporter that on the one hand, due to the gradual decline in traditional agricultural income and the continuous outflow of young people, many houses in the village have become vacant; on the other hand, the convenient transportation and developed commerce and trade in the advantageous location can bring huge potential customer flow. This has opened up a new train of thought for them - why not revitalize the idle residential land along the Xujing River and create a boutique rural consumer experience space?
Village-enterprise cooperation, action-oriented. Through voluntary transfer and arrangements for the elderly, 23 farmhouses have been successfully transferred, providing a physical space carrier for the project. The Hemu Water Street is taking shape.
Makers settle in and businesses thrive
Wang Shouwei, the founder of Hetian Mushi, is from Shandong and has been in the furniture industry for 18 years. He has always had a dream of running a restaurant since he was young. In 2018, he accidentally stumbled upon the rapeseed flower sea in Hemu Village with his daughter, and had his first encounter with this small village. "It is quiet amidst the hustle and bustle here, like a 'Peach Blossom Spring,' it would be a pity not to do business here!"
A casual expression of regret has created an indissoluble bond between Wang Shouwei and Hemu Village. As the fourth entrepreneur to sign up to settle in Hemu Village, Wang Shouwei was undoubtedly one of the first to try something new. During the May Day holiday in 2023, his self-designed and built Hetian Mushi officially opened, claiming to be a "courtyard filled with human fireworks," and it became popular immediately, breaking even in the first month and turning a profit in the second month.
Hetian Mushi was not the first restaurant to open on Hemu Water Street, but its sudden popularity seemed accidental, yet inevitable. The reporter found that Hetian Mushi did not extensively renovate the original farmhouse but preserved the natural texture of the countryside. "Repairing the old as old respects the original architecture and perfectly integrates into the village's style, the courtyard that is both elegant and rustic allows customers to experience the rural atmosphere." Wang Shouwei revealed that at the peak of its popularity, the daily foot traffic exceeded a thousand, with a turnover of over 100,000 yuan.
In fact, when Hetian Mushi settled in, there were only a few scattered merchants on the water street. Dong Chunhui admitted that the initial business recruitment was not as smooth as expected, as many merchants were hesitant. But Wang Shouwei was not worried; he believed, "Hemu Village already has a commercial foundation and natural charm. The precise match with the high-end customer positioning of the nearby outlets, business office buildings, villa areas, and the water street's high-end planning has the potential for commercial development."
With the success of Hetian Mushi, Wang Shouwei opened the Front Yard Backyard (see Figure 1) and Hemu Yan She, covering multiple formats such as homestays, dining, and tea spaces. The Front Yard Backyard consists of four renovated farmhouses, with 25 rooms in various styles such as Chinese, Wabi-Sabi, and Nordic, featuring study rooms, dining rooms, tea rooms, pet playgrounds, fruit and vegetable picking gardens, bamboo forest tea spaces, and other leisure spaces, providing accommodation, tea breaks, parent-child entertainment, dining gatherings, etc. It was rated as the only five-star rural homestay in Qingpu District last year. During the May Day holiday this year, the total turnover of the three stores exceeded one million yuan.
The investor of Sanmao Xiaoyuan, Yuan Sanmao, grew up in rural Shanxi and has a strong rural sentiment. As one of the earliest merchants to settle in Hemu Water Street, Yuan Sanmao has opened four stores on the water street, with an investment exceeding 20 million yuan. Among them, there is the Drink Light Mountain House, which is mainly a tea space suitable for business negotiations, as well as the Hemu Coffee and Sanmao Xiaoyuan, which are affordable and suitable for family and friends gatherings. At the end of May this year, the fourth store, the distinctive Turkish coffee shop "Tuwu TUTU," went online, blending exotic styles with rural charm, attracting many people to come and check in. In the afternoon, 58-year-old Chen Xin and her two sisters came out of the outlet shopping mall and found Tuwu TUTU through social media recommendations, each ordering a cup of Turkish coffee, "We live in Minhang and often come to Hemu Village. Seeing a new store opening, we stop by to rest and chat."
To attract more visitors, in October 2023, Yuan Sanmao leveraged the store on the water street to create the "Hemu Persimmon Market" (see Figure 2), recruiting more than 30 fixed vendors, gathering original products such as intangible cultural heritage, handicrafts, and cultural and creative products, and carefully arranging popular attractions such as giant pandas (see Figure 3) and a popular boat. Every weekend, this market is bustling with people, achieving a two-way flow with the stores.
Four seasons colorful, guests come in droves
The four seasons of Hemu Water Street are colorful. In spring, the bright rapeseed flowers light up with vibrant vitality; in summer, the layers of rice fields turn into endless shades of green; in autumn, the dazzling golden colors surge in the waves of rice; in winter, the most festive Chinese red flows with warmth and joy. In the Front Yard Backyard, the reporter met Lou Xin, a photography enthusiast. He lives in Baoshan District and works near People's Square. He comes to Hemu Village for inspiration every once in a while, "It's easy to take good photos here. Sometimes when I want to shoot night scenes, I stay here for a night."
Good scenery attracts new economies, and the market's sense of smell is the most sensitive. Dong Chunhui revealed that since Hetian Mushi became popular, more and more high-quality merchants have settled down, and a new business format of rural leisure tourism centered around the water street has naturally grown, forming a differentiated temperament and tone. South of the Xujing River is more high-end, with strong privacy, suitable for business receptions; north of the Xujing River is more popular, relatively open, and has a strong market atmosphere.
As the business formats on the water street continue to diversify, a large influx of customers follows. During holidays, Dong Chunhui always looks out the duty room window, "When the traffic increases, we immediately send volunteers to maintain order." To provide a better playing experience, Hemu Village has unearthed nearly 400 parking spaces to meet the parking needs during peak hours.
For the residents of Hemu Village, the water street brings not only popularity and liveliness but also new business opportunities. Not far from the water street, villager Chen Lian took back the farmhouse she had rented out. Having done online business and operated a Taobao store, she returned to her hometown to start a business and opened a private kitchen called "Xixianzhai," with two floors - the first floor serving farmhouse dishes and the second floor serving private dishes. Through word of mouth, the team expanded to 15 people, with over a hundred dishes on the menu. During holidays, business is booming, and reservations are required in advance.
With the water street, Hemu Village has undergone a transformation, and some villagers have found new job opportunities. The reporter noticed that whether it was the Drink Light Mountain House, Sanmao Xiaoyuan, or the Front Yard Backyard, the vegetable gardens in the courtyards were preserved, and villagers were hired to cultivate local vegetables and fruits, allowing customers to experience the joy of picking.
"The Hemu Water Street has brought a significant increase in foot traffic, making the villagers' wallets fuller." Dong Chunhui told the reporter that after the residential land was transferred, the villagers received higher rents than when they managed it themselves, and the rents are regularly increased proportionally. He said that next, Hemu Village will extend the water street area, introduce more business formats, comprehensively upgrade roads, lighting, and other infrastructure, build more integrated agricultural, cultural, and tourism spaces on the basis of thousands of acres of good farmland, and create Hemu Water Street 2.0.
Wang Shouwei noticed a "Ginkgo Stroll Forest" in the rice fields near Hemu Water Street. He plans to continue expanding his business in Hemu Village and open a "Coffee Pet Fun Park" in the forest space, expected to open by the end of this year.
As night falls and the lights come on, the night falls on Hemu Water Street. Many villagers also come to the viewing platform to enjoy the night. Dong Chunhui looks forward to more diverse nighttime economic formats being injected into Hemu Village in the future, injecting new vitality into rural revitalization.

title_en: Do you still need to learn programming to develop intelligent agents without writing code?
body_en:
Is it possible to develop an intelligent agent with a personalized interactive interface and a large model "brain" without writing any code?
At the recent "Unicom Mingxi Cup" intelligent agent development competition, students from Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications achieved this. The initiator of the competition, Associate Professor of Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications and specially appointed expert in digital education, Xu Tong, introduced that in less than a month, undergraduate and graduate students from 13 colleges of the university, based on the self-developed teaching intelligent agent platform "Chufa" by the university's EZCoding student entrepreneurship team, developed over 200 intelligent agent works, including vocabulary challenge games, AI travel assistants, and more.
Xu Tong believes that these intelligent agents are not only the result of student innovation but also a vivid manifestation of the trend of code-free intelligent agent development.
He observed that since ChatGPT introduced the GPTs feature, allowing users to customize their own AI assistants in a code-free manner, the trend of code-free development of intelligent agents has gradually emerged. Currently, a series of code-free intelligent agent development platforms have been launched both domestically and internationally, including Baidu's Wenxin, Tencent's Yuanqi, Alibaba's Tongyi Xingchen, and iFlytek's Xingchen Agent platform.
Why can many platforms achieve "code-free" development? Xu Tong explained that these platforms use large models as the "brain," which can autonomously handle some tasks, greatly reducing the workload of programming. At the same time, some code-free development platforms provide visual interfaces, allowing developers to complete the development of front-end interfaces and back-end workflows through operations such as dragging controls and writing prompts, thus significantly improving efficiency.
He stated that currently, intelligent agents developed through code-free platforms are mainly divided into two categories: chat-based intelligent agents and application-based intelligent agents. In many vertical fields, chat-based intelligent agents may not meet the requirements, necessitating more powerful application-based intelligent agents with user experiences similar to applications (Apps).
However, he learned that currently only a few platforms support the development of code-free application-based intelligent agents, including ByteDance's AI application development platform "Kouzi" and Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications' "Chufa" platform. He said that some intelligent agent development platforms do not yet have the functionality to develop code-free application-based intelligent agents, and even if some platforms do, they may have issues such as "few front-end controls" and "simple functions," making it difficult to meet the specific needs of various vertical fields.
In Xu Tong's view, despite the existing limitations, the trend of developing code-free application-based intelligent agents is unstoppable. He believes that large model-driven, custom interfaces, and code-free development will become the mainstream mode of intelligent agent development. As long as there is good creativity, everyone may develop their own application-based intelligent agents in the future.
As the trend of lowering the threshold for application development emerges, is it still necessary to learn programming?
On the day of the interview, the technical director of the "Chufa" platform, undergraduate student Yang Zhongtian from Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, was given a task on the spot: to create an "editing intelligent agent" with functions to recognize and correct misspelled words, language errors, and expression risks.
He dragged modules such as "buttons" and other front-end controls one by one into the operation interface, likening it to preparing "pre-made dishes." He then entered commands and prompts, directing the controls to run according to the requirements and in the appropriate order. Although this process of "communicating" with the computer does not require writing code, it still requires clear logic and reasonable arrangement, otherwise the "editing intelligent agent" may "strike" at any time. Yang Zhongtian said that although the operator does not need to write code themselves, they still need to have "programming thinking."
As a teacher, Xu Tong also realizes that the trend of lowering the threshold for application development may lead to changes in programming education.
He believes that the focus of teaching and learning modes will change in the future. The focus of programming education will gradually shift from learning programming techniques to learning programming thinking, innovative thinking, and problem-solving methods, while the learning mode will shift from traditional lecture-based learning to project-based learning, where students "learn and apply" in the practical process, greatly improving learning efficiency.

title_en: Government debt drives social financing.
body_en:
On June 13, the People's Bank of China released financial data for May. The data shows that by the end of May 2025, the scale of social financing was 426.16 trillion yuan, an increase of 8.7% year-on-year, unchanged from the previous month. Among them, the balance of RMB loans issued to the real economy was 262.86 trillion yuan, an increase of 7% year-on-year, a decrease of 0.1 percentage points from the previous month; the balance of corporate bonds was 32.91 trillion yuan, an increase of 3.4% year-on-year, an increase of 0.2 percentage points from the previous month; the balance of government bonds was 87.39 trillion yuan, an increase of 20.9% year-on-year, unchanged from the previous month.
In terms of the structure of outstanding loans, the balance of RMB loans issued to the real economy at the end of May accounted for 61.7% of the total social financing scale at the same period, a decrease of 1 percentage point year-on-year; the proportion of government bonds was 20.5%, an increase of 2.1 percentage points year-on-year; the proportion of corporate bonds was 7.7%, a decrease of 0.4 percentage points year-on-year.
In terms of incremental changes, the cumulative increase in the scale of social financing in the first five months of 2025 was 18.63 trillion yuan, which was 3.83 trillion yuan more than the same period last year. Among them, RMB loans issued to the real economy increased by 10.38 trillion yuan, an increase of 112.3 billion yuan year-on-year; net financing of government bonds was 6.31 trillion yuan, an increase of 3.81 trillion yuan year-on-year; net financing of corporate bonds was 908.7 billion yuan, a decrease of 288.4 billion yuan year-on-year.
Analysts pointed out that the rapid growth of social financing in May was mainly driven by direct financing such as government bonds and corporate bonds, with government bonds playing a major role. This year, the pace of government bond issuance has been accelerated, with a net financing scale of over 3.8 trillion yuan in the first quarter, an increase of 2.5 trillion yuan from the same period last year, especially with a significant increase in the issuance of special refinancing bonds for replacing implicit debts. In the second quarter, as the issuance of special refinancing bonds continues to advance, with the launch of special national bonds, the progress of net financing of government bonds has further accelerated, and there are signs of accelerated issuance of local new special bonds.
The above-mentioned analysts also stated that corporate bond financing increased in May. Since the second quarter, the overall cost of corporate bond issuance has been on a downward trend, with the average yield of 5-year AAA-rated corporate bonds in May at 1.97%, further down from the low level in April. Against the backdrop of low interest rates, companies have increased their bond financing efforts, which helps to reduce the overall financing costs.
The data shows that nearly 90% of the scale of social financing is made up of bonds and loans, and although the two have different applications, to some extent they can complement each other and create a good overall financial environment for stable economic growth.
Authoritative sources told reporters that in recent times, the substitution effect of bonds for loans has been more pronounced, mainly due to the following three factors:
First, the issuance of special refinancing bonds to repay bank loans, after the related impact is restored, the loan growth rate is still around 8%. In the short term, the debt replacement of financing platform debts to repay bank loans may affect the total credit volume, but in the long term, it will help alleviate local debt risks, free up more local financial resources for the benefit of the people, promote development, and enhance economic growth momentum.
Second, government bonds are replacing bank loans. Some government bond investments overlap with bank loan investments, such as in infrastructure projects, where special bonds and bank loans can both serve as sources of funding. In the acquisition of existing commercial housing for affordable housing projects, in addition to bank loans, special bonds have recently been added to the policy toolbox and are gradually being implemented.
For example, several banks in an eastern province have reported that since the beginning of this year, fiscal policies have become more proactive, with an increase in local government bond issuances. Local governments and related enterprises are more inclined to use special bonds to meet the funding needs of project construction, which has a certain substitutive effect on bank loans. Official data shows that in the first four months of this year, the source of fixed asset investment funds, including government bonds, increased by 16.7% year-on-year, significantly higher than self-raised funds (3.9%), domestic loans (2.8%), and other sources of funds (-4.2%).
Third, corporate bonds are replacing bank loans. In addition to interest rate effects, some trend and institutional factors are also influencing the choice of financing for enterprises. In recent years, a series of supportive policies have been continuously introduced to facilitate corporate bond issuance, especially in the areas of private and technological innovation, where corporate bond financing has shown more positive changes. In early May, the People's Bank of China and the China Securities Regulatory Commission issued a number of measures to support the issuance of technology innovation bonds. As these measures are gradually implemented, the issuance of technology innovation bonds by enterprises will be facilitated.
Furthermore, he pointed out that in the context of increasingly diverse financing channels and accelerated development of direct financing, the scale of social financing is more comprehensive than loans in measuring the strength of financial support. The transformation and upgrading of the economic structure cannot be achieved without the support of a financing system that is compatible with it. Direct financing has the characteristics of risk sharing, benefit sharing, and long-term companionship, and is more suitable for new areas of high growth, heavy research and development, and light assets, and will play a greater role in the financial system in the future.
At the end of May, the broad money supply (M2) balance was 325.78 trillion yuan, an increase of 7.9% year-on-year; the narrow money supply (M1) balance was 108.91 trillion yuan, an increase of 2.3% year-on-year.
Industry experts analyzed that the M1 statistical caliber currently includes currency in circulation (M0), unit and individual demand deposits, and non-bank payment institution customer reserves (such as WeChat Wallet, Alipay balance, etc.), which are considered as "active money" that is more convenient for payment transactions compared to fixed deposits in bank accounts. The growth rate of this "active money" in May has accelerated significantly, reflecting the effective boost in market confidence from recent comprehensive financial support measures, with signs of improvement in investment, consumption, and other economic activities.
Data released by the National Bureau of Statistics recently showed that the manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) in May increased by 0.5 percentage points from the previous month, with the production index of the PMI increasing by 0.9 percentage points to 50.7% compared to the previous month, indicating marginal improvement in social confidence. Thanks to factors such as the increased efforts in policies supporting the "two new" industries, the growth rate of total retail sales of consumer goods this year has been significantly higher than the same period last year, with the number of domestic trips and consumption during the "May Day" holiday increasing by 6.4% and 8% year-on-year, respectively. Investment continues to expand, with rapid growth in investment in emerging industries, and the value added of high-tech manufacturing industries above a certain scale growing significantly faster than the overall manufacturing industry. External uncertainties still exist, but exports remain stable and growing.
The data also shows that the CPI in May decreased by 0.1% year-on-year, unchanged from March and April; the core CPI, excluding food and energy prices, increased by 0.6% year-on-year, an increase of 0.1 percentage points from April. The PPI in May decreased by 3.3% year-on-year, compared to a decrease of 2.7% in the previous month, with a cumulative year-on-year decrease of 2.6% from January to May.
Industry experts stated that overall, prices have remained low this year, mainly due to the contradictions between supply and demand in the real economy, as well as the impact of external factors such as the decline in international energy prices. In recent years, China's economic structure has been accelerating its transformation and upgrading, with some industries experiencing oversupply compared to demand, which has had an impact on the rise in prices. At the same time, it is also important to note that various macroeconomic policies are boosting domestic demand and the adjustment of supply-side policies is strengthening, accumulating positive factors to support the rise in prices.
The interviewed industry experts also emphasized to reporters that promoting a reasonable increase in prices requires regulating the issue of excessive competition in certain industries. If an industry only competes on price and not on quality, it may eliminate the reasonable profit margin, which is not only detrimental to technological innovation by companies but also to ensuring product quality, and may have a spillover effect on upstream and downstream companies in the supply chain, leading to excessive competition in the entire industry chain.
Boosting consumption is also seen as an important lever to promote a reasonable increase in prices. The experts mentioned that previous policies such as the "trade-in old for new" have had a significant effect on promoting consumption, and in the future, attention should be paid to increasing residents' disposable income and improving social security levels such as pensions, healthcare, and education, to fundamentally enhance residents' consumption capacity and willingness. They suggested further leveraging the income redistribution role of secondary distribution, focusing on increasing the income share of middle and low-income groups.
In their view, the future should support the expansion of high-quality service consumption supply. China has gradually entered a stage of high-quality development, and the structure of residents' consumption is also optimizing and upgrading, with a continuous increase in demand for high-quality services.
"In this process, it is necessary to properly grasp the relationship between finance and consumption." The experts admitted that consumer borrowing is essentially a form of pre-consumption behavior based on future income as collateral. Considering that the leverage ratio of Chinese residents is already high, the development of consumer finance should also consider the debt repayment capacity of consumers, focusing on exploring consumer credit customers supported by genuine consumption needs. Currently, the supply of high-quality service consumption in some inclusive areas is clearly insufficient, making it an important focus of future financial policy support for promoting consumption.
He also reiterated to reporters that theoretically, lowering interest rates has a certain effect on promoting consumption, but the interest rate level for consumer loans is not necessarily the lower, the better. For residents, even if the interest rate for consumer loans is lower, there are still financing costs that need to be supported by income growth; from the perspective of banks, the interest rate level for consumer loans must cover operating costs, balancing financial support for consumption and the sustainable operation of financial institutions.

title_en: Notice on holding the 2024 Academic Annual Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association (Second Round)
body_en: Relevant units: Pharmaceutical excipients are an important foundation in China's pharmaceutical industry, and are one of the key factors determining the quality of generic drugs and the high-quality development of innovative formulations. The supply chain security of pharmaceutical excipients used in high-end formulations in China urgently needs to strengthen the technological innovation and industrial support for domestic pharmaceutical excipients. At the same time, ensuring the quality of clinical medication, reducing drug costs, and alleviating the pressure on medical insurance, to a large extent, also depend on the quality improvement of domestic pharmaceutical excipients. In line with the principle of "promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new quality productivity of the pharmaceutical industry," the "2024 Annual Academic Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association," hosted by the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association, is scheduled to be held in Hefei, Anhui Province from November 8th to 10th, 2024. This academic conference will feature conference reports in the fields of materials science related to pharmaceutical excipients, innovative drugs, and innovative formulations, analyzing the development difficulties and innovations of pharmaceutical excipients; inviting authoritative experts to deeply discuss the in vivo processes of pharmaceutical excipients and drug delivery carriers, as well as the improvement and innovation of excipient quality. The conference will set up expert venues and young scholar sub-venues on the themes of "Pharmaceutical Excipients, Packaging Materials, and Drug Delivery Devices," "New Materials, New Carriers, and Innovative Formulations," and "Pharmaceutical Excipients and Innovative Drugs," promoting the wide participation of enterprises, academia, and young scholars to jointly focus on the technological innovation and industrial research and development of pharmaceutical excipients. The relevant matters are hereby notified as follows: 1. Conference theme Promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new quality productivity of the pharmaceutical industry 2. Time and place November 8th Registration Venue: Hefei Xinji Hotel (2766 Wenzhong Road, Yaohai District, Hefei City, Anhui Province) The main venue and sub-venues on November 9-10 are both at the Shaoquanhu Campus of Anhui University of Chinese Medicine in Hefei, Anhui Province (350 Longzihu Road, Yaohai District, Hefei City, Anhui Province) 3. Conference arrangements The conference will adopt a format of main venue and sub-venue reports for communication. The conference will invite well-known experts and scholars from domestic universities, research institutes, pharmaceutical companies, research and development units, medical institutions, regulatory agencies, etc., to give keynote speeches and special lectures. Please refer to Annex 1 for the detailed schedule. 4. Participants Researchers, managers, and graduate students engaged in research and development related to pharmaceutical excipients, pharmaceutical packaging materials, drug delivery devices, formulation quality control, formulation equipment, pharmaceutical services, etc., from higher education institutions, research institutes, pharmaceutical companies, research and development units, medical institutions, drug regulatory agencies, and other related institutions. 5. Conference paper submission 1. Requirements for paper submission Chinese and English abstracts and paper format. Papers that have not been published in publicly distributed journals or presented at national academic conferences are the responsibility of the authors; please ensure clear expression and accurate data. Researchers in the pharmaceutical field are welcome to actively submit papers. 2. Paper submission method: Please submit the paper abstract before October 20, 2024, by logging on to the conference website https://yyfl2024.sciconf.cn, clicking on the "Online Paper Submission" button on the right, and following the process to upload your paper abstract. After successful upload, you will receive an automatic email confirmation of online submission. After expert review, the organizing committee will select several papers for further communication or publication in the "Drug Analysis" journal. 3. Poster submission method and time: Same as for papers. The conference welcomes poster submissions, which should be in A1 standard size. 6. Registration (1) Registration method 1. Please register by clicking on the "Individual Representative Registration" or "Group Representative Registration" button on the conference website link https://yyfl2024.sciconf.cn; 2. Or scan (or long-press to recognize) the QR code below with your mobile phone, click on the "Individual Representative Registration" or "Group Representative Registration" button to fill in the registration information and submit. (2) Registration deadline The registration deadline is October 30, 2024. (3) Notes on registration 1. To ensure that participants receive registration confirmation, invoices, etc., please fill in accurate and true information such as email address and mobile phone number; 2. This registration website is only for registration, and the payment channel is not yet open; 3. Registered individuals can log in to the conference website's personal center to check and modify their registration information; 4. Participants who do not submit papers can also attend the conference. 7. Conference fees (1) Conference registration fee 1. Registration fee standard The registration fee includes conference material fees and lunch during the conference. 2. Payment methods (1) Telegraphic transfer: After registering for the conference, participants should pay the registration fee by bank transfer, supporting both corporate and personal transfers to the following account: Payee: Chinese Pharmaceutical Association Bank: Bank of China Head Office Account number: 778350009320 It is recommended to use online banking for personal transfers, or you can also use Alipay transfer (to a bank card, with the name field filled in as "Chinese Pharmaceutical Association"). Please indicate "Pharmaceutical Excipients + Participant's Name + Unit Abbreviation" in the remittance note.
