title_en: How do Internet "big companies" build a good employment "reservoir"?
body_en:
This year, the scale of the national college graduates is expected to reach 12.22 million. How to stabilize employment? As an important "reservoir" for employment, internet "big companies" and other platforms have always played a unique role in stabilizing employment. It is understood that currently, various parties are working together to stabilize employment by all means, with some companies focusing on key groups for employment and others launching large-scale employment plans.
Recently, many well-known companies have announced their recruitment plans. Meituan is expected to recruit 5,000 people in the spring campus recruitment in 2025; Alibaba has opened more than 3,000 internship positions this year; Midea Group is expected to provide over 2,000 campus recruitment positions this year...
Not long ago, Tencent launched the "largest employment plan in history," adding 28,000 campus recruitment positions in 3 years. "Campus recruitment is one of Tencent's most important sources of talent." Xidan, Senior Vice President and Chief Talent Officer of Tencent, said that under the theme of technological innovation-driven development, Tencent is also strengthening its forward-looking reserve of technological talents and growing together with young talents.
Baidu also announced that it will open 21,000 internship positions for outstanding campus talents in the next 3 years and continue to strengthen the training of interns to further increase the conversion rate of interns to full-time employees. It is understood that Baidu's 2026 campus recruitment will soon be launched, and the relevant person in charge stated that they will actively recruit and train outstanding talents, hoping to have more outstanding young talents to "shoulder the heavy responsibility." In addition to campus recruitment, companies are also actively absorbing social recruitment talents.
Starting from February, Alibaba has launched the spring 2026 internship recruitment, with a focus on artificial intelligence (AI) talents. Data shows that AI-related positions account for nearly half of the over 3,000 positions opened in this year's spring recruitment. "Alibaba is increasing its efforts to introduce and train talents in the AI field. We hope to provide a broad development space for more outstanding young talents and jointly embrace the huge development opportunities of the AI era," said Jiang Fang, Chief Talent Officer of Alibaba Group.
Under the wave of AI development, the contradiction between the youth's desire for career opportunities in emerging fields and the gap in skills is becoming increasingly prominent. Some large companies are building multi-level skill training systems through systematic engineering and digital service innovation.
At the Create2025 Baidu AI Developer Conference, Baidu's founder Robin Li announced that in the next 5 years, Baidu will intensify its efforts to cultivate 10 million AI talents for society. In terms of AI-empowered employment, Baidu previously collaborated with the Wuhan General Union to launch the "Second Skill Learning Platform for Workers," helping workers acquire a second skill.
New forms of employment such as food delivery riders, online ride-hailing drivers, and e-commerce agricultural entrepreneurs are creating a large number of job opportunities for society. While expanding their own recruitment scale, many large platform companies are also actively responding to policy calls, continuously exerting efforts around new forms of employment, and making every effort to ensure diversified employment and expand employment space.
In supporting high-quality and full employment for delivery riders, since 2023, Meituan has launched the "Spring Wind Sends Jobs" initiative, providing comprehensive employment support for delivery riders through six measures, while innovatively introducing the "Bole Award" incentive, online and offline recruitment linkage, and part-time models at dedicated delivery sites.
"Last year, the average monthly number of single delivery riders reached 3.36 million." A person in charge of Meituan told reporters that the average monthly income of high-frequency delivery riders nationwide last year ranged from 6,650 yuan to 9,344 yuan, with the average income of high-frequency delivery riders in various regions still slightly higher than the average income of local residents.
The rights protection system for delivery riders is gradually being established. In recent years, Meituan has invested 1.4 billion yuan to pay occupational injury insurance premiums for over 6 million delivery riders. From the end of last year to the beginning of this year, Meituan successively launched anti-fatigue mechanisms, canceled overtime deductions, and announced the payment of social security for full-time and stable part-time delivery riders nationwide. On May 8th, the first batch of delivery riders participating in the pilot of Meituan's pension insurance received news of subsidy payments.
Data released by the National Bureau of Statistics recently showed that the national urban surveyed unemployment rate in April was 5.1%, a decrease of 0.1 percentage points from the previous month, marking a two-month consecutive decline. The achievement was made possible not only by policy support but also by the "real money" support from enterprises.
Recently, Pinduoduo launched the "100 Billion Support" plan to assist businesses and benefit farmers, supporting small and medium-sized merchants in starting businesses and further expanding employment capacity. The person in charge of the "100 Billion Support" plan stated that Pinduoduo will use this as the main focus to fully leverage the social effectiveness of platform-type enterprises in stabilizing employment, promoting growth, and building a win-win business ecosystem for users, merchants, and platforms.
Not long ago, Didi announced an additional investment of 2 billion yuan in special funds, focusing on "stabilizing employment and promoting consumption" to help the manufacturing industry "go global." Of the 10 billion yuan, 1 billion yuan will be used to increase driver subsidies, optimize driver income, and enhance driver rights protection. Didi stated that it will fully leverage the role of the employment "reservoir" as a safety net.
sentiment_reason: Alibaba is opening up numerous positions, particularly in the AI field, but without any discernible emotional preference.

title_en: Spend 200 yuan and get a tax refund. Foreigners flock to Huaxiangbei to buy goods.
body_en:
Left picture: Since the beginning of this year, the number of foreign tourists in Huaqiangbei has increased by over 50% compared to the same period last year, with over 7,000 foreign tourists coming to shop every day. The picture shows Thai and British tourists with 28-inch empty suitcases, coming to buy products such as selfie sticks and camera mounts. Upper right picture: West Asian customers buying Bluetooth speakers. Lower right picture: Zimbabwean tourists buying a large quantity of toys.
In order to attract more overseas visitors to travel to China, China introduced a 240-hour transit visa-free policy at the end of last year, and overseas visitors can get tax refunds for shopping. Currently, the minimum amount of tax refundable items purchased by foreign tourists in the same store on the same day has been reduced from 500 RMB to 200 RMB, which is equivalent to a 10% discount on the purchased goods, attracting many foreigners to shop in Shenzhen.
As China's number one electronic street, Huaqiangbei in Shenzhen attracts a large number of foreigners to shop or make bulk purchases of mobile phones, drones, and 3C electronic products. A reporter recently visited Huaqiangbei and found a large number of customers from the UK, France, Russia, West Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and other places gathering there, some bringing large empty suitcases to make purchases, some to give gifts to family members. By Li Changhong, Ta Kung Pao (text, photos)
For decades, Huaqiangbei in Shenzhen, as China's number one electronic street, has been well-known overseas. Since the beginning of this year, the number of foreign tourists in Huaqiangbei has increased by over 50% compared to the same period last year, with over 7,000 foreign tourists coming to shop every day. Tax refund agencies also stated that Chinese-made mobile phones and drones have outstanding sales, accounting for nearly 40% of all tax refund applications.
African tourists: Will purchase more in the future
A reporter recently visited the SEG Market in Huaqiangbei and saw numerous foreigners experiencing products, bargaining with merchants, and making purchases. On the fourth floor of the market, a merchant selling monitoring equipment was testing the effectiveness of the equipment for a tourist from Nigeria. After some bargaining, the tourist decided to purchase three units, each priced at 170 RMB, totaling about 60 RMB less. He said he would use them himself and recommend them to friends, and will purchase more in the future. The merchant said the product supports multiple languages such as Chinese and English, attracting many foreign customers.
British tourists: Alipay payment is too convenient
On the fifth floor of the market, the reporter saw two young tourists from Thailand and the UK, both carrying 28-inch empty suitcases, purchasing camera mounts. The British tourist said, "We have already listed all the things we want to buy, including lightweight selfie sticks, camera tripods, etc., which must be very cheap and lightweight. After trying them out when we get back, we will buy in bulk to sell to our peers. The Thai tourist purchased a three-meter selfie stick and camera mount totaling over 1,000 RMB, and then paid with Alipay. The British tourist exclaimed, "It's too convenient."
At the corner of the elevator on the fourth floor of the market, the reporter saw three tourists from Zimbabwe in Africa buying toy drones, water speedboats, and other toys. One of the tourists told the reporter that the three of them each bought nearly a thousand RMB worth of items to take back home for their children to play with. "Chinese products are very innovative, a toy drone costs 200 RMB, and a water speedboat is about 80 RMB, with a high cost-performance ratio." An employee of the store even gave them a receipt, claiming that if it breaks, they can send it back to China for free repairs. The postage back and forth is definitely not cheap, this kind of service is amazing, and it is also their way of attracting foreign tourists.
Foreigners are limited to purchasing two drones per person
Drones are a popular product that many tourists are very interested in. The reporter saw many customers coming to inquire and purchase at the DJI Huaqiangbei store. Some employees said that recently, many customers have come to buy, including from Europe, the Middle East, Southeast Asia, and Hong Kong, China. Most of the drones purchased are the DJI FLIP versatile VLOG aerial drones, priced between 2,700 RMB and 3,900 RMB, but there are also drones with higher prices for better shooting quality. However, foreigners are limited to purchasing a maximum of two drones per person, and many people go to handle tax refunds when leaving. In addition, many people from Hong Kong also come to buy, but they need to register and report before flying in Hong Kong, while in mainland China, it is not necessary.

title_en: Nanjing leaps from the pivot of world culture to super link.
body_en:
□ Our reporters Lu Lin, Sheng Wenhu, Li Kai, Yan Fang
On June 6, leaders from the three provinces and one city in the Yangtze River Delta, whose combined GDP accounts for over 25% of the national total, gathered in Nanjing to discuss how to elevate the high-quality integrated development of the region.
Development of higher quality is inseparable from smoother flow and more efficient agglomeration.
Agglomeration is like the law of universal gravitation in urban development; resources always flow automatically to regions with the highest output. Enhanced flow is becoming a long-term trend.
On June 6, Nanjing South Railway Station saw over 1,380 inbound and outbound trains, carrying more than 300,000 passengers.
On this day, Nanjing transmitted 10PB of data, equivalent to the data size of 100 million high-definition movies. These pulsing bytes and flowing data embed the city into an invisible fabric of longitude and latitude, connecting everything and making cities interdependent.
Twenty years ago, leaders from the two provinces and one city in the Yangtze River Delta held their first symposium. In the past two decades, high-speed rail, talent, and data have formed super-links, while trade, information, and artificial intelligence have accelerated the reshaping of industrial landscapes and urban capacities. As an important central city in eastern China, Nanjing's hub status has continuously advanced.

Shanghai-Nanjing High-Speed Rail Runs Every Two Minutes
On the afternoon of May 31, Ms. Lu from Nanjing departed from her home on Nanjing Software Avenue and arrived at Nanjing South Railway Station in just 15 minutes. The D5509 high-speed train she boarded departed punctually at 15:22, and 35 minutes later, she arrived at Wuhu Station. After exiting the station, Ms. Lu headed straight to a dessert shop in Jinghu District, with the entire journey taking less than an hour.
Ms. Lu is a dessert enthusiast who loves to visit popular internet-famous food spots. Recently, while browsing Xiaohongshu, she became deeply interested in the signature walnut and matcha mille-feuille at the popular Wuhu dessert shop "always 常伴烘焙坊." To try it, she embarked on a spontaneous "high-speed rail dessert trip."
Traveling across cities just for a bowl of noodles, a small dish, or a dessert is an advanced benefit of the "Yangtze River Delta on Rails."
Convenient transportation has made "going to another city" a daily occurrence.
On the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway, passengers open their laptops on the tray tables to handle work or engage in quiet business discussions. The speeding train serves not only as a mode of transport but also as a mobile office. Despite frequent online interactions and advanced instant messaging, high-value social interactions like business negotiations and emotional exchanges still require face-to-face contact. The sentiment of "let's meet up" is not diminishing but increasing.
Such scenarios are reshaping the lives and work patterns of residents in the Yangtze River Delta, and Nanjing, an ancient capital of a thousand years, is playing an increasingly important role in the integration process of the region.
Nanjing offers direct high-speed rail connections to 25 provincial capitals across the country, forming a "one-hour high-speed rail circle" with Shanghai, Nanjing, Hangzhou, and Hefei. There are over 600 high-speed trains between Nanjing and Shanghai daily, with a train departing or arriving every less than two minutes, truly achieving "bus-like" operations. Even so, tickets for the one-hour Fuxinghao bullet train from Nanjing to Shanghai are often sold out two to three days in advance.
The high-speed rail network in the Yangtze River Delta continues to be densified, presenting both opportunities and threats for Nanjing. The under-construction Yantai-Taizhou-Wuxi-Changzhou-Yixing Railway will connect to the Xuzhou-Yancheng High-Speed Railway in the north and the Nanjing-Hangzhou High-Speed Railway in the south, forming a rapid passage that runs through the central part of Jiangsu Province. This passage shortens the spatial and temporal distance between Taizhou, Yancheng, and other cities with Nanjing, promoting the integration of the Nanjing metropolitan area with central and northern Jiangsu. However, upon the opening of the Yantai-Taizhou-Wuxi-Changzhou-Yixing Railway, passengers traveling from Yancheng and Taizhou to Wuxi and Changzhou will be able to travel directly south, reducing passenger flow at Nanjing South Railway Station.
The Nanjing North Railway Station, currently under construction and scheduled to be operational in 2027, will significantly enhance Nanjing's hub status. The North Station is planned to have 3 stations, 16 platforms, and 30 tracks, exceeding Nanjing South Station (15 platforms, 28 tracks). It will be able to handle an annual passenger throughput of 36.5 million people and accommodate a maximum of 135,000 people at any given time, greatly increasing Nanjing's railway capacity.
Beyond capacity enhancement, Nanjing will further unleash its hub potential. Nanjing North Station is the largest hub station along the Northern Yangtze River High-Speed Railway (Shanghai-Chongqing-Chengdu High-Speed Railway). It will eventually connect to cities like Shanghai, Hefei, and Wuhan, while also incorporating the Ninghai Intercity Railway (Nanjing-Huai'an) and the Ningchu-Bengbu Intercity Railway (Nanjing-Chuzhou-Bengbu). This will form a high-speed rail corridor along the Yangtze River, strengthening Nanjing's radiating influence to northern Jiangsu and northern Anhui, and establishing it as a crucial node between the Yangtze River Delta and the middle reaches of the Yangtze River and the Chengdu-Chongqing urban agglomeration, thereby reinforcing Nanjing's function as an "important central city in eastern China."
Nanjing is one of the few cities in the country with a multimodal transport system encompassing air, rail, water, road, and pipeline transport, and it is designated by the state as an international comprehensive transportation hub. Over 90% of China's foreign trade transportation is conducted via waterways. The Nanjing section of the Yangtze River is known as the "Diamond Waterway," with Longtan Port possessing a particularly prominent geographical advantage. Due to the air draft restrictions of the Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge, Nanjing becomes the last deep-water port area in the lower reaches of the Yangtze River capable of docking large ocean-going vessels. It is also located at the intersection of the Yangtze River channel and the Beijing-Shanghai Railway, with a dense network of expressways. Nanjing Port is the only port in the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River that achieves seamless integration of water and rail transport, offering distinct advantages in cargo transfer. Longtan Port operates five "point-to-point" express voyages from Nanjing to Shanghai Port every week, with the fastest arrival at Shanghai Port in 33 hours. In 2024, Nanjing Port's container throughput increased by 7.2% year-on-year, with white goods from Anhui being one of the main cargo types. These items are gathered in Nanjing, depart from Nanjing, and are then transported to Shanghai, Ningbo, and worldwide.

Shanghai, Nanjing, and Hangzhou Form Their Own Talent Niches
Even more attention is paid to the increasingly frequent movement of people than the flow of goods.
The large-scale movement of talent is bound to produce the creators of a new era.
For example, Jiang Yong, the founder of Jiangsu Ailichen Furniture Group, is shaping the future of his company. Jiang Yong originally followed his factory from Xuzhou, where he engaged in e-commerce for over a decade. He has now transitioned to cross-border business and moved his headquarters to the Jiangbei New Area in Nanjing. Nanjing alone is not enough; he frequently travels between Hangzhou, Shanghai, and Xuzhou.
"Nanjing has many talented people and good policies," Jiang Yong explained. The company has added two major business segments: international marketing, establishing independent websites, and stocking products on Amazon and TEMU (Pinduoduo's international version) to build brands; and building a digital supply chain platform for the furniture industry, led by Chinese supply chains, radiating to the cross-border e-commerce home furnishing industry clusters in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Shanghai, moving from simply trading to leading the industry in informationization and digitalization.
After spending the past half-year traveling extensively in the Yangtze River Delta, Jiang Yong has discovered distinct complementary strengths among the talent pools of Shanghai, Nanjing, and Hangzhou. Nanjing has a large number of software engineers and abundant talent, with ample supply for positions in system development and product design. Hangzhou, on the other hand, has a large number of operation talents, with a richer pool for positions such as live streaming, platform operations, and store management, making it easier to recruit for these roles in Hangzhou. Shanghai is the city closest to international talent, gathering a large number of high-end R&D talents.
Li Yue, an online blogger, moved her team from Shanghai to Nanjing. Her company, Nanjing Caimao Shuangquan Cultural Media Co., Ltd., is a creative media company primarily focused on producing video content. Li Yue explained that Nanjing has many cultural and creative talents. The team uses Nanjing as a hub for content production and creativity, building content assets, refining expression models, and training content IPs. They use Shanghai as a port for brand cooperation and dissemination, establishing efficient connections with platforms, advertisers, and leading institutions. Relying on Hangzhou's platform ecosystem and e-commerce cultural environment, they conduct content monetization experiments and co-creation transformations targeting end consumers.
"We write stories in Nanjing, and sell them to Shanghai to hear in Hangzhou," Li Yue said. The linkage of Nanjing, Shanghai, and Hangzhou, i.e., Nanjing consolidates content → Shanghai releases influence → Hangzhou tests conversion, forms a three-in-one operational closed loop of content, brand, and channels.
In three years, Nanjing Duandian Xingchen Technology Co., Ltd. rapidly expanded from over 50 employees in 2019 to more than 400. The company secured an entire floor of office space in the Jianye District New City Science and Technology Park to accommodate its rapid growth.
Founded in 2012 by entrepreneurs from Alibaba, Duandian Technology was established in Hangzhou. Duandian's core business is providing digital solutions for enterprises. With rapid business expansion, the company recognized Nanjing's abundant university resources and talent advantages and established an independent company in Nanjing. "Nanjing has a high density of universities, ample reserves of technical talent, and we have a significant amount of business in Nanjing, so we established an independent company here," said Lu Yihang, co-founder of Duandian Technology.
Currently, Duandian Technology has established a clear regional division of labor: the Hangzhou headquarters focuses on R&D of the technical platform, the Nanjing company focuses on product delivery and market implementation, and major clients such as Bright Dairy and BP Oil are concentrated in Shanghai. Lu Yihang himself frequently travels between cities in the Yangtze River Delta. He candidly admitted, "When planning and deploying, enterprises must leverage the advantages of each city while achieving optimal resource allocation through efficient collaboration."
As a hub of talent, Nanjing has attracted regional R&D headquarters for Xiaomi, Alibaba, and a large number of central enterprises. These "big companies" attract talent from all directions like a pasture.
In May last year, the Xiaomi Nanjing Science Park officially opened, and the Xiaomi Group East China Headquarters was established. Xiaomi's business in Nanjing began with initial mobile phone R&D and has gradually expanded to cover multiple core business areas, including electric vehicles and internet services. The Xiaomi Group East China Headquarters will grow into a research and development team of tens of thousands. With rapid business expansion, the demand for professional talent with solid technical capabilities has also surged. Xiaomi Group launched its first engineer training camp in Nanjing, collaborating with universities such as Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications.
This year, the Xiaomi Group East China Headquarters laboratory cluster was completed and put into use ahead of schedule, creating a strong demand for hardware engineer talent. The software engineer talent training model that has been successfully implemented in Nanjing is being "replicated" by Xiaomi Group to more fields. Xiaomi Group will launch a hardware engineer training camp at Hefei University of Technology. The training camp will feature R&D personnel with over ten years of experience at Xiaomi serving as mentors, providing "pre-emptive training" to students, guiding them in applying knowledge to specific projects, transforming written theories into business capabilities, and bringing cutting-edge industry technology trends into the campus. Graduates who pass the interviews after the training camp will have the opportunity to directly work at the Xiaomi Group East China Headquarters.

Urban Collaboration Reshapes Industrial Landscape
The flow of talent often offers insights into industrial trends.
With the upgrading of Chinese manufacturing and adjustments in both domestic and international markets, a large number of companies are restructuring their corporate architectures and city layouts. Jiangsu-based enterprises looking to go global often establish their headquarters or new business centers in Nanjing, forming an industrial synergy pattern of "headquarters in Nanjing, production in surrounding areas."
Jiangsu Xinghuo Special Steel Group, which has been based in Dainan Town, Taizhou, the "hometown of stainless steel," for over 30 years, has for the first time moved a significant business unit to Nanjing, establishing a sales company to focus on developing overseas markets. Cui Mingzhe, director of the sales department, stated that the company began to focus on the international market last year. The company is building digital production lines, and with remote control of production, many positions can be relocated to central cities. Future R&D will also be considered for relocation to Nanjing.
It is currently the "summer harvest" season, and millions of agricultural machines are operating across the vast fields of China. In the boundless sky, the Beidou satellite system transmits the location information, operational area, and equipment status of these machines to the foot of Zijin Mountain. At Jiangsu International Data Port, China Machinery Science and Technology's "Agricultural Machinery Cloud," a secondary headquarters of a central enterprise, aggregates this data and simultaneously develops large models such as "Shennong Assistant" and "Shennong Expert," promoting the advancement of agricultural mechanization towards digitalization, intelligence, and precision.
In the AI era, data is the core element for developing new quality productive forces. As early as 2020, Lianhe Investment, Shanghai Xintou, and Lingang Technology City, three state-owned enterprises, established Shanghai Lingang Cross-border Digital Technology to build new infrastructure that aligns with international digital trade rules, covering the entire process and all aspects of international data flow and cooperation.
In September 2023, Xuanwu District Government and Shanghai Lingang Cross-border Digital Technology signed a cooperation agreement to jointly build the Jiangsu International Data Port, explore compliant cross-border data services, build the province's only compliant data flow service platform, and create the core hub for data circulation in Jiangsu.
Since last year, the Jiangsu International Data Port has been cooperating deeply with the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology (CAICT) and has launched the country's first "Battery Product Digital Passport (B-DPP) Construction Project." In early this year, Honeycomb Energy received the first domestically produced "Battery Product Digital Passport."
Nanjing Xuanwu District is cooperating with Jiangsu Telecom to vigorously build the "Xuanwu Large Model Factory," supporting the construction of a computing power scheduling center for the large model industry. The initial phase will provide over 1000P computing power support, and financial products totaling over 1 billion yuan for large model technology innovation loans have been released, continuously improving the industrial ecosystem.
Among the generative AI large model enterprises registered in our province, Youling Technology, founded only two years ago, is the youngest enterprise on the list.
Youling Technology is headquartered in Nanjing with a branch in Hangzhou and has launched "I Am in AI," the industry's first interactive novel platform. Users can create virtual characters and interact through voice and text to experience immersive storylines. This application has become a hit with tens of millions of users in just one year, with users spending an average of over an hour per day on the platform.
"Hangzhou has more talent with internet experience; the main business of the Hangzhou branch is operations and products. Nanjing is rich in educational and scientific resources, making it easier to attract software talent. Senior management is accustomed to the 'dual-city life' of commuting between the two places. The teams in both locations cooperate and support each other, complementing each other, and are indispensable," analyzed He Zixuan, founder of Youling. He believes that as large models are a new track, young people have less path dependency and fewer burdens, and Nanjing has immense potential.
From high-speed trains speeding along to data flowing, from talent interaction to industrial synergy, Nanjing is deeply integrating into the Yangtze River Delta integration with an all-around open posture. With the advancement of major projects such as the Yantai-Taizhou-Wuxi-Changzhou-Yixing Railway and the Northern Yangtze River High-Speed Railway, this former "hub of scholars" is becoming a super-link in tangible and intangible channels.

title_en: 21 editorials | Real-time retail competition is escalating, requiring a better balance between efficiency and fairness.
body_en:
Recently, the instant retail market has seen intense competition. JD.com launched its "self-operated instant delivery" service, while Meituan responded with the launch of its instant retail brand "Meituan Flash Purchase". Following suit, Taobao upgraded its "hourly delivery" to "Taobao Flash Purchase", leveraging the delivery network of Ele.me to accelerate its layout in the instant retail market.

The so-called "instant retail" is to meet the demand of consumers for "buy now, get now", based on an instant delivery system that emphasizes "order online, deliver within 30 minutes". This demand is continuously growing among young people, as indicated by a report from consulting firm Accenture focusing on the consumption habits of post-95s in China, where over 50% of post-95s wish to receive their purchased goods on the same day, making "speed" an important factor influencing the consumption decisions of the younger generation.

For platforms, the online consumer market traffic dividend is becoming saturated, and they must seek new increments. Therefore, by expanding the boundaries of takeaway or express delivery through their respective delivery systems, in addition to catering and fresh produce, categories such as medicine, daily necessities, clothing, and digital products are also included in the scope of "order now, deliver now". As a result, various platforms are competing for this incremental business, but from the perspective of the consumer market, it may be more about replacing existing market share.

From the consumer's perspective, instant retail brings a better experience through efficient and convenient delivery, saving time and enhancing consumer stickiness, reshaping consumption habits, and making consumers more inclined towards online shopping and instant delivery services. This will bring significant pressure to traditional commerce, especially in areas such as emergency consumption and fresh shopping, gradually eroding the market share of traditional commerce.

Technology brings efficiency improvement. With the world interconnected by internet technology, platform enterprises can significantly reduce the cost and time of information communication through the network, leading to sustained rapid growth in e-commerce business. Algorithms provide platforms with more information and decision-making power, enabling them to promote transactions in an efficient and flexible manner in areas such as product pricing and delivery efficiency. As consumers have higher demands for "speed", instant retail will reshape the circulation path of goods from warehouses to users, continuously reducing the time window from "ordering to receiving", changing the traditional retail distribution system.

Traditional supermarkets have already been impacted by e-commerce to some extent. Now, some vertical domain physical stores, community fresh stores, and farmers' markets may lose some customers, and convenience stores, like the catering industry, will provide sources for instant retail while paying some commissions. Some traditional businesses are also undergoing digital transformation, but perhaps in the short term, they cannot compete with the network effects of platforms, as platforms have a large scale of orders and delivery personnel, which can reduce costs, while traditional business delivery costs will be much higher, making it difficult for traditional businesses to resist.

The digital economy brings higher efficiency and more new business models, driving business innovation and revolution. The core of this revolution is efficiency, being able to deliver goods to customers at a lower cost and faster speed, and giving consumers countless choices. This change greatly promotes consumption, improves consumer experience and business dividends, and reduces consumer living costs. Instant retail is bringing consumers a more magical experience: instant satisfaction.

However, the digital economy, which is mainly based on online platform sales, also brings broader impacts, including various online sales such as e-commerce and instant retail, creating a large number of jobs in delivery, warehousing, transportation, etc., directly delivering goods from production sites to customers, and from warehousing directly to consumers. This process will replace a large number of intermediate jobs on one hand, but also increase the demand for related workers, such as delivery drivers and couriers.

It is also necessary to pay attention to the impact of e-commerce on the employment structure of traditional businesses, and create more job opportunities for specific groups. In short, it is necessary to balance efficiency and fairness, rather than blindly pursue efficiency, to make society more equal in income and make people's lives easier, which may be more conducive to promoting consumption and creating more jobs.

title_en: "Promoting physical fitness and cultivating people", sports open up new windows of dreams for children in the village.
body_en:
"Pay attention to defense" "Don't rush" "Good ball" ... Once again representing the school to go out for a game, You Xuan, the captain of the girls' basketball team at Huilong Primary School in Xingren City, Guizhou Province, calmly responds to the changes on the court, with a confident and sunny face, completely unlike the introverted and speechless girl she was at the beginning.
In recent years, with the development of sports education in rural schools and the organization of various sports events, the campus life of rural students has become more colorful. The spiritual outlook of rural students has been injected with new vitality because of sports, and the future of some rural students has become more promising. The inheritance of sports has also promoted the generation of a positive cycle.
This is the "sports dream" of countless rural children today.
Because of sports
What is sports, perhaps can be seen on the playgrounds of rural schools in Guizhou.
During the leisure time at Tangfang Primary School in Baling Town, Xingren City, Guizhou Province, students running and jumping can be seen everywhere on the playground. Playing basketball, badminton, soccer... the laughter of children echoes in the campus.
Over the past 20 years, this rural school, which originally had only 3 teachers and 75 students, has grown with the educational philosophy of "cultivating people with sports and revitalizing the school with sports". Currently, the school has 42 teachers and nearly 500 students, and the average student scores have increased from less than 30 points to over 80 points. Principal Wu Xiong said that the improvement in the level of education is inseparable from the improvement of the teaching environment and the hard work of the teachers, among which sports activities also play an important role.
"Through participating in a variety of sports activities, students become more cheerful in character, stronger in body, and healthier in mind. Going out to participate in competitions also broadens their horizons." Wu Xiong said, making children happy is more important than making them excellent, and sports is a way to make them happier.
In the view of Jiang Dejin, deputy director of the Education and Technology Bureau of Dafang County, Guizhou, sports not only teach students skills, but more importantly, give them a hobby, allowing them to release stress correctly in their spare time from studying, which will benefit them for a lifetime.
Psychologists believe that participating in sports can help students relieve study pressure, cultivate strong willpower, promote interpersonal communication, help establish a positive attitude, and improve psychological adjustment abilities.
Sports have also changed the life trajectories of some rural students, giving them more possibilities for the future.
Sanhe Primary School in Shizhu County, Chongqing, is famous for its soccer. Since the team was established in March 2013, the achievements of the school's women's soccer team have been remarkable: winning the "Chasing the Wind League" championship twice, winning over 30 city-level and above competition championships, 39 former team members have reached the national level athlete standard, 1 has reached the national level athlete standard, 7 have been selected for the Chongqing U18 women's soccer team roster; in 2024, the school's women's soccer team was also selected for the national "New Era Good Teenagers" advanced deeds release list...
Recently, Sanhe Primary School has received good news again. Among the third batch of 10 members of the women's soccer team, one was admitted to Inner Mongolia University last year, and another 6 are currently being provisionally admitted to Chongqing Normal University and other universities. Among the first batch of 21 members of the women's soccer team, 20 have been admitted to universities such as Tongji University.
Yuanbao Tongxin Experimental School in Dafang County, Guizhou, is also well-known for its women's soccer team. Currently, this rural school's women's soccer team has accumulated 14 people who have been admitted to the Southwest Branch of the Chinese Football Academy, and 7 have been admitted to the Shanxi Datong Youth and Children's Sports School...
Assistance from all sides
In addition to local sports teachers and government support, assistance from all sides is also indispensable.
In the exhibition hall of Yuanbao Tongxin Experimental School, there is a novel called "Time Traveler: The Fog of the Middle Ages". In 2017, the author of the novel, Zhang Zhouchen, donated the 50,000 yuan he earned from selling books to the school. The school used this money to build a simple soccer field that is 30 meters long and 18 meters wide, which has become the starting point for the "Yuanbao Women's Soccer" dream.
Now, next to this soccer field, a larger field has been put into use. After school every afternoon, more than 80 members of the school's soccer team will train on the field.
This is not an isolated case. In recent years, various levels of relevant departments, public welfare organizations, caring companies, and individuals have put a lot of effort into improving the sports environment in rural schools and raising the level of sports education in rural schools.
In December 2022, a five-a-side soccer field built with funds from a designated assistance unit was completed and put into use. Lazi Shu Primary School in Puan County, Qiannan Prefecture, Guizhou Province now has its own soccer field, and the training environment for the children has been improved. Previously, the children could only practice on a cement basketball court, and the training conditions were very rudimentary.
Chen Ming, a physical education teacher at Huilong Primary School, said that when the school first formed a basketball team, the Yao Foundation would send volunteers to the school every year to train teachers and guide students in training. Data from the Yao Foundation's official website shows that by the end of 2023, this public welfare project had supported a total of 4661 rural schools, sent 6512 volunteer teachers, trained 1239 rural full-time and part-time physical education teachers, and benefited about 5.4 million rural youth.
At Sanhe Primary School, the arrival of Guo Xin, the former head coach of the Dalian Women's Soccer Youth Training Center, has allowed the children of the women's soccer team to experience more professional and scientific training methods, significantly improving their competitive level. After leading the team to defend their title at the national finals of the "Chasing the Wind League", Guo Xin left the team due to age reasons, but he had already arranged for a new professional coach to come and coach the team. "He still cares about the children of the team and will come back to guide them from time to time," said the former principal, Sun Xiaoming.
In 2019, Alipay announced a 10 billion yuan investment over 10 years to support the development of Chinese women's soccer, and also launched the "Chasing the Wind Plan" to support the development of women's soccer in rural campus. Currently, the plan has supported over 200 rural campus women's soccer teams, helping over 6000 rural girls enjoy soccer more happily and obtain more educational opportunities through soccer.
The General Administration of Sport of China launched the Sports Support Volunteer Service in 2021. This "dream-making project" relies on thousands of volunteers from dozens of universities to alleviate the shortage of grassroots sports teachers and sow the seeds of sports dreams in beautiful rural schools.
Returning to the mountains
Sports have helped the children, and the children have not forgotten sports or their hometown.
"This is Niu Lihua, who graduated from junior high school and went to Tsinghua University High School, and was later admitted to Tsinghua University. She is currently studying for a master's degree at Tsinghua; this is Guo Zhongrui, who won second place in the national marathon championship in 2024 and was selected for national team training in 2021..." When mentioning the students he has taught, Wang Bin is full of pride and satisfaction.
Wang Bin is a physical education teacher at Wumeng Town Middle School in Panzhou City, Guizhou Province. He was born in a local village, where his father was a primary school teacher who loved sports. Influenced by his father, he showed a strong interest in sports from a young age.
In 1992, Wang Bin was sent by his parents to study martial arts at the Wushu School in Beihai, Guangxi. In September 1996, he enrolled in the Guizhou Sports School to study sports. After graduating in 1999, he returned to his hometown to become a primary school teacher. In 2001, he was transferred to Wumeng Town Middle School as a physical education teacher. This is a rural school located at the junction of three counties in Yunnan and Guizhou provinces.
When he first arrived at Wumeng Town Middle School, faced with poor school conditions and outdated training facilities, Wang Bin developed a set of physical training models suitable for rural junior high school students. From demonstration movements to decomposed movements, he taught them step by step. In order to save time and energy for students who had a long way to travel to school, Wang Bin also called some children to his home, provided them with food and accommodation, and personally bought sports uniforms and shoes for the students...
With Wang Bin's efforts, the school has currently sent hundreds of outstanding athletes to regular high schools, sports schools, sports teams, and universities. The students have repeatedly achieved good results in various competitions at all levels, winning over 40 group awards at the national, provincial, municipal, and county levels.
A few years ago, his student Li Micong returned to his hometown after graduating from university and became a primary school teacher in a rural school. Li Micong studied sports, but there was a shortage of teachers in rural schools, so she had to teach subjects other than physical education, making her workload heavier. Even so, she would use her spare time to teach the children basketball, table tennis, and soccer. In recent years, she has taken students to the city to participate in basketball games and sports meetings. Although the results were not ideal, the children trained seriously, gave their all in the competitions, and never gave up, which moved her deeply.
Not long ago, Li Micong organized a fun sports meeting, and the laughter and scenes of students working together and striving for the best at the event left a deep impression on her. "Next semester, we plan to hold an autumn sports meeting to further enrich the students' campus life and make more students fall in love with sports," she said.
Over a thousand miles away from Panzhou City, at Sanhe Primary School, every winter and summer vacation, a group of familiar figures will appear on the campus - the former members of the school's women's soccer team. "Every winter and summer vacation, the former team members will come to the school in pairs and take turns to guide the younger students in training. Passing on the torch and continuing the struggle has become a tradition," said Sun Xiaoming.
Today, Wang Bin is still holding on, but the relay baton of rural sports education has quietly completed its transfer.
(Reporter Zheng Minghong) Xinhua News Agency, Guiyang

title_en: The global trend of playing economy is booming, and brands are competing for "explosive IP".
body_en:
Upright pointed ears, smiling with sharp teeth... A trendy toy called LABUBU started to become popular in 2024, and soon this trend began to sweep the global market. In order to buy LABUBU, overseas consumers directly searched for LABUBU as the top trending keyword on the cross-border e-commerce platform "AliExpress" under Alibaba. With the blessing of LABUBU, the stock price of Pop Mart continues to soar, and its latest market value has exceeded 326.3 billion Hong Kong dollars. At the same time, with the rise of emotional economy and blind box economy in the consumer market, the new force of trendy toys represented by TOPTOY and 52TOYS is also turning their attention to going public.
    LABUBU is popular worldwide
    LABUBU is a character in the Pop Mart trendy toy IP "THE MONSTERS Elf Group". Unlike other blind boxes that are more for static collection, LABUBU's vinyl plush toys have broken through the barriers and enriched application scenarios, moving from closed display cases to public places such as streets and cafes. LABUBU's phenomenal popularity is also due to the strong endorsement of the "star effect", with many A-list celebrities such as Rihanna, Lisa, and Dua Lipa being photographed carrying LABUBU, further promoting the IP's breaking through in the field of trendy culture.
    The popularity of LABUBU can be seen in the frenzy of purchases in offline stores. An employee of a Pop Mart offline store said that the third generation and cola version of LABUBU are currently out of stock. In the Pop Mart store in Stratford, London, queues for buying Pop Mart products have caused chaos. As the first online channel in North America, the 20,000 new products launched in the TikTok Shop live broadcast room were sold out instantly, driving a single session GMV of 1.5 million US dollars (approximately 10.78 million yuan) in 8 hours.
    In addition, in the second-hand market, the highest asking price for new LABUBU products can exceed 1,000 yuan, more than 10 times the original price of 99 yuan, and ordinary styles are generally 1-2 times more expensive than the original price.
    How popular is LABUBU? The following set of data can explain it all: In 2024, the revenue of THE MONSTERS series to which it belongs soared from 368 million yuan in 2023 to 3.04 billion yuan in 2024, a year-on-year increase of 726.6%, with a monthly production capacity of 10 million units, topping the Pop Mart IP list. The overseas market is also skyrocketing, with LABUBU becoming a global trend. On the eve of "6.18" overseas, consumers from markets such as the UK, Australia, and Brazil flocked to AliExpress just to buy LABUBU.
    In the view of analysts, the star effect and globalization marketing are the core factors behind LABUBU's popularity. As the scale of the trendy toy industry continues to expand, the market is also expecting more local trendy toy brands to move from "phenomenal explosive products" to "global classics".
    Pop Mart's market value takes off
    LABUBU sweeping the globe has driven Pop Mart's market value to take off.
    Pop Mart's 2024 financial report shows that its revenue from the four major IPs THE MONSTERS, MOLLY, SKULLPANDA, and CRYBABY all exceeded 1 billion yuan for the first time in 2024, especially with LABUBU's global popularity last year, driving THE MONSTERS' revenue to exceed 3 billion yuan.
    The overseas income growth rate in the first quarter of 2025 reached 475% to 480%. By the end of 2024, Pop Mart had operated 120 stores and 172 robot stores in over 30 overseas markets.
    On June 5, FTSE Russell announced the latest index quarterly review results, with Pop Mart included in the FTSE China 50 Index. On that day, Pop Mart's opening stock price hit a new all-time high, closing at 243 Hong Kong dollars per share, rising more than 5 times since August last year, with a market value approaching 330 billion Hong Kong dollars. Pop Mart, along with Heytea and Lao Pu Huang Jin, were also dubbed the "three golden flowers of Hong Kong stocks" by the market.
    The secondary market is also quickly following suit. Data shows that as of the end of the first quarter of this year, a total of 182 funds were heavily invested in Pop Mart, holding a total of 60.7924 million shares. In the first quarter of last year, only 30 funds were heavily invested in Pop Mart, holding a total of 44.6876 million shares.
    Key to the success of explosive IP products
    The soaring stock prices of "Pop Mart" and others are not only due to the global popularity of top trendy toys, but also to the continuous expansion of the trendy toy market. The "China Trendy Toy and Animation Industry Development Report (2024)" shows that the scale of the "trendy toy" industry has grown nearly tenfold in 8 years, with the total market value increasing from 6.3 billion yuan in 2015 to 60 billion yuan in 2023, and is expected to reach 110.1 billion yuan by 2026.
    Some industry analysts point out that the popularity of the trendy toy market is due to changes in consumer demand. With the improvement of people's living standards, consumer attitudes are gradually shifting from material consumption to spiritual consumption. Trendy toys, as products that combine artistic and collectible value, happen to meet consumers' needs for personalized and emotional consumption.
    In recent years, the strong rise of local IPs is gradually reshaping the market landscape. In addition to Pop Mart, the trendy toy brand TOPTOY under Miniso has also surpassed 3,000 overseas stores. Many consumers are looking forward to more big IPs with long-term influence worldwide.
    The popularity of trendy toy brands is also rising in the Hong Kong stock market. Following Pop Mart, Brucol, and Kayout, the trendy toy company 52TOYS has also submitted an application to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
    Miniso also released an announcement on June 6 regarding rumors of the listing of its TOPTOY brand trendy toy business. The company is conducting a preliminary evaluation of the potential spin-off listing of its trendy toy business operated under the TOPTOY brand in order to optimize shareholder value.
    Earlier, according to media reports, sources revealed that TOPTOY, the trendy toy brand under Miniso, has recently hired JPMorgan Chase and UBS Group to provide services for its Hong Kong IPO. Miniso also hopes to introduce new investments for TOPTOY from potential investors such as sovereign wealth funds before selling shares. This is the second time this year that TOPTOY has been rumored to be seeking a listing in Hong Kong.
    In this regard, some industry insiders point out that in the current hot trendy toy market, the rush of 52TOYS and TOPTOY to go public meets market expectations. The advantage of TOPTOY lies in its backing by Miniso, with strong channel capabilities and IP integration resources, while the challenge lies in whether it can create explosive IP toys, as the series of explosive IP products is the key to its sustainable development.
    Reporter Yang Shuo

title_en:
The Shanghai Cooperation Organization Youth "Perception of Common Wealth Road" activity was held in Zhejiang
"A journey of innovation, discovery, and realization of dreams" (Promoting the "Shanghai Spirit": SCO in action)
body_en:
From June 2nd to 6th, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Youth "Perception of Shared Prosperity" event, organized by the China Association for People's Diplomacy and hosted by the Foreign Affairs Office of the Zhejiang Provincial People's Government, was held in Zhejiang. More than 20 young representatives from Shanghai Cooperation Organization countries visited Hangzhou, Huzhou, Shaoxing, and other places to experience the vibrant energy of China's modernization.

Walking towards the "new," with ample power for high-quality development
"What experiences from Zhejiang Province can be referenced for addressing the issue of unbalanced development?" "Can you further introduce the implementation of pairing urban and rural schools?" "Why was DeepSeek able to be born in Hangzhou?" On the morning of the 3rd, officials from the Zhejiang Provincial Development and Reform Commission introduced the construction of Zhejiang's demonstration area for common prosperity to young representatives from Shanghai Cooperation Organization countries from various angles such as economy, education, and healthcare. The young representatives actively asked questions based on their own work experiences, and there was positive interaction between both sides.

Autonomous guided transport robots shuttle back and forth, picking and moving goods in designated areas on shelves according to instructions; goods are automatically stored and retrieved, and the operation of the automated three-dimensional warehouse is orderly... At Alibaba's Xixi Park, Abdulaziz Nasser Hadad, an engineer from the Industrial Development Department of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry of Qatar, continuously took photos while watching the real-time monitoring screen inside the Cainiao Wuxi Intelligent Warehouse. Hadad said that China's development of the internet economy has matured, not only giving rise to new formats in trade, entertainment, and other fields but also deeply integrating and changing people's daily lives. "Qatar has the foundation for developing related industries and looks forward to deeper cooperation with China in areas such as cross-border e-commerce."

"Hangzhou is a city full of innovative vitality." At the Dream Town in Yuhang District, Hangzhou, Nick Mitchell, the founder and CEO of Hangzhou Xigu Video Technology Co., Ltd., shared his entrepreneurial story in Hangzhou with the young representatives, introducing Hangzhou's entrepreneurial support policies and measures for attracting international talent, hoping that more "foreign entrepreneurs" will come to develop in Hangzhou.

"This is a 'dream incubator' for young entrepreneurs." After listening to Mitchell's experience, Maldivian parliamentarian and Chairman of the Trade Union Federation, Maluf Zajil, said that Hangzhou is a youth-friendly city, and the relevant policies allow young entrepreneurs to have no worries.

At Zhejiang Dahua Technology Co., Ltd., understanding the application of smart IoT solutions in various fields; engaging in dialogue with Alibaba's Ali Entertainment Super Realistic Digital Human Liri; researching the complete entrepreneurial chain of "talent + capital + incubation"... Sherif Zimeti, an independent music producer from Egypt, had a fruitful trip to Hangzhou. He said, "This is a journey of innovation, discovery, and realizing dreams. I came to China 10 years ago. In the past 10 years, China's achievements in high-quality development have become more significant. The China now is completely different from the one I had in mind, which makes me look forward to China's future development even more."

Walking towards the "green," with a beautiful color of sustainable development
The green water meanders away, and the green mountains face each other. After the rain, the Anji Yucun in Huzhou is lush and green.

"Green! There is green everywhere here!" As soon as he got off the car, Yasmin Mufid, the Director of Public Relations and Marketing of the Bahrain Traditional Sports Committee, did not stop taking photos. Today, Yucun is characterized by clear mountains and waters, clean villages, harmonious people and beautiful scenery, and prosperous businesses. Mufid exclaimed, "My Chinese friends had told me before that the villages in Zhejiang are very beautiful. At that time, I was still skeptical, how beautiful can a village be? But when I actually arrived here, everything far exceeded my imagination." The transformation of old factory buildings into village libraries, and old mines into camping parks... Mufid posted the photos he took of Yucun's scenery on social media, captioning it as "The rural landscape of beautiful China."

Green waters and green mountains are as valuable as gold and silver. Over the past 20 years, guided by this concept, Yucun has strengthened environmental governance and infrastructure construction, promoting ecological restoration through methods such as nurturing soil and land reclamation, reshaping the landscape, and human culture.

After hearing the story of Yucun's significant efforts in ecological environment improvement, Anus Kelos, Vice President of the Indian Student Union and President of the Kerala Branch, raised a question: with factories closed and mines shut down, how can the villagers' income be guaranteed? Kelos' hometown, the state of Kerala in India, is about to overcome extreme poverty, and learning from China's poverty reduction experience is her most important goal on this trip.

At the Yucun cinema, a documentary about the transformation of Yucun answered Kelos' questions. From relying on mountains for resources to enriching the mountains, the people of Yucun have redefined their development plan, implementing projects to enhance the village's greenery, lighting along the roads, and beautifying courtyards, constructing ecological landscapes such as colorful rice fields and sunny flower seas, and taking the lead in exploring integrated reforms such as the "three land" reform in rural areas and the bamboo forest carbon sequestration reform. "These are valuable experiences worth learning from. I want to bring back the good practices I learned here to my country and explore practical ways suitable for my hometown," Kelos said.

At the Youth Talent Community in Dayu Village, Mikhail Grinchko, Deputy Minister of the Youth Department of the Belarusian Youth Union, exchanged contact information with relevant community officials. "The Youth Talent Community has achieved a two-way flow of youth and rural values, and this model is worth considering for Belarus," Grinchko said. "The community provides a broad platform for young talent innovation and entrepreneurship. I have just completed the registration and become a 'cloud villager' of Yucun. I look forward to seeing more possibilities in the 'cloud-based Yucun.'"

Walking towards the "heart," with a strong warmth in grassroots governance
As the "last mile" of national governance, grassroots governance is connected to both national policies and the daily lives of the people. Over the past 60 years, the "Fengqiao Experience" has continuously enriched and developed in practice, forming a distinctive new era "Fengqiao Experience."

At the Fengqiao Experience Exhibition Hall in Fengqiao Town, Zhuji, Shaoxing, the wax figure of "Drafting the 'Fengqiao Experience' at the Stove" attracted the attention of Israfil Abdulayev, Chief Advisor of the Foreign Policy Affairs Department of the Office of the President of Azerbaijan, who stopped for a long time. "Various places flexibly apply the 'Fengqiao Experience' according to their actual situations, truly focusing on issues and putting people first." Abdulayev learned that Yiwu has hired foreign mediators specifically to mediate disputes among foreigners, not only resolving the most common commercial and economic disputes but also helping to resolve conflicts arising from cultural and habitual differences.

Entering the convenience service station in Fengyuan Village, Fengqiao Town, Gulbahar Ezturk, Secretary-General of the Youth Department of the Justice and Development Party of Turkey, was curious about the multifunctional government self-service machine and the medical insurance self-service acceptance terminal in the corner of the service station. After learning that villagers can self-query policy information and handle related business here, Ezturk gave a thumbs up: "Without cumbersome procedures, villagers can handle business 'one-stop' without leaving the village, and this intelligent and efficient system is admirable!"

Today, in Fengyuan Village, neighbors can have heart-to-heart talks at neighborhood dispute mediation meetings for small conflicts, and seek advice from local wise men at the council for major issues and challenges. Various social organizations for deliberation and consultation have fully participated in village-level construction and conflict resolution affairs. "The new era 'Fengqiao Experience' makes grassroots governance more humane," said Onto, Director of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Affairs Office of the International Cooperation Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Cambodia.

Walking on the bluestone road in Fengqiao Ancient Town, with white walls and black tiles, the copper bells on the eaves jingled in the wind. In the old grocery store on the street, silver-haired elders sat around chatting; in the coffee shop opened by young people, coconut Americano was selling well in the summer. "A governance model with warmth shapes a city and people with warmth. China's grassroots governance model contains Eastern wisdom, inspiring people," Ezturk said.

title_en: Qing Shan District has over 300 "street corner new homes" to warm the new employment groups.
body_en:
On the morning of June 5th, at 6 o'clock, in the Nalin Pedestrian Street in Baotou City, Meituan rider Chen Xiao parked his electric bike next to a breakfast car with red and white colors and the words "Glorious Community Warm 'New' Service Mobile Car" on it, scanned the code and took out soy milk from the temperature-controlled cabinet. This 3-square-meter service mobile car is now emitting waves of warmth - the indicator lights of the power bank form a starry sea, and the smart screen scrolls with warm tips such as "Today it will rain, riders remember to add clothes". This is not a popular check-in spot, but one of the 300+ "new homes on the street corner" tailored for the new employment groups in Qingshan District, Baotou.

"In the past, when waiting for orders, if my phone ran out of battery, we had to plug it in at the convenience store entrance." SF Express courier Li Liang turned on the direct drinking water tap of the service mobile car and filled his 1.5-liter water bottle. This small space has been designed with "space magic" by the designer: the folding seats unfold to become a "Rider Academy" classroom, the medicine box on the wall is equipped for both winter and summer seasons, with warmers for winter and cool patches for summer regularly rotated. The most popular feature is the intelligent battery exchange cabinet, where riders can scan the code and complete the battery replacement for their electric bikes in 3 seconds, with a daily service volume exceeding 200 people.

During the lunch break, in the "Rider Cinema" set up along the streets for the riders in the community, 20 riders are watching the safety special of the movie "The Captain". This is Chen Xiao's third time participating in the movie learning session. This year, he submitted a party membership application to the Meituan delivery rider party branch. "I also joined the 'Rider Heart Collaboration' volunteer service team," Chen Xiao said happily.

This change began with the "Dual Coverage" action in Qingshan District. Through big data screening by the Civil Affairs and Market Supervision departments, multiple new business formats within the jurisdiction were accurately targeted, and 11 new party organizations were established in emerging fields such as the online car-hailing driver party branch and the live streaming industry joint party branch through the "individual establishment + joint establishment" method. Qingshan District has set up 40 party building guidance stations in commercial buildings, with 412 instructors assisting in the development of the "Rider Refueling Station" mini-program. By clicking on the party emblem on the map, the mini-program immediately displays the nearest charging pile, restroom, and emergency medicine point.

"Wanda Golden Street No. 3 manhole cover has been moved, and a warning sign has been set up." At 11 o'clock at night, Ele.me rider Zhang Xiaojie uploaded his inspection record in the grid staff group chat, this is the 8th time he has reported safety hazards this month. As a mobile grid staff member hired by the community, he now has an additional line of red text on his chest badge: Food Supervision Officer. The innovative "24-hour Citizen Snapshots" launched by Qingshan District has mobilized 63 riders to participate in grassroots governance, eliminating more than 300 safety hazards.

This two-way empowerment is reshaping the urban governance ecosystem. At the Yongshengcheng Supermarket's "Red Energy Station," the second layer of the shelves is dedicated to a rider storage area; the Construction Bank branch has opened a "Rider Express Lane," where riders can enjoy exclusive call services when handling business. What's even more surprising is that the riders have spontaneously formed the "Rider Heart Collaboration" volunteer team, actively carrying out various service activities.

From the core "Flagship Station" in the business district to the "Micro Relay Station" at the community entrance, Qingshan District has spent 3 years weaving a service network for the new employment groups. In the Science Road Street, the "Rider Home" transformed from an old factory building is equipped with a shared kitchen and capsule apartments; at the bank branches, foldable rest cabins provide "1 square meter of warmth"; even the glass windows of pharmacies are labeled with "Red Energy Station" signs, providing free blood pressure measurement services for the riders.

Service is not a one-way street, but a concentric circle of co-construction and sharing. A research report from Qingshan District in Baotou shows that more than 60 new employment groups in new business formats have actively joined the volunteer service team, serving as community mobile grid staff, food supervision officers, etc., assisting in solving more than 300 problems, with the number of people submitting party membership applications in emerging fields doubling compared to the previous year.

When rider Chen Xiao wrote on the message wall of the mobile car, "Here understands riders better than home," another "Red Energy Station" was labeled in the equipment manufacturing industrial park 30 kilometers away. From the transformation experiment of a breakfast car to the systematic upgrade of comprehensive services, Baotou's Qingshan District has proven over time: the temperature of the city is not only hidden in the GDP data, but also flows in those moments on the streets where people are treated gently.

As night falls, the warm yellow lights outline the figures of the riders shuttling back and forth, illuminating the governance answer of "serving a group of people, warming a city".
