《意见》提出要加强电力市场监管，维护市场秩序。请问国家能源局在加强市场监管方面有哪些具体举措？谢谢。
宋宏坤：
谢谢这位记者的提问，这个问题请郝瑞锋先生回答。
郝瑞锋：
谢谢您的提问。市场监管是电力市场健康有序运行的重要保障。国家能源局将继续加强电力市场监管，维护市场秩序，保障市场公平竞争，确保消费者合法权益。具体举措主要包括以下几个方面：
一是加强市场准入监管。我们将继续完善电力市场准入制度，规范市场主体准入行为，加强对新能源发电企业、电力用户、电力交易机构等市场主体的准入监管，确保市场主体合法合规参与市场竞争。
二是强化市场交易监管。我们将继续加强对电力市场交易的监管，规范市场交易行为，加强对电力市场价格形成机制的监督，维护市场价格秩序，防范市场操纵和不正当竞争行为，保障市场公平竞争。
三是加强市场监测和预警。我们将继续加强对电力市场供需情况、价格波动等市场运行情况的监测和预警，及时发布市场监测信息，引导市场主体合理决策，防范市场风险，确保市场平稳运行。
四是加强市场监督检查。我们将继续加强对电力市场主体的监督检查，发现和查处市场违法违规行为，维护市场秩序，保障市场公平竞争，促进电力市场健康有序发展。
五是加强市场信息公开。我们将继续加强电力市场信息公开工作，推动市场信息透明，提高市场参与者对市场情况的了解和把握，促进市场主体合理决策，保障市场公平竞争。
我们将继续加强电力市场监管，维护市场秩序，促进电力市场健康有序发展。谢谢！
谢谢各位记者朋友的提问，也感谢宋主任和郝司长的详细回答。我们今天的发布会到此结束。如果还有其他问题，欢迎随时联系我们。谢谢大家！ Installation and connection of electricity meters. We will continue to summarize good experiences and practices from various regions, guide power supply companies to comprehensively promote new initiatives such as "scanning code for electricity use," continuously innovate the "three-zero" service model, provide rural residents with free installation and fast electricity services, support rural revitalization and development, and help stimulate consumption vitality.
Thirdly, gradually improve the level of equal services in urban and rural areas. We adhere to the overall planning of urban and rural areas, further narrow the gap in power supply between urban and rural areas, guide power supply companies to establish sound rural power supply service standards, standardize and improve service processes, extend high-quality power supply service resources to rural residents through the establishment of rural power stations and convenient service electricity, provide more convenient and efficient electricity installation, repair, and information disclosure services for rural residents, continuously promote the equalization of power supply services between rural and urban areas, and enhance the satisfaction and sense of obtaining electricity services for the masses.
That's all I have to answer, thank you.
China Finance News reporter:
Recently, various central departments including the National Energy Administration have issued a series of policy measures to promote the high-quality development of the private economy. What are the benefits of the "Opinions" issued this time for private economic organizations? Thank you.
Song Hongkun:
Thank you for the question from the China Finance News reporter, it is a very good question because supporting the development of the private economy is also a key focus of the "Opinions." The National Energy Administration attaches great importance to serving the development of the private economy and recently issued the "Notice on Several Measures to Promote the Development of the Private Economy in the Energy Sector," which aims to support private enterprises through policy guidance, service optimization, market opening, and innovation breakthroughs, continuously increasing support for private enterprises. A good electricity business environment is an important guarantee for promoting the healthy development of private enterprises. To better serve the development of the private economy, we have proposed a series of reform measures in the "Opinions" to support private enterprises in electricity installation and use.
Firstly, reduce the electricity installation costs for enterprises. We focus on reducing the burden on private enterprises. Building on the existing "three-zero" service for low-voltage small and micro enterprises, we will further expand the scope of the "three-zero" service to benefit more private economic organizations. For example, individual businesses opening stores, farmers running agritainment, and others who need to apply for electricity can enjoy free electricity connection. We estimate that after the issuance of the "Opinions," it is expected to benefit around 1.5 million households in five years.
Secondly, provide precise services to enterprises. In the process of electricity installation, besides the investment in electricity installation, private enterprises are most concerned about how to apply for electricity and when they can start using electricity. In this regard, the "Opinions" propose that power supply companies should clarify the electricity installation standards and make them public, match capacity needs precisely based on actual electricity demand, characteristics of electricity equipment, and future development considerations, explore the implementation of contract electricity connection services, manage expected electricity connection, private enterprises can agree with power supply companies on project implementation and power delivery time, timely ensure the electricity needs of private enterprises, and better support the production and operation of a large number of private enterprises.
Thirdly, help enterprises save energy and increase efficiency. To further help private enterprises reduce production and operation costs, we will guide power supply companies to provide free energy monitoring, energy efficiency diagnosis, energy efficiency consulting, and other public services. By promoting service models such as "energy efficiency bills," we will help private enterprises optimize their electricity usage structure and reduce electricity expenses. At the same time, we encourage more market entities to carry out comprehensive energy services, providing energy management and energy efficiency services such as energy efficiency transformation for private enterprises, helping them reduce comprehensive energy costs.
Thank you.
Xing Huina:
Please continue to raise your hand for questions, we have two more reporters.
Southern Metropolis Daily Southern+ reporter:
Electricity security and stable supply are important factors in ensuring the production and life of the people. What specific measures will the National Energy Administration take to improve the resilience of the distribution network, reduce power outage time and frequency, etc.? With the peak summer season approaching, what measures are planned for ensuring electricity supply this summer? Thank you.
Song Hongkun:
Thank you for the question, this question will be answered by Mr. Hao Ruifeng.
Hao Ruifeng:
Thank you for your question. Electricity is the foundation of economic and social development, and all industries rely on stable and reliable electricity supply. In recent years, the National Energy Administration has focused on strengthening the planning and construction of the distribution network, continuously enhancing the management of power reliability, and has achieved positive results. Next, we will base ourselves on higher levels and stricter standards, continuously improve power supply capacity and quality, better meet the increasing demand for electricity for a better life for enterprises and the masses.
Firstly, strengthen the planning and construction of the distribution network. A strong and reliable distribution network structure is the prerequisite and foundation for improving power supply quality. Based on the high-quality electricity needs of enterprises and the masses, we guide power supply companies to plan the main distribution network comprehensively, optimize the layout of power grid facilities, enhance the flexibility and self-healing capabilities of the distribution network, build a strong and flexible distribution network, and improve the resilience of the distribution network. At the same time, further optimize investment management, tilt construction and renovation funds towards weak power supply areas such as rural areas and old residential areas, gradually narrow the gap in power supply between urban and rural areas and regions; combined with the development of clean energy, strengthen the upgrade and transformation of the distribution network, and systematically enhance the comprehensive carrying capacity of the distribution network.
Secondly, strengthen the operation and maintenance management of the distribution network. To ensure the safe and stable operation of the distribution network, it is not only necessary to build it well but also to manage it well. We guide power supply companies to strengthen the application of new technologies and equipment, such as using drones for equipment inspections, promoting non-stop power operation technology, continuously improving the lean operation and maintenance management level of the distribution network, further reducing the number of fault power outages, outage time, and impact range. At the same time, we guide power supply companies to optimize the power outage maintenance plan, coordinate and arrange management, implement "one outage, multiple uses," avoid repeated power outages on the same line, and minimize the number of power outages for users.
Thirdly, carry out frequent power outage governance on a regular basis. In 2023, we launched a special campaign to address frequent power outages, focusing on solving 510 power outage problems that were strongly reflected by the people. Based on this, we have established a sound long-term mechanism. Since 2024, we have further intensified our efforts, continuously deepening and solidifying the work of addressing frequent power outages, and have achieved positive results. This year, we will continue to consolidate the results of the rectification, focusing on improving standards, refining measures, and improving mechanisms, making efforts to accelerate the comprehensive governance of problematic substations and lines, requiring power supply companies to achieve zero frequent power outage issues. At the same time, for the first time, the "Opinions" introduce a mechanism for public supervision, using the judgment and feelings of the people as an important criterion to evaluate the effectiveness of governance, jointly promoting the continuous improvement of power supply quality.
You also asked about the upcoming peak summer season. The peak summer season is approaching, and everyone is concerned about ensuring electricity supply during this period. Today, the temperature in Beijing has reached 37 degrees, with some areas in Hebei, Henan, and Shandong exceeding 39 degrees. From the current situation, it is expected that the overall national electricity supply during this year's peak summer season will be guaranteed, but there may be localized electricity supply shortages during peak periods in some areas. The National Energy Administration will resolutely implement the decisions and arrangements of the Party Central Committee, aiming to ensure that there is flexibility in normal supply, measures for short-term shortages in specific areas, and effective responses to extreme situations. We will tighten the responsibilities of all parties, strengthen energy and power monitoring and early warning, fully leverage the potential for ensuring supply during peak periods, accelerate the construction and commissioning of supporting power sources, optimize cross-provincial and regional power optimization and mutual assistance, strengthen demand-side response, and make every effort to ensure the safe and stable supply of electricity during the peak summer season.
That's all I have to say, thank you.
Xing Huina:
One last question.
National Business Daily reporter:
In the context of digital transformation, how do grid enterprises use advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence to enhance the intelligence level of "obtaining electricity" services and optimize user service experience? Thank you.
Song Hongkun:
Thank you for the question, this question will be answered by Mr. Pang Xiaogang.
Pang Xiaogang:
Thank you for your question. Artificial intelligence is a hot topic in today's society. Indeed, artificial intelligence is a strategic technology that leads a new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation, and it is also an important engine for nurturing and developing new productive forces. This year, the government work report proposed to continue to promote the "AI+" action, better integrating digital technology with manufacturing advantages and market advantages. In recent years, State Grid Corporation of China has also conducted some research and applications in artificial intelligence. We focus on future development, deepen reform and innovation, and continue to explore the application of artificial intelligence technology in the electricity industry. Last year, we released the Guangming Power Big Model, which is like an artificial intelligence expert in the field of energy and power, providing a "super brain" for ensuring the safe and stable operation of the power grid, promoting the integration of new energy consumption, and providing good power supply services. Next, we will further implement the national "AI+" action, accelerate the integration and application of the new generation of artificial intelligence technology represented by the big model in the field of power supply services. Below, I will elaborate on three aspects:
The first aspect is to deepen the application of "AI+ electricity installation." We will vigorously promote the construction of a digital twin power grid (which means that we will construct another digital power grid in the digital space that completely mirrors the existing physical power grid), integrate artificial intelligence technology into the power supply solution response process, create a new intelligent electricity installation model, focus on enhancing the deep learning ability of the big model in industry knowledge such as policies, regulations, and technical standards, automatically match power grid resources based on customer electricity installation needs, intelligently generate power supply solutions quickly, and provide multiple sets of intelligent comparison solutions to better support customers in quickly connecting to electricity and early production. Some explorations have been made in this area, for example, our Jiangsu company has applied intelligent power supply solution generation technology to over 50,000 projects, reducing the time for generating solutions by more than half compared to the previous year.
The second aspect is to deepen the application of "AI+ customer service." We will deepen the application of artificial intelligence in online and offline service scenarios to provide customers with more proactive, efficient, and intimate services. In terms of online services, we will upgrade and revamp channels such as 95598 and online State Grid, promote intelligent voice, text recognition, autonomous outbound calls, and other service functions, enhance service interaction and accuracy. In terms of offline services, we will focus on the large volume of routine business transactions and diverse customer needs in current business halls, build "digital employees" for smart services, deploy artificial intelligence service terminals, improve the efficiency of routine business transactions such as payment and repair, provide electricity business consultation, policy answers, intelligent queries, and other services for on-site customers, and enhance the actual experience of users.
The third aspect is to deepen the application of "AI+ repair." We use the Guangming Power Big Model to improve the quality and efficiency of proactive repair services, enhance power supply guarantee capabilities. Strengthen the dynamic topology construction of the digital power grid, realize the "perceptible and fully monitored" status information, analyze the power outage range in real-time, accurately judge the cause of the fault, quickly arrange personnel for on-site repair, promote the transformation of power repair services from passive to proactive and intelligent, and minimize customer waiting time. There are many examples in this area as well, for example, after the pilot project in Tongzhou, Beijing, the efficiency of handling power outage faults has been significantly improved, with an average saving of about 20 minutes in repair time. We will continue to innovate and launch similar "AI+ power" products, and continuously optimize them to make electricity more secure and comfortable.
That's all I have to answer. Thank you!
Xing Huina:
Today's press conference ends here, thank you to the four presenters, and thank you to all the media friends for participating. Goodbye!

title_en: Notice on holding the 2024 Academic Annual Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association (Second Round)
body_en: Relevant units: Pharmaceutical excipients are an important foundation in China's pharmaceutical industry, and are one of the key factors determining the quality of generic drugs and the high-quality development of innovative formulations. The supply chain security of pharmaceutical excipients used in high-end formulations in China urgently needs to strengthen the technological innovation and industrial support for domestic pharmaceutical excipients. At the same time, ensuring the quality of clinical medication, reducing drug costs, and alleviating the pressure on medical insurance, to a large extent, also depend on the quality improvement of domestic pharmaceutical excipients. In line with the principle of "promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new quality productivity of the pharmaceutical industry," the "2024 Annual Academic Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association," hosted by the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association, is scheduled to be held in Hefei, Anhui Province from November 8th to 10th, 2024. This academic conference will feature conference reports in the fields of materials science related to pharmaceutical excipients, innovative drugs, and innovative formulations, analyzing the development difficulties and innovations of pharmaceutical excipients; inviting authoritative experts to deeply discuss the in vivo processes of pharmaceutical excipients and drug delivery carriers, as well as the improvement and innovation of excipient quality. The conference will set up expert venues and young scholar sub-venues with three themes: "Pharmaceutical Excipients, Packaging Materials, and Drug Delivery Devices," "New Materials, New Carriers, and Innovative Formulations," and "Pharmaceutical Excipients and Innovative Drugs," to promote the wide participation of enterprises, academia, and young scholars, and jointly focus on the technological innovation and industrial research and development of pharmaceutical excipients. title_en: In Q1 of 2025, JD's revenue reached 301.1 billion, ranking first in the internet industry.
body_en: On June 5th, it was reported that during this period, major domestic internet companies have successively announced their Q1 2025 performance. Some media outlets have compiled a revenue and profit chart based on the financial data of various companies for comparison and analysis. From this intuitive display chart, it can be clearly seen that JD Group led by Liu Qiangdong topped the list with a revenue of 301.1 billion yuan in Q1 2025, an increase of 15.8% compared to Q1 2024. It is understood that JD Group's revenue in Q1 2025 far exceeded market expectations, achieving the highest year-on-year growth rate in nearly three years, reaching 3.4 times the market growth rate during the same period, leading the industry. In addition, the net profit attributable to ordinary shareholders of the company was 10.9 billion yuan, compared to 7.1 billion yuan in the same period last year, achieving significant growth. Alibaba, another industry giant, ranked second with a total revenue of 236.454 billion yuan in Q1 2025, a year-on-year increase of 7%. In terms of revenue scale, although it is not as high as JD, its growth rate is also not low. Alibaba's annual revenue was 996.347 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 6%, demonstrating strong stability. It is worth mentioning the outstanding achievements of JD here. Some analysts believe that JD's success is due to its continuous efforts in optimizing cost expenditures, focusing on supply chain advantages, and expanding overseas markets. JD's advantages in core categories are becoming more solid. In the first quarter, revenue from electronics increased by 17.1% year-on-year, while revenue from daily necessities increased by 14.9% year-on-year. The supermarket category has maintained double-digit year-on-year revenue growth for five consecutive quarters. At the same time, JD's quarterly active user count has achieved double-digit year-on-year growth for six consecutive quarters, with a growth rate exceeding 20%. In addition, it is necessary to mention the efforts of JD's founder Liu Qiangdong. It is understood that JD's performance has continued to accelerate over the past year, which is closely related to Liu Qiangdong personally overseeing the front line and participating in business innovation at JD Group. Source: 21IC

title_en: Looking at the next round of China's economic "opportunity" from the "Private Economy Promotion Law" | Minmao Perspective
body_en: On May 20th, the Private Economy Promotion Law officially came into effect. Since the proposal to formulate this law in December 2024, to its formal promulgation and implementation in less than a year and a half, it is evident how determined the legislators were. A relevant official from the Ministry of Justice stated that the enactment of the Private Economy Promotion Law is an important measure to implement the important instructions of General Secretary Xi Jinping and the decision-making arrangements of the Party Central Committee. It is a landmark event in the construction of a socialist market economy and holds milestone significance in the development of China's private economy. Since the 20th National Congress, the support for the private economy in the country has significantly increased. In July 2023, the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council issued the "Opinions on Promoting the Development and Growth of the Private Economy," proposing 31 specific measures. In July 2024, the Third Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee listed "formulating the Private Economy Promotion Law" as an important reform measure. In the same year in December, the Central Economic Work Conference made clear requirements for the promulgation of this law. In February 2025, General Secretary Xi Jinping attended a symposium of private enterprises and delivered an important speech. The official promulgation of the Private Economy Promotion Law signifies a dense issuance of policies and laws, indicating that China's private economy is about to usher in a new phase of significant development opportunities. The first chapter of the law aims to eliminate the market bottlenecks and institutional obstacles faced by the current development of the private economy. The stability of enterprises leads to economic stability, and strong enterprises lead to a strong economy. Why is the private economy so important? The answer can be found in the data set "56789": as of 2024, private enterprises have contributed more than 50% of tax revenue, over 60% of the national GDP, more than 70% of technological innovation achievements, over 80% of urban employment, with the number of private enterprises accounting for over 90% of the total number of enterprises, and the total import and export value accounting for over 50% of the total foreign trade value. Behind "56789," the private economy has grown into a solid pillar of the national economy, playing a core role in stabilizing the Chinese economy, ensuring people's livelihoods, promoting innovation, and driving development. However, in recent years, the development of the private economy has faced a series of significant challenges, including the impact of the three-year pandemic, the China-US trade war, and the transformation and upgrading of the Chinese economy. Private enterprises are at the forefront of the market, facing the greatest difficulties and pressures. According to statistics, private investment has been negative for two consecutive years, with the proportion falling to 50.1%, a decrease of 15 percentage points from the peak ten years ago. According to the 2024 national survey data from the China Economic System Reform Research Association of the National Development and Reform Commission, the main operational difficulties faced by private entrepreneurs currently are "few orders, few customers, insufficient consumption" (57.8%), "fierce competition, low profits" (42.2%), while the urgent need for government support for private enterprises includes "strengthening talent and employment demand guarantees" (45.2%), "implementing fair competition policy systems" (42.6%), "improving the normalization of prevention and clearance mechanisms for overdue payments" (32.5%), "improving financing support policy systems" (32.2%), "supporting private enterprises to enhance technological innovation capabilities" (31.4%), and "removing market access barriers" (30.6%), among others. High-quality development and common prosperity are the two core goals of China's economic development in the new era. Looking at the two sets of data mentioned above, with private enterprises contributing over 70% of technological innovation and over 80% of employment, it is clear that to achieve the two major goals of high-quality development driven by innovation and common prosperity, there must be a strong determination and effort to continuously promote the development and growth of the private economy, allowing private enterprises to become bigger and stronger. On the other hand, with over 90% of private enterprises contributing only slightly over 50% of tax revenue and just over 60% of GDP, it indicates that private enterprises currently face challenges such as thin profits, operational difficulties, low technological content, and weak development. It is urgent to eliminate the market bottlenecks and institutional obstacles that hinder the further development of private enterprises, promoting high-quality and leapfrog development of the private economy. The promulgation of the Private Economy Promotion Law is timely. The new law consists of 9 chapters and 78 articles, based on the principles of "equal treatment, fair competition, equal protection, and common development." It comprehensively formulates legal provisions to promote the development and growth of the private economy from seven aspects, including fair competition, investment and financing promotion, technological innovation, and rights protection, focusing on key issues encountered in the current development of the private economy. As the first fundamental law specifically addressing the development of the private economy, the new law explicitly defines the legal status of the private economy for the first time, incorporating the "two adherences" into the law. It also includes the statement that "promoting the sustained, healthy, and high-quality development of the private economy is a major long-term policy of the state" into the legal provisions. This marks a historic leap for China's private economy from "policy support" to "legal escort," fully demonstrating the firm determination of the Party Central Committee to promote the development and growth of the private economy. In the new historical period, the private economy bears a new historical mission. The private economy is the source of innovation for China's economic growth, and establishing a fair competition mechanism is the economic and legal foundation for implementing a unified national market. Strengthening and expanding the private economy is the fundamental guarantee for achieving common prosperity. Whether state-owned enterprises or private enterprises, they are the wealth of the country and the people, an important part of the socialist market economy. State-owned enterprises and private enterprises are the two "economic battle regulars" under the leadership of the Party, each bearing their own economic and social responsibilities. The key to reforming state-owned enterprises lies in "focusing on large and letting go of small," while the key to reforming private enterprises lies in "focusing on small and letting go of large." Each private enterprise is like a "seed," and as long as it is placed under the sunlight of the rule of law and in the soil of the market economy, it has the potential to grow into a towering tree. The development and growth of the private economy are the fundamental driving force for sustainable economic growth and high-quality development in China. Under the perspective of the Private Economy Promotion Law, new trends and patterns of economic development are emerging. Those who follow the natural order will succeed, and those who act with determination will achieve success. "In the new era and on the new journey, the prospects for the development of the private economy are broad and promising, and it is the right time for the vast number of private enterprises and entrepreneurs to demonstrate their capabilities." The promulgation of the Private Economy Promotion Law has provided a "reassurance pill" for the 50 million private enterprises nationwide and injected a "heart-strengthening agent." This is a milestone event in the construction of a socialist market economy. Currently, China's economy is at a critical stage of transformation and upgrading. The future trend of China's economic development is shifting from resource-driven to innovation-driven, from export-driven to domestic demand-driven, from coastal areas to inland regions, from urban to rural areas, ultimately aiming to achieve a unified national market and a new development pattern of dual circulation. Recently, Elon Musk predicted that China's economy will be two to three times the size of the United States in the future. To achieve such a grand goal, China's economy must undergo an explosive growth, with the greatest increment coming from the private economy. The global economic order and China's economic landscape are undergoing profound adjustments, and the economic forces at home and abroad are on the verge of a major battle. At this critical juncture, the country hopes that the private economy can quickly grow stronger and assume greater responsibilities and missions in the fight against challenges. The key directions of state support for the development of the private economy will become the "wind vane" for the next round of economic reform and development in China. By analyzing the relevant legal provisions of the Private Economy Promotion Law, we can make an assessment. 1. Fair competition clause: Ensuring equal development rights for private enterprises. The law stipulates: The country implements a nationwide unified market access negative list system, implements a fair competition review system, and follows the principle of "non-prohibition or entry" for private enterprises; public resource transactions such as bidding, government procurement, and monopolistic industries shall not restrict or exclude private enterprises; in the allocation and use of natural resources, public service resources, and human resources, private enterprises shall be treated equally. One of the main reasons hindering the development and growth of the private economy is the deep-rooted discrimination against private enterprises in society. The phenomenon of "glass doors" and "revolving doors" is very common in market access, resource allocation, and policy measures related to talent treatment. To complement the implementation of the Private Economy Promotion Law, the National Development and Reform Commission, together with the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation, promptly issued a notice on carrying out a campaign to clear and rectify market access barriers to promote the construction of a unified national market. This campaign aims to comprehensively clear and rectify various unreasonable provisions and practices that set up market access barriers in violation of regulations, creating a fair market access environment. Except for a few "restricted areas," all industries and markets are open to private enterprises, and the state legally guarantees the equal rights of private enterprises to use various production factors such as funds, technology, human resources, data, and land. If the above legal provisions can be effectively implemented, the market position of private enterprises and state-owned enterprises will be completely equal. This is a basic requirement for implementing a unified national market and an inevitable requirement for realizing a socialist market economy with Chinese characteristics. Only by fully unleashing the enormous potential for the development of private enterprises can the greatest advantages of the "mixed ownership system" be stimulated, and the best results of the socialist market economy of "1+1>2" be achieved. 2. Investment and financing promotion clause: Financial support must tilt towards private enterprises. The law stipulates: Support private enterprises in investing in national major strategic projects, strategic emerging industries, and the construction of modern infrastructure; relax the tolerance for non-performing loans for inclusive small and micro-enterprise loans, support private enterprises in providing accounts receivable, warehouse receipts, equity, intellectual property rights, and other rights for pledge loans, and provide a green channel for chattel mortgage registration; lower the threshold for private enterprises to go public, etc. Difficulty in investment and financing is another important reason hindering the development and growth of private enterprises. To complement the implementation of the Private Economy Promotion Law, the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission has introduced multiple financial support policies to break the capital bottleneck for the development of private enterprises. The state's key support areas are twofold: one is loans for small and micro-enterprises, as it involves employment and people's livelihoods, the tolerance for non-performing loans has been relaxed to 3%, and the risk capital weight has been discounted from 85% to 75%, in order to increase the enthusiasm of banks to lend. The other area is high-tech and emerging industries, which are the two key directions for state support of private enterprise development. Currently, pilot projects for equity investment by financial asset investment companies are being carried out, promoting the construction of a comprehensive experimental zone for intellectual property finance, focusing on improving the service model of technology finance to support investment in technology innovation enterprises. Only by continuously increasing financial support and promoting the continuous development and growth of private enterprises can the fundamental economic challenges of ensuring people's livelihoods and driving innovation be fundamentally addressed. 3. Technological innovation clause: Promoting private enterprises to become the main force of national science and technology and industrial innovation. The law stipulates: Support private enterprises in strengthening basic and cutting-edge research, developing key core technologies, common basic technologies, and cutting-edge cross-disciplinary technologies, promoting the integration of technological innovation and industrial innovation, fostering new industries, new models, and new drivers; support capable private enterprises in taking the lead in undertaking national major technology research tasks, and open national major scientific research infrastructure to private enterprises; the state strengthens the protection of original innovation by private enterprises and their operators. Technology is the primary productive force, and innovation is the primary driving force. Private enterprises account for over 92% of high-tech enterprises in the country, and specialized and innovative small and medium-sized enterprises account for over 95%. Private enterprises have become the mainstay of national science and technology and industrial innovation. However, due to the incomplete reform of the scientific and technological system and the lack of inclination of national scientific and technological resources towards private enterprises, the market has not fully played its decisive role in resource allocation. During the research on the topic of "Strategies and Paths for Private Enterprises to Participate in Major Technological Innovation" at the Central Party School, it was found that technological innovation, especially in engineering applications, is proposed and solved at the forefront of production. Foundational and disruptive technological innovations are almost entirely the original ideas of scientists or engineers. Under the market economy system, small and medium-sized enterprises are the most dynamic and creative. However, social discrimination against private enterprises still exists widely, with many believing that scientific research institutions and central state-owned enterprises are the main force of scientific and industrial innovation. This is a cognitive misconception. With the rise of a large number of strategic technology-based private enterprises such as Huawei, DJI, Alibaba Cloud, and DeepSeek, the country has gradually realized the importance of private enterprise technology and industrial innovation, and the policy support for them is increasing year by year. Only when all flowers bloom together can the garden be full of spring colors; only by raising a pool of koi can the dragon soar in the sky. The Private Economy Promotion Law stipulates that private enterprises can take the lead in undertaking national major technology research tasks, national major scientific research infrastructure will be open to private enterprises, and the state will strengthen the protection of intellectual property rights of private enterprises. This sends a strong signal: private enterprises will bear the heavy responsibility of national scientific and technological innovation and industrial innovation integration, and national scientific resources will tilt towards and transfer to private enterprises, accelerating the transformation of China's economy from "Made in China" to "Created in China." The enactment of the Private Economy Promotion Law reflects the firm determination and strategic thinking of the legislators to further deepen economic system reform, bringing significant benefits to private enterprises and the private economy. Social organizations are the boosters for the high-quality development of the private economy, and the new law encourages "industrial and commercial federations to play an important role in promoting the healthy development of the private economy and the healthy growth of private entrepreneurs." Among the 17,090 member companies of China's commerce, over 95% are private enterprises. Providing services to member companies is the foundation and basis for the development of China's commerce. Under the guidance of the new law, China's commerce will further improve its service levels, providing more professional and comprehensive consulting services to member companies in coordinating government relations, connecting project resources, promoting investment and financing, and technological innovation, helping private enterprises transition from "trade, industry, and technology" to "excellence, innovation, and strength," increasing efficiency. Contributed by the Policy Research Office of China's Commerce, Edited by the Media Working Committee of China's Commerce.

title_en: AI empowers Chinese listed companies to go global, with overseas revenue approaching 10 trillion yuan.
body_en:
In 2025, going global is no longer an "option," but a "necessity," becoming a significant strategic opportunity for business development.
According to statistics from the China Listed Companies Association, in 2024, listed companies maintained a good development trend in their export business, achieving overseas revenue of 9.44 trillion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 7.97%, with the proportion of revenue from overseas markets increasing by 1.06 percentage points compared to the previous year.
"China has already achieved technological leadership in areas such as 5G, AI, and smart cars. Chinese companies' technology, supply chain, service, and brand capabilities have already had a spillover effect," said Wu Yongming, CEO of Alibaba Group and Chairman and CEO of Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group, at the Alibaba Cloud Enterprise Going Global Conference.
However, against the backdrop of the accelerated restructuring of the global economic landscape, Chinese companies' global expansion process is facing unprecedented complexity and uncertainty. From regulatory compliance to supply chain management, from market environment to cultural adaptation, the barriers that companies need to overcome in going global far exceed traditional understanding.
On one hand, geopolitical conflicts, rising trade protectionism, and technological blockades have intensified external risks; on the other hand, internal capabilities in resource allocation, strategic decision-making, and localization operations within companies are also increasing.
Faced with multiple challenges, companies going global are seeking technological breakthroughs. AI, cloud computing, and other digital technologies have evolved from auxiliary tools to core infrastructure, with Chinese tech giants like Alibaba and Huawei playing important roles.
In this process, technological empowerment is significantly reducing barriers for companies going global, enhancing their international competitiveness, which may be a key turning point for Chinese companies to transition from "going out" to "going up."
The wave of going global has been particularly significant in the past two years, with consumer goods, gaming, manufacturing, and other industries expanding into overseas markets. In addition to large-scale leading companies, many small and medium-sized enterprises are also eyeing the opportunities in overseas markets. However, these companies face diverse challenges when considering expanding into overseas markets.
Cultural differences are unavoidable obstacles for Chinese companies going global. Language is the first barrier to overcome, as businesses need to address the issue of language barriers and communicate in the local language at every step, while also understanding the needs and preferences of overseas consumers. Directly selling Chinese products in overseas markets often yields unsatisfactory results.
Cultural habit differences can lead to misunderstandings, for example, the Middle East region has many taboos related to dietary, clothing, and advertising content due to religious beliefs. If companies are unaware and blindly promote products, they may offend local people and trigger a public relations crisis.
Compliance issues are also relatively complex. There are significant differences in laws and regulations between countries, and companies operating overseas need to comply with local laws and regulations, including taxation, labor laws, environmental protection, and market competition. Companies often need to invest significant resources to ensure compliance, otherwise they may face fines, lawsuits, or even business prohibitions.
Moreover, there is a scarcity of relevant professional talents. These fields require specific professional skills and knowledge, as well as a deep understanding of different cultures and market environments. Finding employees with the necessary skills who are willing to work across different time zones is a challenge, especially when covering multiple markets.
Language and cultural barriers, complex compliance issues, a shortage of professional talents, high customer acquisition costs... these are the numerous challenges that businesses face on the road to going global. The integration of AI brings a turning point.
"When analyzing a company's operational processes and breaking them down into specific tasks, it can be seen that artificial intelligence has potential value in multiple areas," said Zhang Kaifei, Vice President of Alibaba's International Digital Business Group and Head of AI Business, in an interview with 21st Century Business Herald.
For enterprises going global, AI innovation is no longer just an optional auxiliary tool, but a core driver for business growth and localization.
Taking the example of cross-border e-commerce, AI performs excellently in scenarios such as AI customer service and marketing push, bringing double-digit improvements in effectiveness. It is worth noting that such improvements are not only in terms of reducing labor costs and increasing efficiency but in most scenarios, AI can bring a 1% to 30% improvement in conversion rates, click-through rates, and consumer satisfaction.
Alibaba International is at the forefront of AI applications. In November 2023, it launched the AI tool "Business Assistant," equipping small and medium-sized enterprises with AI agents. In 2025, Alibaba announced that its AI foreign trade products had been integrated with advanced models such as DeepSeek.
Other platform-based companies are also following suit. For example, Dunhuang.com released the large-scale AI model "Feitian" in the early 2024 for the cross-border e-commerce vertical field, introducing various AI applications. TikTok recently announced the launch of the AI-driven "Seller Assistant" on its seller center, providing intelligent support to brands and merchants. Focus Technology's core platform, China Manufacturing Network, also introduced AI assistants such as Maico and Mentarc for sellers and a Sourcing AI procurement assistant for buyers.
Zhang Kaifei stated that compared to leading businesses, small and medium-sized businesses usually benefit more, "the smaller the business, the more they can benefit from AI applications."
He told reporters that especially when small and micro-enterprises are trying to expand into overseas markets, they find it more difficult to find talent capable of handling relevant tasks. The application of artificial intelligence technology fills the talent gap for these businesses, providing the possibility to improve operational efficiency and quality, thereby gaining a competitive advantage in the market.
"I believe that the number of small and micro-enterprises will experience tremendous growth, and the threshold for entrepreneurship will decrease," Zhang Kaifei said.
In addition to the empowerment of AI applications, going global requires higher capabilities in digital infrastructure for enterprises.
"Currently, many enterprises in the early stages of development, especially in the early stages, focus mainly on how to make the entire system operate quickly," said Han Hongyuan, Vice President of Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group, in an interview with 21st Century Business Herald.
The challenges faced in going global are more complex. For example, on the supply chain side, as businesses expand their operations globally, the stability of the supply chain will face more tests. Companies going global need to build a diverse supply network, establish global supply chain nodes, use digital technology to monitor the supply chain in real-time, and enhance its resilience and risk management capabilities.
In multinational operations, geographical spans can lead to delayed service responses, potentially causing fragmented user experiences and damaging the company's brand image. Companies should establish a global integrated service network, rely on digital platforms to allocate and share service resources, and optimize the collaborative processes of cross-regional service teams.
It is evident that in the face of diverse challenges, digital and intelligent capabilities have become important means of response, and companies going global need to build a strong, efficient, and flexible digital infrastructure.
The "2025 Alibaba Cloud Enterprise Going Global White Paper" points out that the traditional self-built IT infrastructure model is no longer able to meet the needs of companies to quickly respond to changes in overseas markets. Cloud computing services, with their global layout, elastic expansion capabilities, and full-stack service advantages, have become the best solution to this problem.
"When a startup wants to use high-level IT capabilities, the cloud is the most direct choice," said Han Hongyuan. "If a self-built approach is adopted, all related affairs need to be managed independently, which undoubtedly adds complexity. From this perspective, cloud services provide powerful support for enterprises in the process of exploring new markets."
Leading domestic cloud service providers are strong participants in this field.
Han Hongyuan stated that Alibaba Cloud's overseas business has always existed, but it was not given high priority in the past. Since last year, Alibaba Cloud has significantly increased its focus on overseas business.
Recently, at the 2025 Alibaba Cloud Enterprise Going Global Conference, Wu Yongming stated that Alibaba Cloud will strategically invest in accelerating the construction of a global cloud computing network, speeding up the internationalization of AI products, enhancing the development of overseas consulting, technology, and service teams, and paving the way for Chinese companies going global.
Similarly, Huawei Cloud has also released a series of measures and solutions for Chinese companies going global, launching the Global Business Boosting solution in 2025, covering the four stages of going global: "consulting planning, cloud acceleration, cloud innovation, and ecosystem development," reducing the threshold for companies going global.
Although Alibaba Cloud and Huawei Cloud have different focuses in their support for going global, both emphasize the importance of localized services, including deep integration of technology adaptation, talent, culture, and compliance systems.
As Han Hongyuan mentioned, the biggest difference between Chinese companies going global today and foreign companies entering China during the early days of reform and opening up is the disappearance of the technological gap. Chinese companies now have the technological strength to compete with their global counterparts, and the global layout of cloud service providers further narrows the operational and ecological gaps.
Digital infrastructure is no longer just technical support but has become a key variable determining the global competitiveness of companies going global. In the future, companies going global will enter a stage of "meticulous cultivation."
(Author: Dong Jingyi Editor: Zhu Yimin)

title_en: Chinese brands break through global barriers.
body_en:
Huawei store in Amsterdam, Netherlands. Visual China

The China Online Consumer Brand Index (CBI) has increased from 59.42 to 63.38 from the first quarter of 2023 to the first quarter of 2025. Xinhua News Agency

Read the report

The China Online Consumer Brand Index, Global Brand China Online Top 500, and Online Brand Purchasing Power Index reports released by institutions such as the National Development Institute of Peking University have attracted widespread attention from the economic community.

The data in the report shows that from the first quarter of 2023 to the first quarter of 2025, the China Online Consumer Brand Index (CBI) increased from 59.42 to 63.38. Compared to the base index in the first quarter of 2025, it increased by 6.7 percentage points, indicating a significant improvement in the quality of consumer goods in China.

The China Online Consumer Brand Index CBI report (from the first quarter of 2023 to the first quarter of 2025) believes that with the continuous advancement of high-level opening-up to the outside world, the advantages of China's super-large-scale market are becoming more prominent, making it a core market for global brand layout.

This "development report" of global brands in China not only outlines the upgrading trend of the Chinese consumer market but also shows a pleasing fact: both Chinese and foreign brands are shining in the Chinese market.

Behind the slogan "Global Brands, Winning in China" reflects the unique development logic of global brands and the local market. This column analyzes this in detail.

Looking at China

Chinese Brands: Winning the Favor of Global Consumers

The research data from institutions such as Peking University's National Development Institute introduced multidimensional evaluation criteria based on internet platforms like Taobao. The report evaluates brand quality comprehensively based on dimensions such as sales, prices, searches, and positive reviews, presenting the current development status of brands from different perspectives. Overall, many Chinese brands have achieved success in the domestic market, entering the consumer market deeply with advanced technology, mature management experience, and strong brand influence, successfully integrating into the lives of Chinese consumers through cutting-edge innovation research and development and high-quality production and marketing.

In the wave of high-quality economic development in China, Chinese brands are breaking through from the domestic market to the global stage with unstoppable momentum. From BYD topping the global electric vehicle manufacturers to Heytea "sweetening" Southeast Asia, and DJI drones soaring in the world sky... these remarkable achievements confirm that the rise of Chinese brands is not accidental.

In the increasingly competitive global market, the road for Chinese brands to break through is full of challenges. Technological innovation is undoubtedly the key force driving Chinese brands to achieve cross-border development and successful breakthroughs. For example, many brands are investing in high-end equipment, new energy vehicles, and other emerging industries, competing with international giants on the same stage through technological breakthroughs and innovation, winning the favor of global consumers.

Based on this, Chinese brands have moved away from the competition model of relying on low prices and low costs in the past, building differentiated competitive barriers with technological advantages, achieving a "gorgeous transformation."

At the same time, more and more Chinese brands are exploring traditional cultural elements, integrating them into product design and brand concepts, endowing products with excellent traditional Chinese cultural connotations. In the field of clothing, some brands combine traditional Hanfu elements with modern fashion design to create clothing series that are both Eastern and modern, not only popular in the domestic market but also attracting the attention of many international consumers.

From "a few hundred million shirts for a Boeing" to today's new energy vehicles, smartphones, and other high-end products renowned worldwide, Chinese brands and Chinese manufacturing have made remarkable progress, paving a path of astonishing innovative development.

Viewing the World

International Brands: More and More Choosing China as their "Second Home Field"

Walking with China means walking with opportunities; investing in China means investing in the future; choosing China means winning globally.

In the current global economy facing uncertainty, the "certainty" of the Chinese consumer market has become the biggest attraction.

This certainty comes from the market size of over 1.4 billion people, the consumption potential of a massive middle-income population, and the continuous empowerment at the policy level, providing stable expectations for brand development.

China has always maintained an open and inclusive attitude, welcoming international brands to participate in the Chinese market competition. This not only brings more high-quality choices to Chinese consumers but also provides opportunities for learning and reference for Chinese brands. While strengthening the construction of Chinese brands, China actively creates a fair competitive market environment, promoting mutual learning and progress among global brands.

Looking at the report, the success of Chinese and foreign brands in China is not accidental but a natural result of China's open genes, innovation vitality, ecological integration, and super-large-scale advantages. As more and more international brands choose China as their "second home field" and local brands accelerate towards the global stage, this vibrant market is writing a new chapter of global business cooperation with open arms.

Facing Challenges

Brand Building: Requires Persistent Investment and Innovation

While we applaud the achievements of Chinese brands in breaking through internationally, we must also realize that the road ahead is still long and full of challenges. For Chinese brands to continue to exert force in the global market, achieve long-term and steady development, the road ahead is still arduous.

In the process of brand internationalization, challenges such as cultural differences, trade barriers, and intensified international competition cannot be ignored. At the same time, as consumer demands become increasingly diversified and personalized, how to continuously improve product quality, optimize service experiences, strengthen brand cultural connotations to meet higher-level market demands, becomes the "must-answer question" for the advancement of Chinese brands.

Brand building is a long-term project that requires persistent investment and innovation. China has become the only country in the world with all industrial categories, but the "neck-breaking" issue remains prominent in high-end and cutting-edge technology. Faced with a complex and ever-changing international situation, the solution to this problem, as practice has shown, has no shortcuts, and only by persistently taking one step at a time can we see the light.

From the perspective of the global value chain, although Chinese brands have moved towards the high end, there are still gaps with international top brands in brand premium capabilities, global market operation experience, and sustainable development system construction. This requires Chinese brands to take big steps in innovative development and solidify their foundation, exploring new growth paths while maintaining traditional advantages. (According to Xinhua News Agency)

title_en: 【Meticulous observation of autumn】Stablecoin legislation sets sail, Hong Kong's virtual asset development is on the rise with a broad future ahead.
body_en:
Chen Weiming, Fellow of the Chartered Secretaries Institute, Bachelor of Laws, EMBA, licensed by the Securities and Futures Commission
Last month, the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region officially passed the "Stablecoin Bill", establishing a licensing system for the issuance and operation of fiat-backed stablecoins, laying the regulatory foundation for the development of virtual assets. While this move appears to be a risk control policy on the surface, its deeper significance lies in paving the way for the tokenization of assets and Real World Assets (RWA). This not only solidifies Hong Kong's role as an international financial center in the future but also opens up potential channels for legitimate cross-border financing of mainland assets.
Tokenization refers to the digitization and splitting of physical or traditional assets such as real estate, bonds, accounts receivable, private equity, etc., into tradable tokens in blockchain form. These tokens, linked to specific asset values, fall under the category of RWA, significantly enhancing asset liquidity and expanding investment and financing channels.
According to estimates by Boston Consulting Group (BCG), the global tokenization market is expected to reach $160 trillion by 2030. International financial institutions such as JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and UBS have already been actively involved in the on-chain market for physical assets, issuing tokenized bonds, tokenized funds, tokenized real estate equity, etc., and have conducted trials in locations such as Singapore, Switzerland, and Abu Dhabi.
Mainland RWAs have transitioned from experimentation to practical application
Under the policy framework of "blockchain does not equal virtual currency" in the mainland, blockchain applications that are "regulated, controllable, and serve the real economy" are allowed and encouraged, including pilot projects and practical operations of tokenizing physical assets on the chain. Representative commercial cases include China Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation (China Securities Depository) collaborating with Ant Chain under Ant Group and China CITIC Bank to register, verify, and transfer accounts receivable between enterprises (supply chain finance) on the platform, tokenize them, and convert accounts receivable from small and micro suppliers to large enterprises into digital certificates, circulating them in real-time for financing by financial institutions. Another case is the cooperation between China Merchants Bank and China Trust Registration (China Trust Registration Co., Ltd.) to jointly develop a private chain system, on-chain signatures, and rent verification mechanisms, converting the future 5-year rental income rights of long-term rental apartments in Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Chengdu, etc., into digital certificates, which investors can subscribe to and obtain income rights.
RWA tokenization creates a new bridge for mainland assets to "go global"
Another significant aspect of RWA tokenization is creating a new legal bridge for mainland physical assets to go global. For example, through the following three financial structures: 1. Overseas SPV + RWA issuance platform. Chinese companies can set up SPVs in Hong Kong to hold domestic asset income rights, which can be audited and evaluated before being converted into tokenized notes issued to overseas investors. For example, an energy company can convert its power plant rental income into RWA tokens, finance them on the Hong Kong platform, and settle transactions with stablecoins. 2. Cross-border asset fund channel + tokenized fund. If the fund channel is further opened, mainland asset managers can establish tokenized REITs or private equity funds in Hong Kong, raising funds from international institutional investors within a compliant framework, effectively forming a "tokenized fund channel". 3. RWA mortgage loan platform. After converting mainland assets into RWA, companies can mortgage them on a Hong Kong digital asset platform to obtain stablecoin loans in Hong Kong dollars, renminbi, or US dollars, which can then be exchanged for fiat currency to inject into international projects. This model has been tested in Singapore and Switzerland, and Hong Kong has excellent financial and capital market talent with similar conditions.
Institutional innovation helps enhance financial competitiveness
The passage of the "Stablecoin Bill" signifies a shift in virtual asset policy from "fire prevention" to "city building". If further measures such as guidelines for tokenized bonds, RWA certification systems, and blockchain custody standards are introduced, Hong Kong can not only serve as a global experimental ground for the digitization of physical assets but also become a digital bridge connecting mainland physical assets with global capital. Institutional innovation is the key to future competitiveness in capital markets.

title_en: 2022 "Three Products" National Tour | Chongqing: Improving Supply Quality and Promoting High-Quality Development of Consumer Goods Industry
body_en: Editor's note: In order to implement the requirements of the State Council's "Notice on Issuing a Package of Policies and Measures to Stabilize the Economy Solidly", accelerate the promotion of digitalization to assist in the implementation of the "Three Products" strategy in the consumer goods industry, further boost consumer confidence, tap into consumption potential, consolidate and enhance the fundamental role of consumption in economic development, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology recently organized the 2022 National Tour of the "Three Products". China Electronics News has specially opened a column for the 2022 National Tour of the "Three Products", reporting on the progress of the event, expert opinions, and policy interpretations. Stay tuned. On July 5th, the "Digitalization to Assist the Consumer Goods Industry in the Implementation of the 'Three Products' Action Plan" was announced and the 2022 National Tour of the "Three Products" was launched in Beijing. Luo Li, member of the Party Group and Deputy Director of the Chongqing Economic and Information Commission, stated at the meeting that the consumer goods industry is an important pillar industry in Chongqing. Chongqing will focus on key areas such as research and development design, production manufacturing, and public services, guided by the "Digitalization to Assist the Consumer Goods Industry in the Implementation of the 'Three Products' Action Plan", to promote resource sharing, platform connection, and industry collaboration, improve the quality of Chongqing's consumer goods industry supply system, and promote high-quality development of the entire industry. The consumer goods industry maintains a steady development trend. It was introduced that in recent years, under the guidance of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, Chongqing has vigorously implemented an innovation-driven development strategy led by big data intelligence, deepened the integration of digital and real, and achieved an output value of 483.02 billion yuan for the city's above-scale consumer goods industry enterprises in 2021, a year-on-year increase of 10.5%, maintaining a steady development trend. Firstly, focus on the construction of digital platforms to enhance innovation capabilities. Introduce platforms such as Daqian Huiding and Kaiwu Industry for prototype making and high-end mold making services, establish the Chongqing Consumer Goods Industry Innovation Design Research Institute, the Chongqing Industrial Design Industry Alliance, promote the construction of platforms such as Langjian D+M Intelligent Manufacturing Workshop, and the Southwest Center of the China Industrial Design Institute, and use digital means to carry out collaborative innovation. Promote the construction of the industrial Internet platform for the "Hardware Capital of Western China" in Dazu District, Chongqing, which has registered nearly 500 companies, nearly 100 companies have registered on the identification and analysis secondary node platform, with over 500 million codes used and over 200 million data analyses. Promote the "Chengyu Twin City Economic Circle Intelligent Manufacturing Quality Brand Building Project" of Chongqing Saibo Industrial Technology Research Institute was selected for the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's "Industrial Quality Brand Building Enhancement Special Project". Support Zhixiang Jintai to continue the construction of the new crown vaccine production platform project, support key pharmaceutical industrial parks to collaborate with international leading companies such as Cytiva to create a commercial-scale biopharmaceutical contract manufacturing platform through joint construction and other methods. Secondly, focus on the application of big data intelligence to comprehensively improve the capacity and quality of effective supply. Deepen the application of digital technology. Since 2018, the city has created 170 digital workshops and 31 smart factories. A group of key industry enterprises such as Jiulong Paper, Yihai Kerry, and Tianyou Dairy have successfully created national-level green factories, and 31 companies have created municipal-level green factories. Cultivate 4 5G+ industrial Internet integrated innovation application demonstration scenes, promote the implementation of over 1,200 intelligent transformation projects, build 62 industrial Internet pilot demonstration projects, identify 9 "hidden champions", 15 "small giants", and 345 "specialized, refined, new" enterprises; Duanji Clothing relies on big data to build a 3D fitting system, carry out personalized customization and flexible production, and lead innovation and development with intelligent manufacturing; Sumida, Shangshang Clothing and other leading clothing companies deepen the industrial chain synergy, build a "headquarters base + satellite factory" development model, effectively promote rural revitalization. Promote the development of digital medicine, focus on areas such as inspection and testing, sports medicine, chronic disease rehabilitation, and assisted reproduction, build key platforms such as the Chongqing Medical University Laboratory of Translational Medicine, and enhance clinical transformation capabilities. Thirdly, focus on empowering digital marketing to enhance brand cultivation capabilities. Play an effective guiding role of the government, continuously hold the "Yujian Meipin" Chongqing consumer goods brand promotion theme activities on multiple platforms, innovatively combine brand promotion with urban marketing, attract consumer attention through multiple live broadcast activities, continuously promote brand building through online zones and offline activities, promote industry enterprises to accelerate their "online presence". Collaborate with the municipal tourism group to set up online zones using the "Cloud-based Cultural and Tourism Hotel" and "Chongqing Taobao Cultural and Tourism Boutique Pavilion" to help companies expand their marketing channels. Promote deep cooperation between Dadukou District and Feixiang Industrial Internet to deepen C2M new intelligent manufacturing model cooperation, build a Chongqing noodle industrial demonstration park, and promote the slogan "Chongqing Noodles, Made in Chongqing". Promote Alibaba, Kuaishou Technology, Meituan Technology, and other platform companies to establish the Chongqing Consumer Goods Industry Brand Innovation Service Alliance, build a digital marketing "circle of friends". Regularly hold industrial design and digital marketing empowerment training courses to create an industrial ecological atmosphere. Promote high-quality development of the industry from three aspects Regarding the key tasks for the next step, Luo Li stated that Chongqing will focus on key areas such as research and development design, production manufacturing, and public services, guided by the "Digitalization to Assist the Consumer Goods Industry in the Implementation of the 'Three Products' Action Plan", to promote resource sharing, platform connection, and industry collaboration, improve the quality of Chongqing's consumer goods industry supply system, and promote high-quality development of the entire industry. Firstly, use digitalization to promote innovation empowerment. Use digital technology as a link to promote the "Three-Year Doubling Plan for R&D Institutions of Large-scale Industrial Enterprises", encourage large-scale industry enterprises to carry out research and development activities universally, establish research and development institutions universally, comprehensively promote the construction of enterprise research and development institutions, vigorously promote the construction of a group of high-level national or municipal enterprise research and development institutions such as enterprise technology centers and key laboratories of industry and information technology, build a concentrated area for digital economy empowerment, promote collaborative innovation activities between industry, academia, and research, cultivate a group of industry technology innovation benchmarks, and use high-quality supply to promote consumption upgrading. Secondly, use digitalization to promote intelligent manufacturing efficiency. Continue to promote intelligent transformation, support enterprises to build intelligent manufacturing, environmentally friendly processes, and flexible production technology systems, explore the construction of C2M shared factories, enhance product manufacturing capabilities and green development levels. Build industrial Internet platforms around fields such as food and clothing. Plan to build a home design information sharing platform. Enhance the coordinated supporting capacity of green packaging. Cultivate and build a number of R&D and manufacturing projects for AI imaging, "Internet + personal" and household medical testing equipment. Thirdly, use digitalization to unleash brand effectiveness. Combine platform resources, rely on digital scenarios, deepen the application of online platforms, promote the integrated development of agriculture, industry, commerce, culture, and tourism, support the construction of the Chongqing Noodle Industrialization Digital Marketing Service Center, the Prefabricated Vegetable Innovation Service Center, and the Craft Art Propaganda Platform, promote new product development and brand incubation, expand brand influence through multiple channels, further enhance the industrial symbols of "Chongqing flavor", "Chongqing craftsmanship", and "Chongqing taste". Luo Li emphasized that the 2022 National Tour of the "Three Products" organized by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology is an important event to fully demonstrate industry development achievements, exchange development experiences, and enhance regional cooperation. title_en: Notice on holding the 2024 Academic Annual Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association (Second Round)
body_en: To all relevant units: Pharmaceutical excipients are an important foundation in China's pharmaceutical industry, and are one of the key factors determining the quality of generic drugs and the high-quality development of innovative formulations. The supply chain security of pharmaceutical excipients used in high-end formulations in China urgently needs to strengthen the technological innovation and industrial support for domestic pharmaceutical excipients. At the same time, ensuring the quality of clinical medication, reducing drug costs, and alleviating the pressure on medical insurance to a large extent also depend on the quality improvement of domestic pharmaceutical excipients. In line with the principle of "promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new productive forces of the pharmaceutical industry," the "2024 Annual Academic Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association," hosted by the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association, is scheduled to be held in Hefei, Anhui Province from November 8th to 10th, 2024. This academic conference will feature conference reports in the fields of materials science related to pharmaceutical excipients, innovative drugs, and innovative formulations, analyzing the development difficulties and innovations of pharmaceutical excipients; inviting authoritative experts to deeply discuss the in vivo processes of pharmaceutical excipients and drug delivery carriers, as well as the quality improvement and innovation of excipients. The conference will set up expert venues and young scholar sub-venues with three themes: "Pharmaceutical Excipients, Packaging Materials, and Drug Delivery Devices," "New Materials, New Carriers, and Innovative Formulations," and "Pharmaceutical Excipients and Innovative Drugs," to promote the wide participation of enterprises, academia, and young scholars, and jointly focus on the technological innovation and industrial research and development of pharmaceutical excipients. title_en: Robam Electric Honored as One of China's Top 100 E-commerce Enterprises
