title_en: From traveling in China to shopping in China, we can see the vitality of the Chinese economy.
body_en:
Fan Yu
Recently, on social media, the practical tips of "bringing an empty suitcase to China" have sparked heated discussions. From traveling to shopping in China, the experience of "traveling + shopping" has made foreign tourists exclaim "so good".
With high-quality and affordable products, convenient and fast payment methods, and immediate tax refunds upon departure, as the convenience and attractiveness of traveling in China continue to rise, traveling and shopping in China have become a new choice for more and more international tourists, making China a hot spot for global tourism shopping. From policy dividends, industrial strength to cultural charm, the "China craze" shows the world an open, inclusive, and vibrant modern China.
The appeal of the "China craze" comes from policy impetus. From continuously expanding the visa-free "circle of friends", optimizing the payment environment for overseas tourists to improving the convenience of tax refunds upon departure, China is using concrete policies to extend a warm invitation to global tourists. Recently, China decided to implement visa-free entry policies for five countries in South America, including Brazil, increasing the number of countries with unilateral visa-free policies to 43. The coverage rate of foreign card POS machines has increased, and the capabilities of mobile payments such as Alipay and WeChat for "foreign cards inside binding" and "foreign cards inside use" continue to iterate, allowing many regions to achieve "one-touch" payment. China is also continuing to make efforts in tax refund policies, expanding the "buy now, refund now" service measures for tax refunds upon departure from pilot projects to nationwide, lowering the starting point for tax refunds upon departure, optimizing the layout of tax refund shops upon departure, and improving the supply level of tax refund goods. A series of convenient measures convey China's clear attitude of continuously expanding its opening up to the outside world, promoting the continuous rise of the "China craze". During the "May Day" holiday, the number of foreign nationals entering and exiting China increased by 43.1% compared to the same period last year, and the number and amount of transactions processed by UnionPay and NetsUnion for payments by overseas visitors to China increased by 244.86% and 128.04% respectively compared to the same period last year. China has become a more attractive tourist consumption destination, not only promoting economic, trade, and cultural exchanges between China and foreign countries but also achieving deep integration of domestic and international markets.
The "China craze" reflects the quality core of "Made in China". In recent years, the shopping lists of foreign tourists coming to China have continued to expand, from clothing, food to mobile phones, translators, from small household appliances to smart homes. The high-tech content of "Made in China" has significantly increased, making it more competitive in the global market and attracting foreign tourists to continue to come to China to "hunt for good products". Mobile phones, computers, smart wearable devices, drones, and other products have become popular items for "reverse purchasing", reflecting not only the innovative capabilities and technological strength of China's manufacturing industry but also the increasing status of China in the global value chain. From clothing and shoes to electronic products, from affordable daily necessities to high-end luxury goods, the richness of product categories and the diversity of choices in the Chinese consumer goods market attract foreign consumers in droves. Foreign tourists load their suitcases with goods, which is a "vote of confidence" in "Made in China" and a recognition of China's development. Foreign tourists not only experience the high quality and cost-effectiveness of "Made in China" but also touch the pulse of China's development.
The "China craze" also benefits from the deep practice of the integrated development of Chinese culture and tourism. In addition to traditional products such as silk, tea, and porcelain, modern national trends, cultural and creative products, and technological goods are becoming new favorites of foreign tourists. The upgrading of China's cultural and tourism formats promotes the integration of tourism with culture, technology, and other fields, not only pushing "Made in China" onto the international stage but also allowing foreigners to immerse themselves in the charm of Chinese culture and gain a deeper understanding of China's modern development. They may stroll along the central axis of Beijing, experience Hanfu makeup in Xi'an, enjoy ethnic customs in Yunnan, or experience a sense of the future in Shenzhen's technology park. Many foreign tourists choose to travel to China because of their love for Chinese culture, and through tourism, they can further experience the unique charm of Chinese culture and the pulse of China's development. With its profound cultural heritage and modern urban charm, China is gradually becoming the ideal destination for tourists from all over the world. With better product supply, more diverse consumption scenarios, and more convenient services, the appeal of traveling in China is still on the rise.
Industrial upgrading, the increasingly diverse consumer ecology, and the continuous expansion of opening up to the outside world... These factors work together to become the key to China capturing the world's "flow" and inject new vitality into China's high-quality economic development. Today, when globalization is encountering headwinds and protectionism is rampant, China insists on expanding opportunities through greater openness and deeper cooperation, proving to the world that true economic security comes from deep interconnection rather than isolation. It can be said that the significance of traveling and shopping in China goes beyond the economic level, adding new footnotes to international exchanges and connectivity.
(According to Xinhua News Agency, May 27)

title_en: By the side of the Yongding River, sweet upgrade.
body_en:
From Mangzhong to the beginning of midsummer, the city is filled with the fragrance of melons. On May 28th, by the Yongding River, the 37th Beijing Daxing Watermelon Festival grandly opened. In the Daxing International Hydrogen Energy Demonstration Zone, the "Xinglian No." large van transformed from a hydrogen-powered truck became the high-tech main stage that amazed everyone. Inside the exhibition area, the 97.75 kg champion of this year's National Sweet Melon Competition attracted many people to take photos, while the "Xing Xiaogua" series of cultural and creative products caught the eye. Leading the industry, combining culture and tourism. This year's Watermelon Festival showcased the innovative achievements of Daxing's industry, activating the vitality of cultural and tourism consumption.

Beijing's Daxing District has polished the "watermelon industry" gold sign, deeply cultivating the "leading area for green agricultural development." From the century-old heritage of Panggezhuang to the innovative breakthroughs in Beizang Township, Daxing District, located at 39° north latitude, continues to write the "sweet" story of smart agriculture on its fertile soil.

Little Watermelon: Growing Good Taste
Departing from downtown Beijing, driving south along the Jingkai Expressway. After getting off the highway, you enter Panggezhuang Town in Daxing, where green-skinned watermelons are stacked in trucks by the roadside. As the vendor cuts open a watermelon, the fresh red flesh reveals a "sweet smile" to passersby.

Panggezhuang Town is located at 39° north latitude, where the seasons meet and there is abundant sunlight. The Yongding River flows gently here, forming a gently curved plain, nurturing fertile sandy loam soil that makes this area a golden watermelon producing region with a hundred years of planting history.

Today, on this land, the three generations of the "Old Song Melon King" continue the story of growing melons, writing a new chapter for the "hometown of watermelons." Stepping into the "Old Song Melon King" Watermelon Museum in Panggezhuang Town, a whole wall displays over 30 years of time and honors, including the National Sweet Melon Competition champion, the World Fruit Growers Competition silver medal, and the famous trademark of Beijing... countless trophies have made the name of the "Old Song Melon King" more and more renowned, taking the fame of Daxing watermelons to the world. At the opening ceremony of the 37th Watermelon Festival, the "Old Song Melon King" signed a cooperation intention with a Pakistani company representative, engaging in in-depth exchanges on agricultural technology cooperation between Chinese and Pakistani companies.

In the melon shed, the author met the 90-year-old "Melon King" Song Baosen. Since lifting the first Watermelon Competition trophy in 1988, he won the "Melon King" title for seven consecutive years, becoming a benchmark for melon cultivation in Daxing District. His hands covered in soil, wrinkles all over, he vividly recalls the stories of growing melons in the past. In the early days, melon cultivation depended on the weather, and the melon fields could only be replanted every ten years. To overcome the world's difficult problem of not being able to replant watermelons continuously, Song Baosen and a research team from the Beijing Water Conservancy Research Institute conducted experiments in the melon fields day after day, eventually solving the problem of not being able to replant watermelons continuously and increasing land utilization. In the mid-1990s, with the development of greenhouse technology, Daxing began to witness the phenomenon of "snowflakes outside, melon flowers inside," allowing watermelons to appear on people's tables all year round.

Influenced by his father, Song Baosen's son, Song Shaotang, began to understand that growing melons requires knowledge! So, he closed his home appliance repair shop and returned home to grow melons with his father. In 2000, Song Shaotang registered the "Song Baosen" watermelon brand, established the "Old Song Melon King" Technology Development Co., Ltd., and developed the Song family's dozen acres of melon fields into a 50-acre Old Song Watermelon boutique garden. Today, the "Old Song Melon King" manages 45 watermelon greenhouses, leading more than 500 melon farmers to increase their income, selling over 3,000 tons of watermelons. Last year, the "Old Song Melon King" watermelon was included in the national specialty agricultural product list.

To expand sales, Song Shaotang's son, Song Zhijia, took over the baton from his father, developed e-commerce business, and focused on the thin-skinned, thick-fleshed, sweet and juicy watermelons from Panggezhuang. In a live broadcast in 2020, the "Old Song Melon King" set a record by selling 2,000 boxes of watermelons in 3 minutes. Today, the "Old Song Melon King" has cooperated with online platforms such as JD.com and Tmall, developed an online store, and opened up a new sales channel. The watermelons from Panggezhuang are now being sold all over the country through the e-commerce fast track.

Heading west from Panggezhuang Town, you arrive at Beizang Township, located on the Yongding River alluvial plain at 39° north latitude. In the melon fields, round watermelons with dark green stripes hang on vines or lie on the ground. Li Hongye, a member of the Beizang Township Party Committee and Minister of Propaganda, said, "In recent years, our 'Yongding River' brand watermelons from Beizang Township are writing a new chapter in the development of Daxing's watermelon industry." Under the leadership of the local government, Beizang Township is home to a group of new melon farmers, embarking on a unique path of watermelon development.

Inside the Beijing Yongxingyuan Agricultural Products Production and Marketing Professional Cooperative, 20 different varieties of watermelons are neatly arranged on the table. Zhou Chunxiu, the person in charge, enthusiastically introduced the "Yongding River" brand "Seven Flavors Melon" from Beizang Township, with the red-fleshed "L600" being sweet, crispy, and juicy, and the yellow-fleshed "Beijing Color No. 4" being sweet and juicy, and the red and yellow "Ice Cream" being refreshing and delicious.

Since Zhou Chunxiu has been engaged in agriculture, she has vigorously promoted facility agriculture, introduced new varieties of watermelons and vegetables, and new planting technologies. This year, she has also brought the first red ginger planting in Beijing to this place, and hydroponic leeks are also about to be tested. With more and more new and excellent varieties being promoted and planted in Beizang Township, the quality of agricultural products is getting higher and higher.

Melon Industry: Promoting Digitalization
The taste of "good taste" is inseparable from digital empowerment. Stepping into the Chunhua Digital Twin Farm located in Beizang Township, the pest and disease identification and detection system is always "guarding" the healthy growth of watermelons, various sensors collect real-time environmental parameters and crop growth data, and the intelligent water and fertilizer irrigation system cooperates seamlessly with the automatic ventilation system, continuously providing the nutrients needed for crop growth.

Wang Lili, the general manager of Beijing Zhaojiachang Chunhua Sweet Melon Production and Marketing Professional Cooperative, told the author that the digital twin farm has developed a smart agriculture management system specifically for watermelon greenhouses. "It is worth mentioning that we have created an agricultural management cloud platform, which allows the management of the entire unmanned garden area with just a mobile phone."

As soon as she finished speaking, Wang Lili immediately opened the "Nongzhiyun" mini-program and demonstrated to the author how to use a mobile phone to manage the smart farm. On the mobile screen, information such as carbon dioxide concentration, air temperature, light intensity, soil pH, etc., in each greenhouse is clearly displayed. With a gentle touch and swipe of her finger on the screen, Wang Lili completed the monitoring and control of the crop growth environment in the garden.

According to Wang Lili, in addition to achieving intelligent management, the cloud platform can also analyze agricultural product market trends through big data, helping local farmers effectively improve planting efficiency. Data shows that the cooperative where Wang Lili is located has developed 320 households, radiating to four towns in the surrounding area. The per capita annual income has increased from the previous 3,000 yuan to the current 24,000 yuan, making the cooperative one of the first national demonstration cooperatives.

"Not only do we need to grow good products, but we also need to sell them at a good price. We have opened up platforms such as Taobao, Kuaishou, and Douyin for live streaming." Wang Lili told the author that the cooperative once joined forces with 13 "excellent agricultural" products from agricultural areas and 16 postal branch live streaming teams to sell 1,200 boxes of watermelons in a 4-hour live broadcast for farmers. This year, Wang Lili will also bring the "Yongding River" brand agricultural products to the suburban specialty live broadcast room. In front of the camera, watermelons, honey, vegetables, and other agricultural products from the Yongding River are showcased one after another, attracting many netizens to place orders.

As a "Beijing Model Figure" in 2023, Wang Lili actively promotes intelligent facilities to help villagers get rich together. Under her leadership, the production and marketing cooperative has established supply and sales cooperation with corporate units, supermarkets, and e-commerce platforms, effectively solving the problem of difficult sales of watermelons and other agricultural products.

Currently, smart farms are not only thriving in the Daxing watermelon industry but are also widely used in the cultivation of other crops, bringing new vitality to agricultural production in Beijing's Daxing District.

The author visited the Beijing Hongfu Technology Agricultural Industry Park located in Panggezhuang Town, put on a specially made white protective jumpsuit, then put on a special headgear and shoe covers, and then entered a 50,000-square-meter single-body intelligent planting greenhouse. You Xiaolu, the person in charge of Beijing Hongfu International Agricultural Technology Co., Ltd., introduced to the author, "We have introduced advanced modern greenhouse construction technology and intelligent production equipment from the Netherlands, and carefully selected global tomato varieties for planting."

Entering the greenhouse, a strong sense of technology comes to the fore, with dense traction ropes distributed among them, workers standing on picking cars that can be raised to 2.5 meters to wrap the vines at high plants, high-pressure misting nozzles gently spraying fine mist, as if covering the plants with a thin veil, unmanned transport vehicles shuttling back and forth, automatically transporting the harvested tomatoes to the packaging workshop.

"By building a high-yield and efficient agricultural production system, we have successfully cultivated the excellent tomato variety 'Hongfu Persimmon,' becoming an advanced tomato planting base in Asia." You Xiaolu told the author that to overcome the drawbacks of heavy metal pollution, pesticide residues, and hormone-induced flowering in traditional planting models, the park insists on using "drinkable irrigation water," soilless cultivation, and bumblebee pollination, producing about 1,000 tons of tomatoes annually.

From the days of "living off the land" to the present "scientific farming," from traditional extensive management to refined intelligent management, the watermelon industry in Daxing District is becoming increasingly "smart" under the empowerment of modern technology. Seizing the opportunity of constructing a modern agricultural demonstration zone, Daxing District uses the Internet of Things, agricultural big data, and AI decision-making systems to build an integrated intelligent monitoring network, create intelligent application scenarios, and promote the transformation of agricultural modernization through the application of intelligent equipment.

Melon Culture and Tourism: Playing with New Ideas
Today, the Daxing watermelon industry is not only empowered by technology but is also increasingly extending towards the integration of agriculture, culture, and tourism. On May 16th, the author drove to the Beijing Xingshengda Smart Agriculture Industry Center in Beizang Township, where rows of greenhouses were shining in the sunlight. Led by Li Shousheng, the enthusiastic leader, the author pushed open the glass door of the "Hundred Seeds Corridor," stepping into a microscopic museum of life. In the four major exhibition areas of grains, vegetables, fruits, and Chinese medicinal herbs, the original appearance of crops is displayed in detail: flat watermelon seeds are labeled with planting seasons and methods, round sorghum seeds are placed next to rice-like rice seeds.

Li Shousheng looked at the seeds in these transparent bottles and said, "We hope to show children what seeds look like, how crops are grown, and how watermelons grow." Currently, the "Hundred Seeds Corridor" has 143 varieties of seeds, and the number will further expand in the future. The base covers an area of about 200 acres, mainly planting watermelons, tomatoes, strawberries, organic vegetables, and other crops.

Li Fengqi, a second-level researcher at the Daxing District Agriculture and Rural Bureau, introduced that based on the positioning of the capital as a "seed core area" and the "North China melon and vegetable seed industry base," Daxing District has coordinated technical resources to build the city's only billion-level seedling nursery, with an estimated annual seedling production of 300 million plants this year; currently, over 90% of the seedlings are sold to Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei, and other places in an "order-based" manner, and have expanded to Henan, Sichuan, Hubei, and other places, with the economic benefits of seedlings gradually emerging.

After passing through the "Hundred Seeds Corridor" and entering the row of greenhouses, the thick watermelon vines hang on white equipment racks, and round watermelons are hidden among the green leaves. Li Shousheng introduced that the base currently plants two varieties of high-quality watermelons, "Beijing Color" and "Xuan Color," which will ripen one after another at the end of May and the beginning of June.

Walking towards the depths of the greenhouse, several tomato vines with red and white "Wishful Thinking Recognition Tags" are particularly eye-catching. Looking at the crooked words on the tags, 5-year-old Guo Duanning's adopted tomato seedlings are basking in the sun, and a few green tomatoes have already appeared among the lush vines.

On Mother's Day, May 11th, the Beijing Xingshengda Smart Agriculture Industry Center held a "Love Fruit Fate・Mother's Day Special" tomato public adoption event. Nearly 50 groups of parent-child families and 113 participants entered the greenhouse, and through activities such as fun agricultural challenges, parent-child farming experience classes, and science popularization lectures, they personally adopted exclusive tomato seedlings. When the fruits are ripe, the children will harvest the tomatoes they adopted, feeling the vitality of the land in the joy of harvest. Looking at the watermelon vines not far away, Li Shousheng told the author that the watermelon adoption event is expected to start in mid-June.

In addition to the tomato adoption activity, the Xingshengda Smart Agriculture Industry Center also launched the "Adopt a Plot of Land" farming experience project, allowing more people to deeply experience the charm of modern agriculture and natural farming through firsthand planting, cultivation, and harvesting processes.

In June 2024, the "Beijing Rural Revitalization Promotion Regulations" clearly state that governments and relevant departments in rural areas should improve policies and measures for the integrated development of agriculture, culture, and tourism, support the development of rural homestays, pastoral sightseeing, farming experiences, rural health care, science popularization practices, and other formats. Against this backdrop, new farmers like Li Shousheng, who cherish the farming sentiment, are emerging in the fields of Beijing's Daxing District.

On May 15th, a group of elementary school students from the Cuwei Elementary School Daxing Branch in Haidian District, Beijing, wearing red scarves and khaki vests, walked into the Four Seasons Yangkun Ecological Farm in Panggezhuang Town, Daxing District, embarking on a journey of exploration of modern agriculture.

"Why are watermelons hanging in the air?" "How can we tell if a watermelon is ripe?" Faced with modern agricultural facilities, the children threw one question after another to Liu Fujun, the general manager of Beijing Four Seasons Yangkun Agricultural Technology Development Co., Ltd. Liu Fujun picked up a green watermelon hanging on the vine and said, "Hanging the watermelon on the rack is like building a three-dimensional sunroom for them—allowing every inch of the melon skin to bask in the sun and saving ground space to plant more plants." It is understood that the farm covers an area of 478 acres, with 72 modern greenhouses neatly arranged, equipped with shading systems, intelligent ventilation systems, and other high-tech facilities.

The cultivation history of Daxing watermelons can be traced back to the Taiping period of the Liao Dynasty over a thousand years ago. Today, the sand, sweet, and crispy Daxing watermelons famous in the capital have become an agricultural brand engraved with regional characteristics, moistening the taste buds of the citizens with sweet juice every summer. The annual Watermelon Festival has passed 37 years with the concept of "using melons as a medium, making friends, promoting Daxing, and developing the economy." "Daxing watermelons are not only a booster for industrial development but also a living history book that records the sweet upgrade of people's lives through the process of agricultural modernization." Li Fengqi said.

Now, as the summer sun shines on the melon fields, those watermelons carrying the fragrance of the soil bring not only sweetness on the tongue but also carry the innovative answer of a new era for an agricultural region.

title_en: When you arrive at Wangjing, do not use the meter and ask for 60 yuan.
body_en:
At the no-parking area on the west road of Chaoyang Station, taxi drivers illegally parked and negotiated prices in front of security guards.

Covering license plates, negotiating prices with passengers, long-term parking in temporary drop-off areas... Many passengers have reported to this newspaper hotline that during holidays, there are many traffic violations and irregularities by taxis and ride-hailing cars around Chaoyang Station in Beijing.

According to the clues provided by passengers, reporters went to Chaoyang West Road, which is adjacent to the Chaoyang Station transportation hub. "Need a ride? All are regular taxis!" The drivers soliciting passengers on Chaoyang West Road are even more numerous than the passengers who have just left the train station. According to regulations, various vehicles such as taxis and ride-hailing cars are not allowed to park on Chaoyang West Road. However, whenever they see passengers with large bags, the drivers will come over and claim that their cars are regular. Once they successfully strike up a conversation, they will propose a price increase: "The place you're going to is too far, give me some extra money, how much to add can be negotiated, get in the car first." Even if the passenger's destination is close enough to only require the starting fare, drivers who negotiate prices will still look hesitant and try to persuade the passenger to pay more.

Reporters found that the drivers soliciting passengers not only parked their cars on Chaoyang West Road but also parked them in a small alley on the west side of the road. These drivers either cover the license plate with a cloth or raise the cover of the trunk high, making it difficult to obtain evidence even with surveillance cameras.

On the evening of the 2nd, after being solicited by a driver, the reporter got into a taxi from Jinjian Taxi Company. Before getting in the car, the driver said that the fixed price to the reporter's destination in Wangjing area was 60 yuan. Following the driver to the alley to get in the car, the driver immediately turned off the meter. The reporter noticed that the screen displaying the service supervision card information was also covered tightly by two QR codes for WeChat and Alipay.

After getting off the car, the reporter found that the key information on the invoice issued by the driver was also covered. This invoice was not printed by the meter but was taken out of the driver's pocket. The green tax stamp was firmly stamped on the license plate number, so if the passenger did not record the license plate number on the spot and wanted to complain later based on the invoice, they would not be able to find this car. Subsequently, the reporter found through multiple ride-hailing platforms that the estimated price for this route by taxi was around 40 yuan. The fixed price offered by the driver was nearly 20 yuan more expensive than the normal price.

The reporter found that these taxis that negotiate prices with passengers all come from regular taxi companies, but they all have issues such as covering the information on the service supervision card inside the car and tampering with the invoice.

In response to the situation of operating vehicles negotiating prices with passengers, the Beijing Chaoyang Station Area Management Office replied that the law enforcement team in the station area has been working on related behaviors, and they will handle any problems found in accordance with the law. If citizens encounter similar situations, they should keep specific information such as the vehicle number, driver's identity information, and payment receipts to protect their rights.

Reporters: Chen Shengyu, Jing Yiming, text and photos.

title_en: Stablecoin, the first IPO is coming.
body_en: Download the Sina Finance APP to understand real-time global exchange rates. Caixin Circle was established in October 2013 by Jeremy Allaire (CEO) and Sean Neville (co-founder), focusing on blockchain technology and stablecoins. In 2018, Circle and Coinbase jointly established the Centre Alliance to launch USD Coin (USDC), a stablecoin backed 1:1 by the US dollar, initially positioned against Tether's USDT, boasting greater compliance and transparency. In 2023, the Centre Alliance dissolved, making Circle the sole issuer and manager of USDC. As of April 2025, USDC has become the world's second-largest USD-pegged stablecoin, with a market capitalization of approximately $60.9 billion, second only to Tether's USDT. The Silicon Valley bank crisis in 2023 prompted Circle to consider going public. At that time, Circle's $3.3 billion in the bank was temporarily "frozen," causing USDC to lose its peg. Circle's executives then realized that to truly establish themselves in the global stablecoin competition, they needed to rely on the "triple magic" of "license + listing + transparency," rather than just the support of the crypto community. In 2025, on April 1st local time in the United States, Circle submitted the S-1 form to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to list on the New York Stock Exchange (stock code CRCL), and hired top investment banks such as JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup as underwriters for this IPO. Circle reported that by the end of 2024, its stablecoin-related business generated $1.7 billion in revenue, accounting for 99.1% of total revenue. On May 27th, Circle announced the terms of the IPO, planning to issue 24 million shares of stock (60% from the secondary market), with 9.6 million shares issued by the company and 14.4 million shares from existing shareholders, at a price range of $24 to $26 per share, raising $600 million. Based on the proposed range's midpoint, Circle's fully diluted market value will reach $6.2 billion. This IPO has attracted the attention of institutional investors, including Cathie Wood's ARK Investment Management, who expressed interest in subscribing to up to $150 million worth of shares. Guosheng Securities stated that if Circle successfully goes public, it will further promote the development of the U.S. stablecoin market and accelerate the acceptance of stablecoins by traditional financial users, especially institutional users. The stablecoin market has experienced rapid growth in recent years. In terms of market composition, USDT and USDC are the main products in the market. Since the birth of stablecoins, they have become important tools for participants in the cryptocurrency market - providing value reserves and pricing tools, as well as serving as collateral for various cryptocurrency spot/futures trading, making them the most important type of cryptocurrency tool. If Circle successfully goes public, it will be a significant positive for the market. Stablecoins connect traditional finance and the crypto ecosystem, with multiple RWA projects accelerating. Stablecoins are cryptocurrencies anchored to fiat currencies or assets, with price stability and blockchain compatibility, widely used for trading, settlement, and value storage, essentially tokenizing real-world fiat currencies or assets on the blockchain, seen as a "bridge between traditional finance and the crypto ecosystem." Initially designed for the crypto asset field, stablecoins have rapidly entered traditional financial areas such as payments in recent years. Due to their characteristics of peer-to-peer payments, high efficiency and low cost, relative price stability, and close connection to the crypto asset industry, stablecoins are increasingly being used in conventional financial activities such as cross-border payments and foreign exchange savings, becoming an ideal choice for international payments and asset reserves, as well as having important applications in decentralized finance (DeFi) and other new financial activities. Globally, the strategic position and market size of stablecoins continue to rise. According to Oriental Securities, as of May 31, 2025, the global stablecoin market value exceeded $250 billion, an increase of over $40 billion from the end of 2024. From 2024 to 2025, the tokenization of real-world assets (RWA/Real-World Assets, i.e., digitizing real-world assets and putting them on the blockchain) has accelerated both domestically and internationally. Among them, the two major stablecoins pegged to the US dollar, USDT and USDC, had market values exceeding $153 billion and $61 billion respectively as of May 31, accounting for over 85% of the total global stablecoin market value. Overseas, the United States and the European Union are actively promoting their respective stablecoin bills, trying to seize the first-mover advantage in the global stablecoin market. The U.S. stablecoin bill focuses on maintaining the dollar's leadership in the digital economy, aiming to make the dollar stablecoin a global tool for digital payments, continuing the dominance of the dollar. At the same time, institutions such as Robinhood and BlackRock are promoting unified regulation and the application of high-performance chain technology, with chains like Solana becoming the preferred infrastructure for RWAs. In China, the RWA market began to accelerate in 2024 with several projects landing, such as Langxin Group and Ant Group's new energy RWA; Xin Xin Energy and Ant Group's photovoltaic green asset RWA; Dalian Xiaoping Island digital island project; Shanghai Zuoan Xinhui's "Malu Grape RWA" project; Xunying Group's battery swapping asset RWA; and Yuanlong Yatu exploring the digitization of IP cultural assets to promote the internationalization of cultural asset RWAs. At the policy level, the "Action Plan for High-Quality Development of Digital Finance" proposes to support RWA innovation, emphasizing compliance and data rights; on May 30, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government published the "Stablecoin Ordinance" in the Gazette, which means that the "Stablecoin Ordinance" has officially become law. China International Securities research report believes that recently, both China's Hong Kong and the United States have been advancing stablecoin-related legislation to varying degrees. Stablecoins can provide a stable trading method for RWA token assets, enhance market liquidity, and help promote the further implementation of mainland Chinese companies' RWA issuance projects in Hong Kong. At the same time, stablecoin legislation is expected to indirectly promote the development of digital currency-related payment and settlement interfaces in the Hong Kong financial industry, benefiting financial IT companies with experience in digital currency/digital RMB cross-border settlement and supply chain finance projects. Huaxi Securities stated that RWAs will become the core hub linking the real economy and digital finance. In the future, RWA tokens will expand to more segmented scenarios, such as carbon assets, supply chains, and intellectual property rights, overlaying AI and on-chain large models to achieve automatic valuation and intelligent clearing, activating the digital liquidity of trillion-level physical assets. 24-hour rolling broadcast of the latest financial information and videos, more fan benefits, scan the QR code to follow (sinafinance).

title_en: E-commerce "blocking high-refund groups" urgently needs effective regulatory intervention.
body_en:
Ren Chao
Following the comprehensive cancellation of "refund only" by multiple e-commerce platforms, in May of this year, Taobao once again attempted to promote anti-internal competition in e-commerce by introducing the "high refund population blocking" function to clothing merchants. This allows merchants to set up a blocked population on their custom promotion pages, completely blocking high refund and abnormal refund populations from further contact, while reducing exposure to populations with higher refund rates, thereby reducing the probability of contact. This move has sparked widespread controversy as to whether screening customers is to protect the autonomy of business operations or infringe on consumer autonomy, requiring further exploration of the legal logic behind it and seeking a balance of legal interests between the two.

The deep reason for Taobao's introduction of the "high refund population blocking" function lies in the high return rate in the clothing industry, which increases the operating costs for merchants, squeezes profit margins, and dampens business enthusiasm. Consumers have the right to choose operators, types of goods, and service methods independently, and their choices are not subject to mandatory intervention. Operators in the clothing industry also have the right to choose trading partners and set trading conditions independently. Although merchants do not have the right to discriminate against customers based on race, color, gender, region, etc., they do have the right to choose customers for legitimate reasons, such as preventing malicious fraud. Therefore, blocking high refund populations may constitute discrimination and infringe on consumer autonomy, or it may simply be a reasonable differential treatment to protect the autonomy of clothing e-commerce businesses, which requires a case-by-case analysis.

From the information published by the platform, the "abnormal refund population" refers to those who engage in behaviors such as returning empty packages, falsely claiming not to have received goods, or falsifying return shipping orders. Merchants can completely block such individuals on their custom promotion pages. Since such behaviors objectively involve malice, completely blocking them does not involve infringing on consumer autonomy but rather protects the autonomy of merchants. Furthermore, after merchants activate the blocking feature, although the refund rate may decrease, overall exposure, click-through rates, and number of transactions may also decrease simultaneously. Merchants need to weigh the pros and cons and make decisions, which is a manifestation of their autonomy in business operations.

The "high refund population" refers to consumers whose refund rate in the past 90 days exceeds three times the average of Taobao users and have a large volume of returns. Merchants can also set up complete blocking for such consumers. However, the "one-size-fits-all" criteria may mistakenly affect consumers who have tried on multiple items for reasons such as style or size, and these consumers do not constitute a breach of contract, nor do they engage in malicious activities such as "taking advantage of the system." They may be subject to undue discrimination due to the "one-size-fits-all" criteria, which also constitutes an infringement on consumer autonomy by merchants.

The population with a "relatively high refund rate" is determined by merchants based on a comprehensive consideration of consumer willingness to transact and refund performance, and they can reduce exposure and contact probability. Since this does not involve complete blocking, the possibility of infringing on consumer autonomy is relatively low. However, the determination criteria rely on the independent comprehensive judgment of merchants and may be suspected of violating the principle of fair trade.

In addition, the "high refund population blocking" function may also infringe on consumer privacy rights. E-commerce platforms collect and screen consumer refund records, which belong to information that "reflects the activities of specific natural persons" and when combined with transaction accounts, purchasing habits, etc., may constitute sensitive personal information. If the e-commerce platform does not clearly inform consumers in the privacy policy that "refund rates will be used to limit promotional exposure" and does not provide an option to opt-out, it may be suspected of violating the principle of informed consent and potentially infringing on consumer privacy rights.

From the consumer's perspective, there is also a need to block merchants who frequently sell counterfeit goods. Based on the balance of rights between merchants and consumers, e-commerce platforms should simultaneously provide settings to block merchants. For example, consumers can filter merchants based on indicators such as "credit score: merchant's overall score is below the platform average," "complaint rate: complaints in the last 30 days exceed 50% of similar merchants," "product quality labels: platform-publicized data such as 'counterfeit rate' and 'description discrepancy rate,'" allowing consumers to customize blocking tags. In addition, the platform can also add a "block this merchant" function on product recommendation pages and search lists, and merchants can submit evidence of rectification for reasons of being blocked, allowing consumers to periodically review the blocking list and make adjustments.

Furthermore, the market supervision department should supervise the "high refund population blocking" function introduced by e-commerce platforms in accordance with relevant provisions of the "Interim Provisions on Internet Anti-Unfair Competition," the "E-commerce Law," and the "Regulations on the Management of Internet Information Service Algorithm Recommendations."

On the one hand, regulatory authorities need to conduct in-depth supervision of platform algorithm rules, requiring e-commerce platforms to disclose the core parameters of labeling algorithms (such as the calculation formula for "refund rate exceeding three times the average") and explain their compatibility with Article 25 of the "Consumer Rights Protection Law" (right to return goods without reason). They should establish a dynamic filing mechanism to urge platforms to timely file new feature rules and adjustment plans with local market supervision departments to prevent the "black box" of algorithms from evading responsibility.

On the other hand, there should be a focus on supervising discriminatory screening issues, requiring platforms to establish a system for reporting merchant blocking behavior to promptly grasp the use of the blocking function by merchants. Platforms should submit risk classification criteria for the blocking function (such as the logic for determining "abnormal refunds") and a report on the rate of misjudgment, and focus on reviewing whether merchants are categorizing reasonable returns (such as size discrepancies or quality issues) as malicious refunds. For merchants who abuse the blocking function (such as mass returns due to product quality issues but then blocking consumers in retaliation), regulatory authorities should not only apply penalties for discriminatory trading conditions but also urge platforms to optimize algorithms in a timely manner to prevent merchants from abusing the blocking function.

In conclusion, e-commerce platforms must prioritize the balance of legal interests in their feature openness and rule-making, balancing the rights of merchants and consumers through detailed classification and precise rule-making. Regulatory authorities need to maintain long-term intervention, balancing efficiency and fairness, to strengthen the responsibilities of e-commerce platforms and operators, and build a healthy e-commerce ecosystem where merchants are happy to operate and consumers are willing to consume.

(The author is a professor and doctoral supervisor at the School of Economic Law of East China University of Political Science and Law, and the Executive Director of the Economic Law Research Association of the China Law Society)

title_en: The seed industry's large language model "Fengdeng Rice" is open to the global website.
body_en:
This report (Hainan Daily, reporter Huang Yuanyan) The world's first large language model "Fengdeng Rice" specially designed for rice biological breeding has recently been officially opened to the world on the website (https://seedllm.org.cn/). The model deeply integrates the rice biological knowledge graph, leading the way in building the world's largest scale rice research corpus and the world's first rice multi-omics knowledge graph. It demonstrates significant advantages in information retrieval and knowledge understanding, laying the foundation for the construction of an intelligent decision-making breeding technology system.

The Yajiaowan National Laboratory and the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, in collaboration with China Agricultural University, released China's first seed industry large model "Fengdeng" (SeedLLM) in 2024, pioneering the application of large models in agricultural breeding research. The focus is on building an intelligent model that truly understands crop biology and has professional reasoning capabilities to substantially improve the efficiency and quality of biological breeding research. As a follow-up academic achievement of "Fengdeng," in May 2025, the research team published relevant papers, using rice as an example, detailing the technology and implementation principles of "Fengdeng," showcasing the latest research results, and officially opening the website to the world.

The "Fengdeng" research team first built the world's largest scale rice research corpus, systematically integrating over 1.4 million Chinese and English literature, covering over 98% of publicly published results in the field. Based on this, the research team, using Alibaba's released Tongyi Qianwen model as a foundation, successfully developed the Fengdeng Rice Seed Industry Large Language Model through continuous training and fine-tuning processes. To comprehensively evaluate the model's capabilities, the research team constructed a large model-generated rice knowledge question and answer dataset, SeedBench, containing 1975 pairs of question and answer samples, covering 10 tasks such as question and answer generation, summary extraction, language understanding, and multiple choices. Automated evaluation results show that the Fengdeng model significantly outperforms mainstream general models such as Tongyi Qianwen in accuracy and other metrics.

In addition, the research team, in collaboration with rice domain experts, designed a high-quality human evaluation dataset, HumanDesignRiceQA, containing 253 professional questions focusing on gene function, traditional hybrid breeding, molecular design breeding, and other core topics. The evaluation was completed by 326 reviewers, including 83 senior experts in the field of rice research. The results show that the Fengdeng model comprehensively surpasses OpenAI GPT4 and the average level of undergraduate students in terms of answer quality, demonstrating its leading ability in the agricultural vertical field.

To further enhance the model's scientific practicality, the "Fengdeng" research team built the world's first rice multi-omics knowledge graph, integrating 1879 literature data on rice transcriptome and proteome, systematically aggregating gene expression levels, protein abundance, and genome functional annotation information. The graph contains over 400,000 nodes and 1.57 million edges, covering key knowledge units and biological relationships in rice research.

The head of the "Fengdeng" research team revealed that the large language model, with its powerful language understanding and knowledge reasoning capabilities, is expected to become a key tool to support rice research and intelligent breeding. The "Fengdeng" service achieves graph collaborative reasoning, able to transcend the limitations of pure text expression, and call upon structured graphs to perform precise queries and integrate multidimensional evidence.

title_en: Hong Kong IPO fundraising in May hits a four-year high
body_en:
Comic: Wang Jianming

[Shenzhen Commercial News] (Reporter Chen Yanqing) In the just past May, the Hong Kong IPO market was hot, with the amount raised reaching a new high since March 2021. According to Wind data, calculated by listing date, a total of 10 companies landed on the Hong Kong stock market in May, raising a total of 55.76 billion Hong Kong dollars. Among them, CATL raised as much as 41 billion yuan.

On May 20, CATL officially completed its secondary listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The fundraising amount for this Hong Kong listing is approximately 41 billion Hong Kong dollars, making it the largest IPO fundraising in the world this year.

On May 23, CSPC Pharmaceutical Group was listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, also achieving dual listing in both "A+H" markets, with a fundraising amount of 9.89 billion Hong Kong dollars, making it the largest pharmaceutical IPO in Hong Kong this year.

It is precisely because of the listing of these two industry leaders that the IPO fundraising amount in May increased significantly, reaching a new high in the past four years.

It is worth mentioning that in the first five months of this year, a total of 28 Hong Kong stocks raised 77.32 billion Hong Kong dollars through IPOs, while the total IPO fundraising amount for Hong Kong stocks last year was 88.1 billion Hong Kong dollars. It is not difficult to see that the IPO fundraising amount for Hong Kong stocks this year exceeding last year is a high probability event.

According to Wind data, from 2009 to 2021, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange ranked first in the world in IPO fundraising for 7 consecutive years, but in 2022-2023, Hong Kong IPOs cooled down, and the fundraising amount fell out of the top five globally; in 2024, with the listing of large mainland companies such as Midea Group, Hong Kong IPOs warmed up again, and the fundraising amount returned to fourth place globally.

From a policy perspective, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange has further promoted the streamlining of the approval process. On May 6, the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange issued a joint announcement proposing the introduction of a "Tech Enterprise Fast Track," which allows special technology and biotechnology companies to choose to submit listing applications in a confidential manner, with strict confidentiality of company-related information during the review stage.

Currently, the pipeline of IPO projects in Hong Kong is quite rich. Data shows that as of the end of May, a total of 156 companies have submitted applications to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, spanning multiple industries such as healthcare, consumer goods, TMT, and more. Among them, over 20 A-share companies have submitted applications to list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

In response to this, a senior investment banking executive at a brokerage firm in the north told reporters that the influx of mainland companies to Hong Kong for IPOs is related to the significant improvement in Hong Kong stock liquidity, the continuous optimization of the listing system by the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, and the strengthening of mainland policies to broaden the overseas listing channels for enterprises.

Looking ahead to the full-year IPO market outlook, analyst LI Zhiyi of CGS International predicted in a report that Hong Kong IPO fundraising is expected to reach 160 billion Hong Kong dollars in 2025, and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange will return to being the world's largest IPO market.

Zhang Xia, chief strategy analyst at CMB Securities, pointed out that as the price difference between A-shares and H-shares continues to narrow, companies such as WuXi AppTec, China Merchants Bank, BYD, and CATL are experiencing a phenomenon where H-share prices are lower than A-share prices. Against this backdrop, the wave of companies listing in Hong Kong has been set off, with the revaluation of Chinese assets driving a significant improvement in Hong Kong stock liquidity. Looking ahead, the trend of a weakening US dollar has already taken shape, the renminbi continues to strengthen, and Chinese core assets are expected to continue to be sought after.

Huatai Securities pointed out that the activity in the IPO market reflects the structural changes in Hong Kong stocks. Since the reform of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018, the liquidity and growth of Hong Kong stocks have continued to improve. From 2025 to the present, the average daily turnover of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange has increased by 2.8 times compared to 2018. Currently, consumption and technology account for half of the market value of Hong Kong stocks, with 10 technology giants such as Alibaba, NetEase, BYD, and SMIC International accounting for nearly 30% of the market value of Hong Kong stocks.

title_en: Overall efficiency increased by 50%, social security payment through scanning code is more worry-free.
body_en:
According to the reporter Yu Changxu, recently learned from the Provincial Taxation Bureau that since the offline scanning payment of social security fees went online in May, 76 tax service halls in our province have realized the scanning payment function. The daily social security fee payment completed through scanning accounts for 43.38% of the offline payment volume, and the scanning payment has reduced the processing time for a single transaction from 3 minutes to 1.5 minutes, increasing overall efficiency by 50%.
The person in charge of the social security department of the Provincial Taxation Bureau introduced that in the payment process, the front desk staff display the QR code to the payer through the tax authority's tax management information system, and the payer can complete the payment by scanning the code using a mobile payment app, supporting mainstream payment platforms such as WeChat, Alipay, and UnionPay. The entire process is simple to operate, without the need to carry cash or bank cards, greatly reducing the payment time and avoiding inconvenience caused by limited payment methods.
The offline scanning payment of social security fees is an important achievement of Guizhou's tax "delegation and regulation" reform. The tax departments across the province will continue to pay attention to the needs of payers, continuously optimize payment service measures, further improve payment channels, provide payers with more high-quality, efficient, and convenient social security payment services, and effectively enhance the public's sense of gain and satisfaction.

title_en: Achieve twice the result with half the effort/Enter e-commerce and start live streaming to enhance brand awareness.
body_en:
Image: Zhejiang Yiwu Oulode Company relies on the WeChat ecosystem to conduct live broadcasts for more than 8 hours a day, with daily sales exceeding 100,000 yuan. Interviewee provided image.

Zhejiang Yiwu Oulode Company used to focus on exporting to North America, Europe, and the Middle East, with an annual export of over 500,000 pieces of cookware and an export value exceeding 20 million yuan (RMB, the same below). The company's head, Li Xiongfei, revealed that before the United States wielded the tariff "big stick," the company had gradually adjusted the ratio of foreign trade to domestic sales from the early 7:3 to 3:7, and initiated a branding strategy, launching luxury kitchenware products that meet domestic demand. He admitted that in the past, the company relied on OEM production, lacked bargaining power for its own brand, and transitioning to domestic sales was not easy. Mainland consumers have low awareness of emerging brands, unfamiliar sales channels, and significant operational differences, becoming the "three major obstacles" in front of them.

Oulode had previously entered the Tencent WeChat store. In mid-April, Tencent launched the "New Export Journey Acceleration Plan," proposing to exempt technical service fees for the first 1 million yuan of self-operated transaction volume for qualified foreign trade companies, providing up to 15,000 yuan in live streaming traffic incentives, allowing companies to go into battle lightly. "After the implementation of measures such as the reduction of technical service fees and traffic incentives, I believe that operating costs will be further alleviated," Li Xiongfei said.

From Export to Domestic Sales, Products Need to be Grounded
Relying on the WeChat ecosystem, Oulode conducts live broadcasts for more than 8 hours a day, with daily sales exceeding 100,000 yuan. On the day Tencent released the acceleration plan on April 17, daily sales broke one million for the first time, reaching a new high. Li Xiongfei revealed that by showcasing product solutions for pain points such as "difficult to clean" and "heavy cookware" in a scene-based content in the live broadcast room, user stickiness significantly increased.

In the transition to domestic sales, products are the core. "Overseas users prefer Western-style cooking, while domestic families need multi-functional, space-saving kitchenware." Based on this, Oulode integrates foreign trade craftsmanship with domestic cooking habits, launching a "multi-purpose pot" series suitable for frying, stir-frying, stewing, and boiling. The enamel pot not only retains export-grade quality but also optimizes sealing for Chinese-style stewing, quickly becoming a hot seller.

"At present, domestic sales account for more than 70%, and we plan to further deepen the domestic market while also expanding into emerging overseas markets such as Southeast Asia," Li Xiongfei said.

The success of Oulode is not an isolated case. Under the policy orientation of "stabilizing the foundation of foreign trade and tapping into domestic demand potential," more and more foreign trade companies are leveraging major platforms including Alibaba, JD.com, and Tencent to accelerate the "transition from export to domestic sales."

title_en: Notice on holding the 2024 Academic Annual Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association (Second Round)
body_en: Relevant units: Pharmaceutical excipients are an important foundation in China's pharmaceutical industry, and are one of the key factors determining the quality of generic drugs and the high-quality development of innovative formulations. The security of the supply chain of pharmaceutical excipients used in high-end formulations in China urgently requires the strengthening of technical innovation and industrial support for domestic pharmaceutical excipients. At the same time, ensuring the quality of clinical medication, reducing drug costs, and alleviating the pressure on medical insurance to a large extent also depend on the improvement of the quality of domestic pharmaceutical excipients. In line with the principle of "promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new productive forces of the pharmaceutical industry," the "2024 Annual Academic Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association," hosted by the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association, is scheduled to be held in Hefei, Anhui Province from November 8th to 10th, 2024.
