title_en: Sports open up new windows of opportunity for children in the village.
body_en:
"Pay attention to defense" "Don't rush" "Good ball" ... Once again representing the school to go out for a game, You Xuan, the captain of the girls' basketball team at Huilong Primary School in Xingren City, Guizhou Province, calmly responds to the changes on the court, with a confident and sunny face, completely unlike the introverted and speechless girl she was at the beginning.
In recent years, with the development of sports education in rural schools and the organization of various sports events, the campus life of rural students has become more colorful. The spiritual outlook of rural students has been injected with new vitality because of sports, and the future of some rural students has become more promising. The inheritance of sports has also promoted the generation of a positive cycle.
This is the "sports dream" of countless rural children today.
Because of sports
What is sports, perhaps glimpses of it can be seen on the playgrounds of rural schools in Guizhou.
During leisure time at Tangfang Primary School in Baling Town, Xingren City, Guizhou Province, students running and jumping can be seen everywhere on the playground. Playing basketball, badminton, soccer... the laughter of children echoes in the campus.
Over the past 20 years, this rural primary school, which originally had only 3 teachers and 75 students, has grown with the educational philosophy of "cultivating people with sports and revitalizing the school with sports". Currently, the school has 42 teachers and nearly 500 students, and the average student scores have increased from less than 30 points to over 80 points. Principal Wu Xiong said that the improvement in the level of education is inseparable from the improvement of the teaching environment and the hard work of the teachers, with sports activities playing an important role. "Through participating in a variety of sports activities, students become more cheerful in character, physically stronger, and mentally healthier. Participating in competitions also broadens their horizons." Wu Xiong said that making children happy is more important than making them excellent, and sports is a way to make them happier.
In the view of Jiang Dejin, Deputy Director of the Education and Technology Bureau of Dafang County, Guizhou, sports not only teach students skills, but more importantly, give them a hobby, allowing them to release stress correctly in their spare time from studying, which will benefit them for a lifetime.
Psychologists believe that participating in sports can help students relieve study pressure, cultivate strong willpower, promote interpersonal communication, help establish a positive attitude, and improve psychological adjustment abilities.
Sports have also changed the life trajectories of some rural students, giving them more possibilities for the future.
Sanhe Primary School in Shizhu County, Chongqing, is famous for its soccer. Since the establishment of the girls' soccer team in March 2013, the team's achievements have been remarkable: winning the "Chasing the Wind League" championship twice, winning over 30 city-level and above competition championships and runner-ups; among the former team members, 39 have reached the national level athlete standard, 1 has reached the national level sports elite standard, and 7 have been selected for the Chongqing U18 women's soccer team of 23 people; in 2024, the school's girls' soccer team was also selected for the national "New Era Good Teenagers" advanced deeds list...
Recently, Sanhe Primary School has once again received good news. Among the third batch of 10 members of the girls' soccer team, one was admitted to Inner Mongolia University last year, and another 6 are currently being provisionally admitted to Chongqing Normal University and other universities. Among the first batch of 21 members of the girls' soccer team, 20 have been admitted to universities such as Tongji University.
Yuanbao Tongxin Experimental School in Dafang County, Guizhou, is also well-known for its girls' soccer team. Currently, this rural school's girls' soccer team has accumulated 14 people who have been admitted to the Southwest Branch of the Chinese Football Academy, and 7 people who have been admitted to the Shanxi Datong Youth and Children's Sports School...
Assistance from all sides
In addition to local sports teachers and government support, assistance from all sides is also indispensable.
In the exhibition hall of Yuanbao Tongxin Experimental School, there is a novel called "Time Traveler: The Fog of the Middle Ages". In 2017, the author of the novel, Zhang Zhouchen, donated the 50,000 yuan he earned from selling books to the school. The school used this fund to build a simple soccer field measuring 30 meters long and 18 meters wide, which became the starting point for the "Yuanbao Girls' Soccer" dream.
Now, next to this soccer field, a larger field has been put into use. After school every afternoon, more than 80 members of the school's soccer team will train on the field.
This is not an isolated case. In recent years, various levels of relevant departments, public welfare organizations, caring enterprises, and individuals have put a lot of effort into improving the sports environment of rural schools and raising the level of sports education in rural schools.
In December 2022, a five-a-side soccer field built with funds from a designated assistance unit was completed and put into use. Lazi Shu Primary School in Puan County, Qiannan Prefecture, Guizhou Province now has its own soccer field, and the training environment for the children has been improved. Previously, the children could only practice on a cement basketball court, and the training conditions were very rudimentary.
Chen Ming, a sports teacher at Huilong Primary School, said that when the school first formed a basketball team, the Yao Foundation would send volunteers to the school every year to train teachers and guide students in training. According to the Yao Foundation's official website, as of the end of 2023, this public welfare project has supported a total of 4661 rural schools, sent 6512 volunteer teachers, trained 1239 rural full-time and part-time sports teachers, and benefited about 5.4 million rural youth.
At Sanhe Primary School, the arrival of Guo Xin, the former head coach of the Dalian Women's Soccer Youth Training Center, has allowed the children in the girls' soccer team to experience more professional and scientific training methods, significantly improving their competitive level. After the team defended their title at the national finals of the "Chasing the Wind League", Guo Xin left the team due to age reasons, but he had already arranged for a new professional coach to come and coach the team. "He still cares about the children in the team and will come back to guide them from time to time," said former principal Sun Xiaoming.
In 2019, Alipay announced a 10 billion yuan investment over 10 years to support the development of Chinese women's soccer, and also launched the "Chasing the Wind Plan" to support the development of girls' soccer in rural schools. Currently, the plan has supported over 200 rural school girls' soccer teams, helping over 6000 rural girls enjoy soccer more happily and obtain more educational opportunities through soccer.
The General Administration of Sport of China launched the Sports Support and Education Volunteer Service in 2021. This "dream-building project" relies on thousands of volunteers from dozens of universities to alleviate the shortage of grassroots sports teachers and sow the seeds of sports dreams in beautiful rural schools.
Returning to the mountains
Sports have helped the children, and the children have not forgotten sports or their hometowns. "This is Niu Lihua, who graduated from junior high school and went to Tsinghua University High School, and was later admitted to Tsinghua University, where she is currently studying for a master's degree; this is Guo Zhongrui, who won second place in the national marathon championship in 2024, and was selected for national team training in 2021..." When talking about the students he has taught, Wang Bin is full of pride and satisfaction.
Wang Bin is a sports teacher at Wumeng Town Middle School in Panzhou City, Guizhou Province. He was born in a local village, where his father was a primary school teacher who loved sports. Influenced by his father, he showed a strong interest in sports from a young age.
In 1992, Wang Bin was sent by his parents to study martial arts at the Wushu School in Beihai, Guangxi. In September 1996, he enrolled in the sports school of Guizhou Province. After graduating in 1999, he returned to his hometown to become a primary school teacher, and in 2001, he was transferred to Wumeng Town Middle School as a sports teacher. This is a rural school located at the junction of three counties in Yunnan and Guizhou provinces.
When he first arrived at Wumeng Town Middle School, faced with poor school conditions and outdated training facilities, Wang Bin developed a set of sports training methods suitable for rural junior high school students. From demonstration movements to decomposed movements, he taught them step by step. In order to save time and energy for students who had a long way to travel to school, Wang Bin also called some children to his home, provided them with food and accommodation, and personally bought sports uniforms and shoes for the students...
Thanks to Wang Bin's efforts, the school has now sent hundreds of outstanding athletes to regular high schools, sports schools, sports teams, and universities. The students have repeatedly achieved good results in various competitions at all levels, winning over 40 group awards at the national, provincial, municipal, and county levels.
A few years ago, his student Li Micong returned to his hometown after graduating from university and became a rural primary school teacher. Li Micong studied sports, but there was a shortage of teachers in rural schools, so she had to teach subjects other than physical education, making her workload heavier. Even so, she would use her spare time to teach the children basketball, table tennis, and soccer. In recent years, she has taken students to the city to participate in basketball games and sports meetings. Although the results were not ideal, the children trained seriously, gave their all in the competitions, and never gave up, which moved her deeply.
Not long ago, Li Micong organized a fun sports event, and the laughter and scenes of students working together, bravely competing, left a deep impression on her. "Next semester, we plan to hold an autumn sports event to further enrich the children's campus life and make more students fall in love with sports," she said.
Over a thousand miles away from Panzhou City, at Sanhe Primary School, every winter and summer vacation, a group of familiar figures can be seen on the campus - the former members of the school's girls' soccer team. "Every winter and summer vacation, the former team members come in pairs and take turns to the school to guide the younger students in training. Passing on the torch, continuing the struggle, this has become a tradition," said Sun Xiaoming.
Today, Wang Bin is still holding on, but the relay baton of rural sports education has quietly been passed on. (According to Xinhua News Agency)

title_en: 52TOYS rushes to Hong Kong stocks, can it solve the problem of losses by borrowing "Stitch"?
body_en:
China Business News reporter Li Zhu Sun Jizheng reported from Beijing
Recently, Beijing Le Zi Tian Cheng Cultural Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "52TOYS") officially submitted its prospectus to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, planning to list on the main board, with Citigroup and Huatai International as joint sponsors.
The China Business News noticed that since the second half of last year, the concept of "valley economy" has been hot in the Hong Kong stock market, with the stock prices of companies like Pop Mart (09992.HK) and others rising. Bruco (00325.HK) successfully went public, and there were rumors of a split listing for TOPTOY under Miniso. Currently, other "valley economy" companies aiming for IPO include KAYOU.
In addition to frequent capital market news, the trendy toy market is also growing continuously. According to the "Trendy Toy Industry Development Report (2023)" released by the Institute of Financial Strategy of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the global market size of trendy toys is expected to reach nearly $40 billion in 2023 and $44.8 billion in 2024. In China, with the continuous popularization of trendy toys, the industry's compound annual growth rate is expected to reach 24% from 2022 to 2026, with retail sales reaching 110.1 billion yuan in 2026.
Renowned top-level design expert and strategic marketing consultant at Tsinghua University, Sun Wei, predicts that the trendy toy economy will maintain a compound growth rate of 15% over the next 10 years. He points out that with the current prosperity of the cultural IP industry, the trendy toy industry is in a rapid development stage, standing out in the wave of the Chinese economy. However, in an era of severe product homogeneity, creating a good IP is particularly important because IP is not only a collection of independent personality stories and brand symbols but also the soul of trendy toy series product development.
Riding the wave to go public
In its prospectus, 52TOYS mentioned that it ranked third in GMV among Chinese IP toy companies last year.
"After watching the movie 'Stitch,' I wanted to buy a figurine right away!" Hu Di, a post-00s, couldn't hide her excitement in her words.
The movie she mentioned is the live-action movie "Stitch" adapted from the animated movie "Lilo & Stitch," which was released simultaneously in mainland China and North America on May 23, 23 years later. It is reported that before the movie was released, Disney collaborated with 52TOYS to authorize the development of Stitch trendy blind boxes.
In early May this year, Wanda Films also announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Beijing Times Film E-commerce Co., Ltd., would jointly invest 1.44 billion yuan with affiliated company Shanghai Ruyi Xingchen Enterprise Management Co., Ltd. in 52TOYS. When asked about the cooperation model and future operations, the reporter asked 52TOYS, which stated, "Information is subject to Wanda Films' announcement and prospectus, and there is currently no other information disclosed."
In its prospectus, 52TOYS mentioned that it ranked third in GMV among Chinese IP toy companies last year, following Pop Mart and Bruco, and plans to raise funds through a Hong Kong IPO to further strengthen its IP incubation capabilities, expand product categories and overseas markets, and build a new global IP toy industry ecosystem.
According to the prospectus, from 2022 to 2024, 52TOYS' revenue increased from 463 million yuan to 630 million yuan, with a compound annual growth rate of 16.7%. During the same period, gross profit increased from 134 million yuan to 252 million yuan, with a stable gross profit margin of around 40%, reflecting a high-quality profit structure. It is worth mentioning that the growth in revenue from overseas markets is particularly impressive, increasing from 35.4 million yuan in 2022 to 147 million yuan in 2024.
However, 52TOYS has been in an investment period in recent years and has not yet achieved profitability, with a net loss of 122 million yuan in 2024, further expanding from 2023. The company explained that this was mainly due to the impact of fair value measurement liabilities, fair value changes, and equity incentives; excluding related non-cash items, the adjusted net profit in 2024 was 32.01 million yuan, with an adjusted net profit margin of 5.1%.
According to Wind data, on May 26, the net purchase of Hong Kong bank stocks by southbound funds exceeded 2 billion Hong Kong dollars in a single day. Brand strategy expert and founder of Jingjie Interactive, Chen Jingjing, pointed out that even though the Hong Kong stock market environment is improving, the capital market demands higher profitability logic and growth certainty from companies. While 52TOYS can tell the story of being the "second stock of trendy toys," whether it can gain high recognition from the capital market still remains uncertain.
Limited independent IP
As a trendy IP toy company, 52TOYS' revenue mainly comes from its own IP and licensed IP, but the main source of revenue is still from licensed IP.
Currently, there are three trends in domestic IP: content-oriented IP, product-oriented IP, and design-oriented IP. In the industry's view, IP derivative products and service systems are constantly evolving with changes in consumer relationships. The deeper the customer relationship, the higher the product's unit price, and the greater the customer's value.
According to IP licensing industry practices, mature film, game, and other IPs are usually not exclusively licensed to specific companies but are licensed through IP operation agencies. For example, in the case of Disney IPs, in addition to Disney's self-operated Tmall store, trendy toy companies such as Pop Mart, Jumu Za Wu She, 52TOYS, and TOPTOY all base their blind box or figurine product development on this IP.
The reporter noted that as a trendy IP toy company, 52TOYS' revenue mainly comes from its own IP and licensed IP, but the main source of revenue is still from licensed IP. As of December 31, 2024, it owned 35 proprietary IPs and 80 licensed IPs, including Crayon Shin-chan, Tom and Jerry, and Disney series IPs. However, most of the licensed IPs are not exclusively obtained, and the prospectus disclosed that the only IP exclusively licensed is Pou-kaPouka.
It is worth mentioning that 52TOYS founder Chen Wei had previously stated that he "does not want to be the second Pop Mart" and that 52TOYS aims to be a "collectible toy" in its brand positioning.
Blind boxes are just one way to play with trendy toys, and currently, figurines, art toys, adult assembly toys, and others are also popular. Collectible toys are also becoming a global trend. Analyses by Yi Guan predict that the market size of the domestic collectible toy industry will exceed 150 billion yuan by 2025.
According to senior toy enthusiast Zhang Ji, transformable collectible toys are high in design difficulty and product complexity. Internationally, if a company can create transformable toys, it indicates that the company has strong product capabilities.
52TOYS co-founder Huang Jin once told reporters that the company internally divides an IP into three periods: operational period, incubation period, and maturity period. In the maturity period, IPs with explosive potential are accepted by users, and cross-border cooperation begins. According to his previous introduction, the company internally implements the "721 product strategy," where "70% of the products are the most popular and popular products in the market, ensuring the brand's life cycle; 20% are forward-looking experimental works to cultivate the market's next stage of demand; and 10% are niche, artistic products to maintain creative vitality and market foresight."
Chen Jingjing believes that the trendy toy industry lacks brand loyalty, and consumers are more likely to choose based on image and preferences rather than brand-driven. To attract consumers, companies must differentiate through design or limited edition products. She analyzed, "52TOYS' core advantage lies in its differentiated positioning, especially in the mechanical trendy toy field, attracting hardcore players with strong hands-on abilities and a preference for collecting, clearly distinguishing itself from Pop Mart, which targets a cute style and female audience."
Chen Jingjing believes that although 52TOYS has established competitive barriers through product style and target audience segmentation, and has made some investment in original IPs, its revenue still relies mainly on IP licensing cooperation, with a limited proportion of original IPs. This structure may affect its valuation level in the Hong Kong stock market.
The prospectus shows that in 2022, 2023, and 2024, 52TOYS' sales revenue from its own IP was 132 million yuan, 130 million yuan, and 154 million yuan, respectively, while revenue from licensed IP was 233 million yuan, 286 million yuan, and 406 million yuan, with licensed IP revenue accounting for 64.5% in 2024. In addition, its "Beast Box" series has released over 160 SKUs to date, with cumulative GMV exceeding 190 million yuan.
Difficulties in the IP business
According to data from Zhishi Consulting, the market size of China's IP derivative products was 174.2 billion yuan in 2024 and is expected to reach 335.7 billion yuan by 2029.
With the IP LABUBU igniting the market, young consumers are starting to pay for more trendy toy products. Pop Mart, known as the "Maotai of the trendy toy world," has seen its stock price soar, with its market value peaking at over 300 billion Hong Kong dollars.
However, several industry insiders have pointed out that the IP business is not easy.
Li Xing, Executive Vice Chairman of the Cultural and Creative Committee of the Wenlv Wenchuang Committee of the Henan Provincial Committee of the Democratic Progressive Party, pointed out that the trendy toy industry has shifted from "barbaric expansion" to "high-quality growth." "From the market performance, the demand for trendy toy consumption continues to be strong, especially the pursuit of cultural symbols and emotional resonance by young people has driven industry expansion. However, the industry faces three major challenges: intensified homogenized competition, technological and experiential upgrade demands, and opportunities for going global and globalization."
From the perspective of the capital market and product level, Chen Jingjing believes that there is indeed a certain bubble in the trendy toy industry, especially with individual explosive products being hyped to high prices. However, from the perspective of the younger generation of consumers, this is a way to express social pressure emotions. "Emotional consumption changes rapidly, and once the hot spot fades, the product's value will also decline. Whether companies can continue to hit the next emotional hot spot will directly determine the vitality and growth potential of their IP," Chen Jingjing said.
Sun Wei believes that the essence of the trendy toy economy is "fun with stories." How to win the love of young people and satisfy their emotional value with differentiated products and models is also a consideration for companies after expanding their scale. Original IPs need to have international capabilities, and IP going global needs to integrate local culture and enrich the cultural connotations of IP with local culture so that the developed IP products can be understood and loved by local consumers.
Overall, the IP market size is still expanding. According to Zhishi Consulting data, the market size of China's IP derivative products was 174.2 billion yuan in 2024 and is expected to reach 335.7 billion yuan by 2029. As the largest sub-market in the IP derivative product industry, the IP toy market had a GMV of 75.6 billion yuan in 2024 and is expected to grow to 167.5 billion yuan by 2029. However, the overall growth rate has slowed down, and the trendy toy industry's compound annual growth rate remains around 20%, but compared to the peak in 2021, the industry has entered a stage of refined operation.
According to Pop Mart's financial report, it adopts a "dual-track parallel" strategy in product development, creating original IPs on one hand and collaborating with well-known first-line IPs on the other, conducting secondary development of IPs, including deep cooperation with LEGO, Disney, Warner, and other IPs. At the same time, it has rapidly opened stores in Southeast Asia, Europe, and the United States to sell products.
52TOYS, on the other hand, will choose to bundle with popular movies and TV shows. During the Spring Festival in 2023, as the only official authorized transformer toy partner of "The Wandering Earth 2" IP, 52TOYS introduced the crowdfunding model to the public. Among them, a joint model of a transforming mech toy based on the mechanical dog "Benben" from the movie raised over 10 million yuan in crowdfunding on Taobao.
It is worth mentioning that before the release of "Lilo & Stitch," global retail sales of related themed products had reached $2.6 billion in the 2024 fiscal year. Whether the cooperation between 52TOYS and Wanda can help boost the growth of peripheral products of this IP remains to be seen.

title_en: Seize the 90-day window period "Foreign Trade 6·18" and set sail with the wind.
body_en:
China Business News reporter Li Li reported from Shanghai
Take advantage of the 90-day window to recover losses caused by the tariff turmoil.
On May 12, substantial progress was made in the China-US high-level economic and trade talks, significantly reducing bilateral tariff levels. On the evening of May 12, Ding Linfeng, the general manager of Shanghai Weierda Sunshade Equipment Co., Ltd., received an order worth $100,000 from an American customer; also suddenly hit by a large order was Wu Qingfen, the general manager of Yiwu Wen Import and Export Co., Ltd., as a long-time American buyer directly placed an order for 300,000 pairs of socks.
The reduction of tariffs from 145% to 30% has led to a rapid surge in American buyers stocking up. According to China Business News, on the day when the US tariff adjustment on China officially took effect on May 14, Ali International Station urgently launched a special event for the US. Currently, preparations are underway for the June promotion targeting the US market, quickly launching "Foreign Trade 6·18".
Taking advantage of the 90-day window after the China-US economic and trade agreement, "6·18" officially goes global.
American "explosive orders"
The demand temporarily suppressed by the tariff turmoil is expected to erupt in June.
Ali International Station urgently launched the "US Special Event" and quickly felt the strong demand. According to feedback from merchants, many American buyers basically follow the principle of "no bargaining, just quick delivery", hoping to stock up as much as possible for the next cycle within 90 days. Some American buyers have even started stocking up for the Christmas season as a precaution.
"Customers are now very anxious to place repeat orders, hoping that we can complete production within a month because the subsequent goods will also take a month to arrive by sea. Everyone hopes to seize the 90-day shipping window!" Ding Linfeng revealed that another long-term American client also plans to place orders for 1-2 containers of goods, totaling around $150,000. Roughly estimated, on the night of the tariff reduction, he received orders from the US totaling over one million yuan.
Wang Li, the general manager of Shenzhen Maiqijia Home Furnishings Co., Ltd., also recently experienced a surge in American orders. "The order amount on May 13 exceeded the total amount of orders in a typical half month, and we plan to ship 8 containers of goods to the US that week." Wang Li predicts that her American clients are basically in the replenishment stage, and with the uncertainty of the tariff policy after 90 days, based on the current order amount, they are basically stocking up with three to four months' worth of inventory.
In addition to small businesses on Ali International Station quickly placing orders, there has also been a wave of stocking up on Aliexpress, the "international version of Taobao".
Zhipeng, a Guangdong merchant specializing in wedding simulation flowers on the Aliexpress platform, experienced a small surge - in less than a week, customers from the US had already bought $600,000 worth of wedding simulation flowers from his store.
At the same time, Qiu Guoqing, who operates wedding dresses and formal wear on Aliexpress, found that after the tariff adjustment, customers from Brooklyn, New York, USA, who had several wedding dresses in their shopping carts, promptly made payments.
According to Qiu Guoqing, most wedding supplies in the US come from China, and the advantage of Chinese cross-border e-commerce sellers lies in their fast response, strong design capabilities, and reasonable prices. Sometimes, customers have their own small designs, and sellers try to accommodate them as much as possible. From the demand for this wave of stocking up, many people decisively placed orders, buying several items at once and hoping for quick delivery after placing the order.
Data from Ali International Station shows that on the first day of the US special promotion, orders in various industries began to soar, with a year-on-year growth rate reaching double digits and a month-on-month growth rate exceeding three digits.
Order data shows that clothing and accessories, jewelry, eyewear, watches and accessories, beauty products, home and garden, packaging and printing, consumer electronics, sports and entertainment, mother and baby products, gifts and crafts, and luggage are among the top ten categories. In terms of growth momentum, auto parts increased by 62% year-on-year, machinery and equipment by 46%, and 3C & new energy by 42%.
"6·18" goes global
Feeling the strong short-term demand surge in the US market, the immediate priority is to help merchants seize the 90-day golden window of tariffs.
"We are currently preparing for the June promotion targeting the US market and quickly launching 'Foreign Trade 6·18'." Ali International Station told reporters that they not only need to recover orders affected by US tariffs in the past month but also help merchants sell out their goods for the next three months.
It is understood that this promotion not only allows Chinese foreign trade merchants to enjoy overseas traffic support and better accept American orders, but the greater benefit is that the promotion has no threshold, and all merchants can sign up to participate. This means that even new merchants who have just joined Ali International Station have the opportunity to make big sales.
According to industry analysts, in the past half month, a large number of small and medium-sized enterprises in the US have downloaded the Ali International Station app, temporarily making it the top shopping app in the US App Store. American retailers and private label brands currently only have enough inventory for 1-2 months of consumption. The reduction in US tariffs may stimulate small and medium-sized US enterprises to once again place orders on Ali International Station.
However, it is noted that not only is the Ali International digital business sector taking advantage of the window brought by the reduction in US tariffs to organize "Foreign Trade 6·18", this year's Tmall "6·18" is also further going global. Currently, the domestic "6·18" is entering its peak selling period, and Ali has announced that overseas consumers can also enjoy free shipping on Taobao.
During "6·18", Taobao will expand its "global free shipping plan" to 12 countries and regions, covering Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea, Australia, Japan, Thailand, among others. For the first time, Kazakhstan and Mongolia have joined the Taobao free shipping zone.
During "6·18", consumers in the aforementioned countries and regions can not only enjoy "full free shipping" but Taobao also provides them with "local return" services. If consumers are dissatisfied with their purchases, they can return them to the nearest pick-up point. In terms of discounts, overseas consumers enjoy the same "official discounts" as mainland Chinese consumers: it is worth mentioning that this year, some overseas regions' "88VIP" members can also receive exclusive large coupons for stacking.
Since the beginning of 2025, Taobao's pace of going global has significantly accelerated. Following the landing of the first offline furniture experience store Papa-Home in Hong Kong, China in February, a Russian version was launched in Kazakhstan, and recently, nearly a million merchants signed up for the 2025 Tmall "6·18" overseas venue. According to the person in charge of Taobao's international business, "This year, Taobao will continue to accelerate its global expansion to help merchants tap into overseas markets."
In the view of industry insiders, as the domestic "6·18" campaign expands, consumers are already experiencing aesthetic fatigue, but with the overseas expansion of "6·18", it may bring new business opportunities for merchants. Therefore, going global has become the biggest difference for this year's "6·18".
sentiment_reason: Taobao's 618 event is being promoted globally, and overseas expansion may bring new opportunities and business prospects.

title_en: Notice on holding the 2024 Academic Annual Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association (Second Round)
body_en: Relevant units: Pharmaceutical excipients are an important foundation in China's pharmaceutical industry, and are one of the key factors determining the quality of generic drugs and the high-quality development of innovative formulations. The security of the supply chain of pharmaceutical excipients used in high-end formulations in China urgently requires the strengthening of technical innovation and industrial support for domestically produced pharmaceutical excipients. At the same time, ensuring the quality of clinical medication, reducing drug costs, and alleviating the pressure on medical insurance to a large extent also depend on the improvement of the quality of domestically produced pharmaceutical excipients. In line with the principle of "promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new productive forces of the pharmaceutical industry," the "2024 Annual Academic Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association," organized by the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association, is scheduled to be held in Hefei, Anhui Province from November 8th to 10th, 2024. This academic conference will feature conference reports in the fields of materials science related to pharmaceutical excipients, innovative drugs, and innovative formulations, analyzing the development difficulties and innovations of pharmaceutical excipients; inviting authoritative experts to deeply discuss the in vivo processes of pharmaceutical excipients and drug delivery carriers, as well as the improvement and innovation of excipient quality. The conference will set up expert venues and young scholar sub-venues on the themes of "Pharmaceutical Excipients, Packaging Materials, and Drug Delivery Devices," "New Materials, New Carriers, and Innovative Formulations," and "Pharmaceutical Excipients and Innovative Drugs," promoting the wide participation of enterprises, academia, and young scholars to jointly focus on the technological innovation and industrial research and development of pharmaceutical excipients. The relevant matters are hereby notified as follows: 1. Conference theme: Promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new productive forces of the pharmaceutical industry. 2. Time and place: November 8th Registration location: New Ji Hotel, Hefei (2766 Wenzhong Road, Yaohai District, Hefei City, Anhui Province) The main venue and sub-venues on November 9-10 are both at the Shaoquanhu Campus of Anhui University of Chinese Medicine in Hefei, Anhui Province (350 Longzihu Road, Yaohai District, Hefei City, Anhui Province). 3. Conference arrangements: The conference will adopt a format of main venue and sub-venue reports. The conference will invite well-known experts and scholars from domestic universities, research institutes, pharmaceutical companies, research and development units, medical institutions, regulatory agencies, etc., to give keynote speeches and special lectures. Please refer to Annex 1 for the detailed schedule. 4. Participants: Researchers, managers, and graduate students engaged in research and development related to pharmaceutical excipients, pharmaceutical packaging materials, drug delivery devices, formulation quality control, formulation equipment, pharmaceutical services, etc., from universities, research institutes, pharmaceutical companies, research and development units, medical institutions, drug regulatory agencies, and other related institutions. 5. Call for papers: 1. Requirements for submission of papers: Chinese and English abstracts and paper formats. Papers that have not been published in publicly distributed journals or presented at national academic conferences are the responsibility of the authors; please ensure clear expression and accurate data. We welcome active submissions from researchers in the pharmaceutical field. 2. Paper submission method: Please submit the paper abstract to the conference website https://yyfl2024.sciconf.cn before October 20, 2024, click on the "Online Paper Submission" button on the right, and follow the process to upload your paper abstract. After successful upload, you will receive an automatic email confirmation of online submission. After expert review of the papers, the organizing committee will select several papers for further communication or publication in the "Drug Analysis" journal. 3. Poster submission method and time: Same as for papers. The conference welcomes poster submissions, which should be in A1 standard size. 6. Registration: (1) Registration method: 1. Please register by clicking on the "Individual Representative Registration" or "Group Representative Registration" button on the conference website link https://yyfl2024.sciconf.cn; 2. Or scan (or long-press to recognize) the QR code below with your mobile phone, click on the "Individual Representative Registration" or "Group Representative Registration" button to fill in the registration information and submit. (2) Registration deadline: The registration deadline is October 30, 2024. (3) Notes on registration: 1. To ensure that participants receive registration confirmation, invoices, and other information, please fill in accurate and true email addresses, phone numbers, and other information; 2. This registration website is only for registration, and the payment channel is not yet open; 3. Registered individuals can log in to the conference website's personal center to check and modify their registration information; 4. Participants who do not submit papers can also attend the conference. 7. Conference fees: (1) Conference registration fee: 1. Registration fee includes conference materials and lunch during the conference. 2. Payment methods: (1) Telegraphic transfer: After registering for the conference, participants should pay the registration fee by bank transfer, supporting both corporate and personal transfers to the following account: Payee: Chinese Pharmaceutical Association Bank: Bank of China Head Office Account number: 778350009320 It is recommended to use online banking for personal transfers, or you can also use Alipay transfer (to a bank card, with the name field filled in as "Chinese Pharmaceutical Association"). Please indicate "Pharmaceutical Excipients + Participant's Name + Unit Abbreviation" in the remittance note. After successful payment, please upload the remittance voucher to the conference website promptly for the secretariat to confirm the payment information and issue the invoice; (2) On-site payment: Registration fees can be paid on-site through mobile banking transfers, or by scanning the payment QR code (Alipay, WeChat) on-site; there is no POS machine on-site, and payment methods such as card swiping and UnionPay QuickPass are not supported. After uploading the personal remittance voucher (photo, screenshot, etc., of the complete order) to the conference system, please accurately fill in the invoice information in the billing instructions section of your personal information. 2. title_en: Setting up a scam in the name of borrowing a hand, using fake screenshots to deceive.
body_en:
Self-proclaimed as the "red envelope snatching" leader, he gained the trust of the WeChat group owner by introducing players to come and gamble, and then used fake transfer screenshots to deceive the other party's money. After being prosecuted by the Hanshou County Procuratorate in Hunan Province, on March 10, the court sentenced Deng to three years and nine months in prison for fraud and fined him 40,000 yuan.
Yang (handled separately) created a gambling WeChat group and invited players to join the group to gamble in the form of "sending red envelopes." On June 7, 2024, a "A Shui" netizen who claimed to be an intermediary added Yang's WeChat and said he wanted to play in his WeChat group. Yang had long known that "A Shui" was a reputable leader in the "red envelope snatching" circle, who could bring in big players to participate in gambling, and he was excited. "A Shui" then asked Yang for 30,000 points of empty credit (WeChat gambling chips) to introduce players to join the group.
That afternoon, two players lost all the empty credit provided by Yang, and Yang paid the gambling capital. Afterwards, Yang asked for payment, and "A Shui" lied that his WeChat and Alipay were both limited in amount, and needed to pay later, and asked for Yang's receiving account. Later, "A Shui" photoshopped a fake transfer screenshot of over 36,000 yuan and sent it to Yang, while indicating that Yang should return the extra 6,000 yuan to him through WeChat transfer, which Yang immediately did. Seeing that Yang easily fell for it, "A Shui" used the excuse of gambling to photoshop bank transfer screenshots of over 19,000 yuan and over 27,000 yuan respectively to Yang, and then lured Yang to transfer over 53,000 yuan under the pretext of settling accounts for gambling.
Afterwards, Yang found that his bank account did not receive any money, and realized he had been deceived, so he immediately reported to the police. The police locked down the identity of the suspect through investigation, and it turned out that "A Shui" and the two players were all Deng. After Deng was arrested, he truthfully confessed his criminal facts, and the proceeds of the crime had been used for gambling and consumption.
On January 10, 2025, the Hanshou County Procuratorate prosecuted Deng for suspected fraud. (Wang Gang)

title_en: "Underage movie viewing discount policy 'hide and seek'?"
body_en:
Behind a regular movie ticket, there is a hidden "invisible barrier" to protect the rights of minors! China's Law on the Protection of Minors clearly stipulates that cinemas should implement a policy of free or discounted admission for minors. However, in reality, some cinemas have turned this statutory benefit into a "paper welfare".

Recently, it was learned through interviews that the Dongcheng District Procuratorate of Beijing used a big data legal supervision model to accurately identify some cinemas with issues such as lack of transparency in the preferential policies for minors. By issuing administrative public interest litigation procuratorial suggestions to the relevant authorities, they pushed for comprehensive rectification of 16 cinemas in the jurisdiction, building a solid "protective net" for the viewing rights of minors.

Big data "sweeping" revealed 39 complaints exposing industry loopholes
"Why is there no prompt when the child clearly meets the free ticket criteria when purchasing tickets?" In March of this year, when analyzing data on the 12345 government service hotline, the Beijing Procuratorate keenly discovered the frequent appearance of the keyword "minor discount" in movie ticket purchase disputes, and immediately transferred this clue to the Dongcheng District Procuratorate for in-depth investigation.

"Through the derivation and application of big data models and manual verification, our procuratorate accurately identified 39 related complaint cases. These disputes were concentrated on the lack of public disclosure of the preferential policies for viewing on the third-party ticketing platform pages of some cinemas, leading to many parents mistakenly purchasing tickets due to not understanding the policy of 'children of qualifying height can enjoy free tickets'," explained Liu Chaoying, a prosecutor handling the case at the Dongcheng District Procuratorate.

It was also learned during the interviews that many parents were not aware of Article 44 of the Law on the Protection of Minors, which stipulates that cinemas and other venues should provide free or discounted access to minors according to relevant regulations, becoming a major cause of subsequent disputes.

To ensure the effectiveness of supervision, the Dongcheng District Procuratorate adopted a "online + offline" and "data + on-site" three-dimensional investigation model: in terms of electronic evidence collection, key evidence such as platform ticket purchase pages and user complaint records were fully preserved; in the on-site verification stage, the case-handling team conducted a comprehensive inspection of cinemas in the jurisdiction, focusing on whether the location of the preferential policy disclosure was prominent, whether the staff accurately understood the policy, and whether the ticket inspection points were equipped with standard measuring tools, comprehensively examining the implementation of Article 44 of the Law on the Protection of Minors.

Through the investigation, the procuratorial organs found two common illegal situations in some cinemas in the jurisdiction: first, online and offline ticket purchase channels did not provide prompt information about the preferential policies; second, the policy benefits were improperly limited, narrowing the scope of beneficiaries from all minors to specific height or student groups.

"The industry problems discovered this time reflect the obvious shortcomings in the current supervision of cinemas in implementing the special protection system for minors, infringing on the legitimate rights and interests of an unspecified majority of minors," Liu Chaoying said.

Market-regulated price ≠ exemption from legal obligations
It is understood that China implements a price mechanism mainly based on market formation. According to the Price Law, the formulation of prices should comply with the law of value, with most goods and services prices subject to market-regulated prices, and a very small number of goods and services subject to government-guided prices or government-set prices.

"Market-regulated price refers to a price set by operators independently and formed through market competition. The basic basis for pricing by operators is production and operation costs and market supply and demand conditions," Liu Chaoying told reporters. Beijing manages projects subject to government-set or government-guided prices through a pricing catalog. The "Beijing Pricing Catalog" shows that the current 13 major items under management include 35 pricing contents, none of which include pricing for movie and theater ticket prices. This means that movie theater ticket prices are subject to market-regulated prices, and their ticket sales activities are considered market operations.

"According to Article 44 of the Law on the Protection of Minors, cinemas and other venues should provide free or discounted access to minors according to relevant regulations. This is a legal obligation of cinemas and cannot be evaded," the case-handling team analyzed. Cinemas should provide prompts for the preferential policies for minors purchasing tickets, reaching a level that can attract consumer attention. The beneficiaries of the policy should not be limited to children of a specific height, but should cover all minors. The specific implementation standards can be reasonably set by operators, but should not compromise the legitimate rights and interests of other minors.

16 cinemas complete rectification of publicizing preferential ticket purchase for minors
On March 18, the Dongcheng District Procuratorate issued a procuratorial suggestion to the relevant authorities regarding the inadequate implementation of preferential ticket prices for minors in cinemas, urging the cinemas to provide free or discounted access to minors as required, prominently display this information at ticketing locations and online ticketing platforms, and promote the introduction of policies for reducing ticket prices for minors, strengthening the protection of minors' rights and interests.

After the procuratorial suggestion was issued, the Dongcheng District Procuratorate held several discussions with the relevant authorities on issues such as legal application and rectification standards, and closely followed up on the progress of rectification. The relevant authorities attached great importance to this matter, quickly establishing a rectification working group, and a special action to protect the viewing rights of minors was launched comprehensively in the Dongcheng District.

On May 7, the relevant authorities provided a written reply on the implementation of rectification. Recently, this authority has supervised 16 cinemas in the jurisdiction to implement preferential policies for minors at ticketing locations. For minors who do not meet the criteria for free tickets, those with identification cards, student IDs, and other documents can also enjoy discounted ticket prices.

Recently, reporters visited several cinemas in Dongcheng District and found that they had placed signs on the front desk clearly publicizing the preferential policies for minors purchasing tickets, such as "Minors above 1.3 meters (including 1.3 meters) need to present their ID card or student ID at the cinema front desk to purchase tickets and enjoy discounted student tickets for viewing" and "Notice for purchasing student tickets: The valid age for purchasing student tickets is under 18 years old (including the day of turning 18), tickets can only be used by the student who purchased them, student tickets can only be purchased with cash, bank cards, WeChat, Alipay, discounts cannot be shared with other cinema activities or third-party activities," and so on.

It is worth noting that the relevant authorities recently established a long-term supervision mechanism of "self-inspection + regular inspection + quick handling of complaints", including the preferential viewing for minors in daily inspections; they also carried out legal publicity activities in cinemas, allowing the concept of protecting minors to take root through poster displays, on-site explanations, and other means.

Reporter's Note
Invisible barriers to discounts? Procuratorial supervision makes them visible
The "invisible threshold" of a movie ticket reflects the real dilemma of protecting the rights of minors. The Dongcheng District Procuratorate of Beijing used big data as a "probe" to accurately identify the problem of cinemas hiding their discount policies, leveraging a procuratorial suggestion to drive industry rectification, demonstrating the rigid power of legal supervision. The significance of this case lies not only in "correcting deviations", but also in building a long-term mechanism - the relevant authorities have included the preferential viewing for minors in daily supervision, while legal publicity has entered cinemas, providing a "double insurance" for the implementation of rights. When legal provisions move from paper to reality, every discounted movie ticket will become a vivid testimony to the protection of minors.

title_en: Platform economy stimulates the vitality of small businesses.
body_en:
Individual industrial and commercial households are the largest operating entities in our country and are an important part of the private economy, playing an irreplaceable role in stabilizing growth, promoting employment, and benefiting the people. Recently, the State Administration for Market Regulation held a symposium on platform companies supporting the development of individual industrial and commercial households, encouraging platform companies to launch more practical measures to support the development of individual industrial and commercial households based on their own characteristics.

As intermediaries and carriers connecting supply and demand, platform companies are continuously exerting efforts through digital empowerment, traffic support, market expansion, and other ways to expand the development space for individual industrial and commercial households.

Real money and silver to reduce operating burdens

In the first quarter of this year, 3.949 million new individual industrial and commercial households were established nationwide. By the end of March, the number of individual industrial and commercial households in the tertiary industry reached 111 million, accounting for nearly ninety percent of the total number of individual industrial and commercial households.

Li Mingtao, an expert from the National E-commerce Demonstration City Expert Committee, introduced that industries such as wholesale and retail, accommodation and catering, and residential services are relatively competitive, coupled with high offline operating costs, resulting in generally low industry profit margins. Therefore, after platform companies entered, they attracted a large number of individual industrial and commercial households in the tertiary industry to conduct online operations.

In recent years, due to the impact of platform companies' low-price competition strategies, the online operating profits of small and micro merchants have gradually decreased. At the same time, the continuously increasing platform service fees and marketing traffic investment have further squeezed the profit margins of small and micro merchants.

To effectively reduce the operating costs of small and micro merchants and promote the healthy development of the platform economy, platform companies in China have introduced a series of support policies.

"We are small merchants and have always faced the pressure of high offline store opening costs. Therefore, in March this year, we switched to selling goods through Kuaishou live streaming," said Gao Jingsheng, the owner of Hebei Cangzhou Jiajia Fashion.

"Zero-cost store opening" is the main reason for attracting Jiajia Fashion to join Kuaishou e-commerce. In order to help small businesses open stores quickly and start operations at lower costs, Kuaishou e-commerce has launched "zero deposit" store opening rights for limited store types and categories, helping more businesses obtain profits through zero-cost "trial operations" on Kuaishou and then pay the deposit later. Currently, Kuaishou's "zero-cost store opening" covers over ten thousand product categories.

At the end of last year, Meituan invested 1 billion yuan to support the innovative development of high-quality catering merchants, of which 500 million yuan was used to support the development of small and medium-sized catering merchants. For high-quality small and medium-sized catering merchants who have been operating on the platform for more than three years, have high repurchase rates, and good reputations, cash support ranging from 5,000 yuan to 50,000 yuan is provided based on their online operating scale. As of now, 38,000 merchants have received cash support.

At the policy level, in order to regulate the collection of commissions, deductions, membership fees, and other behaviors by platforms from operators, the State Administration for Market Regulation recently issued the "Compliance Guidelines for Network Trading Platform Fee Collection (Draft for Soliciting Opinions)," clearly stating that platforms should reasonably set fee standards and improve fee rules, fee disclosure, and other institutional mechanisms. With the implementation of relevant policies, platform companies will further optimize fee compliance construction, promote industry healthy development, and build a good ecological environment for harmonious coexistence between platforms and operators.

Technological innovation activates traffic value

"The aroma of wine is afraid of deep alleys" is a pain point for small and medium-sized individual industrial and commercial households in platform development, and platform traffic plays an important role in enabling operating entities to conduct online operations. By helping businesses accurately connect with traffic through technological means, individual industrial and commercial households can be "seen" and help them obtain tangible benefits.

The State Administration for Market Regulation issued the "Opinions on Guiding Network Trading Platforms to Play a Positive Role in Traffic Support for the Development of Small, Medium, and Micro Enterprises" last year, encouraging platforms to further optimize algorithms based on their own operational conditions, reasonably allocate traffic resources, help operating entities improve brand and product awareness, and expand the market.

Earlier this year, Douyin e-commerce announced nine new measures to support merchants, proposing an "upgrade traffic mechanism." Small businesses on the platform can receive up to 6,000 yuan in traffic vouchers and targeted traffic subsidies to increase the exposure of businesses and products. For new businesses without experience points within 90 days, the platform will also launch a fast operation green channel to help them participate in platform activities and enter the selected alliance.

"With the support of new merchant traffic on the platform, more and more users are coming to our live broadcast room to buy fishing gear, and sales have doubled, gradually developing the company from a small family workshop to a small-scale business," said Zhang Yongjie, founder of the fishing gear brand "Qiaoyufu" from Weihai, Shandong.

The application of technologies such as artificial intelligence has brought many conveniences to businesses within the platform. For example, in Kuaishou's live broadcast room, Magnet has pioneered the use of AIGC technology to help advertisers efficiently produce creative materials; Nuwa Digital Human simplifies the live broadcast process, lowers the threshold for going live; and Digital Employee Intelligent Bot can automatically identify user questions and respond quickly, improving conversion rates.

Li Mingtao suggested that platforms should fully utilize AI and other tools to provide comprehensive operational assistance to individual industrial and commercial households, helping them reduce related operating costs, improve marketing and operational efficiency. At the same time, based on platform big data, provide more targeted customer traffic services to individual merchants, formulate more fair and reasonable traffic distribution algorithms, improve the accuracy of supply and demand matching and customer conversion rates, help individual merchants develop new customers, and increase exposure opportunities for small and medium-sized merchants.

Innovative rules build a solid business barrier

Many individual industrial and commercial households within platforms have long been plagued by problems such as malicious returns, high shipping costs, and negative reviews. To address this, many platforms are innovating mechanisms and upgrading services to build a more fair business ecosystem and create a solid business barrier for merchants.

The return rate of clothing items has always been high. Gao Jingsheng told reporters that the return rate of his store is basically maintained at around 50%, sometimes even as high as 80%, and the cost of freight insurance seriously eats into profits. In response to the issue of freight insurance that concerns merchants, Douyin has introduced a policy to reduce costs, coordinating partners to reduce the freight insurance costs by 10% to 40% for eligible merchants or influencers, expecting to save over 4.5 billion yuan for merchants this year.

Focusing on the pain points of the rating system, Meituan has upgraded the "single subjective rating" to a "multi-dimensional comprehensive rating," evaluating the service level of merchants from multiple dimensions such as food quality, delivery efficiency, and packaging service, while also upgrading the "AI negative review identification system" to automatically intercept fake reviews and malicious attacks, reducing the response time by 12 hours.

To address the issue of some consumers maliciously exploiting the "refund only" clause to take advantage, in November last year, the State Administration for Market Regulation summoned six e-commerce platforms, notifying them of the impact of the "refund only" rule on squeezing the survival space of merchants. Kuaishou has set trigger conditions for "refund only" and given merchants certain choices, and has upgraded its automatic identification capabilities for groups identified as high-frequency unreasonably returning buyers, cracking down on malicious "refund only" behavior.

In optimizing after-sales rules, Taobao and Tmall have established the first account integrity system in the e-commerce industry. For consumer behaviors such as returning goods and dropping packages, merchants can complain and enter the integrity system, and the platform will reject after-sales or implement purchase restrictions as appropriate; Pinduoduo has established a "Merchant Rights Protection Committee" to continuously improve the operational security of small and medium-sized merchants through mechanisms such as dedicated services and rapid dispute resolution.

Li Mingtao stated that through comprehensive empowerment of e-commerce platforms, supporting a group of merchants with certain innovative capabilities, fostering an industry atmosphere that encourages innovation, quality, and branding, not only helps meet the diverse needs of new consumers but also drives industry and merchants to differentiate through competition, moving away from homogenized "price wars."
